fams.label: Painting
fams.test: a picture made by laying paint or ink on a movable flat support — paper, vellum, panel, canvas, cloth or silk. Wall painting fixed to a building is L.
key: 1. Small-format opaque watercolour or ink on paper or vellum, made for a book or an album? → A1.
2. Ink and colour with the brush on silk or paper in the East Asian formats (hanging scroll, handscroll, screen, album)? → A2.
3. A devotional image on a wooden panel in the icon tradition? → A3. A painting on cloth made to be hung or carried (thangka, pata, phad)? → A4.
4. Oil, tempera or acrylic on canvas or panel in the easel tradition and its modern and contemporary lineages? → A5.
5. A folk or popular painting named as its own tradition (reverse glass, coffeehouse painting, bark painting)? → A6.

subs.label: Manuscript & Album Painting
subs.axis: Axis: the painting tradition (a court and school lineage). Small-format pictures in opaque watercolour or ink on paper or vellum, made to illustrate a book or to be mounted in an album (miniature painting).

leaves.label: Arab Painting
leaves.defn: manuscript painting of the Arab lands from the 12th to the 15th century: illustrated scientific texts, the Maqamat of al-Hariri and Kalila wa Dimna, made in Baghdad, Mosul, Syria and Mamluk Egypt (al-Wasiti's 1237 Maqamat).
leaves.aliases: Arabic miniature; Baghdad school; Mesopotamian school
leaves.axis: Schools by centre (Baghdad, Mosul, Mamluk Cairo and Damascus); works: every gathered illustrated Arabic manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 1 (Qur'ans, papyri and text-only items excluded), by phase; then collections and painter-scribes.
catalogues: digitised manuscripts and prints of the Bibliothèque nationale de France
survey of Arab book painting with its principal illustrated manuscripts

leaves.label: Persian Miniature
leaves.defn: Persian manuscript and album painting from the Mongol conquest to the 19th century, taught in court workshops whose schools are named after their centres (Herat, Tabriz, Qazvin, Isfahan, Shiraz, Bukhara); kinds are those schools and their masters (Bihzad, Sultan Muhammad, Riza-yi 'Abbasi).
leaves.see: A1-3 Ottoman Miniature; A1-4 Mughal Painting; I2-1 Persian Lacquer. Possession taxonomy: Persian and Indian miniature painting (F2 Art); Safavid manuscript miniature (F2 Art); Isfahan album miniature (F2 Art).
alias_rows: Shahnameh and Persian illustrated epics (see islamic_world.py)
Attributed to Safavid master Sultan Muhammad
Attributed to Muhammad Qasim, died Hegira 1070 / AD 1659/60 (miniature)
leaves.axis: Schools by dynasty and centre (Ilkhanid Tabriz to Safavid Isfahan), canonical sequence; works: every gathered Persian illustrated manuscript or album folio with sitelinks ≥ 1 (Mughal, Deccani and Ottoman items go to those leaves; Qur'ans to Islamic Illumination), by school; then collections; painters grouped by school.
catalogues: illustrated Shahnama manuscripts and their paintings, catalogued worldwide
digitised manuscripts of the Bodleian Libraries, Oxford

leaves.label: Ottoman Miniature
leaves.defn: painting of the Ottoman court workshop (nakkaşhane) for histories, festival books and albums, from Mehmed II to the 18th century (Matrakçı Nasuh's topographies, Nakkaş Osman's Hünername, Levni's Surname-i Vehbi).
leaves.axis: Workshop and phase (nakkaşhane of Mehmed II to the Tulip Period); works: every gathered Ottoman illustrated manuscript or album (illuminated flag, sitelinks ≥ 1; Qur'ans excluded), by reign; then collections and painters by date.
catalogues: The Met collection search: Ottoman manuscript
survey with the principal illustrated Ottoman manuscripts

leaves.label: Mughal Painting
leaves.defn: painting of the Mughal court atelier and its offshoots in South Asia, 16th–19th century: the Hamzanama and the illustrated histories of Akbar, Jahangir's portraits and natural history, and the sub-imperial and provincial schools (Lucknow, Murshidabad).
leaves.see: A1-5 Deccan Painting; A1-6 Company Painting. Possession taxonomy: Mughal miniature (F2 Art).
alias_rows: Attributed to Manôhar and his studio

leaves.label: Deccan Painting
leaves.defn: painting of the Deccan sultanates (Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, Golconda) and of Hyderabad after them, 16th–19th century, with its lyrical colour and Persian, Turkman and Vijayanagara sources.
leaves.see: A1-4 Mughal Painting. Possession taxonomy: Deccani miniature (F2 Art).
leaves.axis: Schools by sultanate (Ahmadnagar, Bijapur, Golconda, Hyderabad); works: every gathered Deccani manuscript or painting with sitelinks ≥ 1, by sultanate; then collections and painters.
catalogues: survey with schools and principal works

leaves.label: Company Painting
leaves.defn: paintings made by Indian artists for officials of the East India Company and other Europeans, 18th–19th century, in a hybrid of Mughal technique and European natural history and topography (Delhi, Lucknow, Patna, Murshidabad, Tanjore).
leaves.axis: Centres of production (Murshidabad, Patna, Calcutta, Lucknow, Delhi, Tanjore, Trichinopoly, Punjab), then collections and painters.
catalogues: British Museum collection search: Company school
all British Museum objects matching 'Company school'

leaves.label: Rajput Painting
leaves.defn: Court painting of the Rajput kingdoms of Rajasthan and Central India, 16th–19th century, in schools named for their courts: Mewar Ragamala sets, Bundi and Kota hunting scenes, Kishangarh portraits of Radha, Jodhpur durbar paintings.
leaves.see: A1-4 Mughal Painting; A1-8 Pahari Painting. Possession taxonomy: Rajasthani miniature (F2 Art).
leaves.axis: Court schools in canonical order (Mewar, Bundi, Kota, Kishangarh, Jaipur, Marwar, Bikaner, Malwa, then smaller thikanas); then named painters by school. No gathered named-manuscript catalogue exists for the tradition; Collections ranks museums by objects.
catalogues: national portal of Indian museum collections
survey of the court schools and their works

leaves.label: Pahari Painting
leaves.defn: Painting of the Hindu courts of the Punjab Hills, 17th–19th century, from the bold Basohli Rasamanjari to the lyrical Guler and Kangra Gita Govinda and Bhagavata Purana series of the family of Pandit Seu.
leaves.see: A1-7 Rajput Painting; A1-4. Possession taxonomy: Pahari miniature (F2 Art).
leaves.axis: Hill-court schools from the Basohli phase to the Guler–Kangra phase (Basohli, Nurpur, Mankot, Jasrota, Guler, Kangra, Chamba, Mandi, Kulu, Bilaspur, Garhwal, Jammu); works: every gathered Pahari manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 1; then collections and painters (family of Pandit Seu first).
catalogues: national portal of Indian museum collections
survey of schools and their works

leaves.label: Jain Manuscript Painting
leaves.defn: The Western Indian style of manuscript painting on palm leaf and then paper (11th–16th century), chiefly Jain scriptures with angular figures and projecting far eyes: Kalpasutra, Kalakacharyakatha, painted wooden covers (patli).
leaves.aliases: Western Indian style;Jain painting;Western Indian painting
leaves.axis: Sub-types by text (Kalpasutra, Kalakacharya-katha), then every gathered Jain illustrated manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 1 by date, then collections.
catalogues: survey including the Western Indian manuscript style

leaves.label: Sikh Painting
leaves.defn: Painting in the Punjab under Sikh patronage, late 18th–19th century, in Pahari and Company-influenced idioms: portraits of Ranjit Singh and his court, Janamsakhi illustrations, Gurus series.
leaves.axis: Sub-types (court portraiture, Janamsakhi illustration), then Lahore and hill painters active for Sikh patrons, by date; collections ranked by gathered Sikh (Punjab) objects. No named Sikh manuscript with sitelinks in the gathered data.

leaves.label: Assamese Manuscript Painting
leaves.defn: Manuscript painting of Assam on sanchipat (agarwood-bark) folios, 16th–19th century, in sattriya and Ahom court styles: Hastividyarnava, illustrated Bhagavata.
leaves.axis: Styles (Sattriya, Ahom court Garhgaya, Darrang), then named manuscripts known from the literature (the gathered rows are noise), then painters; collections ranked by gathered Assam objects.
catalogues: national portal of Indian museum collections

leaves.label: Burmese Parabaik Painting
leaves.defn: Painting in watercolour on white parabaik (folding books of mulberry paper) by the royal and monastic painters of Konbaung Burma, 18th–19th century: court ceremonies and processions, Life of the Buddha, Jataka cycles, cosmologies.
leaves.axis: Sub-types (white and black parabaik), then the Konbaung court workshops and named painters by date; collections ranked by gathered parabaik and court-painting objects.
catalogues: the Burmese folding-book form and its painting

leaves.label: Thai Manuscript Painting
leaves.defn: Paintings in gouache and gold on khoi-paper folding books of Siam, late 17th–19th century, chiefly funerary chanting books: Phra Malai manuscripts, Traiphum cosmologies, Ten Great Jatakas.
leaves.aliases: samut khoi painting;Phra Malai manuscript painting
alias_rows: Thai manuscript painting (samut khoi, Phra Malai)
leaves.axis: Sub-types by text (Phra Malai, Traiphum, treatises), then every gathered named Thai manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 1, then collections.

leaves.label: Nara-ehon
leaves.defn: Illustrated books and scrolls of tales painted in bright mineral colours by largely anonymous town painters of Kyoto, late 16th–18th century: Tales of Ise, Bunshō zōshi, otogi-zōshi booklets.
leaves.weak: Nara-ehon redirects to E-hon; anonymous workshop tradition, so built here rather than in the artist pass
leaves.axis: Sub-types (book and scroll formats, otogi-zōshi texts), then every gathered illustrated tale manuscript (monogatari copies) with sitelinks ≥ 1, then collections.

leaves.label: Ethiopian Manuscript Painting
leaves.defn: Painting in Ethiopian Christian manuscripts on parchment, from the Aksumite-era gospel books to the Gondarine Marian miracle books: Garima Gospels evangelist portraits, Miracles of Mary (Täammərä Maryam) cycles, illustrated Psalters.
leaves.see: Ethiopian Icon Painting; Ethiopian Manuscripts; C2
leaves.axis: Phases (Aksumite and early Solomonic, Gondarine); works: every gathered Ethiopian painted manuscript (illuminated flag or Gospel book, sitelinks ≥ 1; scrolls go to Ethiopian Magic Scrolls), by phase; then collections.
catalogues: Hill Museum & Manuscript Library digitised manuscripts (Ethiopia, Mali, Middle East, Armenia...)

leaves.label: Byzantine Illuminated Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Painted miniatures in Greek manuscripts of the Byzantine empire, 4th–15th century, from late antique codices to the classicising Macedonian Renaissance and Palaiologan books: Vienna Dioscurides, Rossano Gospels, Paris Psalter, Menologion of Basil II.
leaves.axis: Phases (Early, Macedonian Renaissance, Komnenian, Palaiologan, post-Byzantine); works: every gathered Byzantine manuscript with painted miniatures (illuminated flag or recorded miniature cycle; numbered New Testament witnesses excluded), sitelinks ≥ 1, by phase; then collections and illuminators.

leaves.label: Borgia Group
leaves.defn: The pre-Hispanic ritual and divinatory screenfold codices painted on deerskin in the Mixteca-Puebla style of central Mexico, 14th–early 16th century: Codex Borgia, Codex Laud, Codex Fejérváry-Mayer, Codex Cospi.
leaves.see: A1-18 Mixtec Codices; A1-19 Aztec Codices; C2-16 Maya Codices

leaves.label: Mixtec Codices
leaves.defn: Genealogical and historical screenfold codices painted on deerskin by Mixtec (Ñudzavui) tlacuiloque of Oaxaca, 14th–16th century: Codex Zouche-Nuttall, Codex Vindobonensis Mexicanus I, Codex Bodley, Codex Colombino.
leaves.see: A1-17 Borgia Group; G3-13 Mixtec Goldwork
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered Mixtec screenfold codex with sitelinks ≥ 1 (misattributed Vienna and Bodleian European items excluded), pre-Hispanic first then colonial; then collections.

leaves.label: Aztec Codices
leaves.defn: Pictorial manuscripts of the Nahua of central Mexico, from the few pre-Hispanic and early colonial ritual books to the colonial histories, tribute rolls and encyclopedias painted by indigenous tlacuiloque: Codex Borbonicus, Codex Mendoza, Florentine Codex, Codex Azcatitlan.
leaves.see: A1-17 Borgia Group; A1-18 Mixtec Codices
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered Aztec / Nahua codex with sitelinks ≥ 1, by type (ritual and calendrical, historical and tribute, colonial encyclopaedic); then collections.

leaves.label: Armenian Manuscript Illumination
leaves.defn: Painting and ornament of Armenian Gospel books and service books from the 10th to the 18th century, taught in monastic schools named after their regions: Etchmiadzin Gospels, Mugni Gospels, Toros Roslin's Gospels, Glajor Gospels.

leaves.label: Nepalese Manuscript Painting
leaves.defn: Paintings on the palm-leaf folios and wooden covers of Buddhist and Hindu manuscripts made by Newar artists of the Kathmandu Valley from the 11th century, in the Pala-derived style that fed Tibetan painting: illustrated Prajnaparamita and Pancharaksha manuscripts, painted book covers.

leaves.label: Pala Painting
leaves.defn: The manuscript painting of Bengal and Bihar under the Pala dynasty (c. 10th–12th century), the earliest surviving Indian book painting: small panels of Buddhist deities and scenes on the palm leaves and painted wooden covers of Buddhist texts, above all the Prajnaparamita; the style was carried on in Nepal and Tibet. The manuscripts as books are C2-5.
leaves.see: C2-5 Palm-Leaf Manuscripts; D5-4 Pala Art; A4-7 Thangka

leaves.defn: Scholar-amateur painting of China (wenrenhua) and its Korean and Japanese reflexes, valuing brushwork, poetry and calligraphy over likeness: Ni Zan's Rongxi Studio, Huang Gongwang's Dwelling in the Fuchun Mountains, Dong Qichang's landscapes.

leaves.label: Zhe School
leaves.defn: The professional Ming school of landscape continuing Southern Song Ma–Xia painting (15th–16th century): Dai Jin's Returning Home Late from a Spring Outing, Wu Wei's figures.

leaves.label: Wu School
leaves.defn: The Ming literati school of Suzhou (15th–16th century) around Shen Zhou and Wen Zhengming: Shen Zhou's Lofty Mount Lu, Wen Zhengming's Old Trees by a Cold Waterfall.
leaves.see: A2-3 Literati Painting; A2-4 Zhe School

leaves.label: Shanghai School
leaves.defn: The commercial-literati painting of late Qing Shanghai, bold in colour and subject: Ren Bonian's portraits, Wu Changshuo's flowers.
leaves.see: A2-3 Literati Painting; A2-7 Lingnan School

leaves.label: Lingnan School
leaves.defn: The Cantonese school (early 20th century) of the Gao brothers and Chen Shuren that joined Chinese brushwork with Japanese and Western realism: Gao Jianfu's Flying in the Rain, Zhao Shao'ang's birds.
leaves.axis: Generations: the three founders, then their pupils of the second generation (artist-led leaf).

leaves.label: Yamato-e
leaves.defn: The classical Japanese narrative and court painting style from the Heian period, continued by the Tosa school: the Tale of Genji scrolls, the Shigisan engi emaki, Tosa Mitsuoki's Quail and Millet.
leaves.see: A2-9 Kanō School; A2-10 Rinpa School

leaves.label: Kanō School
leaves.defn: The hereditary school of Japanese official painting (15th–19th century) joining Chinese ink and Yamato-e colour: Kanō Eitoku's Cypress Trees, Kanō Tan'yū's Nijō Castle screens.
leaves.see: A2-8 Yamato-e; A2-10 Rinpa School. Possession taxonomy: Painted folding screen (F2 Art); Kanō gold-ground screen (F2 Art).

leaves.label: Rinpa School
leaves.defn: The decorative Japanese school of Sōtatsu, Kōrin and Hōitsu (17th–19th century): Sōtatsu's Wind God and Thunder God, Kōrin's Irises.

leaves.label: Nanga
leaves.defn: Japanese literati painting (bunjinga) of the later Edo period and its Meiji continuation: Ike no Taiga and Yosa Buson's Ten Conveniences and Ten Pleasures, Uragami Gyokudō's Frozen Clouds.

leaves.label: Maruyama–Shijō School
leaves.defn: The naturalistic Kyoto painting of Maruyama Ōkyo and Matsumura Goshun (from the 1770s) and its modern heirs: Ōkyo's Pine Trees in Snow, Goshun's Woodcutters and Fishermen.

leaves.axis: Sub-types (painted panels, chased-silver revetments), then centres and named icons by date; collections.
catalogues: national collections incl. the treasury of medieval icons

leaves.label: Palaeologan Renaissance
leaves.defn: Late Byzantine painting (1261–1453), classicising and intensely expressive in icons and frescoes: the Chora Church frescoes, Theophanes the Greek's icons.
leaves.see: A3-3 Cretan School; A3-6 Russian Icons
leaves.axis: Workshops: Thessaloniki and Macedonian painters, Constantinople, painters in Rus' (artist-led leaf).
catalogues: the period with its works and painters

leaves.label: Russian Icons
leaves.defn: Icon painting of Rus' and Muscovy and its schools (Novgorod, Moscow, Vologda, Stroganov): Rublev's Trinity, Dionisius's Ferapontov icons.
alias_rows: Old Believer icons and cast icons
leaves.axis: Schools in order (Novgorod, Pskov, Moscow, Vologda, Stroganov, Armoury Chamber, Old Believer and Urals), then painters by school; secular Petrine painters wrongly gathered here last.
catalogues: State Catalogue of the Museum Fund of the Russian Federation
the main collection of Old Russian icons

subs.label: Cloth & Scroll Painting
subs.axis: Axis: tradition. Built at scale (thangka, pata, phad, kalighat).

leaves.label: Pattachitra
leaves.defn: Cloth-based painting of Odisha by the chitrakar community of Puri and Raghurajpur, in mineral colour on gum-and-chalk-primed cotton: Jagannath images, Gita Govinda panels, palm-leaf pothis.
leaves.see: A4-2; A4-3. Possession taxonomy: Pattachitra (F2 Art).
leaves.axis: Sub-types (pata on cloth, palm-leaf engraving, ganjifa), then centres and painters; collections ranked by gathered Odisha pata objects.
catalogues: national portal of Indian museum collections

leaves.label: Bengal Patachitra
leaves.defn: The narrative scroll painting of the patuas (chitrakars) of West Bengal and Bangladesh, unrolled frame by frame while the painter sings (pater gaan): Manasamangal scrolls, Jadupatua scrolls of the Santal.
leaves.axis: Sub-types (narrative jorano scrolls, chauko square pats, Santal jadupatua), then centres and patua painters; collections.
catalogues: the patua community and their scroll painting

leaves.label: Kalighat Painting
leaves.defn: Watercolours on mill paper sold by patua painters at the Kalighat temple in Calcutta, 19th–early 20th century, with bold outlines and satire of urban life: Durga and Kali icons, Tarakeswar scandal, babu and courtesan pictures.
leaves.see: A4-2; A1-6. Possession taxonomy: Kalighat painting (F2 Art).
leaves.axis: Painter families of the Kalighat bazaar by date, then the modern heir Jamini Roy; collections ranked by gathered Kalighat objects (V&A first).

leaves.label: Pichwai
leaves.defn: Large painted cloth hangings made at Nathdwara to hang behind the image of Shrinathji: Sharad Purnima, Annakut, cows and lotus ponds.
leaves.axis: Sub-types by festival and subject, then the Nathdwara centre and painters; collections.

leaves.label: Mata ni Pachedi
leaves.defn: Ritual cloth shrines of the Vaghri community of Ahmedabad, hand-painted and block-printed in red and black around the Mother Goddess: Mata on her vahana, temple cloth panels.
leaves.axis: Sub-types (pachedi cloth, chandarvo canopy), then the Ahmedabad centre and makers; collections.
catalogues: V&A Collections search: Mata ni pachedi
all V&A objects matching 'Mata ni pachedi'
V&A Collections search: Mata ni pachedi
all V&A objects matching 'Mata ni pachedi'

leaves.label: Cheriyal Scroll Painting
leaves.defn: Narrative scrolls of Cheriyal in Telangana painted for the bardic storytellers of the Kaki Padagollu: Markandeya Purana scrolls, Gauda Purana.
leaves.axis: Sub-types by narrative (Puranas of the caste storytellers), then the Cheriyal centre and painters; collections.
catalogues: national portal of Indian museum collections

leaves.label: Thangka
leaves.defn: Buddhist painting on cotton or silk mounted in a textile frame to be hung, rolled and carried, the principal portable painting of Tibet, Bhutan, Ladakh and Mongolia: deity and lineage portraits, mandalas, wheel-of-life paintings, appliqué festival thangkas.
leaves.see: A4-8 Beri; A4-9 Menri; A4-10 Khyenri; A4-11 Karma Gadri; A4-13 Paubha; L2-13. Possession taxonomy: F4: Devotional scroll painting (F2 Art); thangka (F4 Religious & Ceremonial Objects); paubha (F4 Religious & Ceremonial Objects); mandala (F4 Religious & Ceremonial Objects).
leaves.axis: Painting styles in historical order (Pala-derived, Beri, Gyantse, Menri, Khyenri, Karma Gadri, eastern Tibetan schools, Qing court), then regional centres; collections ranked by gathered Himalayan painting objects.
catalogues: over 60,000 images of Himalayan and Tibetan art, indexed by tradition and painting style

leaves.label: Beri
leaves.defn: The Newar-derived style of Tibetan painting (13th–15th century) and its later continuations, with dense red and blue grounds and Nepalese figure canons: Sakya lineage thangkas, Ngor mandala sets.
leaves.axis: Phases (13th–15th-century Beri, Ngor mandala style), then centres; collections ranked by gathered Beri and Ngor objects.
catalogues: over 60,000 images of Himalayan and Tibetan art, indexed by tradition and painting style

leaves.label: Menri
leaves.defn: The central Tibetan painting tradition founded by Menla Döndrub (15th century), with Chinese-inspired landscape and a canon of peaceful deities, renewed as New Menri by Choying Gyatso at Tashi Lhunpo (17th century): arhat sets, lineage paintings.
leaves.axis: Phases (Old Menri, Tashi Lhunpo Menri, New Menri), then founders and masters by date; collections.
catalogues: over 60,000 images of Himalayan and Tibetan art, indexed by tradition and painting style

leaves.label: Khyenri
leaves.defn: The central Tibetan painting style created by Khyentse Chenmo of Gongkar Chöde (15th century), known for wrathful deities, bright palettes and near-circular haloes: Gongkar Chöde murals, wrathful protector thangkas.
leaves.axis: Founder and followers by date; collections ranked by gathered Khyenri objects.
catalogues: over 60,000 images of Himalayan and Tibetan art, indexed by tradition and painting style

leaves.label: Karma Gadri
leaves.defn: The 'encampment' painting tradition of the Karma Kagyu, founded by Namkha Tashi (16th century) and renewed by Situ Panchen at Palpung (18th century), with open Chinese-style landscapes and pale grounds: Situ Panchen's Eight Great Mahasiddhas, Tenth Karmapa paintings.
leaves.axis: Phases (Namkha Tashi foundation, Choying Dorje, Palpung revival), then painters by date; collections.
catalogues: over 60,000 images of Himalayan and Tibetan art, indexed by tradition and painting style

leaves.label: Regong Arts
leaves.defn: The thangka painting (with murals, sculpture and appliqué) of the monastic artists of Rebkong (Tongren) in Amdo, from the 17th century to the present, on UNESCO's list since 2009: Wutun monastery thangkas, contemporary Rebkong painting.
leaves.axis: Sub-types (thangka, mural, appliqué, sculpture), then villages and painters; collections.
catalogues: over 60,000 images of Himalayan and Tibetan art, indexed by tradition and painting style

leaves.label: Paubha
leaves.defn: Newar Buddhist and Hindu painting on cloth of the Kathmandu Valley, from the 12th century to the present, with flat red grounds and donor registers: Vasudhara mandalas, Chakrasamvara paubhas, long narrative vratha paintings.
leaves.axis: Phases (Early Malla, Late Malla, Shah), then painters by date; collections ranked by gathered Newar painting objects.
catalogues: over 60,000 images of Himalayan and Tibetan art, indexed by tradition and painting style

leaves.label: Dunhuang Paintings
leaves.defn: The portable Buddhist paintings and banners on silk, hemp and paper deposited in the Library Cave (Cave 17) at the Mogao Caves, 8th–10th century: Tejaprabha and the Five Planets (897), bodhisattva banners, Famous Images of the Buddha.
leaves.axis: Sub-types (banners, silk paintings, paper sketches), then the Library Cave and collections ranked by gathered Dunhuang objects.
catalogues: digitised manuscripts and paintings from Dunhuang and the Silk Road
the site and its Library Cave

leaves.label: Kamasan Painting
leaves.defn: The classical wayang-style painting of Kamasan village in Klungkung, Bali, on cloth and bark paper for temples and palaces since the Gelgel court (16th century): ider-ider friezes, langse hangings, palelintangan calendars, Kerta Gosa ceilings.
leaves.aliases: Kamasan wayang painting;wayang style painting;sangging Kamasan
leaves.axis: Sub-types (ider-ider, langse, calendar paintings), then the Kamasan centre and painters by date; collections.

leaves.label: Wayang Beber
leaves.defn: Javanese narrative scroll painting on dluwang bark paper, unrolled scene by scene by a dalang: Panji scrolls of Pacitan and Gunung Kidul.
leaves.axis: Sub-types (Panji cycle scrolls), then the surviving village sets (Pacitan, Gunung Kidul); collections.

leaves.label: Ethiopian Magic Scrolls
leaves.defn: Protective parchment scrolls cut to the owner's height and painted by däbtära (church-trained scholars) with talismanic figures, eyes, angels and nets beside Ge'ez prayers: healing scrolls, talismanic eyes and faces, Solomon's net designs.
leaves.axis: Sub-types by protective figure, then makers (däbtära); works: every gathered Ethiopian scroll with sitelinks ≥ 1; collections.
catalogues: Hill Museum & Manuscript Library digitised manuscripts (Ethiopia, Mali, Middle East, Armenia...)

leaves.label: Plains Hide Painting
leaves.defn: Painting on tanned or raw hide by the peoples of the Great Plains: men's figurative war-exploit and calendar painting and women's geometric designs, on painted buffalo robes, tipi covers and liners, parfleches and winter counts.
leaves.axis: Sub-types (men's figurative robes, women's geometric robes, parfleche, winter counts), then peoples and named painters; collections ranked by gathered Plains painted-hide objects.
catalogues: Smithsonian Collections Search: painted hide robe
Smithsonian objects (incl. Freer|Sackler) matching 'painted hide robe'

leaves.label: Quillango
leaves.defn: The painted guanaco-skin robes of the Tehuelche (Aónikenk) of Patagonia, sewn from many pelts, worn fur inward with the painted side out, decorated with red, black and yellow geometric designs.
src: Archivo General de la Nación, Argentina
leaves.axis: types, then the peoples who make it, then holding institutions

leaves.label: Naskapi Painted Coats
leaves.defn: The painted caribou-skin coats of the Innu (Naskapi) of Quebec and Labrador, cut on the model of European frock coats and painted with dream-given designs in mineral and plant pigments bound with fish roe, with a triangular back gusset for the mountain of the Caribou Master; worn for one hunting season.
leaves.axis: types, then the peoples who make it, then holding institutions
catalogues: The Met collection search: Naskapi Painted Coats
Naskapi Painted Coats in the Metropolitan Museum

leaves.label: Yao Ritual Paintings
leaves.defn: The Taoist ceremonial scroll paintings (mien fang) of the Yao (Iu Mien) of South China, northern Vietnam, Laos and Thailand: sets of about seventeen hanging scrolls of the Three Pure Ones, the Jade Emperor, marshals and other deities displayed in ordinations and rites.
src: Pha Tad Ke, Yao Mien Ceremonial Paintings
leaves.axis: types, then the peoples who make it, then holding institutions
catalogues: The Met collection search: Yao Ritual Paintings
Yao Ritual Paintings in the Metropolitan Museum

leaves.label: Tangut Buddhist Painting
leaves.defn: The Buddhist painting of the Tangut Western Xia (1038–1227), known chiefly from the hoard of Khara-Khoto excavated by Kozlov in 1908–1909: thangkas and silk paintings of Amitabha, Chakrasamvara, Vajravarahi and other deities in Tibetan and Chinese styles, with clay sculpture and xylograph frontispieces.
leaves.axis: types, then the peoples who make it, then holding institutions
catalogues: The Met collection search: Tangut Buddhist Painting
Tangut Buddhist Painting in the Metropolitan Museum

subs.label: Easel Painting
subs.axis: Axis: period style, school or movement. Built at scale for the European lineage and modern and contemporary painting; the pilot holds one non-European court tradition.

leaves.label: Qajar Painting
leaves.defn: court painting of Qajar Iran (1789–1925) in oil on canvas and in watercolour: life-size royal portraits and figures of pleasure (Mihr 'Ali), and the realist watercolours of Abu'l-Hasan Ghaffari (Sani' al-Mulk).
leaves.see: A1-2 Persian Miniature; I2-1 Persian Lacquer
leaves.axis: Reigns: Fath-Ali Shah court painters, then the Naser al-Din Shah era; photographers of Qajar Iran last; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: The Met collection search: Qajar painting
survey of Qajar painting and its masters

leaves.label: Balinese Painting
leaves.defn: The modern painting of Bali from the late 1920s on paper and canvas, in the village schools that grew up around the Pita Maha association: Ubud genre and landscape, Batuan dense ink-and-wash scenes, Lempad's line drawings.
leaves.weak: the Balinese painting article redirects to Balinese art; woodcarving of Mas in the source row has no leaf yet
alias_rows: Balinese woodcarving and painting (Ubud, Batuan, Mas)
leaves.axis: Schools by village and group: Batuan, Ubud and the Pita Maha association, Sanur, Penestanan Young Artists; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: survey of Balinese painting schools and painters

leaves.label: Sơn Mài
leaves.defn: Vietnamese lacquer painting on panel, developed as a fine art at the École des Beaux-Arts de l'Indochine from the 1930s: landscape and genre panels, gold- and eggshell-inlaid screens.
leaves.see: I2-7. Possession taxonomy: Lacquer painting (F2 Art); Vietnamese sơn mài panel (F2 Art).
leaves.axis: Founders at the École des Beaux-Arts de l'Indochine, then later masters; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Fayum Mummy Portraits
leaves.defn: Portraits painted in encaustic or tempera on wooden panels and bound over the faces of mummies in Roman Egypt, 1st–3rd century: Hawara and Er-Rubayat portraits, Tomb of Aline, portraits from Antinoöpolis.
leaves.axis: Sub-types by technique, then the excavated sites (Hawara, er-Rubayat, Antinoöpolis), named works with holding museum, collectors; collections ranked by gathered mummy-portrait objects.
catalogues: The Met collection search: mummy portrait
British Museum collection search: mummy portrait
all British Museum objects matching 'mummy portrait'
survey of the genre and its sites

leaves.label: New Spanish Baroque
leaves.defn: The painting of the Viceroyalty of New Spain in the Baroque idiom, 17th–18th century, from the large altarpieces and sacristy canvases of Mexico City to devotional and civic pictures: Villalpando's Puebla cathedral dome, Juan Correa's sacristy canvases, Miguel Cabrera's Virgins of Guadalupe.
leaves.see: A5-6 Casta Painting; A5-7 Enconchado; A5-8 Biombo; A5-9 Cusco School
leaves.axis: Generations: Mannerist founders, 17th-century Baroque masters, 18th-century painters of the Academy generation; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: The Met collection search: New Spain painting
all Met objects matching 'New Spain painting'
Museo Nacional de Arte, Mexico City
national collection of New Spanish painting

leaves.label: Casta Painting
leaves.defn: Sets of paintings made in 18th-century New Spain (and occasionally Peru) depicting the hierarchy of racial mixtures as family groups with their dress and produce: Miguel Cabrera's casta series (1763), José de Páez series.
leaves.axis: Painters of casta series by date, then the series as works with holding museum; collections ranked by gathered casta objects.
catalogues: survey of the genre with known series

leaves.label: Enconchado
leaves.defn: Paintings of late 17th- and early 18th-century New Spain in oil on panel with inlaid fragments of mother-of-pearl under translucent glazes, influenced by Japanese namban lacquer: González family Conquest of Mexico series, Virgin of Guadalupe (1698).
leaves.see: A5-5 New Spanish Baroque; A5-8 Biombo; I2-15 Mexican Lacquerware
leaves.weak: pool QID Q135448181 not verified; Met object record names the technique
leaves.axis: Workshop (the González family of Mexico City) and named series; collections.

leaves.label: Biombo
leaves.defn: Painted folding screens made in New Spain from the early 17th century after Japanese byōbu, with views of Mexico City, the Conquest and festivities: Biombo of the Conquest and View of Mexico City, Indian wedding and flying pole screen.
leaves.see: A5-5 New Spanish Baroque; A5-7 Enconchado
leaves.axis: Sub-types by subject (Conquest, city views, allegories), then centres and named screens; collections.

leaves.label: Cusco School
leaves.defn: The school of religious painting centred on Cusco in the Viceroyalty of Peru, 16th–18th century, with Andean painters working from Flemish prints and adding brocade gold (brocateado) and local flora: Corpus Christi series, archangel arquebusiers, Diego Quispe Tito's zodiac series.
leaves.see: A5-10 Potosí School; A5-11 Quito School; A5-5 New Spanish Baroque
leaves.axis: Generations: European founders, 17th-century Andean masters, 18th-century workshop production; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: The Met collection search: Cuzco school

leaves.label: Potosí School
leaves.defn: The school of painting of the silver city of Potosí in Upper Peru (Bolivia), 17th–18th century, led by Melchor Pérez de Holguín: Entry of Viceroy Morcillo into Potosí, Virgin of the Cerro.
leaves.axis: Masters of the Potosí school by date, then works; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: the school's master and his works

leaves.label: Quito School
leaves.defn: The painting and polychrome sculpture of the Audiencia of Quito, 16th–18th century, known for its realist carved and estofado images and its painting workshops: Miguel de Santiago's Augustinian series, Legarda's winged Virgin of Quito, Caspicara's sculptural groups.
leaves.axis: Painters, then sculptors of the Quito school, each by date; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Western Desert Painting
leaves.defn: The acrylic painting movement of the Central and Western Desert begun at Papunya in 1971, in which Dreaming (Tjukurrpa/Jukurrpa) designs once made in sand, body paint and ceremony are painted on canvas and board in dotted and concentric-circle fields, carried on by community art centres: Papunya Tula boards, Warlukurlangu Jukurrpa canvases, Utopia and APY Lands painting.
leaves.aliases: Western Desert art movement;dot painting;Papunya Tula painting;acrylic desert painting
leaves.see: A5-13; H8-26; L1-31. Possession taxonomy: Western Desert dot painting (F2 Art).
leaves.weak: Western Desert art movement and Dot painting both redirect to Papunya Tula; art centres are kinds; Utopia (Anmatyerre/Alyawarr, Arandic) is placed here by convention as Central Desert painting
leaves.axis: Art centres from Papunya Tula (1971) outward across the Western and Central Deserts, then artists grouped by their centre
catalogues: searchable collection incl. the largest holding of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art
the founding art centre's site and artists

leaves.label: Contemporary Indigenous Australian Art
leaves.defn: Painting by Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander artists from the 1970s onward outside the Western Desert and bark-painting lineages, in ochre and acrylic on canvas, worked through community art centres: Warmun (Turkey Creek) ochre paintings, Mangkaja and Ngukurr acrylics, Mornington Island painting, Mowanjum Wandjina paintings.
leaves.axis: Regions and art centres (East Kimberley, Mowanjum, Fitzroy Crossing, Mornington Island, Utopia, Arnhem Land and Tiwi), then artists grouped by their centre
catalogues: searchable collection incl. the largest holding of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art
Art Gallery of New South Wales collection
major holding of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art

leaves.label: Hermannsburg School
leaves.defn: The Western Arrernte watercolour landscape school of the Hermannsburg mission (from 1934), founded by Albert Namatjira after lessons with Rex Battarbee and carried on by his family and followers: MacDonnell Ranges landscapes, ghost gums.
leaves.axis: The Namatjira family and the Arrernte watercolourists of Hermannsburg by generation, with their teacher
catalogues: searchable collection incl. the largest holding of Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander art
secs: Pareroultja brothers and other Arrernte painters

leaves.label: Romanesque Painting
leaves.defn: Panel, book and wall painting of Latin Europe in the 11th–12th centuries, with flat, linear, hieratic figures: the Master of Pedret, painted altar frontals of Catalonia, the Registrum Gregorii.
leaves.see: A5-16 Gothic Painting; L2 Wall Painting
leaves.axis: Medium of the named masters: wall and panel painters, illuminators and scribes, Byzantine and Georgian painters, metalworkers, runemasters; by date within each; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: Museu Nacional d'Art de Catalunya collection
the largest collection of Romanesque mural painting

leaves.label: Gothic Painting
leaves.defn: Painting in Latin Europe from the 13th to the late 14th century, from Italo-Byzantine panel crosses to the narrative altarpieces of Giotto and his followers: Coppo di Marcovaldo's crucifixes, Giotto's Ognissanti Madonna, Catalan Gothic retables.
leaves.see: A5-17 Sienese School; A5-18 International Gothic

leaves.label: Sienese School
leaves.defn: The school of painting of Siena, 13th–15th century, with its gold grounds, lyrical line and colour: Duccio's Maestà, Simone Martini's Annunciation, Lorenzetti's Allegory of Good Government.
leaves.see: A5-16 Gothic Painting; A5-18 International Gothic
leaves.axis: Generations: Duccio and the 13th-century founders, Trecento (Simone Martini, the Lorenzetti), late Trecento, Quattrocento, 16th-century Sienese Mannerism
catalogues: the principal collection of Sienese painting

leaves.label: International Gothic
leaves.defn: The courtly late Gothic style shared by painters across Europe c. 1375–1425, elegant, decorative and richly detailed: the Wilton Diptych, Gentile da Fabriano's Adoration of the Magi, the Très Riches Heures.
leaves.see: A5-16 Gothic Painting; A5-19 Early Netherlandish Painting
leaves.axis: by court and regional school: Siena, Florence, the Marche, Venice, Bologna and Verona, Lombardy; Paris and the Valois courts, Provence, German lands (Soft Style), Crown of Aragon; by birth year

leaves.label: Early Netherlandish Painting
leaves.defn: Oil painting of the Burgundian and Habsburg Netherlands in the 15th and early 16th centuries, with minute naturalism and luminous glazes: the Ghent Altarpiece, the Arnolfini Portrait, Rogier van der Weyden's Descent from the Cross.
leaves.see: A5-22 Northern Renaissance; C2-30 Ghent-Bruges School
leaves.axis: Generations and centres: founders (Campin, van Eyck, van der Weyden), Bruges, Brabant (Brussels, Leuven), Ghent, Northern Netherlands (Haarlem, Leiden, Delft), Antwerp c. 1500–1530, illuminators, painters active abroad

leaves.label: Italian Renaissance Painting
leaves.defn: Painting in Italy c. 1400–1530, from the perspective and naturalism of the Florentine Early Renaissance to the High Renaissance: Masaccio's Trinity, Piero della Francesca's Flagellation, Leonardo's Last Supper, Raphael's School of Athens.
leaves.see: A5-21 Venetian School; A5-23 Mannerism; A5-22 Northern Renaissance. Possession taxonomy: Cassone (B1 Furniture & Storage).

leaves.label: Venetian School
leaves.defn: The painting of Venice and its terraferma from the Bellini to the 18th century, built on colour and light: Giovanni Bellini's San Zaccaria Altarpiece, Giorgione's Tempest, Titian's Assumption, Veronese's Wedding at Cana.
leaves.axis: Generations: early Renaissance (Vivarini, Bellini, Crivelli), High Renaissance (Giorgione, Titian, Palma), late Renaissance (Tintoretto, Veronese, Bassano), then the 17th-century followers and printmakers

leaves.label: Northern Renaissance
leaves.defn: The Renaissance north of the Alps (German lands, the Low Countries, France, England), c. 1490–1580: Dürer's Self-Portrait of 1500, the Isenheim Altarpiece, Holbein's Ambassadors, Bruegel's Hunters in the Snow.

leaves.label: Mannerism
leaves.defn: The artificial, elongated and complex style that followed the High Renaissance, c. 1520–1600: Pontormo's Deposition, Parmigianino's Madonna with the Long Neck, Bronzino's Allegory with Venus and Cupid.
leaves.see: A5-24 School of Fontainebleau; A5-25 Baroque Painting
leaves.axis: by centre and generation: Florence (first generation, court Mannerism, reform), Rome (Raphael's heirs, late Mannerism), Parma, Bologna, Venice, Lombardy and Cremona, Genoa, Urbino and the South; Northern Mannerism; Fontainebleau; Iberia; others last; by birth year

leaves.label: School of Fontainebleau
leaves.defn: The Mannerist decoration and painting of the French court at Fontainebleau, led by Rosso and Primaticcio (c. 1530–1610): the Galerie François I, Gabrielle d'Estrées and One of Her Sisters.
leaves.axis: First School (Italian founders under Francis I) then Second School (Henri IV)
catalogues: Louvre database, incl. Fontainebleau school paintings and drawings

leaves.label: Baroque Painting
leaves.defn: European painting of the 17th and early 18th centuries, dramatic in light, movement and emotion, from Rome to Madrid and the colonial Americas: Rubens's Elevation of the Cross, Velázquez's Las Meninas, Pietro da Cortona's Barberini ceiling.
leaves.see: A5-26 Caravaggisti; A5-27 Flemish Baroque Painting; A5-28 Dutch Golden Age Painting; A5-29 Rococo
leaves.axis: by regional school: Caravaggisti, Bologna, Rome, Naples, Genoa, Venice, Florence, Lombardy, other Italian centres; Spain and colonies; France (Lorraine, classicism, Académie, Régence); Flanders, Dutch Republic, Holy Roman Empire, Central Europe, Britain, Scandinavia; quadratura, architects and others last; by birth year within groups

leaves.label: Caravaggisti
leaves.defn: Followers of Caravaggio's dramatic tenebrism and naturalism across Europe, c. 1600–1640: Gentileschi's Judith Slaying Holofernes, Ter Brugghen's Calling of Saint Matthew, Valentin de Boulogne's Concert.
leaves.axis: Circles: Roman and Italian Caravaggisti, French Caravaggisti in Rome, Utrecht Caravaggism, other Netherlandish followers

leaves.label: Flemish Baroque Painting
leaves.defn: Painting of the Southern Netherlands c. 1585–1700 around Rubens, van Dyck and Jordaens: Rubens's Descent from the Cross, van Dyck's Charles I at the Hunt, Snyders's market stalls.
leaves.see: A5-25 Baroque Painting; A5-28 Dutch Golden Age Painting
leaves.axis: by generation and Antwerp circle: pre-Rubens Mannerists, the Brueghel dynasty and cabinet painting, Rubens and his studio, Flemish Caravaggisti, then specialisms (still life, landscape, genre), Brussels and Bruges, émigrés; by birth year within groups

leaves.label: Dutch Golden Age Painting
leaves.defn: Painting of the Dutch Republic in the 17th century, its genres sold on an open market: Rembrandt's Night Watch, Vermeer's View of Delft, Ruisdael's Jewish Cemetery, Heda's breakfast pieces.
leaves.see: A5-27 Flemish Baroque Painting; A5-25 Baroque Painting
leaves.axis: by city school and circle (Haarlem, Amsterdam, Rembrandt's pupils, Leiden fijnschilders, Delft, Utrecht, Dordrecht), then the named specialisms of the period (Italianates, landscape phases, marine, genre, still life, architecture, portraiture), the late classicist phase, Dutch Brazil, printmakers and non-painters last; by birth year within groups

leaves.label: Rococo
leaves.defn: The light, ornamental, intimate style of the 18th century, from the French fêtes galantes to Venetian ceilings: Watteau's Pilgrimage to Cythera, Fragonard's The Swing, Tiepolo's Würzburg ceiling.
leaves.axis: by school: fête galante, French history and decorative painting, portrait and pastel, genre and still life, landscape, ornament and print; Venice; other Italian centres; South German and Austrian fresco; German courts; Switzerland; Low Countries; Britain; colonies; Scandinavia, Russia, Iberia; by birth year within groups
catalogues: searchable database of over 50,000 European paintings and sculptures, 3rd–19th century

Chardin and French genre, still life and animal painting

Rome, Naples and other Italian centres
South German and Austrian Rococo (fresco and altarpiece)
Prussian, Saxon and other German courts
Spanish colonial Rococo (New Spain, Peru, Upper Peru, Puerto Rico)

leaves.label: Neoclassicism
leaves.defn: Painting of the later 18th and early 19th century modelled on antiquity, severe in line and moral in subject: David's Oath of the Horatii, Mengs's Parnassus, Ingres's Grande Odalisque.
leaves.axis: by atelier or circle first (David's atelier, Ingres and his pupils, the Troubadour painters, the Deutschrömer in Rome, the founders of the Society of Painters in Water Colours, the Peale family); sculptors and architects moved to Neoclassical Sculpture and Neoclassical Architecture. Then the remaining artists by country of activity (historic states folded into present-day countries, Czech, Polish, South Slavic and Baltic artists of the empires listed separately; groups over 150 split by birth year; countries with fewer than 3 artists pooled by region); each group ordered by birth year.
catalogues: complete online catalogue, incl. David and his school
secs: Society of Painters in Water Colours

leaves.label: Romanticism
leaves.defn: Painting c. 1780–1850 that put feeling, the sublime and the imagination before rule: Friedrich's Wanderer above the Sea of Fog, Géricault's Raft of the Medusa, Delacroix's Liberty Leading the People, Turner's Slave Ship.
leaves.see: A5-30 Neoclassicism; A5-38 Academic Art; A5-32 Nazarene Movement
leaves.axis: by named circle or national school first (Troubadour style, juste milieu, German Romanticism, Biedermeier, the Ancients, Bristol School, Society of Painters in Water Colours, Norwegian romantic nationalism, School of Posillipo, Scapigliatura, Venetsianov school, Western American Art); Nazarenes, Düsseldorf, Danish Golden Age, Norwich, Hudson River, Luminism, Lyon and Orientalist painters moved to their own leaves. Then the remaining artists by country of activity (historic states folded into present-day countries, Czech, Polish, South Slavic and Baltic artists of the empires listed separately; groups over 150 split by birth year; countries with fewer than 3 artists pooled by region); each group ordered by birth year.
catalogues: British Romantic painting incl. the Turner Bequest
complete online catalogue of the Louvre, incl. French Romantic painting
images of Romantic works by artist
secs: Society of Painters in Water Colours

leaves.label: Nazarene Movement
leaves.defn: German Romantic painters in Rome (from 1809) who revived the religious art of Dürer and early Raphael: Overbeck's Italia and Germania, the Casa Bartholdy frescoes.
leaves.axis: Founders of the Brotherhood of St Luke in Vienna and Rome, the Munich and Düsseldorf successors, then Purismo and other followers

leaves.label: Danish Golden Age
leaves.defn: Danish painting of the first half of the 19th century, around Eckersberg and his pupils: Købke's View of Lake Sortedam, Eckersberg's views of Rome.
leaves.axis: Eckersberg and his Academy pupils first, then the national-romantic landscape painters of the 1840s
catalogues: Danish Golden Age paintings and drawings

leaves.label: Düsseldorf School of Painting
leaves.defn: Painters trained at the Düsseldorf Academy c. 1819–1918, known for detailed landscapes and history scenes: Achenbach's seascapes, Leutze's Washington Crossing the Delaware.
leaves.see: A5-31 Romanticism; A5-36 Hudson River School
leaves.axis: Teachers (the Achenbach brothers and the Academy), then the Scandinavian Düsseldorfers, then other national students; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Barbizon School
leaves.defn: French landscape painters working from nature in the forest of Fontainebleau c. 1830–1870: Rousseau's Forest of Fontainebleau, Millet's The Gleaners, Corot's Souvenir de Mortefontaine.
leaves.axis: The Barbizon founders first, then second-generation French followers, Belgian, American and other national followers
catalogues: the largest holding of Barbizon painting

leaves.label: Hudson River School
leaves.defn: American Romantic landscape painting c. 1825–1875: Cole's The Oxbow, Church's Heart of the Andes, Bierstadt's Rocky Mountains.
leaves.axis: First generation (Cole, Durand and contemporaries), then the second generation (Church, Bierstadt, Gifford, Kensett, Moran), then associated painters
catalogues: Wikipedia: List of Hudson River School artists
complete list of the school's painters

leaves.label: Norwich School of Painters
leaves.defn: The regional landscape school of Norwich (1803–1833) around John Crome and John Sell Cotman: Crome's Mousehold Heath, Cotman's Greta Bridge.
leaves.axis: Founders (Crome, Cotman), then the second generation and associated painters by date
catalogues: principal collection of the Norwich School

leaves.label: Academic Art
leaves.defn: Painting shaped by the European academies and their Salons in the 19th century, finished, idealising and hierarchical in subject: Cabanel's Birth of Venus, Bouguereau's Nymphs and Satyr, Gérôme's Pollice Verso.
leaves.see: A5-30 Neoclassicism; A5-40 Realism; A5-39 Neo-Grec
leaves.axis: by named academy, school or circle first (Écouen, Victorian classicism, The Clique, St John's Wood Clique, fairy painting, Weimar, Tervuren, Generation of the National Theatre, Romanian Official Salon, American Renaissance, Western American Art, San Carlos, Imperial Academy of Brazil); Salon painters already in named school leaves (Munich, Düsseldorf, Hague, Barbizon, Neo-Grec, Orientalism...) moved out. Then the remaining artists by country of activity (historic states folded into present-day countries, Czech, Polish, South Slavic and Baltic artists of the empires listed separately; groups over 150 split by birth year; countries with fewer than 3 artists pooled by region); each group ordered by birth year.
catalogues: every work exhibited at the Paris Salons, 1673–1914
French national catalogue of museum collections
images of academic paintings by artist and museum
secs: Tinerimea artistică and the Official Salon (Romania)

leaves.label: Neo-Grec
leaves.defn: A mid-19th-century French current of small-scale, archaeologically detailed antique genre scenes: Gérôme's Cock Fight, Hamon's My Sister Is Not In.
leaves.axis: French Néo-Grecs of Gleyre's studio, then the Victorian classicists, then the Italian neo-Pompeian painters

leaves.label: Realism
leaves.defn: The mid-19th-century movement that painted contemporary life and labour without idealisation: Courbet's A Burial at Ornans, Millet's The Angelus, Repin's Barge Haulers on the Volga.
leaves.see: A5-45 Naturalism; A5-35 Barbizon School; A5-41 Costumbrismo
leaves.axis: by named school or colony first (École d'Écouen, Volcano School, Molse School, Verismo); Peredvizhniki moved to their own leaf, Soviet painters to Socialist Realism and 20th-century realists to their movements. Then the remaining artists by country of activity (historic states folded into present-day countries, Czech, Polish, South Slavic and Baltic artists of the empires listed separately; groups over 150 split by birth year; countries with fewer than 3 artists pooled by region); each group ordered by birth year.
catalogues: French national catalogue of museum collections

leaves.label: Costumbrismo
leaves.defn: Spanish and Latin American painting of local customs, types and manners in the 19th century: Bécquer's Andalusian scenes, Pancho Fierro's Lima watercolours.
leaves.axis: Country of activity (Spanish costumbrismo, then Latin American and foreign costumbristas)

leaves.label: Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood
leaves.defn: The English brotherhood (1848) and its circle that painted with the detail and colour of art before Raphael: Millais's Ophelia, Rossetti's Beata Beatrix, Hunt's The Light of the World.
leaves.see: A5-32 Nazarene Movement; A5-52 Aestheticism; A5-51 Symbolism
leaves.axis: by circle: the founding Brotherhood, associates and first circle, patrons and muses, the Liverpool school, the second (Aesthetic) generation, later British followers, American and continental followers; by birth year
catalogues: the largest public collection of Pre-Raphaelite art, fully online
complete hypermedia archive of Dante Gabriel Rossetti's pictures and texts
secs: Patrons, critics and women of the circle
Second generation: Morris, Burne-Jones and Aesthetic Pre-Raphaelitism

leaves.label: Hague School
leaves.defn: Dutch painters working in The Hague c. 1860–1900 in grey-toned realist landscape and genre: Mesdag's Panorama, Mauve's Morning Ride on the Beach.
leaves.axis: Romantic precursors, the core Hague School painters, then the second generation and Amsterdam Impressionists, then the Laren School
catalogues: RKD – Netherlands Institute for Art History
artists and images database for Netherlandish and Flemish art

leaves.label: Macchiaioli
leaves.defn: Tuscan painters of the 1850s–1870s who built pictures from patches (macchie) of light and shade: Fattori's The Rotonda di Palmieri, Lega's The Visit.
leaves.axis: The Florentine Caffè Michelangiolo group, then associated and later painters

leaves.label: Naturalism
leaves.defn: Late-19th-century plein-air painting of rural and working life with photographic truth: Bastien-Lepage's Haymaking, Stanhope Forbes's A Fish Sale on a Cornish Beach, the Skagen Painters.
leaves.axis: by artists' colony or group first (Grupo do Leão, Cranbrook Colony, Idyllic school, Concarneau, Étaples, Wissant, Nagybánya); Newlyn and Skagen painters moved to their own leaves. Then the remaining artists by country of activity (historic states folded into present-day countries, Czech, Polish, South Slavic and Baltic artists of the empires listed separately; groups over 150 split by birth year; countries with fewer than 3 artists pooled by region); each group ordered by birth year.
catalogues: French national catalogue of museum collections

leaves.label: Munich School
leaves.defn: Painters trained at the Munich Academy c. 1850–1914 in dark, painterly realism: Leibl's Three Women in Church, Gyzis's works, Chase's early portraits.
leaves.axis: German masters and teachers of the Munich Academy, then the Greek Munich School
catalogues: Neue Pinakothek holdings of the Munich school

leaves.label: Impressionism
leaves.defn: The French movement of the 1860s–1880s that painted modern life and light in broken colour outdoors, and its national offshoots: Monet's Impression, Sunrise, Renoir's Bal du moulin de la Galette, Morisot's The Cradle.
leaves.see: A5-48 Neo-Impressionism; A5-49 Post-Impressionism; A5-45 Naturalism
leaves.axis: by group: precursors, the Batignolles group and Impressionist exhibitions, later French Impressionists, Crozant and Rouen schools; American (Ten, Giverny, Boston, Old Lyme and Cos Cob, Hoosier, California); Heidelberg School, Canada, NEAC; German Secessions, Atmospheric Impressionism, Belgian Luminism, Skagen; then countries of activity; by birth year

leaves.label: Neo-Impressionism
leaves.defn: The systematic colour-division of Seurat and Signac from 1886 and its Italian divisionist branch: Seurat's A Sunday on La Grande Jatte, Signac's Portrait of Félix Fénéon.
leaves.axis: Founders (Seurat, Signac), French pointillists, Belgian Neo-Impressionists of Les XX, Italian Divisionism, then other national branches; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: Art Institute of Chicago collection: Neo-Impressionism

leaves.label: Post-Impressionism
leaves.defn: Painting after Impressionism c. 1886–1905 that turned colour and form to structure and expression: Cézanne's Mont Sainte-Victoire, Van Gogh's Starry Night, Gauguin's Vision after the Sermon.
leaves.see: A5-50 Pont-Aven School; A5-51 Symbolism; A5-57 Fauvism
leaves.axis: by group: founders, Les Nabis, later French post-Impressionists, Belgian Intimism; British (Camden Town, Bloomsbury, Scottish Colourists); Jack of Diamonds; then countries of activity; by birth year

leaves.label: Pont-Aven School
leaves.defn: Painters around Gauguin and Émile Bernard in Brittany from 1886, flat colour and bounding line (synthetism, cloisonnism): Bernard's Breton Women in the Meadow, Sérusier's The Talisman.
leaves.axis: Gauguin's Synthetist circle, the Nabis who passed through Pont-Aven, later followers, then the earlier international colonists of Pont-Aven (1860s–80s)

leaves.label: Symbolism
leaves.defn: Late-19th-century painting of dream, myth and inner states: Moreau's The Apparition, Redon's The Cyclops, Khnopff's I Lock My Door Upon Myself.
leaves.see: A5-42 Pre-Raphaelite Brotherhood; I3-15 Art Nouveau; A5-52 Aestheticism
leaves.axis: by national school and circle: precursors, French founders, Rose + Croix and Idealists, Belgian Les XX, Dutch, Deutschrömer, Munich and Vienna Secessions, Swiss, Nordic, Young Poland, Czech, Hungarian, Russian (with Blue Rose), British, Catalan Modernisme, Italian, Americas; later echoes last; by birth year

leaves.label: Aestheticism
leaves.defn: The British "art for art's sake" painting of the 1860s–1890s: Whistler's Symphony in White, Leighton's Flaming June, Albert Moore's Midsummer.
leaves.axis: Country of activity: the British Aesthetic painters, then the Americans; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Tonalism
leaves.defn: American (and Australian) landscape painting c. 1880–1915 in muted, atmospheric tones: Inness's Home of the Heron, Dewing's The Recitation.
leaves.axis: American Tonalism first, then the Australian and Canadian branches; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Luminism
leaves.defn: American landscape painting c. 1850–1875 of calm, hidden-brushwork light: Fitz Henry Lane's Owl's Head, Heade's Approaching Thunder Storm.
leaves.see: A5-36 Hudson River School; A5-53 Tonalism
leaves.axis: Two movements: American Luminism (mid-19th-century landscape), then Belgian and Dutch Luminism (Neo-Impressionist light painting)

leaves.label: Glasgow School
leaves.defn: The Glasgow Boys (c. 1880–1900), Scottish painters of plein-air naturalism and decorative colour: Guthrie's A Highland Funeral, Henry and Hornel's The Druids.
leaves.axis: The Glasgow Boys, then the Glasgow Girls
catalogues: Kelvingrove's holding of the Glasgow Boys and Girls

leaves.label: Expressionism
leaves.defn: Painting from c. 1905 that distorted colour and form for emotional force, centred in Germany and Austria: Kirchner's Street, Berlin, Kokoschka's The Bride of the Wind, Marc's Blue Horse.
leaves.see: A5-57 Fauvism; A5-68 New Objectivity; A5-98 Neo-Expressionism
leaves.axis: by named group: forerunners, Die Brücke, NKVM and Der Blaue Reiter, Rhenish Expressionists, Berlin (Sturm, Pathetiker), Dresden Secession, Hamburg Secession, Lost Generation; Austria, Latem schools, Bergen School and De Ploeg, Swiss Rot-Blau, School of Paris émigrés; then countries of activity; by birth year

leaves.label: Fauvism
leaves.defn: The French painting of pure, arbitrary colour around Matisse and Derain, 1904–1908: Matisse's Woman with a Hat, Derain's Charing Cross Bridge.
leaves.axis: Core Fauves, Moreau's studio, the Le Havre group, other French Fauves, then national branches (Hungarian Fauves, Brabant fauvism, others); unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: Musée national d'art moderne works tagged fauvism

leaves.label: Cubism
leaves.defn: The movement of Picasso and Braque (from 1907) that fractured objects into planes and multiple viewpoints, with its Salon Cubist and Section d'Or circles: Les Demoiselles d'Avignon, Braque's Violin and Candlestick, Gris's Portrait of Picasso.
leaves.axis: Picasso–Braque Cubism, Salon Cubism and Section d'Or, Cubist sculptors, Purism, Post-cubism, then national branches (Czech, American, others); unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Futurism
leaves.defn: The Italian movement (1909) celebrating speed, machines and the city, and its Russian Cubo-Futurist branch: Boccioni's The City Rises, Balla's Dynamism of a Dog on a Leash, Severini's Armoured Train.
leaves.axis: Italian Futurism (first wave), Second Futurism and Aeropittura, Russian Futurism and Rayonism, then other national branches; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Orphism
leaves.defn: Abstract painting of prismatic colour around Robert and Sonia Delaunay and Kupka, c. 1912: Robert Delaunay's Simultaneous Windows, Kupka's Amorpha.
leaves.axis: Orphism proper (the Delaunays, Kupka), then Synchromism, Musicalism and the Portuguese and Irish followers; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Vorticism
leaves.defn: The British avant-garde of 1914–1915 around Wyndham Lewis and the magazine BLAST: Bomberg's The Mud Bath, Lewis's The Crowd.
leaves.axis: Signatories of BLAST and the Rebel Art Centre

leaves.label: Suprematism
leaves.defn: Malevich's abstraction of pure geometric forms from 1915: Black Square, Suprematist Composition: White on White.
leaves.axis: Malevich, the Supremus group in Moscow, UNOVIS in Vitebsk, then related painters

leaves.label: Constructivism
leaves.defn: The Russian movement from c. 1915 of art as construction and production, and its international heirs: Tatlin's Monument to the Third International, Rodchenko's Pure Colours, El Lissitzky's Proun.
leaves.see: A5-62 Suprematism; A5-64 De Stijl; A5-87 Concrete Art
leaves.axis: Russian Constructivism, then International Constructivism (Bauhaus, Hungary, Poland), the Cologne Progressives, Universal Constructivism, Neo-Constructivism; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: De Stijl
leaves.defn: The Dutch movement (1917) of Neoplasticism, reducing art to primaries and the right angle: Mondrian's Composition with Red, Blue and Yellow, van Doesburg's Counter-Composition.
leaves.axis: Founding members of the magazine (1917), then later members and followers (Abstraction-Création, American Abstract Artists)
catalogues: RKD – Netherlands Institute for Art History
artists and images database for Netherlandish and Flemish art
the largest Mondrian and De Stijl collection

leaves.label: Dada
leaves.defn: The anti-art movement born in Zurich in 1916 and spread to Berlin, Paris and New York: Duchamp's Fountain, Höch's Cut with the Kitchen Knife, Arp's collages.
leaves.axis: Centres in chronological order: precursors (Incoherents), Zurich, New York, Berlin, Cologne and Hanover, Paris, later Dada; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: digital archive of Dada publications and documents

leaves.label: Surrealism
leaves.defn: The movement launched by Breton in 1924 that painted dream and the unconscious: Dalí's The Persistence of Memory, Magritte's The Treachery of Images, Ernst's Europe after the Rain.
leaves.see: A5-65 Dada; A5-67 Metaphysical Painting; A5-69 Magic Realism
leaves.axis: by group: Paris Surrealist group, Belgian Surrealism, British Surrealist Group, Mexico, Spain, American Surrealism and Post-Surrealism, Art and Liberty (Egypt), Japan, Central and Eastern Europe, Latin America; fantastic realism and later echoes last; by birth year

Fantastic realism and later fantastic art

leaves.label: Metaphysical Painting
leaves.defn: Giorgio de Chirico's and Carrà's painting of uncanny piazzas and mannequins, 1910–1920: The Disquieting Muses, Mystery and Melancholy of a Street.
leaves.axis: The Ferrara founders (1917), then later adherents

leaves.label: New Objectivity
leaves.defn: The sober, sharp-focus realism of Weimar Germany in the 1920s: Dix's Portrait of Sylvia von Harden, Grosz's Pillars of Society, Schad's Self-Portrait with Model.
leaves.axis: Verists (Berlin, Dresden, Karlsruhe), the Hanover group, Classicists, then Swiss and other branches; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Magic Realism
leaves.defn: Realist painting of the 1920s–1950s that makes the everyday strange: Carel Willink's Wilma, Pyke Koch's Shooting Gallery, Ivan Albright's The Picture of Dorian Gray.
leaves.axis: Dutch magic realism, Italian and German magic realism, American magic realism, then the Vienna School of Fantastic Realism and others; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: the art movement and its painters

leaves.label: Precisionism
leaves.defn: American painting of the 1920s–1930s rendering industry and the city in crisp geometric planes: Sheeler's American Landscape, Demuth's My Egypt.
leaves.axis: Country of activity (American Precisionism)

leaves.label: Regionalism
leaves.defn: American painting of the 1930s of the rural Midwest: Wood's American Gothic, Benton's America Today, Curry's Tragic Prelude.
leaves.axis: The Regionalist triumvirate first, then other Regionalist and American Scene painters
catalogues: Art Institute of Chicago collection: Regionalism
secs: Other Regionalists and American Scene painters

leaves.label: Ashcan School
leaves.defn: New York realist painters of the early 20th century who depicted the city's streets and poor: Bellows's Stag at Sharkey's, Sloan's McSorley's Bar.
leaves.axis: The Eight (1908 Macbeth exhibition), then the Henri circle and followers
catalogues: The Met collection search: Ashcan School

leaves.label: Social Realism
leaves.defn: Politically engaged realist painting of the 1920s–1940s on labour and poverty: Ben Shahn's The Passion of Sacco and Vanzetti, Isabel Bishop's working women.
leaves.see: A5-74 Socialist Realism; A5-71 Regionalism; L2-40 Mexican Muralism
leaves.axis: American Social Realism of the 1930s first, then the Mexican and Latin American branch, Italian and British Neorealism, and 19th-century forerunners; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: The Met collection search: social realism
secs: Mexican and Latin American Social Realism

leaves.label: Socialist Realism
leaves.defn: The official style of the Soviet Union from 1932 and of the socialist states: Gerasimov's Lenin on the Tribune, Deineka's Defence of Petrograd.
leaves.axis: Soviet Socialist Realism (Moscow masters, Leningrad School, Union republics), then the Eastern Bloc branches; Peredvizhniki forerunners first; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Harlem Renaissance
leaves.defn: The flowering of African-American art in the 1920s–1930s centred in Harlem: Aaron Douglas's Aspects of Negro Life, Archibald Motley's Nightlife, Augusta Savage's The Harp.
leaves.axis: The 1920s painters and sculptors of the New Negro movement, then the 1930s generation of the Harlem Artists Guild

leaves.label: School of Paris
leaves.defn: The international, often émigré artists working in Paris c. 1900–1940 outside a single movement: Modigliani's Jeanne Hébuterne, Chagall's I and the Village, Soutine's Carcass of Beef.
leaves.axis: The pre-war École de Paris (Montparnasse émigrés and Montmartre), then the post-war Nouvelle École de Paris; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: Centre Pompidou collection: École de Paris
Musée national d'art moderne works of the École de Paris

leaves.label: Scuola Romana
leaves.defn: Roman painters of the 1920s–1930s around Scipione and Mafai, expressionist in colour against the classicising Novecento: Mafai's Demolitions, Scipione's Cardinal Decano.
leaves.axis: The Via Cavour founders, then the second Roman generation
catalogues: national collection of Italian modern art incl. the Scuola Romana

leaves.label: Neo-Romanticism
leaves.defn: Figurative painting of the 1930s–1950s (Berman, Tchelitchew; the British Neo-Romantics) reviving Romantic landscape and mood: Paul Nash's Totes Meer, Sutherland's Entrance to a Lane.
leaves.axis: British Neo-Romantics first, then the French neo-romantics around Tchelitchew, then other national neo-romantic painters; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Naïve Art
leaves.defn: Painting by artists without academic training, flat, detailed and frontal: Henri Rousseau's The Dream, Séraphine Louis's Tree of Paradise, Ivan Generalić's Hlebine paintings.
leaves.see: A5-80 Art Brut; A6 Folk & Popular Painting
leaves.axis: French naïfs, American folk and self-taught painters, the Hlebine school and Yugoslav naïve art, then other countries; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
secs: Hlebine school and Yugoslav naïve art

leaves.label: Art Brut
leaves.defn: Dubuffet's "raw art" of outsiders, the untrained and the institutionalised, and its successor outsider art: Adolf Wölfli's illustrated books, Aloïse Corbaz's theatres.
leaves.axis: Dubuffet's European art brut (Collection de l'Art Brut, Lausanne), Art singulier, then American self-taught and outsider artists; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: the founding collection of art brut
Intuit: The Center for Intuitive and Outsider Art

leaves.label: Abstract Expressionism
leaves.defn: The New York painting of the 1940s–1950s, gestural or field-based: Pollock's Autumn Rhythm, de Kooning's Woman I, Kline's Chief.
leaves.see: A5-82 Color Field; Art Informel; A5-83 Lyrical Abstraction
leaves.axis: by circle and generation: teachers and precursors, New York School first generation, colour field, sculptors, second generation, Bay Area and Los Angeles, Chicago Allusive Abstractionists, Native American abstraction, Canada (Automatistes, Painters Eleven); then parallel movements abroad by region; by birth year

leaves.label: Color Field
leaves.defn: Abstraction of large expanses of flat or stained colour from the late 1940s: Rothko's No. 61 (Rust and Blue), Frankenthaler's Mountains and Sea, Newman's Vir Heroicus Sublimis.
leaves.see: A5-81 Abstract Expressionism; A5-86 Hard-edge Painting
leaves.axis: New York Color Field painters, the Washington Color School, Post-painterly Abstraction, then others; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Lyrical Abstraction
leaves.defn: Post-war gestural abstraction in Paris (abstraction lyrique) and its American 1960s sense: Georges Mathieu's Capetians Everywhere, Zao Wou-Ki's large canvases.
leaves.axis: Parisian Abstraction lyrique, American Lyrical Abstraction, New Horizons in Israel, then others; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Informalism
leaves.defn: European post-war abstraction of matter, sign and gesture (art informel, tachisme, matter painting): Fautrier's Hostages, Wols's It's All Over, Tàpies's matter paintings.
leaves.axis: Tachisme and French art informel, Spanish Informalism (El Paso, Dau al Set), Italian informale and Movimento Spaziale, then others; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: COBRA
leaves.defn: The Copenhagen–Brussels–Amsterdam movement (1948–1951) of spontaneous, childlike expressionist painting: Appel's Questioning Children, Jorn's Letter to My Son.
leaves.axis: Founding cities of the group (Copenhagen, Brussels, Amsterdam), then later members

leaves.label: Hard-edge Painting
leaves.defn: Abstraction of crisp-edged flat colour areas from the late 1950s: Ellsworth Kelly's Red Blue Green, Karl Benjamin's compositions.
leaves.see: A5-82 Color Field; A5-87 Concrete Art; A5-88 Op Art
leaves.axis: California Hard-edge (Abstract Classicists), New York hard-edge, then Les Plasticiens in Montreal; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Concrete Art
leaves.defn: Geometric abstraction built from pure plastic means, after van Doesburg's 1930 manifesto, in Switzerland, Italy and Latin America: Max Bill's Endless Ribbon, Lygia Clark's Bichos, Tomás Maldonado's works.
leaves.see: A5-64 De Stijl; A5-63 Constructivism; A5-88 Op Art
leaves.axis: Founding Art Concret group and Zurich Concretes, Movimento Arte Concreta (Milan), Argentine and Uruguayan Madí, Brazilian concretism and Neo-concretism, then others; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Op Art
leaves.defn: Abstraction of the 1960s exploiting optical effects: Bridget Riley's Movement in Squares, Vasarely's Vega series.
leaves.see: D5-120 Kinetic Art; A5-87 Concrete Art
leaves.axis: Precursors (Albers, Vasarely, Escher), GRAV in Paris, Gruppo N and Italian arte programmata, Latin American kinetic op, then British and American Op; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Pop Art
leaves.defn: Art of the late 1950s–1960s drawn from mass media, advertising and consumer goods: Warhol's Campbell's Soup Cans, Lichtenstein's Whaam!, Hamilton's Just What Is It ....
leaves.see: A5-90 Neo-Dada; A5-91 Nouveau Réalisme; A5-96 Photorealism
leaves.axis: by scene: Independent Group and British Pop, American proto-Pop, New York Pop, West Coast Pop, Capitalist realism, Figuration narrative, other European Pop, Japan, Latin America, Australasia; Neo-pop and later last; by birth year
catalogues: the museum's online collection of Warhol's work
Pop Art in the Metropolitan Museum
