Europe: Italy, Scandinavia, Austria and Yugoslavia

leaves.label: Neo-Dada
leaves.defn: American art of the late 1950s reviving Dada assemblage and found imagery: Rauschenberg's Monogram, Johns's Flag.
leaves.axis: American Neo-Dada, then the Japanese Neo-Dadaism Organizers and Fluxus-linked artists; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Nouveau Réalisme
leaves.defn: The French movement founded in 1960 around Restany, appropriating the real (décollage, accumulation, wrapping): Arman's Accumulations, Yves Klein's Anthropometries, Villeglé's torn posters.
leaves.axis: Signatories of the 1960 declaration, later members, then associated artists; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: Musée national d'art moderne works of the group

leaves.label: Funk Art
leaves.defn: Irreverent figurative art of the San Francisco Bay Area in the 1960s, often in ceramics: Robert Arneson's self-portrait busts, Roy De Forest's paintings.
leaves.see: A5-89 Pop Art; A5-93 Bay Area Figurative Movement
leaves.axis: Country of activity (Bay Area Funk)

leaves.label: Bay Area Figurative Movement
leaves.defn: San Francisco painters of the 1950s–1960s who returned from abstraction to the figure: Diebenkorn's Cityscape I, David Park's Four Men.
leaves.axis: First generation (Park, Bischoff, Diebenkorn), then the second generation

leaves.label: Northwest School
leaves.defn: Painters of the Pacific Northwest in the 1930s–1950s, mystical and Asian-influenced: Mark Tobey's white writing, Morris Graves's Blind Bird.
leaves.axis: The 'Big Four' of the 1953 Life article, then associated Seattle artists

leaves.label: Pattern and Decoration
leaves.defn: The American movement of the mid-1970s that reclaimed ornament, textile and craft: Miriam Schapiro's femmages, Robert Kushner's costumes.
leaves.axis: Country of activity (American P&D around the Holly Solomon Gallery)

leaves.label: Photorealism
leaves.defn: Painting from the late 1960s that reproduces photographs with exacting fidelity: Richard Estes's storefronts, Chuck Close's Big Self-Portrait.
leaves.axis: American Photorealism of the Meisel generation, then European hyperrealism; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Neo-figurative
leaves.defn: The return to the figure in 1960s Latin America and Spain (Otra Figuración): Jorge de la Vega's works, Luis Felipe Noé's Introduction to Hope.
leaves.axis: Argentine Otra Figuración, French Nouvelle Figuration, then others; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Neo-Expressionism
leaves.defn: Figurative, expressive painting of the late 1970s–1980s: Baselitz's upside-down figures, Kiefer's Margarethe, Basquiat's Untitled (Skull).
leaves.axis: German Neo-Expressionism and the Neue Wilde, Italian Transavanguardia, French Figuration Libre, American Neo-Expressionism and Bad Painting, then others; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Lettrism
leaves.defn: Isidore Isou's movement (from 1945) of letters and signs as the material of poetry and painting: Isou's hypergraphic novels, Lemaître's works.
leaves.axis: Isou's Lettrist group in Paris, then the Czech letter-painters and the Situationist offshoot; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Black Arts Movement
leaves.defn: The African-American art movement of 1965–1975 tied to Black Power (AfriCOBRA, the Wall of Respect): Jeff Donaldson's Wives of Shango, Wadsworth Jarrell's Revolutionary.
leaves.see: A5-75 Harlem Renaissance; A5-101 British Black Arts Movement
leaves.axis: AfriCOBRA (Chicago), the Weusi collective (Harlem), then other Black Arts artists

leaves.label: British Black Arts Movement
leaves.defn: Black British artists of the 1980s (the BLK Art Group) addressing race and diaspora: Lubaina Himid's A Fashionable Marriage, Keith Piper's works.
leaves.axis: The BLK Art Group (Wolverhampton), then other artists of the 1980s British Black Arts Movement
catalogues: Tate collection search: British Black Arts Movement
Tate works and texts matching 'British Black Arts Movement'

leaves.label: Lowbrow
leaves.defn: Californian pop-surrealist painting from the late 1970s rooted in comics, hot-rod and tattoo culture: Robert Williams's paintings, Mark Ryden's The Meat Show.
leaves.axis: Founders around Juxtapoz, then the pop-surrealist generation

leaves.label: Mission School
leaves.defn: San Francisco artists of the 1990s working from street, folk and graffiti culture: Barry McGee's installations, Margaret Kilgallen's murals.
leaves.axis: Core members of the San Francisco Mission District scene

leaves.label: Stuckism
leaves.defn: The figurative painting movement founded in London in 1999 against conceptual art: Charles Thomson's Sir Nicholas Serota Makes an Acquisitions Decision.
leaves.axis: Founders (1999), then later Stuckists; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity

leaves.label: Superflat
leaves.defn: Takashi Murakami's Japanese postmodern movement (2000) of flat anime and print-derived imagery: Murakami's Tan Tan Bo, Aya Takano's paintings.
leaves.axis: Murakami and the Kaikai Kiki artists, then associated Superflat painters

leaves.label: Hurufiyya Movement
leaves.defn: Modern art of the Arab world and Iran (from the 1950s) that uses Arabic letters as abstract form: Madiha Omar's works, Shakir Hassan Al Said's The Contemplative Dimension, Parviz Tanavoli's Heech.
leaves.axis: Regional groups: Saqqa-khaneh school (Iran), Baghdad groups (One Dimension), Khartoum School, the Maghreb, then later calligraffiti; unplaced artists fall back to their country of activity
catalogues: collection of modern Arab art including Hurufiyya

leaves.label: Dakar School
leaves.defn: Senegalese painting of the 1960s–1970s fostered by Senghor's Négritude policy: Papa Ibra Tall's tapestries, Iba N'Diaye's works.
leaves.axis: Founders of the Dakar School under Senghor, then the later generation

leaves.label: Yōga
leaves.defn: Japanese painting in Western oil technique from the Meiji period: Kuroda Seiki's Lakeside, Takahashi Yuichi's Salmon, Kishida Ryūsei's Reiko.
leaves.axis: by phase and exhibiting society: Bakumatsu and early Meiji pioneers, Meiji Bijutsukai/Taiheiyō Gakai (old school), Hakubakai (new school), Taishō generation, early Shōwa; by birth year

leaves.label: Bengal School of Art
leaves.defn: The Indian nationalist painting movement of Abanindranath Tagore and his pupils (c. 1900–1940) reviving Mughal and Ajanta idioms: Abanindranath Tagore's Bharat Mata, Nandalal Bose's Haripura posters.
leaves.see: A1-4 Mughal Painting; A5-110 Modern Art

leaves.label: Modern Art
leaves.defn: Painters born c. 1860–1944 active in Europe (and a few in the Americas) whose work is modern but who belong to no movement with its own leaf here; artists of a named movement (Fauvism, Cubism, Expressionism, Surrealism, Vienna Secession, Novecento Italiano, St Ives School ...) are listed in that leaf instead. Small named groups without a leaf of their own are kept as sections.

leaves.defn: The period style of painters and artists born from about 1945 who work after modernism in plural, global practices: post-colonial figurative painting, new abstraction, appropriation, art of the biennial circuit. Artists who belong to a named post-1945 movement (Neo-expressionism, Young British Artists, Pictures Generation, Superflat, Stuckism...) sit in that movement's leaf; this leaf keeps the rest.

leaves.label: Hispano-Flemish Style
leaves.defn: Fifteenth-century painting of Castile and Aragon shaped by Early Netherlandish oil technique and realism, under the patronage of Isabella I: Bartolomé Bermejo's Saint Michael Triumphant, Fernando Gallego's Pietà, Pedro Berruguete's altarpieces.

leaves.axis: Kingdoms: Castile, the Crown of Aragon (Valencia, Catalonia), Portugal

leaves.label: Dansaekhwa
leaves.defn: The Korean monochrome painting movement of the 1970s: Park Seo-bo's Ecriture, Yun Hyong-keun's Umber-Blue, Chung Sang-hwa's grids, Ha Chong-hyun's Conjunction.
leaves.see: Installation Art (Mono-ha kind); A5-82 Color Field
leaves.axis: First generation of the 1975 Tokyo exhibition, then later Dansaekhwa painters

leaves.label: Orientalism
leaves.defn: Western painting of North Africa, the Ottoman lands, the Middle East and India, c. 1780–1914, from travel sketches to Salon harem and street scenes: Delacroix's Women of Algiers, Gérôme's The Snake Charmer, Lewis's The Hhareem. Membership: painters known chiefly for such subjects (or tagged Orientalist in Wikidata) whom no narrower school claims.

leaves.label: Peredvizhniki
leaves.defn: The Russian realist artists' cooperative (Society for Travelling Art Exhibitions, 1870–1923) that toured exhibitions of national genre, history and landscape painting: Repin's Barge Haulers on the Volga, Savrasov's The Rooks Have Come Back, Surikov's Boyarynya Morozova. Membership: members or regular exhibitors of the Society.

leaves.label: Skagen Painters
leaves.defn: The Scandinavian artists' colony at Skagen in northern Jutland, c. 1875–1910, painting fishermen, beaches and the summer light: Krøyer's Summer Evening on Skagen's Southern Beach, Michael Ancher's Will He Round the Point?. Membership: painters who worked at Skagen as part of the colony.
leaves.axis: by nationality within the colony: Danish core members first, then Norwegian and Swedish members; each group ordered by birth year.

leaves.label: Newlyn School
leaves.defn: The colony of plein-air naturalist painters at Newlyn and Lamorna in Cornwall, from c. 1882: Stanhope Forbes's A Fish Sale on a Cornish Beach, Langley's Never Morning Wore to Evening, Bramley's A Hopeless Dawn. Membership: painters who settled or worked at Newlyn as part of the colony.
leaves.axis: one group: painters of the Newlyn colony from its founding in the early 1880s, ordered by birth year.

leaves.label: Lyon School
leaves.defn: The school of painting of Lyon, from the Troubadour painters around Révoil and Richard to the religious and idealist painters of the July Monarchy and Second Empire: Révoil's Joan of Arc in Prison, Janmot's The Poem of the Soul, Orsel's Good and Evil. Membership: painters trained at or working from the École des Beaux-Arts of Lyon.
leaves.axis: by phase and subject: the Troubadour founders of c. 1800, the religious and idealist painters of the 1830s–1860s, then landscape, flower and genre painters; each group ordered by birth year.

the principal collection of the school

leaves.label: Golden Age of Finnish Art
leaves.defn: Finnish painting of c. 1880–1910, from Paris-trained naturalism to national romanticism and the Kalevala: Edelfelt's Conveying the Child's Coffin, Gallen-Kallela's The Defence of the Sampo, Schjerfbeck's The Convalescent. Membership: Finnish painters active in that generation.
leaves.axis: by phase: Paris-trained naturalists of the 1880s first, then national-romantic painters of the 1890s; each group ordered by birth year.

overview with the painters of the period

leaves.label: Young British Artists
leaves.defn: Loose group of artists, many from Goldsmiths College, who showed together from the Freeze exhibition (London, 1988) and were collected by Charles Saatchi, culminating in Sensation (Royal Academy, 1997): Hirst, Emin, Lucas, Whiteread, the Chapman brothers, Ofili, Gordon.

leaves.label: Pictures Generation
leaves.defn: American artists of the late 1970s–80s, named after Douglas Crimp's Pictures exhibition (Artists Space, New York, 1977), who used appropriation, montage and photography to examine mass-media images: Sherrie Levine, Richard Prince, Barbara Kruger, Robert Longo, Cindy Sherman.

leaves.defn: The London group of Post-Impressionist painters formed in 1911 around Walter Sickert at 19 Fitzroy Street (Gore, Gilman, Ginner, Bevan, Drummond, Manson, Lightfoot, Innes), with the women of the Fitzroy Street Group who were barred from membership (Sands, Gosse, Lessore).

leaves.defn: The figurative painting school of the Leipzig Academy of Visual Arts in the German Democratic Republic: the founding generation (Heisig, Tübke, Mattheuer, Sitte) and their students (Rink, Stelzmann, Zander). Not the post-1990 New Leipzig School.

leaves.label: Nazi art
leaves.defn: Officially sanctioned art of the Third Reich (1933–1945): painters shown and bought at the Great German Art Exhibitions in Munich (Ziegler, Wissel, Peiner, Eichhorst, Saliger), and designers of party imagery. Membership test: work defined by the regime's cultural policy.

leaves.label: Novecento Italiano
leaves.defn: The Milan movement of a modern classical 'return to order' founded in 1922 by Margherita Sarfatti with seven painters (Bucci, Dudreville, Funi, Malerba, Marussig, Oppi, Sironi) and widened in the national exhibitions of 1926 and 1929 (Tosi, Carena, Campigli, Martini).

leaves.defn: Catalan modernism in painting, c. 1888–1911: Rusiñol and Casas's Sitges festivals, the Els Quatre Gats tavern circle and the Colla del Safrà, and the decorative painters of Barcelona. Architecture of the movement sits under Art Nouveau Architecture.

leaves.defn: The Catalan cultural movement of a Mediterranean classicism (c. 1906–1923) named by Eugeni d'Ors, reacting against Modernisme: Sunyer, Torres-García, Togores, Galí, Obiols, the sculptors Clarà and Manolo Hugué.

leaves.defn: Twentieth-century Native American easel painting in opaque watercolour with flat, outlined colour and little shading or perspective, showing dances, ceremonies and daily life: the San Ildefonso watercolourists (1910s), Hopi painters, the Kiowa Six (Southern Plains style), Dorothy Dunn's Studio at the Santa Fe Indian School (1932–62) and the Bacone school.

leaves.defn: Movement founded by Lucio Fontana in Milan in 1947 (anticipated by the Manifiesto blanco, Buenos Aires 1946) that sought to fuse colour, sound, space, movement and time, projecting art into real space with neon, television and the slashed and punctured canvas (Buchi, Tagli).

leaves.label: Supports/Surfaces

leaves.label: Synchromism
leaves.defn: American colour abstraction founded in Paris in 1912–1913 by Morgan Russell and Stanton Macdonald-Wright, orchestrating colour on the analogy of music (synchromies); the first American avant-garde movement to receive international attention.

leaves.label: American Scene Painting

leaves.defn: The influence of Japanese art, especially ukiyo-e prints, on Western painting, prints and decorative arts after the opening of Japan in the 1850s: flat colour, cropped compositions and asymmetry in Manet, Whistler, Degas, Van Gogh and the Nabis, and the Anglo-Japanese style in design.

leaves.label: Minhwa

leaves.label: Nizhny Tagil Tray Painting
leaves.defn: Painted and lacquered iron trays made in Nizhny Tagil in the Urals from the 18th century, with flowers and genre scenes under a translucent varnish, the forerunner of Zhostovo.
leaves.axis: Sub-types and styles first, then centres, makers by date, and named works with holding museum; collections ranked by gathered objects.

leaves.label: Naïve Painting of Kovačica
leaves.defn: Naïve painting of the Slovak community of Kovačica in Vojvodina (Serbia) from the 1950s, in oil on canvas and on objects, with village life, harvests and weddings (UNESCO 2024).

leaves.label: Pysanka
leaves.defn: Easter eggs decorated in the Slavic and East European wax-resist (batik) technique with layered dyes and symbolic patterns; regional schools and related types (krashanka, krapanka, drapanka) are kinds: Hutsul pysanky, Boyko pysanky.
leaves.axis: Sub-types by technique (pysanka, krashanka, krapanka, drapanka), then regional schools (Hutsul, Boyko, Polish, Belarusian, Russian); collections ranked by gathered decorated-egg objects.

leaves.label: Haitian Painting
leaves.defn: Painting in Haiti since the founding of the Centre d'Art in Port-au-Prince (1944), from the self-taught masters around DeWitt Peters to the Vodou-inspired Saint-Soleil group (1972) and the Jacmel and Cap-Haïtien schools: Hyppolite's Ogoun Ferraille, Philomé Obin's Funeral of Charlemagne Péralte, Bigaud's Murder in the Jungle, Saint Fleurant's Mother with Children.

leaves.label: Kwoma Bark Painting
leaves.defn: The painted sago-palm bark panels of the Kwoma of the Washkuk Hills, upper Sepik, Papua New Guinea, made to line the ceilings of ceremonial houses with clan designs and spirit figures in ochre, white and black. Arnhem Land bark painting is A6-18.

leaves.label: Saz Style
leaves.defn: the Ottoman court style of feathery serrated leaves, rosettes and fabulous creatures drawn in ink by the nakkaşhane under Shahkulu and Kara Memi (16th century), and carried from drawings into tiles, textiles and bindings.
leaves.see: E2-7 Iznik Pottery; H3-3 Ottoman Silk Textiles

leaves.label: Ledger Art
leaves.defn: Plains narrative drawing in pencil, crayon and ink on the pages of account ledgers and on muslin, from the 1860s, continuing hide painting on paper: the Fort Marion drawings, Cheyenne and Kiowa warrior ledgers, Lakota ledger books.
leaves.axis: Peoples (Cheyenne, Kiowa, Lakota, Arapaho), then the Fort Marion artists and later ledger artists by date, then collections.

leaves.label: American Comics
leaves.defn: Comic strips and comic books of the United States from the newspaper Sunday pages of the 1890s through the superhero comic book, underground comix and the graphic novel: Winsor McCay's Little Nemo in Slumberland, Herriman's Krazy Kat, Kirby and Lee's Fantastic Four, Spiegelman's Maus.

leaves.defn: Japanese comics and their drawn idiom from the 20th century: Tezuka's Astro Boy, Oda's One Piece, Takeuchi's Sailor Moon.

leaves.label: Đông Hồ Painting
leaves.defn: Woodblock prints of Đông Hồ village in Bắc Ninh on điệp (shell-coated) paper with natural colours, sold for Tết: Mouse Wedding, Jealousy, pig and piglets.

leaves.label: Hàng Trống Painting
leaves.defn: Hanoi's urban folk pictures, printed in outline from woodblocks and hand-coloured: Five Tigers, Carp Gazing at the Moon, Mother Goddess images.
leaves.axis: Sub-types by subject, then the Hanoi street and its workshops; collections.

leaves.label: Kim Hoàng Painting
leaves.defn: Woodblock prints of Kim Hoàng village west of Hanoi, printed on red or yellow paper: Tết pigs and roosters, calligraphic scrolls.

leaves.axis: Sub-types by subject, then the villages; collections.

leaves.label: Nianhua
leaves.defn: Chinese New Year pictures: popular colour woodblock prints of door gods, auspicious children and opera scenes pasted up at the New Year, made in named print towns: Yangliuqing, Taohuawu, Yangjiabu, Zhuxianzhen.

leaves.label: Cordel Literature
leaves.defn: The chapbooks of north-eastern Brazil sold hung on strings, whose covers are woodcuts (xilogravura) by popular printmakers: J. Borges woodcuts, cordel covers of Caruaru and Juazeiro.
leaves.axis: Printmakers by generation (Caruaru and Bezerros), then sub-types; collections.

leaves.axis: Community studios (Kinngait / Cape Dorset first, then Baker Lake, Puvirnituq, Holman, Pangnirtung), then printmakers by date; collections.

leaves.label: Torres Strait Islander Printmaking
leaves.defn: The linocut and etching movement of the Torres Strait (Zenadth Kes) from the 1990s, cutting island cosmology, totems and turtle-shell mask forms into large black-and-white prints: Badu and Moa linocuts, Mabuiag etchings.

leaves.axis: Sub-types by technique and subject, then named prints with holding collection; collections.

leaves.label: Poster Art
leaves.defn: The artistic lithographic poster from the colour posters of Jules Chéret in 1870s Paris through the Belle Époque, the Italian, Swiss and British schools and the psychedelic concert poster: Chéret's Bal du Moulin Rouge, Mucha's Gismonda, Toulouse-Lautrec's Divan Japonais, Cappiello's Le Thermogène.

leaves.defn: The German 'poster style' founded by Lucian Bernhard's Priester matches poster (1906): a single object, flat colour and a brand name: Bernhard's Priester and Stiller posters, Hohlwein's Riquet, Erdt's Opel, Klinger's Berlin posters.
leaves.axis: The Berlin founders around Hollerbaum & Schmidt, then Munich and Vienna practitioners

leaves.axis: Phases: Civil War posters and ROSTA windows, 1920s constructivist and film posters, Stalin-era and World War II (TASS windows), postwar

leaves.label: Kufic
leaves.defn: the angular early Arabic script of Qur'ans on parchment and of inscriptions, with its later Eastern (broken cursive), floriated, plaited and square (banna'i) forms.

leaves.label: Maghribi Script
leaves.defn: the rounded scripts of al-Andalus, North Africa and West Africa (mabsut, mujawhar, Andalusi, Sudani), written with a pointed pen.
leaves.axis: Sub-types (mabsut, mujawhar, Andalusi, Sudani, musnad), then named works and calligraphers by date.

leaves.label: Six Pens (al-Aqlam al-Sitta)
leaves.defn: the proportioned cursive scripts — thuluth, naskh, muhaqqaq, rayhani, tawqi' and riqa' — codified by Ibn Muqla and Ibn al-Bawwab and perfected by Yaqut al-Musta'simi, then carried by his pupils and by the Ottoman masters (Sheikh Hamdullah, Hafiz Osman).

leaves.label: Mongolian Calligraphy

leaves.axis: Sub-types (Classical Mongolian script, Soyombo, Galik), then works and calligraphers.

leaves.label: Georgian Calligraphy
leaves.defn: Writing of the Georgian scripts (asomtavruli, nuskhuri, mkhedruli) as an art, in manuscripts and inscriptions.
leaves.axis: Sub-types by script (asomtavruli, nuskhuri, mkhedruli), then manuscripts with sitelinks ≥ 1, then collections.
catalogues: Korneli Kekelidze Georgian National Centre of Manuscripts

leaves.label: Chinese Calligraphy
leaves.defn: The art of writing Chinese characters with the brush, in seal, clerical, regular, running and cursive scripts: Wang Xizhi's Lantingji Xu, Huaisu's Autobiography, Mi Fu's Poems Written on a Boat on the Wu River.
leaves.see: C1-10 Japanese Calligraphy. Possession taxonomy: Hu brush (C4 Craft & Art Supplies); Hui ink (C4 Craft & Art Supplies); Xuan paper (C4 Craft & Art Supplies); Huzhou brush (C5 Office & Stationery); Hui ink (C5 Office & Stationery); Xuan paper (C5 Office & Stationery); Name seal (C5 Office & Stationery); Seal paste (C5 Office & Stationery); and 1 more.
leaves.axis: sub-types first; then calligraphers by dynasty and lineage: Han and Three Kingdoms, Jin (the Wangs), Southern and Northern dynasties, early Tang, high and late Tang, Five Dynasties and Song, Yuan and Chan monks, Ming, Qing epigraphic school, Republican and modern; by birth year
catalogues: the former Qing imperial collection of Chinese painting and calligraphy
paintings and calligraphy of the Forbidden City collection
Chinese calligraphy in the Freer|Sackler and other Smithsonian collections
Chinese calligraphy in the Metropolitan Museum
secs: Han and Three Kingdoms (clerical and early regular script)
Jin dynasty: the Wangs and Eastern Jin masters
Early Tang masters (Ouyang Xun, Yu Shinan, Chu Suiliang)
High and late Tang (Zhang Xu, Yan Zhenqing, Huaisu, Liu Gongquan)
Five Dynasties and Song (incl. the Four Masters of Song)
Yuan dynasty and Chan monk calligraphers

leaves.label: Japanese Calligraphy
leaves.defn: Shodō: the Japanese art of the brush in kanji and kana, with its court lineages (Sesonji-ryū) and Zen bokuseki: Ono no Michikaze's works, Fujiwara no Yukinari's Hakubunshū.
leaves.see: C1-9 Chinese Calligraphy. Possession taxonomy: Kozogami (C4 Craft & Art Supplies); Ganpishi (C4 Craft & Art Supplies); Mitsumatagami (C4 Craft & Art Supplies); Kaisho (C4 Craft & Art Supplies); Gyōsho (C4 Craft & Art Supplies); Sōsho (C4 Craft & Art Supplies); Nara sumi (C5 Office & Stationery); Ink stick (C5 Office & Stationery); and 9 more.
leaves.axis: Lineages: Nara court, the Sanpitsu, the Sanseki and Sesonji-ryū court lineage, other Heian–Kamakura court calligraphers, Zen bokuseki, Edo–Meiji and modern calligraphers
catalogues: integrated collections database of Japan's four national museums
Japan's national database of designated cultural properties

leaves.label: Western Calligraphy
leaves.defn: The art of Latin-script writing, from Renaissance chancery hands and writing masters to modern lettering: Arrighi's La Operina, Palatino's writing book.
leaves.see: C1-12 Type Design. Possession taxonomy: Oblique pen holder (C5 Office & Stationery); Gillott 303 (C5 Office & Stationery); Dip pen nib (C5 Office & Stationery); Hunt 101 (C5 Office & Stationery).
leaves.axis: Burgundian and Italian scribes and illuminators, Renaissance writing masters, then engrossers and penmen of the 17th–19th centuries; scripts first
secs: Burgundian and Italian scribes and illuminators

leaves.label: Type Design
leaves.defn: The design of typefaces and lettering for print and screen since the 19th century: Johnston's Underground typeface, Frutiger's Univers, Miedinger's Helvetica.
leaves.see: C1-11 Western Calligraphy. Possession taxonomy: Private press book (F1 Media & Publications).
leaves.axis: Phases: early printing types, Arts and Crafts and private-press types, American type founders, German and Swiss modernism, non-Latin types, digital type; calligraphers gathered here last
catalogues: museum of type and book art
secs: Arts and Crafts and private-press types

leaves.label: Korean Calligraphy
leaves.defn: seoye: the Korean art of the brush in Hanja and Hangul, from Silla and Goryeo masters to the Joseon court and the Chusa style of Kim Jeong-hui: Kim Saeng's works, Han Ho's Seokbong style, Kim Jeong-hui's Chusa-che.
leaves.see: C1-9 Chinese Calligraphy; C1-10 Japanese Calligraphy. Possession taxonomy: Name seal (C5 Office & Stationery); Korean calligraphy (seoye) (F2 Art).
leaves.axis: Masters by period (Silla, Goryeo, Joseon court, Chusa), then sub-types and works.
catalogues: collections of Korea's national and public museums

subs.label: Illuminated Manuscripts & Illumination
subs.axis: Axis: manuscript tradition.

leaves.label: Early Qur'anic Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Qur'ans written on parchment in Hijazi and Kufic scripts from the 7th to the 10th century, in horizontal format with sparse illuminated headings (the Blue Qur'an, the Tübingen and Birmingham fragments).
leaves.aliases: early Qur'ans; Hijazi Qur'ans; Kufic Qur'ans
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered Qur'an dated before 1000 with sitelinks ≥ 1, by phase (Hijazi and early Kufic, Abbasid Kufic); then collections and makers.
catalogues: The Met collection search: Kufic Qur'an

leaves.label: Islamic Illumination
leaves.defn: the illumination of Qur'ans and books after about 1000: gilded and painted frontispieces, sura headings, margins and borders, in the Abbasid, Mamluk, Ilkhanid, Timurid and Safavid (tazhib), Ottoman (tezhip) and Mughal traditions, with its named illuminators.
alias_rows: Islamic book arts: Maghrebi / Andalusi (see islamic_world.py)
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered illuminated Qur'an from 1000 on with sitelinks ≥ 1, by dynasty and region (Maghribi, Mamluk, Ilkhanid, Timurid–Safavid, Ottoman, South and Southeast Asian); then collections and illuminators.
catalogues: The Met collection search: illuminated Qur'an
Qur'ans and illumination of the Khalili Collection
digitised manuscripts of the Bodleian Libraries, Oxford

leaves.label: Timbuktu Manuscripts
leaves.defn: the manuscripts of the West African Islamic scholarly tradition (Timbuktu, Djenné, the Sahel), in Arabic and in Ajami (African languages in Arabic script), with their Sudani script and leather satchel bindings.
leaves.axis: Libraries and centres (Timbuktu, Djenné, the Sahel), sub-types (Arabic, Ajami), then collections; no gathered manuscript with sitelinks.
catalogues: Hill Museum & Manuscript Library digitised manuscripts (Ethiopia, Mali, Middle East, Armenia...)

leaves.label: Malay Manuscripts
leaves.defn: illuminated Malay manuscripts in Jawi script from the Islamic sultanates of the Malay world (Aceh, Terengganu, Java), with their floral frontispieces.
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered Jawi and Malay manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 1, then Bugis and Makassar items; collections.
catalogues: Indonesian, Malay and other Asian manuscripts of Leiden University Library

leaves.label: Palm-Leaf Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Books of incised or inked palm leaves strung between wooden boards, the manuscript tradition of South Asia and Sri Lanka: Tamil and Grantha olas, Odia incised and painted pothis, Sinhalese Pali texts, Pala Buddhist Prajnaparamita.
leaves.see: A1-9; A1-11. Possession taxonomy: Palm-leaf manuscript (F1 Media & Publications).
leaves.axis: Regional sub-types (South Indian, Odia, Sinhalese, Pala, Newar, Khmer), then every gathered named palm-leaf manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 1; collections.
catalogues: palm-leaf manuscript collection (UNESCO Memory of the World)

leaves.label: Lontar
leaves.defn: Manuscripts on incised leaves of the lontar palm, blackened with soot, the book form of Bali, Lombok and older Java: Kakawin Sutasoma, Nagarakretagama, illustrated prasi leaves.
leaves.see: C2-4; C2-9; H8-3; C2-5 Palm-Leaf Manuscripts
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered named lontar with sitelinks ≥ 2 (≥ 1 gives 263 items, mostly single-wiki stubs), Balinese then Old Javanese; then the prasi sub-type and collections.
catalogues: Indonesian, Malay and other Asian manuscripts of Leiden University Library

leaves.label: Folding-Book Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Concertina-folded books of mulberry or khoi paper, lacquered at the ends, in Burma, Thailand, Laos and Cambodia: parabaik, samut khoi, Lanna phap sa, kraing.
leaves.aliases: folding book manuscript;parabaik;samut khoi;samut thai;kraing;phap sa
alias_rows: Thai samut khoi and Lanna manuscripts
leaves.axis: Sub-types by country (parabaik, samut khoi, Lao and Khmer folding books), then gathered named works; collections.
catalogues: British Museum collection search: folding book
all British Museum objects matching 'folding book'

leaves.label: Kammavaca
leaves.defn: Burmese ordination texts written in square tamarind-seed script in lacquer and gold on lacquered palm leaf, cloth or metal: gilt kammavaca leaves, painted covers.
leaves.axis: Sub-types by support (palm leaf, cloth, metal), then collections.

leaves.label: Pustaha
leaves.defn: The divination and ritual books of the Batak datu, written on folded tree bark between carved wooden covers: Great Pustaha.
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered pustaha with sitelinks ≥ 1, then sub-types; collections.
catalogues: Indonesian, Malay and other Asian manuscripts of Leiden University Library

leaves.label: Dunhuang Manuscripts
leaves.defn: The manuscripts sealed in the Library Cave (Cave 17) of the Mogao Caves about 1000 and opened in 1900: Buddhist sutras, documents and the earliest dated printed book, the Diamond Sutra of 868, with illustrated sutra frontispieces.
leaves.axis: Sub-types (Buddhist sutras, documents, printed books), then named works and collections ranked by gathered Dunhuang objects.
catalogues: digitised manuscripts and paintings from Dunhuang and the Silk Road

leaves.label: Uigwe
leaves.defn: Illustrated royal protocol books of the Joseon court (1392–1910), recording ceremonies, weddings and funerals in text and painted processions: Hwaseong seongyeok uigwe, Banchado procession paintings.
leaves.axis: Works: royal protocol books by ceremony (weddings, funerals, processions), then the Oegyujanggak and collections.
catalogues: collections of Korea's national and public museums
the royal protocols (UNESCO Memory of the World)

leaves.label: Sutra Copying
leaves.defn: Buddhist sutras transcribed as acts of devotion and decorated with gold and silver on dyed paper, frontispiece paintings and ornamented rollers in Japan and Korea: the Heike Nōkyō, Lotus Sutra fan papers, Goryeo sagyeong in gold on indigo paper.
leaves.axis: Sub-types (decorated sutras, frontispiece paintings, fan sutras), then every gathered illustrated sutra with sitelinks ≥ 1 by period; collections.
catalogues: integrated collections database of Japan's four national museums
Japan's national database of designated cultural properties

leaves.label: Dongba Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Ritual manuscripts of the Naxi Dongba priests of Lijiang in Yunnan, written in pictographic Dongba script and painted with deities, with painted ritual cards and scrolls.
leaves.axis: Sub-types (ritual manuscripts, scroll paintings), then collections.

leaves.label: Ethiopian Manuscripts
leaves.defn: The Ge'ez (and later Amharic) manuscript tradition of the Ethiopian and Eritrean church: parchment codices in wooden boards with blind-tooled leather, written in Ge'ez script with ornamental harag frames: gospel books, Psalters, Arganonä Maryam prayer books.
leaves.see: Ethiopian Manuscript Painting; C2-3 Timbuktu Manuscripts. Possession taxonomy: Manuscript book (F1 Media & Publications).
leaves.weak: pool QID Q16632158 not verified; Gondarine and early (to 1500) rows are period tags
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered Ge'ez codex with sitelinks ≥ 1 (scrolls go to Ethiopian Magic Scrolls), by phase; then collections.
catalogues: Hill Museum & Manuscript Library digitised manuscripts (Ethiopia, Mali, Middle East, Armenia...)
database of Ethiopian and Eritrean manuscripts

leaves.label: Book of the Dead
leaves.defn: Illustrated Egyptian funerary papyri of spells for the afterlife, with painted vignettes, New Kingdom to Ptolemaic: Papyrus of Ani, Papyrus of Hunefer, Greenfield Papyrus.
leaves.aliases: Egyptian funerary papyri;Coming Forth by Day
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered funerary papyrus (Book of the Dead and related books) with sitelinks ≥ 1, by date; then collections.
catalogues: database of all known Book of the Dead manuscripts
British Museum collection search: Book of the Dead
all British Museum objects matching 'Book of the Dead'

leaves.label: Maya Codices
leaves.defn: The surviving bark-paper screenfold books of the Postclassic Maya, written in hieroglyphs with painted almanacs: Dresden Codex, Madrid Codex, Paris Codex, Maya Codex of Mexico.
leaves.see: A1-17 Borgia Group; L2-36 Maya Mural Painting
leaves.axis: Works: the four surviving Maya codices (sitelinks ≥ 1), then collections.

leaves.label: Late Antique Illumination
leaves.defn: Illustrated and decorated Latin books of late antiquity, 4th–7th century, in rustic capitals and uncial: Vergilius Vaticanus, St Augustine Gospels, Codex Argenteus.
leaves.weak: Wikidata 'art of Late Antique illumination'; no English Wikipedia article
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered late antique Latin and Gothic codex with sitelinks ≥ 1, by date; then collections.
catalogues: digitised manuscripts of the Vatican Library

leaves.label: Insular Illumination
leaves.defn: Manuscript art of Ireland and Britain, c. 600–900, joining Celtic, Germanic and Mediterranean ornament in carpet pages and great initials: Book of Durrow, Lindisfarne Gospels, Book of Kells, Book of Armagh.
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered Insular manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 1 (non-illuminated glossaries and lists excluded), by date; then collections and scribes.
catalogues: Wikipedia: List of Hiberno-Saxon illustrated manuscripts
complete list of Insular illuminated manuscripts
the Book of Kells, Book of Durrow and other Insular manuscripts digitised

leaves.label: Merovingian Illumination
leaves.defn: Book decoration of Frankish Gaul, 7th–8th century, with zoomorphic initials of fish and birds: Gellone Sacramentary, Gelasian Sacramentary.
leaves.axis: Works: the principal Merovingian manuscripts known from the literature (no gathered item has sitelinks), then centres.
catalogues: digitised manuscripts and prints of the Bibliothèque nationale de France

leaves.label: Carolingian Illumination
leaves.defn: Manuscript painting of the Frankish empire, c. 780–900, in its court and monastic schools: Godescalc Evangelistary, Coronation Gospels, Utrecht Psalter, Codex Aureus of St. Emmeram.
leaves.axis: Schools (Court School of Charlemagne, Palace School, Reims, Tours, Metz, Court of Charles the Bald, St Gall); works: every gathered Carolingian manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 1, by date; then collections and scribes.
catalogues: digitised manuscripts and prints of the Bibliothèque nationale de France
virtual manuscript library of Switzerland (St Gall, Einsiedeln...)

leaves.label: Ottonian Illumination
leaves.defn: Manuscript painting of the Ottonian empire, c. 950–1050, at Reichenau, Trier, Echternach, Cologne and Regensburg: Gospels of Otto III, Pericopes of Henry II, Registrum Gregorii, Bamberg Apocalypse.
leaves.weak: Ottonian illumination redirects to Ottonian art#Manuscripts
leaves.axis: Schools (Reichenau, Trier, Echternach, Cologne, Regensburg); works: every gathered Ottonian manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 1; then collections and masters.

leaves.label: Anglo-Saxon Illumination
leaves.defn: Late Anglo-Saxon manuscript art, 10th–11th century, in the acanthus-bordered Winchester style and in outline drawing: Benedictional of St Æthelwold, Harley Psalter, Ramsey Psalter.
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered late Anglo-Saxon manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 1 (text-only poetry codices included), then collections.

leaves.label: Mozarabic Illumination
leaves.defn: Manuscript painting of early medieval Christian Iberia, 10th–11th century, in flat banded colour, above all the illustrated commentaries of Beatus of Liébana: Morgan Beatus, Gerona Beatus, León Bible of 960.
leaves.aliases: Spanish illumination of the Early Middle Ages;Visigothic illumination
src: Wikidata Q18214676 (art of illumination in early medieval Spain)
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered Mozarabic and Beatus manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 1, by date; then collections and painters.

leaves.label: Romanesque Illumination
leaves.defn: Manuscript painting of Latin Europe c. 1050–1200, with large-format Bibles and monumental figure style: Bury Bible, Winchester Bible, St Albans Psalter, Hortus deliciarum.
leaves.see: C2-29 Gothic Book Illustration; G1-49 Mosan Art; L2-43
leaves.axis: Sub-types (giant Bibles, psalters, Exultet rolls), then works: every gathered Romanesque illuminated manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 1 (documents and text-only codices excluded), by region; then collections and makers.
catalogues: digitised manuscripts and prints of the Bibliothèque nationale de France
digitised manuscripts of the Bodleian Libraries, Oxford

leaves.label: Renaissance Illumination
leaves.defn: Manuscript illumination of the 15th–16th century influenced by Renaissance painting, in Italy, France and the courts that collected it: Farnese Hours, Bible of Borso d'Este, Hours of Étienne Chevalier, Corvinian manuscripts.
leaves.see: C2-29 Gothic Book Illustration; C2-30 Ghent-Bruges School
leaves.axis: Regional schools (Italian, French, Corvinian, German, Iberian); works: every gathered Renaissance illuminated manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 1, by school; then collections and illuminators.
catalogues: digitised manuscripts and prints of the Bibliothèque nationale de France

leaves.label: Hebrew Illuminated Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Decorated and illustrated Hebrew books of the Middle Ages and early modern period — Bibles, haggadot and mahzorim — with micrography and painted cycles: Sarajevo Haggadah, Golden Haggadah, Birds' Head Haggadah, Rothschild Miscellany.
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered illuminated Hebrew manuscript (illuminated flag or Bible, haggadah, mahzor) with sitelinks ≥ 1, by region (Sephardi, Ashkenazi, Italian, other); then collections.
catalogues: Ktiv portal of digitised Hebrew manuscripts
digitised manuscripts of the Bodleian Libraries, Oxford

leaves.label: Russian Illuminated Manuscripts
leaves.defn: Gospel books, chronicles and service books of Kievan Rus' and Muscovy, 11th–17th century, with Byzantine-derived miniatures and teratological headpieces and initials: Ostromir Gospels, Khitrovo Gospels, Radziwiłł Chronicle.
leaves.axis: Sub-schools (Kievan, Novgorod, Muscovite, Vyg/Pomor Old Believer), then works: every gathered Old Rus' and Muscovite manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 2 (127 at ≥ 1, mixed with South Slavic), by phase; then collections.
catalogues: State Catalogue of the Museum Fund of the Russian Federation

leaves.label: Fraktur
leaves.defn: Illuminated folk documents of the Pennsylvania Germans, 18th–19th century, lettered in a broken script and painted with birds, hearts and tulips: Taufschein (birth and baptismal certificates), Vorschrift (writing samples).
leaves.axis: Sub-types (Taufschein, Vorschrift, bookplates), then artists by date; collections.
catalogues: one of the largest fraktur collections, digitised

leaves.label: Gothic Book Illustration
leaves.defn: The illumination of Gothic manuscripts (13th–15th century), from Paris workshops to the Books of Hours: Jean Pucelle's Hours of Jeanne d'Évreux, the Douce Apocalypse, the Bedford Hours.
leaves.see: A5-16 Gothic Painting; C2-30 Ghent-Bruges School. Possession taxonomy: Illuminated manuscript (F1 Media & Publications).
leaves.axis: sub-types, then regional schools; works: every named Gothic manuscript in the gathered manuscript records with a Wikipedia article (sitelinks >= 1; calendar leaves merged into their book), plus canonical named manuscripts with Wikipedia articles from the literature, by school then date; collections ranked by gathered items; illuminators by school (Paris court, provincial France, England, Burgundian Netherlands, Italy, Central Europe, Iberia)
catalogues: the BL's fully digitised Gothic psalters, Apocalypses and books of hours
the Bibliothèque nationale de France's digitised manuscripts
Oxford's digitised manuscripts, including the Douce Apocalypse
union catalogue of medieval manuscripts in American collections
the Getty's collection of illuminated manuscripts and leaves
secs: Eastern Christian illuminators in the data

leaves.label: Ghent-Bruges School
leaves.defn: Flemish manuscript illumination c. 1475–1560 with illusionistic borders: the Grimani Breviary, Simon Bening's Da Costa Hours.
leaves.see: C2-29 Gothic Book Illustration; A5-19 Early Netherlandish Painting
leaves.axis: Works: every gathered Ghent-Bruges and Flemish manuscript with sitelinks ≥ 1 (text-only devotional items excluded), by date; then collections and illuminators.

leaves.label: Tibetan Manuscript Illumination
leaves.defn: Illuminated and illustrated Tibetan books in the long pothi format, from the Dunhuang finds (8th–10th c.) to the gold-and-silver on indigo-paper Kangyur and Tengyur sets of monasteries, with painted miniatures of deities and carved and painted book covers.
leaves.axis: sub-types (canonical sets and book parts) first, then centres
catalogues: catalogue of the manuscript departments of the Bibliothèque nationale de France
image database of Tibetan art including manuscript folios and covers
Tibetan manuscripts and book covers at the V&A

leaves.label: Coptic Manuscript Illumination
leaves.defn: Illuminated and decorated manuscripts in Coptic (Sahidic and Bohairic) of the Egyptian church, from the 4th century onward: interlace frontispieces, ornamented initials and full-page saints, from the White Monastery, the Hamuli (Fayum) library and the Wadi Natrun monasteries.
leaves.axis: centres (monastic libraries) by date; then named manuscripts' collections
catalogues: catalogue of the manuscript departments of the Bibliothèque nationale de France
holds the Hamuli Coptic manuscripts (9th–10th c.)
Coptic manuscripts and papyri in the British Museum

leaves.label: Syriac Manuscript Illumination
leaves.defn: Illuminated manuscripts of the Syriac churches of Mesopotamia and Syria from the 6th century: canon tables and full-page miniatures, as in the Rabbula Gospels (586), the Syriac Bible of Paris and the Jacobite lectionaries of Tur Abdin and Mosul (12th–13th c.).
leaves.see: Late Antique Illumination; Armenian Manuscript Illumination
leaves.axis: named manuscripts' traditions and centres by date
catalogues: catalogue of the manuscript departments of the Bibliothèque nationale de France
vHMML: digitised Syriac manuscripts of the Middle East
the largest Syriac manuscript collection in Europe

subs.label: Bookbinding
subs.axis: Axis: tradition.

leaves.label: Islamic Bookbinding
leaves.defn: the bindings of the Islamic book: tooled, stamped and filigree-cut leather with the envelope flap, and from the 15th century painted lacquer bindings.
leaves.see: I2-1 Persian Lacquer. Possession taxonomy: Illuminated manuscript (F1 Media & Publications); Manuscript book (F1 Media & Publications).
leaves.axis: Sub-types (tooled and stamped leather, filigree, lacquer bindings), then binders by date; collections.
catalogues: The Met collection search: Islamic bookbinding

leaves.label: Treasure Binding
leaves.defn: Medieval European book covers worked by goldsmiths in gold, silver-gilt, enamel, gems and carved ivory for Gospel books and altar books, c. 700–1200: Lindau Gospels upper cover, Codex Aureus of St. Emmeram, Ashburnham Pentateuch ivory covers, Gospels of Theodelinda.
leaves.aliases: jewelled binding;jeweled book cover;cover of a Gospel book
leaves.see: C3-3 Fine Binding; C3-1 Islamic Bookbinding; G1-49 Mosan Art; D2 Ivory & Bone Carving
leaves.axis: Works: the surviving treasure bindings with holding place, by date; then goldsmith workshops.
catalogues: The Met collection search: book cover

leaves.label: Fine Binding
leaves.defn: Decorated leather bookbinding of Europe and America from the Gothic blind-stamped binding through Renaissance gold tooling to the designer bindings of the 20th century, named after binders, patrons and tooling styles: Grolier bindings, à la fanfare, Le Gascon pointillé, Derome dentelle, Cobden-Sanderson's Doves bindings, Legrain's Art Deco bindings.
leaves.aliases: European fine binding;fine bindings;decorated bookbinding;gold-tooled binding
leaves.see: C3-1 Islamic Bookbinding; C3-2 Treasure Binding. Possession taxonomy: Fine binding (F1 Media & Publications).
leaves.axis: Phases (late Gothic, Renaissance gold-tooling, Arts and Crafts, Art Deco designer bindings), then binders by date; collections.

leaves.label: East Asian Bookbinding
leaves.defn: the book forms of China, Korea, Japan and Vietnam, from scrolls, concertina and butterfly bindings to side-stitched thread binding (xianzhuang) of folded leaves in cloth cases: Ming and Qing xianzhuang books, Japanese fukuro-toji wahon, Korean five-hole bindings.
leaves.aliases: xianzhuang; thread binding; stab binding; fukuro-toji
leaves.see: C3-3 Fine Binding; C2-12 Sutra Copying. Possession taxonomy: Japanese thread-bound book (F1 Media & Publications); Chinese thread-bound book (F1 Media & Publications).
leaves.axis: Sub-types by book form (scroll, concertina, butterfly, wrapped-back, thread binding), then centres; collections.

subs.label: Paper Arts
subs.axis: Axis: technique.

leaves.label: Ebru
leaves.defn: paper marbling as practised in Ottoman Turkey and Iran: colours floated on size and transferred to paper, used for album margins and endpapers.
leaves.see: Possession taxonomy: Suminagashi (C4 Craft & Art Supplies); Ebru (C4 Craft & Art Supplies); Western marbled endpapers (C4 Craft & Art Supplies); Fine binding (F1 Media & Publications)
leaves.axis: Sub-types (battal, tarakli, çiçekli, hatip, Persian abri), then masters by date; collections.
catalogues: The Met collection search: marbled paper

leaves.label: Sanjhi
leaves.defn: Paper-stencil cutting of the Braj temples of Mathura and Vrindavan, used to lay coloured powder images: Krishna lila stencils.
leaves.axis: Sub-types and centres, then makers; collections.

leaves.label: Chinese Paper Cutting
leaves.defn: Designs cut from red and coloured paper with scissors or knives for windows, doors and festivals across China (UNESCO 2009): window flowers (chuanghua), xi double-happiness cuts, embroidery patterns.
leaves.see: Possession taxonomy: Paper-cut window decoration (B4 Decor); Jianzhi (F2 Art)
leaves.axis: Regional sub-types (northern and southern styles), centres and masters; collections.

leaves.label: Papel Picado
leaves.defn: Mexican cut tissue paper banners chiselled through stacked sheets with designs for the Day of the Dead and fiestas.
leaves.see: A6-14 Amate Painting. Possession taxonomy: Papel picado (F2 Art).
leaves.axis: Sub-types by occasion, then centres; collections.

leaves.label: Vytsinanka
leaves.defn: Belarusian folk paper cutting, symmetrical designs cut with scissors from folded paper for interiors and festivals (UNESCO 2024).
leaves.axis: Sub-types and makers; collections.
catalogues: European museum and library records matching 'vycinanka'

leaves.label: Slovenian Paper Flower Making
leaves.defn: The Slovenian craft of making crepe and tissue paper flowers for church feasts, processions and festive decoration.
leaves.axis: Sub-types and centres.

leaves.label: Oil-Paper Umbrella
leaves.defn: the craft of bamboo-ribbed umbrellas covered in hand-made paper, waterproofed with tung or persimmon oil and painted with flowers, birds and calligraphy, from China to Japan and Southeast Asia: Luzhou and Meinong oil-paper umbrellas, Japanese wagasa, Pathein umbrellas.
leaves.see: C4 Paper Arts; C4-8 Fan Making. Possession taxonomy: Parasol (A4 Bags & Accessories); Oil-paper umbrella (A4 Bags & Accessories); Wagasa (A4 Bags & Accessories); Janome-gasa (A4 Bags & Accessories); Pathein hti (A4 Bags & Accessories).
leaves.axis: Regional sub-types (Chinese, Japanese, Burmese), then centres; collections.

leaves.label: Fan Making
leaves.defn: the making and painting of hand fans, folding and flat, in paper, silk, bamboo, ivory and lacquer, studied as decorated objects with named centres: Kyoto sensu and uchiwa, Hangzhou folding fans, Valencian painted fans, Parisian éventails.
leaves.aliases: éventail; hand fan; sensu; uchiwa; shanzi

leaves.defn: Statuary, relief and figurines of the Nubian kingdom of Kush in its Napatan (c. 750–300 BCE) and Meroitic (c. 300 BCE–350 CE) phases, Egyptianising royal statues of the 25th Dynasty and Meroitic ba-statues and temple reliefs: Taharqa sphinx, Jebel Barkal statues, Meroë reliefs.

leaves.defn: The sculpture of ancient Cyprus: Chalcolithic picrolite cruciform figurines, Bronze Age terracotta plank figures, and the limestone and terracotta votive statues dedicated in the island's sanctuaries from the Cypro-Archaic to the Hellenistic period, in a local style that absorbed Near Eastern, Egyptian and Greek forms.

leaves.defn: Check-stamped and simple-stamped pottery of the Deptford culture of the south-eastern Atlantic and Gulf coasts (c. 800 BCE–700 CE), preceding Swift Creek.

leaves.label: St. Johns Pottery
leaves.defn: Chalky, sponge-spicule-tempered pottery of the St. Johns culture of north-eastern Florida (c. 500 BCE–1565 CE), plain, incised and later check-stamped.

leaves.label: Christian Nubian Pottery
leaves.defn: Wheel-made painted pottery of the Christian kingdoms of Nubia (c. 550–1500), decorated with birds, crosses and vegetal designs in the manner of manuscripts, from the workshops of Faras and Old Dongola.

leaves.label: Multan Blue Pottery
leaves.defn: Blue-and-turquoise painted, glazed earthenware and tiles (kashi) of Multan in Punjab, used on its Sufi shrines and still made by kashigar families: dishes, vases and tile panels.

leaves.label: Ancient Cypriot Pottery
leaves.defn: The pottery of ancient Cyprus from the Chalcolithic to the Cypro-Classical period: Red-on-White and Red Polished handmade wares of the Chalcolithic and Early–Middle Bronze Age, the Late Bronze Age Base Ring and White Slip wares exported across the Levant, and the Iron Age White Painted, Bichrome and Black-on-Red wares with free-field figural jugs and barrel-shaped jugs.

leaves.label: Predynastic Egyptian Pottery
leaves.defn: The pottery of prehistoric Upper Egypt, c. 4400–3000 BCE, in Petrie's sequence: Badarian and Naqada black-topped red ware, the White Cross-lined ware of Naqada I, and the Decorated ware of Naqada II–III painted in red on buff marl clay with boats, figures and spirals, with the wavy-handled jars used to date the sequence.
leaves.aliases: Naqada pottery; Amratian pottery; Gerzean pottery
leaves.see: E2-15 Egyptian Faience; D5-55 Ancient Egyptian Sculpture

leaves.label: Paracas Pottery
leaves.defn: The pottery of the Paracas culture of the south coast of Peru (first millennium BCE): incised vessels painted after firing with resin-based colours, double-spout-and-bridge bottles and feline-face bottles, in geometric, zoomorphic and abstract designs; the forerunner of Nazca polychrome.
leaves.see: H4-32 Paracas Textiles; E1-48 Nazca Pottery
leaves.axis: sub-types, then holding institutions

leaves.label: Lydian Pottery
leaves.defn: The pottery of Lydia in western Anatolia, centred on Sardis (8th–6th century BCE): streaked and marbled wares, black-on-red and bichrome painted vessels in an East Greek-related style, and the lydion, the footed spherical perfume jar named after Lydia and adopted by Greek potters.
leaves.see: E1-30 East Greek Vase Painting; K3 Ancient Mediterranean & Near Eastern Architecture
leaves.axis: sub-types, then holding institutions

leaves.label: Lapita Pottery
leaves.defn: Low-fired earthenware of the Lapita culture of the western Pacific (c. 1500–500 BCE), tempered with shell or sand and decorated with dentate-stamped geometric designs, carried from the Bismarck Archipelago to Fiji, Tonga and Samoa by the ancestors of the Polynesians; plain ware followed it before pottery ceased in Western Polynesia.
leaves.axis: sub-types, then holding institutions

leaves.label: Sepik Pottery
leaves.defn: Coiled earthenware of the Sepik River region of Papua New Guinea: the incised and painted storage jars, sago bowls and hooks of the Sawos and the modelled, face-decorated pots of Aibom on Chambri Lake, traded along the river.
leaves.see: D5-85 Sepik Carving; E1-147 Lapita Pottery

leaves.defn: Painted pottery of the Samarra culture of northern and central Mesopotamia (c. 6200–5700 BCE): fine buff wares painted in dark brown with geometric bands and whirling figures of women, birds, fish and scorpions, named after the finds at Samarra on the Tigris.

leaves.label: Halaf Pottery
leaves.defn: The polychrome painted pottery of the Halaf culture of northern Mesopotamia and Syria (c. 6100–5100 BCE), fired in two-chambered kilns: thin-walled bowls and jars painted in red, black and white with bucrania, rosettes, Maltese squares and checker patterns.

leaves.label: Ubaid Pottery
leaves.defn: The greenish-buff pottery of the Ubaid period of Mesopotamia (c. 5500–3700 BCE), painted in dark geometric designs and increasingly made on the slow wheel, spread from southern Iraq to the Gulf and Anatolia before the Uruk period.
leaves.see: E1-149 Samarra Ware; E1-150 Halaf Pottery
leaves.axis: sub-types, then holding institutions

leaves.label: Triana Pottery
leaves.defn: The tin-glazed pottery and tiles of Triana, the potters' quarter of Seville across the Guadalquivir: cuerda seca and cuenca (arista) tiles and later painted azulejos and maiolica, the tile industry that clad Seville's buildings.
leaves.see: L3 Mosaic & Tile Revetment; E1-81 Talavera de la Reina Pottery

leaves.label: Sesklo Pottery
leaves.defn: The painted pottery of the Neolithic Sesklo culture of Thessaly (7th–6th millennium BCE), among the earliest in Europe: red-on-white wares with geometric designs turning to flame motifs late in the culture, followed by the Dimini wares.
leaves.axis: sub-types, then holding institutions

leaves.label: Harappan Pottery
leaves.defn: The wheel-made pottery of the Indus Valley Civilisation (c. 3300–1300 BCE): fine red ware painted in black with intersecting circles, pipal leaves and fish-scale patterns, large storage jars, dishes-on-stand and perforated jars.
leaves.axis: sub-types, then holding institutions

leaves.label: Lenca Pottery
leaves.defn: The pottery of the Lenca of western Honduras and eastern El Salvador, made by hand by women from pre-Columbian times to the present: orange and brick-coloured household ware, and since the 1980s the black-and-white painted pottery of the La Campa and Gracias cooperatives.

fams.label: Textiles, Carpets & Dress
fams.test: made of fibre: carpets and rugs, woven, embroidered, dyed and felted textiles, and dress. Decorated leather is H10.
key: 1. Knotted pile? → H1. 2. A flatweave (tapestry-woven kilim, soumak, warp-faced weaving)? → H2.
3. A figured or patterned woven textile (silk, brocade, lampas, velvet, tapestry, shawl)? → H3.
4. Decorated with the needle (embroidery, appliqué, needle lace)? → H4. 5. Patterned by resist-dyeing or printing (ikat, block print)? → H5. 6. Felt? → H6.
7. A dress tradition curated as such (a named costume ensemble)? → H7. A garment type alone is not an art tradition (P10).
8. Basketry, matting or barkcloth? → H8. Beadwork, porcupine quillwork or featherwork as the work? → H9.
10. Decorated leather (tooled, carved, stamped, embroidered or appliquéd) where the leather is the work? → H10.

fams.label: Architecture
fams.test: a building or designed built whole, placed by its style; buildings are representative works and architects are kinds. The plant and floral arts of the garden traditions (bonsai, penjing, ikebana) are K14.
key: 1. A revival built outside the tradition it revives? → K2 (P8).
2. A style of the Islamic world? → K1.

3. Otherwise the style's own tradition: ancient Mediterranean and Near East → K3; medieval Europe → K4; Europe and its colonies 1400–1850 → K5; modern and contemporary movements → K6; South Asia → K7; East Asia → K8; Southeast Asia → K9; Africa → K10; the Indigenous Americas → K11; named vernacular and Oceanic traditions → K12.
4. A living plant shaped in a container, or a flower arrangement, made as a work (bonsai, penjing, ikebana)? → K14.

fams.label: Art in Place

key: 1. Pecked, engraved or painted on rock? → L1. 2. Painted on a wall or ceiling? → L2. 3. Mosaic, tile revetment or mirror work assembled on site? → L3. 4. A ground figure? → L4. 5. On the body (tattoo, body painting, henna)? → L5.
6. An ephemeral design drawn on a floor or the ground in powder, sand or paste? → L6.

familyKey: 1. Is it a building or a designed built whole (a garden, a complex), placed by its style? → K Architecture. Ornament carved, painted or tiled on a building and studied where it stands is asked next (2); loose architectural fragments in a museum go by their material (D, E, I). Living plant and floral arts (bonsai, ikebana) are K14.
2. Is it made on or into a fixed surface and studied where it stands: rock art, wall painting, in-situ mosaic and tile revetment, a geoglyph, or art on the living body? → L Art in Place.

3. Is it a photograph or made with a camera? → J Photography. Is it time-based, installed or performed (video, installation, performance, digital)? → M New Media, Installation & Performance. Is it a design for serial production held as a landmark of design (a chair, lamp, appliance or poster in a design collection)? → N Design (P17).

4. Is the written or decorated book the work: calligraphy, illumination (ornament), binding, paper decoration, or a manuscript tradition studied as the book? → C Book Arts & Calligraphy. Pictures in a manuscript belong to a painting tradition and go on to 6 (precedence P1).
5. Is it a drawing made as an end in itself or as a design, or a print pulled from a matrix? → B Drawings & Prints.
6. Is it a picture made with paint or ink on a movable flat support (paper, vellum, panel, canvas, cloth, silk)? → A Painting.

7. Is it carved, modelled or cast as an image or as carving for its own sake: statues, reliefs, carved stucco, ivory, bone, jade, rock crystal and hardstone, masks and puppets? → D Sculpture & Carving. A vessel carved from rock crystal or jade stays here; a cast metal vessel is G.

8. Otherwise place it by its material: fired clay → E Ceramics; glass → F Glass; metal (vessels, instruments, arms, jewellery) → G Metalwork, Arms & Jewellery; fibre (carpets, woven, embroidered, dyed and felted textiles, dress, decorated leather) → H Textiles, Carpets & Dress; wood, lacquer and papier-mâché, furniture → I Woodwork, Lacquer & Furniture.
Inside a family, run the family's own key (on each family card), then choose the leaf whose definition fits; a leaf's kinds are its named sub-schools, centres, workshops, sub-types and makers.
precedence: Pictures painted in a manuscript or for an album go to A1 Manuscript & Album Painting when the tradition is studied as painting (Persian, Ottoman, Mughal, Deccan, Arab); the book as an object — its script, illumination ornament and binding — goes to C. An illustrated manuscript is placed by what makes it notable: its pictures → A1, its script or illumination → C.

A tile is placed by its ware in E Ceramics (Iznik tiles under Iznik Pottery; Kashan lustre tiles under Kashan Lustreware). A revetment assembled on site as a named technique — cut-tile mosaic, zellige, kashi kari, mirror mosaic — is L3, because the work is the wall.

Carved stucco, stone and wood that survive as museum fragments go to their material family (D1 carving, I1 woodwork). The building that carries them is K; a named in-situ programme of painting or mosaic is L.
Lustre is a surface technique, not a sub-family: a lustreware is placed by its body (earthenware lustre → E1; fritware lustre → E2) and then by its named ware.
A vessel carved from rock crystal, jade or other hardstone is D3 (the carving is the work), not glass or metalwork, even when mounted in metal.

A dynasty, reign, empire or period (Mamluk, Safavid, Qajar, Akbar's reign) is a period tag, never a node. The node is the tradition the work belongs to in its medium: Mamluk enamelled glass (F3), Mamluk metalwork (G1), Mamluk carpets (H1), Mamluk architecture (K).

A city, production centre, country or culture label (Iznik, Kashan, Tabriz, 'Iranian', 'Syrian') is a place tag. A centre becomes a kind under a leaf only when the field names a distinct school or ware after it (Herat school, Kashan lustreware, Ushak carpets).

A revival built outside the original tradition (Moorish Revival synagogues, Neo-Mamluk, the First National Architectural Movement) is a leaf in K Historicist & National Revivals, never a kind of the style it revives.

A named maker is a kind under the leaf of the tradition they worked in, linked to their school or atelier where one is recorded. A maker active in two traditions is placed where most of their recorded work sits, with a see-also to the other (Mir Sayyid Ali and Abd al-Samad: Persian schooling, Mughal atelier → Mughal Painting).

A folk or vernacular craft that the field names on its own (suzani, kilim, Berber jewellery) is its own leaf in the medium family; a court or urban tradition of the same medium is a separate leaf. Garment types (abaya, shemagh, ghutra) are not art traditions: they belong to the Possession Taxonomy.

In artist-led cells a painter, sculptor or printmaker goes to the movement or school their work is attested in; with no attested movement, to the period-style leaf of their medium (Baroque Painting, Romantic Painting ...), never to a country.

A culture is never a leaf by itself: its leaves are its traditions in each medium (Yoruba sculpture, Yoruba beadwork), so one culture can hold several leaves across families. A culture known for one medium only gets one leaf there.

An archaeological culture known for one dominant medium (Nok terracottas, Jōmon pottery) is a leaf in that medium; its other finds are kinds or see-also, not separate leaves, unless the field names them.

A gathered culture row (Ewe, Mende, Asante) is a kind of the tradition that holds most of its objects when one medium tradition of that people has a leaf; otherwise it is a place tag (P12). A named carving school, provincial painting school or centre (Te Arawa, Murshidabad, Swat) is a kind of its leaf.

With no attested movement, an artist goes to the period-style leaf of their medium by birth year: academic and salon art for those trained in the academies before the modern movements (born before c. 1850), Modern Art (born c. 1850–1944), Contemporary Art (born 1945 or later). The artist's own medium decides, not the medium recorded in the source when it is plainly wrong (a photographer recorded as a painter is a photographer).
Period leaves for architects, designers and photographers

P15 applies to every medium: an architect with no attested style goes to the period architecture leaf of their birth (Neoclassical, Modern, Contemporary Architecture); a designer to the decorative-arts style of their working years (I3: Art Nouveau to Contemporary Design); a photographer to the photographic school of their working years (Pictorialism, Straight, Modernist, Documentary, Contemporary Photography). A designer or architect known first for one medium is placed by that medium.

N holds designs for serial production by the design movement or school that canonised them, the designed object being the kind. I3 keeps the period styles of furniture and the decorative arts with their designers and makers; a designer stays a kind of I3 while N is being gathered. A poster made and studied as a print is B2, a typeface C1-12, and studio crafts made by hand (studio pottery, studio glass) stay with their material.

The thing a person buys and owns, and who makes and sells it, is the Possession taxonomy's (a Persian rug, a Murano vase, Harris Tweed cloth, a bonsai tree); the tradition of making or decorating it to be looked at is placed here (Persian carpet weaving, Murano glassblowing, bonsai as an art). Ways of using things stay in Possession. A leaf that holds a tradition whose products Possession files names them under See also. Brands, sellers and product versions are never kinds here; artists and works taken out of Possession's art category are placed by P11 and P15.

Explicitness alone never decides. A work made for the art or mainstream circuit (studios, patrons, galleries, museums, the regular print and publishing trades) is placed here by its tradition even when explicit (shunga under Ukiyo-e, Khajuraho sculpture, Courbet, Koons's Made in Heaven, Mapplethorpe). An explicit work made for the adult trade (adult magazines and photo trades, adult imprints, adult doujinshi, Tijuana bibles) belongs to the Pleasure Taxonomies, with a finder row here; the circuit of first publication decides, not later museum acquisition (docs/ruling-s3-erotic-line.md).
modifiers: Period and dynasty — a filter on every kind and leaf (Umayyad, Abbasid, Fatimid, Seljuq, Ilkhanid, Mamluk, Timurid, Safavid, Ottoman, Mughal, Qajar ...). Never a node (P6).
Region and place — the 20-region grid of the gathering, plus production centre and country as tags (P7).

Ornament and motif — girih (geometric strapwork), arabesque (islimi), muqarnas, saz leaves, cintamani: a tag across media, never a leaf, since one motif runs through tiles, carpets, metalwork and buildings (open question Q6).
Holding institution and collection — evidence, never a node.
Patron and reign — a tag (Akbar, Shah Tahmasp, Süleyman); a royal atelier is a kind only when it is a recorded workshop (Imperial Mughal atelier, the Ottoman nakkaşhane).

Object type — bowl, ewer, tile, folio, page: an attribute of representative works, not a node. A leaf is a tradition, not an object type, except where the field treats the type as a tradition (astrolabes).
Inscription and script on objects — an attribute; calligraphy as an art (C1) is placed by script.
Subject and genre — portrait, landscape, still life, history painting, genre scene, religious image: a tag on works and kinds, never a node.

Technique and process — oil, tempera, fresco, watercolour, gouache, acrylic; woodcut, engraving, etching, lithography, screen print; daguerreotype, albumen, gelatin silver, colour and black-and-white photography: tags, never nodes (a fresco cycle is Art in Place by its site, an etching is a print by its school).
Abstraction and figuration — abstract art is a tag across movements (Abstract Expressionism, Suprematism, Dansaekhwa …), not a leaf of its own.
Building type — skyscraper, mosque, temple, castle, palace, house, garden pavilion: a tag on architecture kinds; styles are the leaves.
Folk and popular art — a filter that gathers the folk leaves of every medium (Mexican folk art = the Mexican folk leaves in A6, D5, E1, C4, H …).

fams.label: Film
fams.test: a film made as a single work for cinema, festival, television or streaming release, in live action or as documentary: features of more than 40 minutes (A1–A20, by movement and genre) and short films of 40 minutes or less (A21). An animated film of any length is C Animation.
key: A1 Art-Cinema Movements — by named art-cinema movement or school, in rough order of emergence; Slow Cinema, a transnational style, last. These movements are mainly drama; a movement defined by another genre or form sits in that sub-family (popular musical cinema A18, underground features A20, documentary and underground shorts A21).

A2 Crime — by the criminal world and engine the story is built on — organised crime and its named national cycles first, then street-crime cycles, the heist and the swindle, the law's agents, prison and courts, real and social crime; noir as a mode and crime played for laughs last

A3 Thriller & Mystery — by the source of suspense — the puzzle to be solved first, then the predator, the threatened mind and home, the abduction and the trap, the hunt and the chase; the state and its secrets last

A4 Horror — by the source of fear: the dead and the damned, national schools of the supernatural, classic and natural monsters, science and the body, the mind, human killers, gore, then the forms (found footage, anthology) and comedy last.

A5 Science Fiction — by the speculative premise: space, aliens, giant monsters, time and other realities, machines and biology, societies of the future and their ending, then soft and comic science fiction last.

A6 Fantasy & Adventure — by the source of the wonder or the quest: invented and magical worlds first, then myth and fairy tale, then the superhero franchises, then terrestrial adventure from the swashbuckler to the expedition.

A7 Action & Martial Arts — by the action engine: Hollywood action scenarios first, then the gun and assassin cycles, then the martial-arts traditions (Hong Kong and Chinese first), then the buddy cop, adaptation and exploitation hybrids.

A8 Historical & Period Film — by the representational mode of the past: epic spectacle by era first, then national period traditions, literary costume film, and last the reconstruction of real political, social and documented events.
A9 War Film — by war in chronological order (pre-modern battles to the War on Terror), then by mode (aftermath, anti-war).
A10 Western — by the western's historical cycle and its transpositions: silent and classical forms first, then revisionist and European cycles, transposed and contemporary westerns last.

A11 Biographical Film — by the field in which the subject is known: power (royals, politics, war, religion), discovery (exploration, science, business), the arts (visual, literary, music, show business), sport, crime, and private lives last.

A12 Comedy — by comic mode and engine (what makes the film funny): the clown and stage traditions first, then named national cycles, satire and dark modes, parody and performance forms, situational premises, youth and raunch comedy, crime and action hybrids, and comedy-drama by subject last.

A13 Romance — by the love-story engine, what draws the lovers together or keeps them apart; dramatic engines first (obstacle, suffering, obsession, betrayal, the couple itself, war, period, youth, queer love), then the comic engines of the romantic comedy, the romantic fantasy last.

A14 Musical & Dance Film — by how music and dance enter the story: integrated song (book musical, operetta), song as performance (revue, backstage), all-sung forms, rock and pop forms, recorded stage shows, dance, and films about musicians without musical numbers last.
A15 Erotic Film — by how sex drives the film and the production tradition: art-house erotic drama first, erotic thriller, then softcore and exploitation traditions, national erotic cycles last.

A16 Drama — by the dramatic engine — the bond, inner state, social condition, institution, contest or journey the drama turns on: family and home first, then the self, youth, society and its institutions, faith, sport, and journeys and animals last.
A17 Children's & Family Film — by the family-film engine: fantasy and animals first, then children's adventure, drama and comedy, then the teen television film, then the Christmas film by mode.
A18 Popular Cinema Modes — by popular industry and its named mode: Indian masala by language industry first, then the other South Asian, African and Turkish popular cinemas.

A19 Documentary — by documentary mode first (observational, ethnographic, poetic, essay, personal, archival, hybrid, propaganda), then by subject (politics, investigation, crime, war, history, people, art, cinema, music, sport, travel, nature); mondo last.
A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde — by avant-garde strategy for feature-length work: dream logic, underground, system, appropriation, tone poem, altered state, then avant-garde narrative.
A21 Short Film — by short-film mode: early cinema forms first, then fiction shorts by genre, then nonfiction shorts by purpose, avant-garde shorts last.

subs.label: Art-Cinema Movements
subs.axis: Axis: by named art-cinema movement or school, in rough order of emergence; Slow Cinema, a transnational style, last. These movements are mainly drama; a movement defined by another genre or form sits in that sub-family (popular musical cinema A18, underground features A20, documentary and underground shorts A21).

leaves.label: German Expressionism
leaves.defn: A film of the Weimar Expressionist movement: painted, distorted décor, chiaroscuro and stylised acting expressing inner states (The Cabinet of Dr. Caligari, Nosferatu, Metropolis). Later Expressionist-influenced genre films go to their genre (A4 Horror).
leaves.see: A1-2 French Impressionist Cinema; A4 Horror

leaves.label: French Impressionist Cinema
leaves.defn: A film of the 1919–1929 French avant-garde narrative school (Gance, Epstein, Dulac) using rhythmic montage and subjective optical effects to render feeling (J'accuse!, Napoleon, The Fall of the House of Usher).
leaves.see: A1-1 German Expressionism; A21-15 Avant-Garde Short

leaves.label: Soviet Montage
leaves.defn: A Soviet silent film built on montage theory, meaning made by the collision of shots (Battleship Potemkin, Strike, Earth). Vertov's documentary Man with a Movie Camera sits in A19-3.

leaves.label: Poetic Realism
leaves.defn: A 1930s French film of fatalistic working-class romance in studio-built, mist-laden settings (Port of Shadows, L'Atalante, Daybreak).

leaves.label: Italian Neorealism
leaves.defn: A postwar Italian film shot on location with non-professional actors about poverty and reconstruction (Bicycle Thieves, Rome, Open City, Umberto D.).

leaves.label: Parallel Cinema
leaves.defn: An Indian art-cinema film of the realist, non-commercial alternative to the mainstream, from Ray and Ghatak onward (Pather Panchali, Charulata, The Cloud-Capped Star). Popular Hindi cinema goes to A18.
leaves.see: A1-5 Italian Neorealism; A18 Popular Cinema Modes
leaves.axis: by filmmaker, in order of first film in the leaf; other filmmakers last

leaves.label: Polish Film School
leaves.defn: A Polish film of 1955–1961 reckoning with war and resistance (Ashes and Diamonds, Kanal, A Generation).
leaves.see: A1-25 Cinema of Moral Anxiety; A9 War Film

leaves.label: French New Wave
leaves.defn: A film by the late-1950s/1960s Cahiers-generation directors breaking classical continuity: location shooting, jump cuts, cinephile reference (The 400 Blows, Breathless, Jules and Jim). The Resnais–Marker–Varda wing with literary modernist leanings goes to A1-9.
leaves.see: A1-9 Left Bank; A1-31 Cinéma du look
leaves.axis: by phase of the movement: forerunners and first features, high period, late and politicised films

leaves.label: Left Bank
leaves.defn: A film of the Rive Gauche group (Resnais, Marker, Varda, Duras) joining literary modernism to fractured memory and time (Hiroshima Mon Amour, Last Year at Marienbad, Muriel).
leaves.see: A1-8 French New Wave; A19-4 Essay Film

leaves.label: British New Wave
leaves.defn: A British film of c.1959–1970 adapting kitchen-sink realism to working-class lives in the industrial North (Saturday Night and Sunday Morning, A Taste of Honey, Kes).

leaves.label: Japanese New Wave
leaves.defn: A Japanese film of the 1960s–70s nūberu bāgu breaking with studio humanism through sex, politics and formal rupture (Death by Hanging, Woman in the Dunes, The Insect Woman).
leaves.see: A1-8 French New Wave; A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde
leaves.axis: by filmmaker, in order of first film in the leaf; other filmmakers last

leaves.label: Czechoslovak New Wave
leaves.defn: A Czechoslovak film of 1963–1970 using absurdist humour, surreal fantasy or non-professional realism against official culture (Daisies, Closely Watched Trains, The Firemen's Ball).
leaves.axis: by country of production, largest first; other countries last

leaves.label: Yugoslav Black Wave
leaves.defn: A Yugoslav film of the 1960s–early 1970s whose dark, sexually frank critique of socialist society drew censure (WR: Mysteries of the Organism, I Even Met Happy Gypsies, Early Works).

leaves.label: Portuguese New Cinema
leaves.defn: A film of the 1960s Novo Cinema in Portugal, modernist breaks with the Estado Novo studio tradition (The Green Years, Change of Life).

leaves.label: New German Cinema
leaves.defn: A West German film of the 1960s–early 1980s auteur renewal after the Oberhausen Manifesto (Aguirre, the Wrath of God, Fear Eats the Soul, Kings of the Road).
leaves.axis: by filmmaker, in order of first film in the leaf; other filmmakers last

leaves.label: Cinema Novo
leaves.defn: A Brazilian film of the 1960s movement of "an idea in the head and a camera in the hand", poverty, violence and myth in the sertão (Black God, White Devil, Barren Lives, Entranced Earth).
leaves.see: A20-11 Cinema Marginal; A1-18 Third Cinema
leaves.axis: by filmmaker, in order of first film in the leaf; other filmmakers last

leaves.label: Third Cinema
leaves.defn: A militant anti-colonial film of the Latin American, African and Arab "third cinema" manifesto against Hollywood and auteur cinema (The Battle of Algiers, Memories of Underdevelopment, Blood of the Condor). Its militant documentaries sit in A19.
leaves.see: A1-16 Cinema Novo; A19-4 Essay Film

leaves.label: New American Cinema
leaves.defn: A New York independent film of the late-1950s/1960s New American Cinema Group, improvised and anti-Hollywood (Shadows, The Cool World). Its underground and diary films sit in A20-2 and A19-5.
leaves.see: A20-2 Underground Film; A1-20 New Hollywood

leaves.label: New Hollywood
leaves.defn: An American studio-era film of 1967–1980 made by the auteur generation that took over Hollywood, with downbeat endings, sex, violence and European influence (Bonnie and Clyde, Taxi Driver, Nashville, Jaws).
leaves.see: A2 Crime; A1-19 New American Cinema
leaves.axis: by the strand of the movement: counterculture, crime revision, paranoia and horror, character studies, Vietnam and late epics; the blockbuster turn last

leaves.label: L.A. Rebellion
leaves.defn: A film by the Black filmmakers of UCLA's 1967–1990s L.A. School, neorealist and Third Cinema-informed (Killer of Sheep, Daughters of the Dust, Bush Mama).

leaves.label: No Wave Cinema
leaves.defn: A late-1970s/1980s Lower East Side underground film, punk, Super 8 or 16mm, deadpan (Stranger Than Paradise, Permanent Vacation, Born in Flames).

leaves.label: Australian New Wave
