leaves.defn: An Australian film of the 1970s–early 1980s revival, landscape-haunted and period-set (Picnic at Hanging Rock, Wake in Fright, Breaker Morant).

leaves.label: Second Golden Age of Philippine Cinema
leaves.defn: A Filipino film of the 1970s–early 1980s auteur renaissance under martial law (Manila in the Claws of Light, Insiang, Oro, Plata, Mata).
leaves.axis: by filmmaker, in order of first film in the leaf; other filmmakers last

leaves.label: Cinema of Moral Anxiety
leaves.defn: A Polish film of 1976–1981 probing compromise and corruption in socialist life (Camera Buff, Man of Iron, Blind Chance).

leaves.label: Iranian New Wave
leaves.defn: An Iranian art film from the late 1960s onward, often child-centred, reflexive and near-documentary (Close-Up, Taste of Cherry, The White Balloon, A Separation).
leaves.axis: by filmmaker, in order of first film in the leaf; other filmmakers last

leaves.label: Taiwan New Cinema
leaves.defn: A Taiwanese film of the 1980s–90s movement of long takes and historical memory (A City of Sadness, Yi Yi, A Brighter Summer Day).
leaves.see: A1-39 Slow Cinema; A1-28 Hong Kong New Wave

leaves.label: Hong Kong New Wave
leaves.defn: A Hong Kong film of the late-1970s/1980s new wave and its second wave (Boat People, Rouge, Chungking Express).

leaves.label: Fifth Generation
leaves.defn: A mainland Chinese film by the 1982 Beijing Film Academy graduates, allegorical and visually lavish (Yellow Earth, Red Sorghum, Farewell My Concubine).

leaves.label: Sixth Generation
leaves.defn: A mainland Chinese film of the 1990s–2000s urban, semi-underground generation (Platform, Suzhou River, Still Life).
leaves.see: A1-29 Fifth Generation; A1-39 Slow Cinema

leaves.label: Cinéma du look
leaves.defn: A 1980s French film of glossy, youth-oriented, music-video visual style (Diva, Subway, Betty Blue).

leaves.label: New Queer Cinema
leaves.defn: An early-1990s independent queer film, defiant and formally transgressive in the AIDS era (Poison, My Own Private Idaho, The Living End).

leaves.label: New Argentine Cinema
leaves.defn: An Argentine film of the 1990s–2000s renewal, minimalist and observational (The Swamp, Pizza, Beer, and Cigarettes, Los Muertos).

leaves.label: Dogme 95
leaves.defn: A film certified under the Dogme 95 "vow of chastity": handheld, location sound, no added lighting or score (The Celebration, The Idiots, Julien Donkey-Boy).

leaves.label: Mumblecore
leaves.defn: A 2000s–2010s American micro-budget film of improvised talk among twenty-somethings (Funny Ha Ha, Drinking Buddies, Tiny Furniture).

leaves.label: Berlin School
leaves.defn: A German art film of the 1990s–2010s Berliner Schule, restrained and observational (Yella, Everyone Else, Toni Erdmann).

leaves.label: Romanian New Wave
leaves.defn: A Romanian film of the 2000s onward, long-take realist dramas of post-communist bureaucracy and morality (The Death of Mr. Lazarescu, 4 Months, 3 Weeks and 2 Days, Police, Adjective).

leaves.label: Greek Weird Wave
leaves.defn: A Greek film of the 2009–2010s crisis-era wave of deadpan, absurdist family and social allegory (Dogtooth, Attenberg, Alps).

leaves.label: Slow Cinema
leaves.defn: A narrative art film whose defining device is duration: very long takes, minimal action, contemplative observation (Jeanne Dielman, Sátántangó, Stalker, Uncle Boonmee). National movements with a slow strand (Taiwan New Cinema, Romanian New Wave) keep their own leaf.
leaves.see: A1-27 Taiwan New Cinema; A20-3 Structural Film
leaves.axis: by lineage and region: European modernist precursors first, then later European, Asian, Turkish and Ibero-American practitioners

leaves.label: Ukrainian Poetic Cinema
leaves.defn: The Kyiv (Dovzhenko Studio) school of the mid-1960s to late 1970s — Parajanov, Ilyenko, Osyka, Ivchenko, Mykolaichuk — making folkloric, painterly, ritual-saturated films of Ukrainian village and legend (Shadows of Forgotten Ancestors, The White Bird Marked with Black).

leaves.label: Korean New Wave
leaves.defn: The South Korean art cinema of c. 1987–1996 (Park Kwang-su, Jang Sun-woo, Lee Myung-se, Park Jong-won) that, after democratisation, turned realist and modernist means on division, labour and the Gwangju massacre (Chilsu and Mansu, A Petal, A Single Spark); it precedes the commercial Korean Wave of the 2000s.

leaves.label: Thai New Wave
leaves.defn: The revival of Thai cinema from 1997 by directors from advertising and music video — Pen-Ek Ratanaruang, Nonzee Nimibutr, Wisit Sasanatieng, the Pang brothers — mixing pastiche, colour stylisation and genre (Tears of the Black Tiger, 6ixtynin9, Monrak Transistor).

leaves.label: Nuevo Cine Mexicano
leaves.defn: The 1990s–2000s renewal of Mexican cinema (Arturo Ripstein's late films, María Novaro, Jorge Fons, Alfonso Cuarón, Alejandro González Iñárritu, Antonio Serrano) after the IMCINE reforms: urban, frank, internationally co-produced films (Danzón, Midaq Alley, Y tu mamá también).

subs.label: Crime
subs.axis: Axis: by the criminal world and engine the story is built on — organised crime and its named national cycles first, then street-crime cycles, the heist and the swindle, the law's agents, prison and courts, real and social crime; noir as a mode and crime played for laughs last

leaves.label: Gangster Film
leaves.defn: A film whose protagonist is a member or boss of a criminal organisation and whose story is the gang's rise, wars and fall (Little Caesar, Once Upon a Time in America, Gomorrah, Vada Chennai). Hindi-language underworld films go to A2-2 Mumbai Noir, Japanese ones to A2-3; a film that follows the police against the mob goes to A2-15/A2-16.
leaves.aliases: mob film; mafia film; underworld film
leaves.see: A2-2 Mumbai Noir; A2-3 Yakuza Film; A2-25 Neo-Noir
leaves.axis: by the criminal tradition: the classical American cycle and the mafia saga first, then crime-boss biography and the national gangster traditions

leaves.label: Mumbai Noir
leaves.defn: A Hindi-language film of the Bombay underworld (or its Shakespearean transpositions to the gangland of the Hindi heartland), shot in a realist, violent register (Satya, Maqbool, Omkara). South Indian gangster sagas stay in A2-1.

leaves.label: Yakuza Film
leaves.defn: A film about the Japanese yakuza, from the ninkyo chivalry films through Fukasaku's jitsuroku and Kitano's deadpan cycle (Battles Without Honor and Humanity, Sonatine, Outrage).
leaves.aliases: yakuza eiga; ninkyo eiga; jitsuroku eiga
leaves.axis: era / production cycle of the Japanese yakuza film

leaves.label: Poliziottesco
leaves.defn: An Italian crime-action film of the 1970s cycle of violent cops, mobsters and kidnappers (Caliber 9, Rabid Dogs).

leaves.label: Hitman Film
leaves.defn: A film whose protagonist is a professional killer and whose drama is the contract, its code and its cost (The Mechanic, Ghost Dog, The American, The Killer). Stylised existential killers of the Melville line sit in A2-25 Neo-Noir.
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Drug Film
leaves.defn: A crime film whose engine is the illegal drug trade or drug addiction: cartels and mules, the dealer's world, the junkie's crimes (Traffic, Maria Full of Grace, Pusher, Drugstore Cowboy).
leaves.see: A2-8 Hood Film; A2-16 Police Film
leaves.axis: by the place in the trade: the cartel and the trafficking route first, then the dealer's street world, then the addict

leaves.label: Blaxploitation
leaves.defn: A 1970s American exploitation film made for Black urban audiences, with Black heroes against the Man, pimps and pushers (Shaft, Super Fly, Coffy), including its horror and Afrofuturist offshoots.

leaves.label: Hood Film
leaves.defn: An African-American (or Caribbean, Latino and Black British) film of street life, gangs and drugs in the inner-city neighbourhood (Boyz n the Hood, Menace II Society, Kidulthood).
leaves.see: A2-7 Blaxploitation; A16-22 Social Problem Film

leaves.label: Cine Quinqui
leaves.defn: A Spanish film of the late-1970s/80s cycle about juvenile delinquents of the urban periphery, often cast with real delinquents (Deprisa, Deprisa).

leaves.label: Pinky Violence
leaves.defn: A 1970s Toei exploitation film of female gangs and avenging women prisoners (Female Prisoner #701: Scorpion).
leaves.see: A2-19 Prison Film; A3-10 Revenge Thriller

leaves.label: Heist Film
leaves.defn: A film built around planning and executing a robbery, told from the thieves' side (Rififi, Ocean's Eleven, Heat, Reservoir Dogs). A swindle with no break-in goes to A2-12; a standoff with hostages to A3-12.
leaves.see: A2-12 Con-Artist Film; A3-12 Hostage & Siege Thriller
leaves.axis: by the heist's engine: the meticulous caper and the ensemble crew first, then the job that goes wrong, the professional thief, action spectacle; comic heists last

leaves.label: Con-Artist Film
leaves.defn: A film whose engine is a confidence trick: grifters, swindlers and the marks they play, often with a twist that cons the viewer (Nine Queens, House of Games, The Grifters, Focus).
leaves.aliases: con film; grifter film; swindle film
leaves.see: A2-11 Heist Film; A2-13 White-Collar Crime Film
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: White-Collar Crime Film
leaves.defn: A film about crime committed by the respectable in suits: fraud, embezzlement, financial and corporate crime (Wall Street, Boiler Room, Arbitrage, Lord of War).
leaves.see: A2-12 Con-Artist Film; A3-18 Conspiracy Thriller

leaves.label: Gambling Film
leaves.defn: A crime film whose world is the gambling table and the debt it creates (Rounders, Croupier, Uncut Gems, Hard Eight).

leaves.label: Police Procedural
leaves.defn: A film that follows police or federal investigators working a case step by step, its drama in the method of the inquiry (Stray Dog, The Night of the 12th, In the Heat of the Night, Mississippi Burning). A hunt for a serial killer goes to A3-6; a film about the cop's own conduct goes to A2-16.
leaves.see: A2-16 Police Film; A3-6 Serial-Killer Thriller
leaves.axis: by the investigating force: city homicide squads first, then the rural lawman, the federal agent

leaves.label: Police Film
leaves.defn: A film whose subject is the police officer rather than the case: the rule-breaking maverick, the corrupt cop, the undercover cop, the beat or tactical unit (Dirty Harry, Training Day, Infernal Affairs, Elite Squad).
leaves.see: A2-15 Police Procedural; A2-1 Gangster Film
leaves.axis: by the cop's relation to the law: the maverick first, then corruption, life undercover, the street and tactical unit

leaves.label: Nordic Noir
leaves.defn: A Scandinavian crime film in the bleak, procedural, socially critical Nordic-noir manner (The Girl with the Dragon Tattoo, Department Q, Insomnia 1997).

leaves.label: Private-Eye Film
leaves.defn: A film whose investigator is a private detective outside the noir canon: modern and comic private eyes and gentleman sleuths (Harper, Gone Baby Gone, Detective Byomkesh Bakshy!, Veronica Mars). Classic hardboiled eyes go to A2-24 and A2-25; closed-circle puzzles to A3-1.

leaves.label: Prison Film
leaves.defn: A film set inside a prison whose drama is incarceration itself: escape, survival among inmates, guard and riot (The Shawshank Redemption, Escape from Alcatraz, A Prophet, A Man Escaped).
leaves.see: A2-10 Pinky Violence; A16-25 Legal Drama
leaves.axis: by what the prisoner wants: out first, then survival inside, then the action brawl; political and wartime prisons last

leaves.label: True-Crime Film
leaves.defn: A dramatisation of a real crime case, centred on the criminal, the victim or the case itself rather than on a fictional investigation (In Cold Blood, 10 Rillington Place, Snowtown, Killers of the Flower Moon).
leaves.see: A3-6 Serial-Killer Thriller; A11 Biographical Film
leaves.axis: by whose story is told: the killer first, then the abducted victim, the notorious case, the swindle

leaves.label: Crime Social Problem Film
leaves.defn: A crime film that presents crime as the product of a social condition, youth, gangs, slum, poverty or vice, rather than as a genre puzzle (The Young and the Damned, City of God, Pickpocket, A Touch of Sin).
leaves.aliases: social realist crime film; juvenile-delinquency film
leaves.see: A2-8 Hood Film; A2-9 Cine Quinqui; A16 Drama
leaves.axis: by the social condition: youth first, then the gang, the slum, rural and provincial want, poverty and desperation; vice exposés last

leaves.label: Lovers-on-the-Run Film
leaves.defn: A film of a criminal couple in flight from the law, the outlaw road movie of Bonnie and Clyde (You Only Live Once, Breathless 1983, True Romance, Ain't Them Bodies Saints).

leaves.label: American Film Noir
leaves.defn: A Hollywood crime film of the classical noir period (c.1940–1960), with its fatalistic, shadowed visual style and doomed protagonists, plus late-1930s American precursors (Double Indemnity, Out of the Past, The Asphalt Jungle, Touch of Evil). British noir and non-Anglophone noir of the same years are separate leaves; post-classical noir goes to A2-25.
leaves.axis: Paul Schrader's phases of classic noir ("Notes on Film Noir", 1972)

leaves.label: British Noir
leaves.breadth: British crime films of the 1930s–early 1960s in the noir manner
leaves.defn: A British crime film of c.1929–1963 sharing film noir's fatalism and night-time urban style — spiv films, post-war crime melodramas and their quota-quickie precursors (Odd Man Out, The Third Man, Brighton Rock, It Always Rains on Sunday, Night and the City).
leaves.axis: by era

leaves.label: International Film Noir
leaves.breadth: classical-era noir and its precursors outside Hollywood and Britain
leaves.defn: A crime film of c.1913–1967 made outside the US and UK in the noir manner — French poetic-realist and policier precursors and contemporaries, Italian, Spanish and other European noir, Japanese and East Asian noir, and Mexican and Argentine cine negro (Le Corbeau, Touchez pas au grisbi, Drunken Angel, Pale Flower, Hardly a Criminal).
leaves.aliases: international noir; world noir; cine negro; film noir outside the United States
secs: Italian, German, Spanish & Other European Noir
leaves.axis: national tradition

leaves.label: Neo-Noir
leaves.defn: A post-classical crime film that revives noir's fatalism, moral ambiguity and stylisation (Chinatown, Blood Simple, Le Samouraï, Drive). Classical-period noir goes to A2-24.
leaves.axis: by the noir engine: the private eye and the femme fatale first, then country noir, the professional criminal, the payback, the urban underworld, the dream; the East Asian new noirs and pastiche last

leaves.label: Crime Comedy
leaves.defn: A crime film played for laughs: bungling crooks and mob farce (The Pope of Greenwich Village, Amateur, Caught Stealing). Comic heists stay in A2-11; most crime comedies are in A12 Comedy.
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

subs.label: Thriller & Mystery
subs.axis: Axis: by the source of suspense — the puzzle to be solved first, then the predator, the threatened mind and home, the abduction and the trap, the hunt and the chase; the state and its secrets last

leaves.label: Whodunit
leaves.defn: A mystery whose engine is the fair-play puzzle of which suspect committed the murder, solved by a detective (Murder on the Orient Express, Gosford Park, Knives Out). Inquiries by police squads go to A2-15.
leaves.see: A3-2 Inverted Detective Story; A2-18 Private-Eye Film
leaves.axis: by the shape of the puzzle: the great detective first, then the closed circle, the comic sleuths, the modern ensemble; twist-puzzle thrillers last

leaves.label: Inverted Detective Story
leaves.defn: A crime story that shows the murder and the murderer first, its suspense in the cover-up and the investigator closing in (Drishyam, Match Point, A Hard Day, Dial M for Murder).

leaves.label: Mystery Film
leaves.defn: A mystery whose enigma is not a murder puzzle but a disappearance, a buried past or a riddle, pursued by an ordinary person (Bunny Lake Is Missing, A Simple Favor, The Da Vinci Code, Blow-Up).
leaves.axis: by the enigma: the disappearance first, then the buried past, the esoteric riddle; the unresolved art-film enigma last

leaves.label: Krimi
leaves.defn: A West German Edgar Wallace (or Bryan Edgar Wallace) crime-mystery film of the 1959–1972 Rialto cycle (Face of the Frog).
leaves.axis: production series

leaves.label: Giallo
leaves.defn: An Italian murder-mystery thriller of the 1960s–80s cycle: black-gloved killer, stylised set-piece murders, amateur sleuth (Blood and Black Lace, The Bird with the Crystal Plumage, Deep Red).
secs: Other Gialli of the Classic Cycle (1968–1982)
leaves.axis: auteur (the field's own division of the giallo) and late/neo phase

leaves.label: Serial-Killer Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose engine is a serial or spree killer, followed by the hunter, the killer himself or the survivor (The Silence of the Lambs, Zodiac, The Chaser). Dramatised portraits of real killers go to A2-21.
leaves.see: A2-15 Police Procedural; A2-21 True-Crime Film; A3-5 Giallo
leaves.axis: by whose eyes: the manhunt first, then the killer's own, then the threatened witness or survivor

leaves.label: Psychological Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose threat comes from the mind: a protagonist's unstable perception, a double, lost memory, obsession or a mind game played on them (Vertigo, Memento, Black Swan, Shutter Island). Threats from spouse, family or lodger go to A3-8.
leaves.see: A3-8 Domestic Thriller; A3-3 Mystery Film
leaves.axis: by the source of the threat: the unreliable mind first, then the double, lost identity, obsession, the impostor; the mind game played by another last

leaves.label: Domestic Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose danger lives in the home and its intimacies: the murderous spouse, the intruder who moves in, the stalker, the poisoned family (Gaslight, Sleeping with the Enemy, The Hand That Rocks the Cradle, Single White Female). Desire-driven danger goes to A3-9..
leaves.aliases: domestic noir; '...from hell' thriller; female Gothic
leaves.see: A3-7 Psychological Thriller; A3-9 Erotic Thriller; A3-13 Home-Invasion Thriller
leaves.axis: by who threatens: the spouse first, then the intruder who moves in, the stalker, the family itself

leaves.label: Erotic Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller in which sexual desire is the engine of danger and crime (Body Heat, Fatal Attraction, Basic Instinct, The Handmaiden).
leaves.see: A3-8 Domestic Thriller; A2-25 Neo-Noir; A15 Erotic Film
leaves.axis: by the shape of the danger: the femme fatale first, then the obsessive affair, voyeurism, the art-house variant; sexual power games last

leaves.label: Revenge Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose engine is the protagonist's vengeance for a wrong (Death Wish, Oldboy, I Spit on Your Grave, Blue Ruin).
leaves.see: A2-5 Hitman Film; A7 Action & Martial Arts
leaves.axis: by the shape of the vengeance: the Korean revenge cycle first, then the vigilante, rape and revenge, the personal vendetta; the revenge action spree last

leaves.label: Kidnapping Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose engine is an abduction: the ransom demand, the frantic search, or the captive's ordeal (High and Low, Ransom, Prisoners, Misery).
leaves.see: A3-12 Hostage & Siege Thriller; A2-21 True-Crime Film
leaves.axis: by the kidnapper's aim: ransom first, then abduction and the search, then captivity

leaves.label: Hostage & Siege Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller of a standoff: hostages taken, a building besieged, a plane or train hijacked (The Negotiator, Toy Soldiers, Captain Phillips, The Taking of Pelham One Two Three).
leaves.see: A2-11 Heist Film; A3-13 Home-Invasion Thriller
leaves.axis: by the place held: the standoff first, then the siege, then the hijacked vehicle

leaves.label: Home-Invasion Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller in which intruders break into a home and hold or hunt its occupants (Panic Room, Cold Creek Manor, Borgman).
leaves.see: A3-12 Hostage & Siege Thriller; A4 Horror

leaves.label: Survival Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller of staying alive against nature, a pursuer or a trap (Deliverance, Duel, Buried, Alive).
leaves.see: A3-15 Death Game Film; A6 Fantasy & Adventure
leaves.axis: by the hostile space: wilderness first, then the road and its pursuers, the water, the confined trap; escape from civil unrest last

leaves.label: Death Game Film
leaves.defn: A film in which people are forced into a lethal game or contest with rules (Battle Royale, The Hunger Games, Cube, Escape Room), including the human hunt of The Most Dangerous Game.
leaves.see: A3-14 Survival Thriller; A5 Science Fiction

leaves.label: Real-Time Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose suspense depends on unfolding in (near) real time in a confined frame, a phone line, a screen or a race against the clock (Phone Booth, The Guilty, Run Lola Run, Profile).

leaves.label: Wrong-Man Thriller
leaves.defn: A Hitchcockian thriller of an innocent accused or mistaken for someone else, who must flee and prove his innocence (The 39 Steps, North by Northwest, The Fugitive, Tell No One).

leaves.label: Conspiracy Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller in which the protagonist uncovers a hidden plot by the powerful, the state, corporations or secret societies (The Parallax View, All the President's Men, The Insider, Enemy of the State).
leaves.see: A3-19 Political Thriller; A3-21 Spy Film
leaves.axis: by who conspires: the shadowy cabal of the paranoid thriller first, then corporations, then the press investigation, then the state cover-up

leaves.label: Political Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose stakes are political power itself: assassination, terrorism, military crisis, dictatorship, intrigue (Z, The Day of the Jackal, The Lives of Others, Conclave).
leaves.see: A3-18 Conspiracy Thriller; A3-21 Spy Film
leaves.axis: by the political threat: assassination first, then terror, military and nuclear crisis, dictatorship; intrigue for office last

leaves.label: Techno-Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose engine is a technology: hacking, surveillance, AI, computer crime (The Net, Blackhat, Eagle Eye, Who Am I).
leaves.see: A3-18 Conspiracy Thriller; A5 Science Fiction

leaves.label: Spy Film
leaves.defn: A film about espionage as tradecraft: agents, moles, defectors and covert operations for a state, played as suspense rather than action spectacle (Notorious, The Spy Who Came in from the Cold, Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy, Munich). Gadget-and-stunt superspy films go to Spy-Action Film.
leaves.see: A12-50 Spy Comedy; A3-18 Conspiracy Thriller
leaves.axis: by the spy's war: the interwar years and World Wars first, then the Cold War, the covert operation, today's intelligence world; the inter-Korean spy film last

leaves.label: Spy-Action Film
leaves.breadth: Superspy adventures of gadgets, stunts and global villains
leaves.defn: A spy film built as action spectacle: a superspy or agency team, gadgets, chases, exotic locations and a world-threatening villain, usually in a franchise (Dr. No, Goldfinger, Mission: Impossible, The Bourne Identity, Pathaan). Tradecraft and mole-hunt espionage stays in Spy Film.
leaves.aliases: superspy film; Bondian film; spy action
secs: Franchise Spy-Action (Bourne, Mission: Impossible, Jack Ryan)
leaves.axis: by cycle: the James Bond series, its 1960s imitators and the Eurospy wave, the post-Cold War franchises, then the Indian spy universe

subs.label: Horror
subs.axis: Axis: by the source of fear: the dead and the damned, national schools of the supernatural, classic and natural monsters, science and the body, the mind, human killers, gore, then the forms (found footage, anthology) and comedy last.

leaves.label: Ghost Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is the spirit of a dead person acting on the living, outside a single haunted dwelling (The Phantom Carriage, The Sixth Sense, Mama, The Devil's Backbone). A ghost bound to one house goes to the Haunted House Film; a Japanese onryō to J-Horror.
leaves.see: A4-2 Haunted House Film; A4-9 J-Horror; A4-3 Curse Film
leaves.axis: by how the dead reach the living: literary apparition, vengeful spirit, the medium who sees them, the place they are bound to

leaves.label: Haunted House Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is a dwelling or building itself, haunted by presences that menace whoever lives in or visits it (The Haunting, Poltergeist, The Conjuring, The Shining). A house haunted by a single cursed Japanese spirit goes to A4-9 J-Horror.
leaves.see: A4-1 Ghost Film; A4-4 Possession & Exorcism Film
leaves.axis: by who confronts the house: literary classic, besieged family, professional investigators, the institution, the grieving modern household

leaves.label: Curse Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose engine is a curse or rule-bound supernatural pursuit that is laid, summoned or passed on, so that knowing the rules is survival (It Follows, Candyman, Ouija, Final Destination). The Japanese curse cycle (Ringu) goes to A4-9 J-Horror.
leaves.see: A4-9 J-Horror; A4-1 Ghost Film; A4-20 Killer Toy Film
leaves.axis: by how the curse is caught: laid and passed on, summoned by saying or believing a legend, carried by an object or game, death's own design

leaves.label: Possession & Exorcism Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is a demon or spirit inhabiting a human body, usually met by an exorcism (The Exorcist III, The Rite, The Possession, Under the Shadow). A demon that besieges a house rather than a body goes to A4-2 or A4-5.
leaves.see: A4-5 Satanic Film; A4-6 Religious Horror
leaves.axis: by the rite and tradition: the Exorcist cycle, Catholic exorcist procedurals, the possessed child or woman at home, jinn, dybbuk and other non-Christian possession

leaves.label: Satanic Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose source of fear is Satan, his worshippers or the demonic hosts of Hell (The Omen, The Devil Rides Out, Hereditary, Hellraiser, The Evil Dead). A single possessed body goes to A4-4; nuns and convents to A4-6.
leaves.see: A4-4 Possession & Exorcism Film; A4-7 Witchcraft Horror
leaves.axis: by the form evil takes: the Antichrist child, the cult, the Devil in person, a demonic outbreak, Hell's otherworld, angels at war

leaves.label: Religious Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose fear grows from faith itself: convents, saints, zealotry and sacred ritual (The Nun, Saint Maud, Immaculate, Alucarda). Exorcism plots go to A4-4; Satanist cults to A4-5.
leaves.see: A4-4 Possession & Exorcism Film; A4-5 Satanic Film

leaves.label: Witchcraft Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is a witch, a coven or a practitioner of black magic (Suspiria, The Craft, The Lords of Salem, The Boxer's Omen). Rural pagan communities go to A4-8 Folk Horror.
leaves.see: A4-8 Folk Horror; A4-5 Satanic Film; A4-13 Indonesian Horror
leaves.axis: by the craft: the witch and coven, then sorcery and black magic rituals

leaves.label: Folk Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose dread comes from a rural landscape, its old beliefs and the community that keeps them (The Wicker Man, Witchfinder General, Midsommar, The Witch). A witch in a modern city goes to A4-7.
leaves.see: A4-7 Witchcraft Horror; A4-29 Backwoods Horror
leaves.axis: by where the old ways survive: British and Irish countryside, the pagan community, the wilderness, folk traditions elsewhere

leaves.label: J-Horror
leaves.defn: The Japanese horror wave from the late 1990s, built on vengeful onryō, technology as a channel for the dead and urban isolation, plus its Hollywood remakes (Ringu, Ju-on: The Grudge, Pulse, The Ring). Pre-modern Japanese ghost tales go to A4-10 Kaidan Film.
leaves.see: A4-10 Kaidan Film; A4-3 Curse Film; C9 Horror Anime
leaves.axis: by strand: the onryō curse cycle, techno-urban dread, then the Hollywood remakes of Asian horror

leaves.label: Kaidan Film
leaves.defn: A Japanese film of a pre-modern ghost or supernatural tale in the kaidan tradition (Ugetsu, Kwaidan, Onibaba, Kuroneko).
leaves.see: A4-9 J-Horror; A8 Historical & Period Film

leaves.label: Korean Horror
leaves.defn: A South Korean supernatural horror film drawing on shamanism, han and family guilt (A Tale of Two Sisters, The Wailing, Exhuma, Gonjiam: Haunted Asylum). Korean zombie films go to A4-18.
leaves.see: A4-9 J-Horror; A4-4 Possession & Exorcism Film

leaves.label: Thai Horror
leaves.defn: A Thai supernatural horror film built on phi spirits, Buddhist karma and village belief (Nang Nak, Shutter, The Medium, Death Whisperer). Thai horror-comedy goes to A4-38.

leaves.label: Indonesian Horror
leaves.defn: An Indonesian supernatural horror film drawn from local folklore, black magic (ilmu hitam) and Islamic belief, from the Suzzanna era to the 2010s revival (Satan's Slaves, Impetigore, Mystics in Bali, KKN di Desa Penari).
leaves.see: A4-7 Witchcraft Horror; A4-12 Thai Horror

leaves.label: Jiangshi Film
leaves.defn: A Hong Kong horror-comedy of hopping corpses and the Taoist priests who fight them (Mr. Vampire). Kept as the named cycle; European vampires go to A4-16.
leaves.see: A4-16 Vampire Film; A4-38 Comedy Horror

leaves.label: Gothic Horror
leaves.defn: A period horror film in the Gothic tradition of castles, ancestral curses and literary monsters, from Universal and Hammer to modern revivals (Frankenstein, Horror of Dracula, Black Sunday, Crimson Peak). Dracula and vampire films go to A4-16; werewolves to A4-17.
leaves.see: A4-16 Vampire Film; A4-17 Werewolf & Shapeshifter Film; A8 Historical & Period Film
leaves.axis: by studio cycle and period: early gothic, Universal monsters, Corman's Poe cycle, Hammer, Italian gothic, later revivals

leaves.label: Vampire Film
leaves.defn: A film whose monster is a blood-drinking undead, from Dracula adaptations to vampire comedies and action franchises (Nosferatu, Let the Right One In, The Lost Boys, Underworld). Hopping corpses go to A4-14 Jiangshi Film.
leaves.see: A4-15 Gothic Horror; A4-14 Jiangshi Film
leaves.axis: by register: Dracula adaptations first, then art-house, comic, teen/romantic, action, and siege/plague vampires

leaves.label: Werewolf & Shapeshifter Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose monster is a human who turns into a wolf or another beast (An American Werewolf in London, The Howling, Ginger Snaps, Cat People). Universal's The Wolf Man stays in A4-15.
leaves.see: A4-15 Gothic Horror; A4-19 Creature Feature
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Zombie Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is the reanimated or infected dead, from voodoo to rage virus (Night of the Living Dead, 28 Days Later, Shaun of the Dead, Train to Busan). Lab reanimation played for gore-comedy goes to A4-37 Splatstick.
leaves.axis: by what raises the dead: voodoo, Romero's ghouls, the Italian cycle, comedy, viral infection, action franchises, revenant drama

leaves.label: Creature Feature
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is an invented monster that is neither a real animal nor an alien (Creature from the Black Lagoon, Tremors, Gremlins, The Descent). Real animals go to A4-21 Natural Horror; aliens to A4-22; giant city-smashers to A5-6 Kaiju.
leaves.see: A4-21 Natural Horror; A4-22 Science Fiction Horror; A5-6 Kaiju
leaves.axis: by where the creature lives: water, underground, folklore and the demonic, small mischief-makers, prehistory and cryptids

leaves.label: Killer Toy Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is a doll, puppet, toy or animatronic come alive (Child's Play, Puppet Master, Annabelle, Five Nights at Freddy's). An AI android doll goes to A4-22.
leaves.see: A4-3 Curse Film; A4-22 Science Fiction Horror

leaves.label: Natural Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is real animals or nature turned predator, including enlarged or mutated real species (Jaws 2, The Birds, Cujo, Them!, Long Weekend). Invented monsters go to A4-19.
leaves.axis: by the attacker: sharks and sea beasts, reptiles, swarms and giant bugs, mammals and birds, nature itself

leaves.label: Science Fiction Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat comes from a science-fictional premise: aliens, space, experiments, contagion or machines (Alien, The Thing, Invasion of the Body Snatchers, The Fly). Bodily transformation as the point goes to A4-23 Body Horror; cosmic unknowability to A4-24.
leaves.see: A5 Science Fiction; A4-23 Body Horror; A4-24 Lovecraftian Horror
leaves.axis: by the scientific source of the threat: alien predator, alien replacement, space and remote stations, the lab, contagion, machines

leaves.label: Body Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose fear is the transformation, invasion or mutilation of the human body itself (Videodrome, Tetsuo: The Iron Man, The Substance, Titane). A creature born in a lab goes to A4-22.
leaves.see: A4-22 Science Fiction Horror; A4-32 New French Extremity
leaves.axis: by what happens to the body: Cronenbergian mutation, metamorphosis, surgery and beauty, infection and parasites

leaves.label: Lovecraftian Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film of cosmic dread before entities or realities beyond human comprehension (In the Mouth of Madness, Color Out of Space, The Void, The Mist).
leaves.see: A4-22 Science Fiction Horror; A4-5 Satanic Film

leaves.label: Psychological Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose terror lies in the mind: breakdown, grief, trauma, unreal worlds or obsession, with any monster kept ambiguous (Repulsion, Jacob's Ladder, The Babadook, Black Swan). Doubles and split selves go to Doppelgänger Film; horror as social allegory to Social Thriller; a killer stalking victims to A4-28 Slasher Film.
leaves.see: A3 Thriller & Mystery; A4-26 Psycho-Biddy; A4-28 Slasher Film
leaves.axis: by where the horror sits: the unravelling mind, grief and family, purgatory and unreality, obsession and art, confinement

leaves.label: Doppelgänger Film
leaves.breadth: Horror of doubles, twins, alter egos and split selves
leaves.defn: A psychological horror film built on the double: an evil twin, a look-alike, a split personality or an alter ego that takes over (The Other, Dead Ringers, Santa Sangre, Split, Us, Goodnight Mommy).
leaves.aliases: double film; evil-twin film; doppelganger horror
leaves.axis: by the kind of double: twins and mirror doubles, split personalities and alter egos, then digital and media doubles

leaves.label: Social Thriller
leaves.breadth: Horror as social allegory of race, gender and class
leaves.defn: A horror film that makes a social structure the monster — racism, patriarchy, class or the codes of politeness — in the manner Jordan Peele named with Get Out (Get Out, Antebellum, Master, Nanny, Speak No Evil, The Killing of a Sacred Deer).
leaves.axis: by the structure made monstrous: race and its legacy, gender and the body, then class, conformity and social ritual

leaves.label: Psycho-Biddy
leaves.defn: A horror-thriller cycle built on an ageing woman as a deranged menace (What Ever Happened to Baby Jane?, Hush...Hush, Sweet Charlotte, Strait-Jacket).

leaves.label: Home Invasion Film
leaves.defn: A horror or thriller film whose engine is intruders breaking into a home and besieging those inside (Funny Games, The Strangers, You're Next, Don't Breathe).
leaves.see: A3 Thriller & Mystery; A5-18 Dystopian Film
leaves.axis: by who holds the house: siege thrillers, masked strangers, then reverse invasions where the home is the trap

leaves.label: Slasher Film
leaves.defn: A horror film in which a stalking killer murders a group of victims one by one, often till a final girl remains, in the classic cycle from the proto-slashers to the mid-1990s (Black Christmas, Halloween, Friday the 13th, A Nightmare on Elm Street). Slashers after Scream (1996) go to Neo-Slasher; rural killer clans to A4-29; holiday-themed killers to A4-30.
leaves.see: A4-29 Backwoods Horror; A4-30 Holiday Horror; A3 Thriller & Mystery
leaves.axis: by phase of the classic form: proto-slashers, the big franchises, the golden age, supernatural killers

leaves.label: Neo-Slasher
leaves.breadth: Slasher films after Scream: revival, meta, retro and parody slashers
leaves.defn: A slasher film of the cycle that Scream (1996) relaunched: self-aware teen slashers, horror-comedy and time-loop slashers, retro and new-wave throwbacks, and public-domain parody slashers (Scream, I Know What You Did Last Summer, Happy Death Day, X, Winnie-the-Pooh: Blood and Honey). Pre-1996 slashers stay in Slasher Film.
leaves.axis: by phase: the post-Scream revival, comic, meta and time-loop slashers, retro and new-wave slashers, public-domain parodies

leaves.label: Backwoods Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film in which travellers stray into the countryside and are hunted by rural killers or inbred clans (The Texas Chain Saw Massacre, The Hills Have Eyes, Wrong Turn, Wolf Creek). Pagan rural communities go to A4-8 Folk Horror.
leaves.see: A4-28 Slasher Film; A4-8 Folk Horror
leaves.axis: by the killers: the Leatherface cycle, cannibal and mutant clans, lone predators of tourists, swamp and forest stalkers

leaves.label: Holiday Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film whose killer or curse is built around a named holiday and its rituals (Silent Night, Deadly Night, My Bloody Valentine, Krampus, Trick 'r Treat). The Halloween franchise stays in A4-28.
leaves.see: A4-28 Slasher Film; A4-36 Anthology Horror
leaves.axis: by holiday: Christmas, then other holidays and Halloween night

leaves.label: Splatter Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose primary attraction is graphic gore and the spectacle of the opened body (Blood Feast, Guinea Pig 2: Flower of Flesh and Blood, Nekromantik, Ichi the Killer). Prolonged captivity and torture go to A4-33.

leaves.label: New French Extremity
leaves.defn: The French-language extreme horror cycle of the 2000s, transgressive in violence and sexuality (High Tension, Inside, Martyrs, Frontier(s)).

leaves.label: Torture Porn
leaves.defn: A horror film whose engine is captivity and the prolonged torture of victims (Saw, Hostel, The Collector, Would You Rather).
leaves.see: A4-31 Splatter Film; A4-25 Psychological Horror

leaves.label: Cannibal Film
leaves.defn: A horror film whose threat is people who eat people, including the Italian jungle cycle (Cannibal Holocaust, Cannibal Ferox, Raw, Ravenous). Rural killer families go to A4-29.
leaves.see: A4-29 Backwoods Horror; A4-31 Splatter Film

leaves.label: Found-Footage Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film presented as recovered recordings made by the characters (The Blair Witch Project, REC, Paranormal Activity, Lake Mungo). Sources are the form; the threat may be any.
leaves.see: A4-1 Ghost Film; A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde
leaves.axis: by the camera that records it: lost tapes, investigation crews, home video, faux broadcasts and mock documentaries, screens and livestreams, anthologies

leaves.label: Anthology Horror
leaves.defn: A horror film made of separate stories, usually joined by a frame (Dead of Night, The House That Dripped Blood, Creepshow 2, Southbound). Found-footage anthologies stay in A4-35.
leaves.see: A4-35 Found-Footage Horror; A4-30 Holiday Horror

leaves.label: Splatstick
leaves.defn: A horror comedy whose humour is excessive gore staged as slapstick (Evil Dead II, Bad Taste, Re-Animator, Deathgasm). Zombie splatstick such as Braindead stays in A4-18.
leaves.see: A4-38 Comedy Horror; A4-31 Splatter Film; A4-18 Zombie Film

leaves.label: Comedy Horror
leaves.defn: A film in which horror's monsters, killers or hauntings drive a comic engine (Ghostbusters, Beetlejuice, Stree, The Cabin in the Woods, Ready or Not). Gore-as-slapstick goes to A4-37; pure parody of horror films to A12.
leaves.axis: by the comic engine: monster-rally spoof, supernatural comedy, Asian horror-comedy, creature comedy, camp and cult, dark satire, meta-horror

leaves.label: Fantaterror
leaves.defn: The Spanish horror boom of c. 1968–1980 — Paul Naschy's Waldemar Daninsky werewolf films, Amando de Ossorio's Blind Dead, Narciso Ibáñez Serrador, Vicente Aranda, León Klimovsky — mixing gothic monsters, Templar ghouls and late-Franco-era sexual and Catholic dread (Tombs of the Blind Dead, The House That Screamed).
secs: Amando de Ossorio & the Blind Dead
leaves.axis: auteur / series

leaves.label: Ramsay Brothers Horror
leaves.defn: The Hindi low-budget horror cycle of the Ramsay family (1972–1990s): haunted havelis, cursed temples, monster-men and songs, the B-movie strand of Bollywood horror (Purana Mandir, Veerana).

subs.label: Science Fiction
subs.axis: Axis: by the speculative premise: space, aliens, giant monsters, time and other realities, machines and biology, societies of the future and their ending, then soft and comic science fiction last.

leaves.label: Hard Science Fiction
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose drama rests on plausible physics, biology and engineering, usually in spaceflight (2001: A Space Odyssey, The Martian, Interstellar, The Andromeda Strain). Space adventure with empires and aliens goes to A5-2.
leaves.see: A5-2 Space Opera; A5-5 First Contact
leaves.axis: by distance from Earth: orbit, Moon and laboratory; Mars; deep-space voyages

leaves.label: Space Opera
leaves.defn: A science fiction adventure of interstellar empires, wars and heroes on a grand scale (Star Wars, Star Trek II: The Wrath of Khan, Dune, Avatar). Plausible spaceflight goes to A5-1.
leaves.see: A5-1 Hard Science Fiction; A5-3 Military Science Fiction
leaves.axis: by mode: the Star Wars and Star Trek sagas, planetary romance, space westerns, family space adventure

leaves.label: Military Science Fiction
leaves.defn: A science fiction film centred on soldiers, armies and future warfare (Starship Troopers, Battle Los Angeles, Universal Soldier, Ender's Game).
leaves.see: A5-4 Alien Invasion; A9 War Film

leaves.label: Alien Invasion
leaves.defn: A science fiction film in which extraterrestrials attack or occupy Earth (The War of the Worlds, Independence Day, They Live, Attack the Block). Peaceful contact goes to A5-5; alien horror to A4-22.
leaves.see: A5-5 First Contact & Alien Visitor; A4-22 Science Fiction Horror; A5-3 Military Science Fiction

leaves.label: First Contact & Alien Visitor
leaves.defn: A science fiction film about humanity meeting extraterrestrials who are not simply invaders: messages, visitors, friends and abductors (Arrival, E.T. the Extra-Terrestrial, Starman, Fire in the Sky).
leaves.see: A5-4 Alien Invasion; A17 Children's & Family Film
leaves.axis: by the encounter: first contact, the visitor among us, the alien friend, abduction and UFO encounters

leaves.label: Kaiju
leaves.defn: A film of giant monsters that rampage through cities or fight each other, from Toho's Godzilla to its imitators (Godzilla, Gamera, King Kong, The Host). Ordinary-sized monsters go to A4-19.
leaves.axis: era of the Japanese kaiju eiga (Shōwa / Heisei / Millennium / Reiwa) and tradition outside Japan

leaves.label: Tokusatsu
leaves.defn: A live-action special-effects superhero film in the Japanese tradition of costumed transforming heroes, including adaptations (Shin Ultraman, Shin Kamen Rider, Mighty Morphin Power Rangers: The Movie).
secs: Henshin Heroes (Ultra, Rider, Sentai & Power Rangers)
leaves.axis: production tradition

leaves.label: Time Travel Film
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose premise is movement through time or a broken flow of time (Back to the Future, 12 Monkeys, Primer, Edge of Tomorrow).
leaves.see: A5-12 Artificial Intelligence & Robots; A5-9 Parallel Universe Film
leaves.axis: by what time travel does: tourism in time, changing the past, the loop, comic culture clash, messages across time

leaves.label: Parallel Universe Film
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose premise is alternate worlds or versions of reality existing side by side (Another Earth, Coherence, Mr. Nobody, The One).
leaves.see: A5-8 Time Travel Film; A5-10 Simulated Reality

leaves.label: Simulated Reality
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose premise is a manufactured reality: virtual worlds, game spaces, dream and memory technology (Inception, Total Recall, eXistenZ, Ready Player One). The Matrix films stay in A5-11 Cyberpunk.
leaves.see: A5-11 Cyberpunk; A5-9 Parallel Universe Film

leaves.label: Cyberpunk
leaves.defn: A science fiction film of high-tech, low-life futures: corporations, cyborgs, hackers and networked cities (Blade Runner, The Matrix, RoboCop, Tetsuo II: Body Hammer).
leaves.see: A5-10 Simulated Reality; A5-12 Artificial Intelligence & Robots; C2 Mecha & Science Fiction Anime

leaves.label: Artificial Intelligence & Robots
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose premise is thinking machines: rogue computers, androids, robot companions and giant robots (The Terminator, Ex Machina, Short Circuit, Transformers). A killer AI as horror goes to A4-22.
leaves.see: A5-11 Cyberpunk; A4-22 Science Fiction Horror
leaves.axis: by the machine's role: uprising and war, synthetic person, companion, giant robot, uploaded mind

leaves.label: Biopunk
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose premise is biotechnology: cloning, genetic engineering and chemical enhancement of humans and animals (The Boys from Brazil, Okja, Limitless, Mickey 17). Lab monsters as horror go to A4-22.
leaves.see: A4-22 Science Fiction Horror; A5-18 Dystopian Film

leaves.label: Scientific Romance
leaves.defn: A Verne- and Wells-type science adventure of submarines, inventions and fabulous journeys, and its retro-futurist pastiches (20,000 Leagues Under the Sea, Things to Come, Invention for Destruction).
leaves.see: A6-21 Lost World; A6 Fantasy & Adventure

leaves.label: Size-Change Film
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose premise is people shrunk or enlarged (The Incredible Shrinking Man, Fantastic Voyage, Honey, I Shrunk the Kids, Downsizing).
leaves.see: A5-22 Science Fiction Comedy; A17 Children's & Family Film

leaves.label: Psionics
leaves.defn: A science fiction or horror film whose premise is psychic powers such as telekinesis, telepathy or teleportation (Scanners, Carrie, Jumper, Midnight Special).
leaves.see: A4-25 Psychological Horror; A7 Action & Martial Arts

leaves.label: Dystopian Film
leaves.defn: A science fiction film set in a future society organised as oppression (1984, Brazil, The Hunger Games: Mockingjay, Snowpiercer). A world after collapse goes to A5-19.
leaves.axis: by the mechanism of control: the state, the lethal game, the YA system, control of age and birth, the class enclosure, the lawless city, absurdist satire

leaves.label: Post-Apocalyptic Film
leaves.defn: A science fiction film set during or after the collapse of civilisation (Threads, Mad Max: Fury Road, The Road, Planet of the Apes). The catastrophe itself as spectacle goes to A5-20.
leaves.see: A5-20 Disaster Film; A5-18 Dystopian Film; A4-18 Zombie Film
leaves.axis: by what ended the world and what follows: nuclear war, the wasteland, the last survivors, the apes, slow collapse, then comic and cult wastelands

leaves.label: Disaster Film
leaves.defn: A film whose spectacle is a large-scale catastrophe and the struggle to survive it (The Towering Inferno, Twister, Armageddon, Contagion). Life after the collapse goes to A5-19.
secs: Cosmic Impacts & End of the World
leaves.axis: by the catastrophe: earthquake, volcano and flood; cosmic impact; transport and structures; pandemic; storms and climate

leaves.label: Soft Science Fiction
leaves.defn: A science fiction film whose speculative conceit serves human, social or philosophical questions rather than technology or spectacle (Solaris, The Man from Earth, The Fountain, Hard to Be a God).
leaves.see: A5-1 Hard Science Fiction; A16 Drama
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Science Fiction Comedy
leaves.defn: A film whose comic engine is a science-fictional premise, often aliens among ordinary people (The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Kin-dza-dza!, Earth Girls Are Easy, Iron Sky).
leaves.see: A12 Comedy; A5-5 First Contact & Alien Visitor
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Afrofuturist Film
leaves.defn: Science fiction of the Afrofuturist movement (the term is Mark Dery's, 1993): Black diasporic and African speculative futures, cosmic myth and technoculture (Space Is the Place, The Brother from Another Planet, Neptune Frost).

subs.label: Fantasy & Adventure
subs.axis: Axis: by the source of the wonder or the quest: invented and magical worlds first, then myth and fairy tale, then the superhero franchises, then terrestrial adventure from the swashbuckler to the expedition.

leaves.label: High Fantasy
leaves.defn: A feature set wholly in an invented secondary world with its own peoples, history and magic, built around an epic quest or war (The Lord of the Rings: The Fellowship of the Ring, Willow, The Dark Crystal, Wicked). A pulp-barbarian hero of muscle and steel goes to A6-2; a child who crosses into the world from ours goes to A6-4.
leaves.see: A6-2 Sword and Sorcery; A6-4 Portal Fantasy

leaves.label: Sword and Sorcery
leaves.defn: A fantasy adventure of a lone warrior or mercenary band fighting sorcerers and monsters in a barbaric pre-modern world, with personal rather than world-saving stakes (Conan the Barbarian, The Beastmaster, Deathstalker, Red Sonja). An epic secondary-world war goes to A6-1.
leaves.see: A6-1 High Fantasy; A6-3 Arthurian Film
leaves.axis: era (the field dates the screen genre from the 1982 Conan boom)

leaves.label: Arthurian Film
leaves.defn: A film retelling the Matter of Britain: King Arthur, the Round Table, Camelot, the Grail or its knights, in any register from epic to parody (Excalibur, Perceval le Gallois, The Green Knight, Kaamelott: First Installment). Robin Hood and other outlaw legends go to A6-18.
leaves.see: A6-1 High Fantasy; A6-18 Swashbuckler; A8 Historical & Period Film

leaves.label: Portal Fantasy
leaves.defn: A fantasy in which a protagonist from our world crosses through a door, book, dream, game or screen into another realm and must find the way back (The Wizard of Oz, Labyrinth, The Chronicles of Narnia: The Lion, the Witch and the Wardrobe, Pleasantville). A film set wholly in the other world goes to A6-1.
leaves.see: A6-1 High Fantasy; A17-1 Children's Fantasy Film
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Dark Fantasy
leaves.defn: A fantasy whose wonders are menacing and whose tone is grim, cruel or uncanny, without being built to frighten in the manner of horror (Pan's Labyrinth, The City of Lost Children, Tideland, Border). A dark retelling of a named fairy tale goes to A6-12; a film built for fear goes to A4.

leaves.label: Contemporary Fantasy
leaves.defn: A fantasy in which a hidden society of wizards, demigods or magical beings exists alongside the modern world and a young hero is initiated into it, usually through a school or secret order (Harry Potter and the Sorcerer's Stone, Fantastic Beasts and Where to Find Them, Percy Jackson & the Olympians: The Lightning Thief, Miss Peregrine's Home for Peculiar Children). Adult supernatural action in a modern city goes to A6-7.
leaves.see: A6-7 Urban Fantasy; A17-1 Children's Fantasy Film

leaves.label: Urban Fantasy
leaves.defn: A fantasy action film in which vampires, immortals, demons, witches or sorcerers wage hidden wars in a present-day city (Night Watch, Highlander, Big Trouble in Little China, Bright). A youth-initiation story of a hidden wizarding school goes to A6-6; a film built to frighten goes to A4.
leaves.see: A6-6 Contemporary Fantasy; A4 Horror; B9 Speculative Series

leaves.label: Magical Realism
leaves.defn: A film that treats the marvellous as an unremarked part of an otherwise realistic world, or stages the afterlife and heavenly messengers with the same matter-of-factness (Dona Flor and Her Two Husbands, Big Fish, Wings of Desire, After Life). A comedy built on a magic gimmick goes to A12-28.
leaves.see: A12-28 Fantasy Comedy; A16 Drama; A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde
leaves.axis: by where the marvellous enters: the everyday world first, then the afterlife and angels

leaves.label: Mythological Fantasy
leaves.defn: A fantasy that dramatises a named mythology, epic, religious cosmology or folk legend, with gods, demigods, demons and heroes of that tradition (Jason and the Argonauts, Journey to the West: Conquering the Demons, Yeelen, The Seventh Seal). A fairy tale goes to A6-12; a historical epic without gods goes to A8.
leaves.see: A6-12 Fairy-Tale Film; A8 Historical & Period Film; A18-4 Pan-Indian Film
secs: Indian & East Asian Mythological Fantasy (shenmo, puranic)
leaves.axis: by mythic tradition: classical and peplum myth first, then Indian and East Asian myth, folk legend from elsewhere, and last heaven, hell and the devil

leaves.label: Fairy-Tale Film
leaves.defn: A film that adapts, retells or parodies a named fairy tale or literary tale (Grimm, Perrault, Andersen, Arabian Nights, Collodi) or invents one in its form (Beauty and the Beast 1946, The Singing Ringing Tree, Snow White and the Huntsman, The Princess Bride). A myth or epic goes to A6-11.
leaves.see: A6-11 Mythological Fantasy; A17-1 Children's Fantasy Film; C12 Animated Feature
leaves.axis: by treatment of the tale: European studio fairy-tale films first, then auteur and poetic versions, Hollywood live-action versions and remakes, revisionist and dark retellings, and last romances and parodies

leaves.label: Marvel Cinematic Universe
leaves.defn: A feature produced by Marvel Studios as part of its shared continuity of Marvel Comics heroes (Iron Man, The Avengers, Black Panther, Thunderbolts*). Marvel characters filmed by other studios outside that continuity go to A6-15.
leaves.see: A6-15 Marvel Comics Film outside the MCU; B9 Speculative Series
leaves.axis: by saga of the shared continuity: the Infinity Saga, then the Multiverse Saga

leaves.label: DC Comics Film
leaves.defn: A live-action feature adapting DC Comics characters, in any of the studio's successive continuities (Superman 1978, Batman 1989, The Dark Knight, Wonder Woman). Deconstructions such as Watchmen go to A6-17.
leaves.see: A6-13 Marvel Cinematic Universe; A6-17 Superhero Parody & Deconstruction
secs: Other DC Adaptations & the DC Universe
leaves.axis: by continuity: the Superman series, the Batman series, the DC Extended Universe, then other DC adaptations and the DC Universe

leaves.label: Marvel Comics Film outside the MCU
leaves.defn: A live-action feature adapting Marvel Comics characters made by a licensee studio outside the Marvel Studios continuity (X-Men, Spider-Man 2002, Blade, Venom). A Marvel Studios feature goes to A6-13.
leaves.aliases: Fox Marvel films; Sony's Spider-Man Universe
leaves.axis: by licensed franchise: X-Men, Spider-Man and its Sony spin-offs, then other licensed Marvel films

leaves.label: Standalone Superhero Film
leaves.defn: A superhero film outside the Marvel and DC franchises: a pulp or comic-strip avenger, an independent-comics or manga hero, a hero created for the screen, or a national industry's own superhero (The Rocketeer, Hellboy, Darkman, Krrish). Parody and deconstruction go to A6-17.
leaves.see: A6-17 Superhero Parody & Deconstruction; A5 Science Fiction
leaves.axis: by the hero's origin: pulp and comic-strip heroes first, then independent-comics and manga adaptations, screen-original heroes, children's superhero comedies, and superhero cinema outside Hollywood

leaves.label: Superhero Parody & Deconstruction
leaves.defn: A film that mocks the superhero form or takes its premise apart: what powers, costumes and vigilantism would really mean (Watchmen, Kick-Ass, Unbreakable, Mystery Men). A straight franchise entry with jokes goes to its franchise leaf.
leaves.see: A6-14 DC Comics Film; A6-16 Standalone Superhero Film; A12 Comedy

leaves.label: Swashbuckler
leaves.defn: A costume adventure of sword-fighting heroes, outlaws and avengers in a pre-modern Europe or its colonies, built on duels, rescues and daring escapes (The Adventures of Robin Hood, The Mark of Zorro, The Three Musketeers 1973, Scaramouche). Sea-rovers go to A6-19.
leaves.aliases: cape-and-sword film; cloak and sword; film de cape et d'épée
leaves.see: A6-19 Pirate Film; A8 Historical & Period Film
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Pirate Film
leaves.defn: An adventure of pirates, buccaneers or smugglers at sea or on their islands, often with buried treasure (Captain Blood, Treasure Island 1950, Cutthroat Island, Pirates of the Caribbean: The Curse of the Black Pearl). Land-bound duellists go to A6-18.

leaves.label: Treasure-Hunt Adventure
leaves.defn: A pulp adventure in which an archaeologist, prospector or rogue follows clues, maps and traps to a lost artefact or hoard (Raiders of the Lost Ark, Romancing the Stone, National Treasure, The Mummy 1999). A whole hidden world of survivals goes to A6-21; a video-game hero such as Lara Croft goes to A7-16.
leaves.see: A6-21 Lost World; A6-22 Jungle Adventure; A7-16 Video Game Adaptation

leaves.label: Lost World
leaves.defn: An adventure in which explorers find a hidden land where prehistoric creatures, vanished peoples or a utopia survive (Journey to the Center of the Earth 1959, Lost Horizon, Congo, Baby: Secret of the Lost Legend). An artefact hunt goes to A6-20.
leaves.see: A6-20 Treasure-Hunt Adventure; A5 Science Fiction

leaves.label: Jungle Adventure
leaves.defn: An adventure set in jungle, savannah or colonial frontier, built on the hero's survival among wild animals, rivers and peoples, including Tarzan, Mowgli and the imperial adventure of the British Empire film (Tarzan and His Mate, Gunga Din, The African Queen, Jungle Cruise). A hunt for a single artefact goes to A6-20.
leaves.aliases: jungle film; safari film; imperial adventure film; Empire film
leaves.see: A6-20 Treasure-Hunt Adventure; A6-21 Lost World
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Nautical Adventure
leaves.defn: An adventure at sea or on a desert island in which the ocean, a whale, a raft or a wreck is the antagonist, including the Robinsonade (Moby Dick, Kon-Tiki, Life of Pi, Swiss Family Robinson). Pirates go to A6-19; naval combat goes to A9.
leaves.see: A6-19 Pirate Film; A9 War Film

leaves.label: Prehistoric Fiction
leaves.defn: An adventure set among early humans in the Stone Age, built on the struggle for fire, food and survival (Quest for Fire, 10,000 BC, Alpha).
leaves.see: A6-21 Lost World; A6-11 Mythological Fantasy

leaves.label: Expedition Adventure
leaves.defn: An adventure of a journey or expedition against distance and nature, by balloon, plane, horse or on foot, in the tradition of the voyages extraordinaires (Around the World in 80 Days 1956, The Aeronauts, Hidalgo, Letter Never Sent). A voyage at sea goes to A6-23.

leaves.label: Bergfilm (Mountain Film)
leaves.defn: The German mountain film of the 1920s–30s (Arnold Fanck, Leni Riefenstahl, Luis Trenker): real Alpine climbing and skiing photographed on location, elemental storms and avalanches, romantic rivalry and heroic summits (The Holy Mountain, The White Hell of Pitz Palu, The Blue Light).

subs.label: Action & Martial Arts
subs.axis: Axis: by the action engine: Hollywood action scenarios first, then the gun and assassin cycles, then the martial-arts traditions (Hong Kong and Chinese first), then the buddy cop, adaptation and exploitation hybrids.

leaves.label: Action-Hero Film
leaves.defn: An action film built around a single indestructible hero who takes on an army, a gang or a town alone, from silent stunt serials to the muscle cinema of the 1980s and its ensemble revivals (Commando, Rambo: First Blood Part II, Road House, The Expendables). A hero trapped in one besieged place goes to A7-2; a revenge mission goes to A7-3.
leaves.see: A7-2 Die Hard Scenario; A7-3 Vigilante Film; A7-4 Military Action Film
leaves.axis: by the hero's situation: silent stunt and serial action, one-man army, fugitive and drifter heroes, then ensemble and legacy action

leaves.label: Die Hard Scenario
leaves.defn: An action thriller in which a lone hero is trapped in one sealed location (a tower, plane, ship, train, school or White House) taken by terrorists or criminals (Die Hard, Speed, Under Siege, Olympus Has Fallen). A hero who roams freely goes to A7-1; a pure hostage-negotiation thriller goes to A3.
leaves.aliases: Die Hard on a…; siege action
leaves.see: A7-1 Action-Hero Film; A3 Thriller & Mystery
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Vigilante Film
leaves.defn: An action film in which a wronged individual takes the law into their own hands to punish criminals or rescue a kidnapped relative (Taken, The Equalizer, Nobody, The Man from Nowhere). A professional killer for hire goes to A2-5.
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Military Action Film
leaves.defn: An action film of special forces, commandos, fighter pilots or tactical units on missions, rescues and counter-terror strikes outside a declared war narrative (Missing in Action, Top Gun, Extraction, Kandahar). A film about a historical war goes to A9.
leaves.see: A9 War Film; A7-1 Action-Hero Film

leaves.label: Car Chase Film
leaves.defn: An action film whose set pieces are vehicle chases, street races, getaways and stunt driving (The Fast and the Furious, The Transporter, Wheelman, Premium Rush). A heist plot without the driving goes to A2.

leaves.label: Girls with Guns
leaves.defn: An action film whose fighting hero is a woman or girl (assassin, cop, avenger or princess), the cycle named in Hong Kong and global since (Yes, Madam!, La Femme Nikita, The Villainess, Kill Boksoon). A male professional killer goes to A2-5.
leaves.see: A2-5 Hitman Film; A7-10 Hong Kong Action Cinema

leaves.label: Gun Fu
leaves.defn: An action film whose gunfights are choreographed like martial arts: close-quarter shooting, acrobatics and a fight ballet (John Wick, Desperado, Shoot 'Em Up, Crank). The Hong Kong source tradition goes to A7-9.
leaves.see: A7-9 Heroic Bloodshed; A2-5 Hitman Film

leaves.label: Heroic Bloodshed
leaves.defn: The Hong Kong gangster-action cycle of brotherhood, loyalty and operatic gunplay launched by John Woo, and its direct successors (A Better Tomorrow, The Killer, Hard Boiled, Exiled). Its stylised global offspring go to A7-8.
leaves.see: A7-8 Gun Fu; A7-10 Hong Kong Action Cinema

leaves.label: Hong Kong Action Cinema
leaves.defn: A modern-dress Hong Kong action film of stunt-driven police, adventure and crime set pieces (Police Story, Project A, Wheels on Meals, Twilight of the Warriors: Walled In). Period kung fu goes to A7-11; swordplay to A7-12; gangster gunplay to A7-9.
leaves.see: A7-9 Heroic Bloodshed; A7-11 Kung Fu Film

leaves.label: Kung Fu Film
leaves.defn: A martial arts film of Chinese unarmed and weapon styles, usually set in the late imperial or Republican past, built on training, schools and revenge (Enter the Dragon, The 36th Chamber of Shaolin, Drunken Master, Ip Man). Swordsmen of the jianghu go to A7-12.
leaves.see: A7-12 Wuxia; A7-10 Hong Kong Action Cinema
secs: Folk-Hero Kung Fu (Wong Fei-hung, Ip Man)
leaves.axis: by cycle: Bruce Lee films, Shaw Brothers and Shaolin films, kung fu comedy, then folk-hero kung fu (Wong Fei-hung, Huo Yuanjia, Ip Man)

leaves.label: Wuxia
leaves.defn: A Chinese martial-chivalry film of wandering swordsmen and swordswomen in the jianghu underworld, with lightness-skill and codes of honour (Come Drink with Me, A Touch of Zen, Crouching Tiger, Hidden Dragon, Hero). Hand-to-hand kung fu goes to A7-11.
leaves.see: A7-11 Kung Fu Film; B4 Chinese-Language Drama
secs: New-School Wuxia (1966–1984: King Hu, Chang Cheh, Chu Yuan)
leaves.axis: era / school of the wuxia film

leaves.label: Martial Arts Film
leaves.defn: A martial arts film of Japanese, Korean, Southeast Asian or Western fighting styles (judo, karate, kickboxing, muay thai, silat) built on training, tournaments and hand-to-hand set pieces (The Karate Kid, Bloodsport, Ong-Bak: The Thai Warrior, The Raid: Redemption). Chinese kung fu goes to A7-11; ninjas to A7-14.
leaves.see: A7-11 Kung Fu Film; A7-14 Ninja Film
leaves.axis: by fighting tradition: Japanese budō, the karate-dojo film, tournament and fight-circuit films, martial-arts star vehicles, Thai, Indonesian, then other Asian martial arts cinema

leaves.label: Ninja Film
leaves.defn: A martial arts film whose fighters are ninja, from the 1980s ninja boom to its revivals (Ninja III: The Domination, American Ninja, Ninja Assassin, Snake Eyes).
leaves.axis: national tradition / production cycle

leaves.label: Buddy Cop Film
leaves.defn: An action film or action comedy built on two mismatched police partners (or a cop and an unlikely partner) forced to work a case together (48 Hrs., Lethal Weapon, Rush Hour, Hot Fuzz). A comedy without police work goes to A12.
leaves.axis: by register: straight mismatched-partner action, comedy and spoof, then buddy-cop films beyond Hollywood

leaves.label: Video Game Adaptation
leaves.defn: A live-action feature adapted from a video game franchise, whatever its genre (Mortal Kombat, Lara Croft: Tomb Raider, Warcraft, A Minecraft Movie). A film merely set inside a game goes to its genre.
leaves.see: A6-1 High Fantasy; A6-20 Treasure-Hunt Adventure; A17 Children's & Family Film

leaves.label: Exploitation Action Film
leaves.defn: A low-budget action film sold on excess (gore, nudity, absurd stunts), from grindhouse and direct-to-video cult items to deliberate grindhouse homages (Samurai Cop, Hard Ticket to Hawaii, Riki-Oh: The Story of Ricky, Hobo with a Shotgun).

leaves.label: Lucha Film
leaves.defn: The Mexican luchador film (1952–1980s): masked professional wrestlers — El Santo, Blue Demon, Mil Máscaras, the Wrestling Women — fighting vampires, mummies, mad scientists and Martians in action-horror-science-fiction serials (Santo vs. the Vampire Women).

subs.label: Historical & Period Film
subs.axis: Axis: by the representational mode of the past: epic spectacle by era first, then national period traditions, literary costume film, and last the reconstruction of real political, social and documented events.

leaves.label: Historical Epic
leaves.defn: A large-scale, long-form spectacle that sweeps a nation, dynasty or family through decades of real history, with the historical upheaval itself as the subject (Intolerance, Gone with the Wind, 1900, Ponniyin Selvan: Part I). Ancient Mediterranean spectacles go to A8-2; epics built around a battle campaign go to A9-1.
leaves.see: A8-2 Sword-and-Sandal Film; A9-1 War Epic
leaves.axis: by setting, foundation sagas first, ancient and pre-contact worlds last

leaves.label: Sword-and-Sandal Film
leaves.defn: A spectacle set in Greco-Roman or biblical antiquity, built on gladiators, legions, mythic heroes or Old Testament stories (Ben-Hur, Spartacus, The Ten Commandments, 300). Lives of Jesus and the saints go to A11-4 Religious Biopic.
leaves.see: A11-4 Religious Biopic; A6 Fantasy & Adventure
secs: Hollywood & British Epics of the Studio and Widescreen Era (1932–1966)
leaves.axis: era / national production tradition

leaves.label: Medieval Film
leaves.defn: A film set in the European or Near Eastern Middle Ages whose world of knights, sagas, crusades and feudal law is the subject rather than a single battle campaign (The Northman, The Last Duel, Flesh+Blood, Arn: The Knight Templar). Battle-centred medieval epics go to A9-1.
leaves.see: A9-1 War Epic; A6 Fantasy & Adventure

leaves.label: Royal Court Drama
leaves.defn: A period drama of intrigue inside a royal or imperial court, where succession, favour and palace politics drive the story and no single royal life is traced (The Lion in Winter, Queen Margot, Curse of the Golden Flower, The King's Warden). A film tracing a monarch's life goes to A11-1 Royal Biopic.
leaves.see: A11-1 Royal Biopic; B4 Chinese-Language Drama

leaves.label: Jidaigeki
leaves.defn: A Japanese period drama set before the Meiji Restoration in which manners, clan duty and social hierarchy, not sword combat, carry the story (Sansho the Bailiff, Rashomon, Ran, The Twilight Samurai). A film driven by swordplay goes to A8-6 Chanbara.
leaves.axis: era

leaves.label: Chanbara
leaves.defn: A Japanese swordplay film in which sword combat by samurai or ronin is the engine of the drama (Yojimbo, Seven Samurai, The Tale of Zatoichi, 13 Assassins). Swordless period dramas go to A8-5 Jidaigeki.
leaves.see: A8-5 Jidaigeki; A7 Action & Martial Arts
secs: Lone Wolf and Cub & Revenge Manga Films
leaves.axis: by series and era: classic ronin films, the Zatoichi series, the Lone Wolf and Cub revenge cycle, modern revival

leaves.label: Colonial & Slavery Film
leaves.defn: A period film whose subject is chattel slavery or colonial rule and resistance to it, told from the plantation, the mission or the colony (Burn!, The Last Supper, 12 Years a Slave, The Camp at Thiaroye). Battle-centred colonial wars go to A9-1.
leaves.see: A9-1 War Epic; Movements & Schools (Third Cinema)
leaves.axis: by system: slavery and abolition first, colonial rule and revolt second

leaves.label: Heritage Film
leaves.defn: A British (or British-set) period film of gentility, country houses and pre-war manners, usually from a classic English novel, valued for its nostalgic re-creation of the national past (A Room with a View, Pride & Prejudice, Howards End, Downton Abbey). Continental and American literary costume films go to A8-9.
leaves.axis: by literary period: Austen first, then Georgian and Victorian novels, Edwardian, and the interwar country house

leaves.label: Costume Drama
leaves.defn: A period drama, usually adapted from a classic novel or play, whose dress, manners and social codes of a past society are the dramatic material (Les Misérables, The Leopard, Anna Karenina, Portrait of a Lady on Fire). British gentility films go to A8-8 Heritage Film.
leaves.axis: by literary tradition of the source, original screenplays and twentieth-century pieces last

leaves.label: Shakespeare Film
leaves.defn: A screen adaptation of a Shakespeare play, in period or transposed dress, with the play's text and structure carrying it (Hamlet, Chimes at Midnight, Henry V, The Tragedy of Macbeth). Free transpositions into another culture such as Throne of Blood stay with their tradition.

leaves.label: Historical Political Drama
leaves.defn: A period drama of private lives under a named political regime, where dictatorship, purge, occupation or revolution is the pressure that shapes the story (Mephisto, Burnt by the Sun, No, A Taxi Driver). Dramatised single events go to A8-13 Docudrama; lives of politicians go to A11-2.
leaves.axis: by regime: fascism first, Stalinism, Latin American juntas, other twentieth-century histories, earlier revolutions last

leaves.label: Historical Social Problem Film
leaves.defn: A period drama that dramatises a social injustice of its era, such as labour, emigration, women's rights, race, sexuality or persecution, through fictional representative lives (Germinal, Vera Drake, The Help, The Crucible). Real activists' lives go to A11-2.
leaves.axis: by the social question: labour first, then emigration, women, race, queer history, religious persecution last

leaves.label: Docudrama
leaves.defn: A dramatised reconstruction of one documented real event, crisis or case, where the event rather than a person's life is the subject (A Night to Remember, Apollo 13, United 93, The Post). A film tracing a person's life goes to A11.
leaves.aliases: based on a true story, drama-documentary
leaves.axis: by the kind of event: disasters and expeditions, political crises, massacres and terror, legal cases, journalism, humanitarian crises

leaves.label: Sageuk Film
leaves.defn: The Korean historical film (sageuk), set chiefly in the Goryeo and Joseon courts and countryside: palace intrigue, royal doubles, scholars, painters and kisaeng (The King and the Clown, Masquerade, Untold Scandal).

subs.label: War Film
subs.axis: Axis: by war in chronological order (pre-modern battles to the War on Terror), then by mode (aftermath, anti-war).

leaves.label: War Epic
leaves.defn: A large-scale battle spectacle of a pre-twentieth-century war or an early-twentieth-century revolution, with the campaign as the narrative spine (Alexander Nevsky, Braveheart, Zulu, Glory). WWI and later go to their own leaves.
leaves.see: A8-1 Historical Epic; A8-3 Medieval Film
secs: Revolutions & Civil Wars of the Early 20th Century
leaves.axis: by era: ancient and medieval, early modern and colonial, American wars, twentieth-century revolutions and civil wars

leaves.label: World War I Film
leaves.defn: A film of the First World War, its trenches, air war and immediate aftermath (All Quiet on the Western Front, Paths of Glory, Gallipoli, 1917).
leaves.see: A9-14 Anti-War Film; A9-13 Returning Veteran Film
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: World War II Combat Film
leaves.defn: A combat film of the Second World War in Europe and the Mediterranean, centred on soldiers, aircrews or sailors in action (Saving Private Ryan, Das Boot, The Guns of Navarone, Come and See is A9-5). Pacific theatre goes to A9-4.
leaves.see: A9-4 Pacific War Film; A9-5 Partisan & Resistance Film
leaves.axis: by front and mode: Western Front, air and sea, commando missions, Eastern Front, Nordic fronts

leaves.label: Pacific War Film
leaves.defn: A film of the Pacific and Asian theatres of the Second World War, including the Second Sino-Japanese War (The Burmese Harp, The Human Condition, Letters from Iwo Jima, The Thin Red Line). POW camps go to A9-7.
leaves.see: A9-7 Prisoner-of-War Film; A9-9 Atomic Bomb Film
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Partisan & Resistance Film
leaves.defn: A film of irregular fighters and resistance networks against occupation in the Second World War, with the Yugoslav partisan film as its named canon (The Battle of Neretva, Walter Defends Sarajevo, The Ascent, Army of Shadows). Old leaf Partisan Film merged here with resistance films.
leaves.see: A9-3 World War II Combat Film; A9-6 Holocaust Film
leaves.axis: by region: the Yugoslav cycle first, Soviet and East European partisans, Western European resistance

leaves.label: Holocaust Film
leaves.defn: A fiction film of the Nazi persecution and murder of European Jews: camps, ghettos, deportations, hiding and the reckoning afterwards (Schindler's List, The Pianist, Son of Saul, The Zone of Interest).
leaves.see: A9-5 Partisan & Resistance Film; A19 Documentary
leaves.axis: by the site of persecution: camps, ghettos and round-ups, hiding and rescue, perpetrators and aftermath

leaves.label: Prisoner-of-War Film
leaves.defn: A war film set among captured soldiers in a POW camp, built on survival, collaboration or escape (Stalag 17, The Great Escape, The Bridge on the River Kwai, Rescue Dawn).
leaves.see: A9-3 World War II Combat Film; A2 Crime (prison film)

leaves.label: Home Front Film
leaves.defn: A war film centred on civilians, families and children living through a war away from or overrun by the front (Mrs. Miniver, Forbidden Games, Two Women, Empire of the Sun).
leaves.see: A9-13 Returning Veteran Film; A16 Drama
leaves.axis: by war and viewpoint: world-war home fronts, children in war, civilians in later wars

leaves.label: Atomic Bomb Film
leaves.defn: A Japanese film of the atomic bombings and the hibakusha who survived them (Black Rain).

leaves.label: Vietnam War Film
leaves.defn: A film of the Vietnam War, American or Vietnamese, in combat or in its training camps (Platoon, Full Metal Jacket, Wild Field, Da 5 Bloods). Veterans' homecoming goes to A9-13.
leaves.see: A9-13 Returning Veteran Film; A9-14 Anti-War Film

leaves.label: Modern War Film
leaves.defn: A film of a post-1945 war other than Vietnam and the War on Terror: Korea, decolonisation, the Balkans, the Middle East, insurgencies and Ukraine (Tae Guk Gi, No Man's Land, Lebanon, Beasts of No Nation).
leaves.see: A9-12 War on Terror Film; A9-10 Vietnam War Film
leaves.axis: by conflict, roughly chronological: Korea and the Cold War, African wars, Balkans and Caucasus, Middle East, insurgencies, Ukraine, Afghanistan and South Asia

leaves.label: War on Terror Film
leaves.defn: A film of the Gulf, Iraq and Afghanistan wars and counter-terror operations after 1990, often built on a single real mission (The Hurt Locker, Black Hawk Down, Jarhead, Warfare).
leaves.aliases: Iraq War film, Afghanistan War film
leaves.see: A9-11 Modern War Film; A3 Thriller & Mystery

leaves.label: Returning Veteran Film
leaves.defn: A film of a war's aftermath for those who fought or occupied: homecoming, trauma, mine-clearing and reckoning (The Best Years of Our Lives, Birdy, Land of Mine, Beanpole). Weakly attested label; the field also says homecoming film.
leaves.see: A9-8 Home Front Film; A16 Drama
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Anti-War Film
leaves.defn: A film whose primary mode is protest against war itself, by allegory or by satire, rather than depiction of one campaign (Johnny Got His Gun, Shame, Three Kings, Jojo Rabbit).
leaves.axis: by mode: allegory and protest, satire and comedy

subs.label: Western
subs.axis: Axis: by the western's historical cycle and its transpositions: silent and classical forms first, then revisionist and European cycles, transposed and contemporary westerns last.

leaves.label: Silent Western
leaves.defn: A western of the silent era, from William S. Hart to John Ford's first epics (Hell's Hinges, The Iron Horse, The Wind).

leaves.label: Classical Western
leaves.defn: A Hollywood sound western of the studio era and its later classical survivors, built on the frontier code of lawmen, cattlemen, cavalry and gunfighters (Stagecoach, The Searchers, Rio Bravo, Winchester '73). Westerns that interrogate the myth go to A10-6.
leaves.axis: by story type: cavalry and epic, lawman and town-tamer, range and homestead, psychological revenge, Mexico-border mercenaries

leaves.label: Singing Cowboy Western
leaves.defn: A B-western musical vehicle for a singing cowboy star (Under Western Stars, Melody Ranch).

leaves.label: Comedy Western
leaves.defn: A western played for comedy or parody of the frontier code (Go West, Destry Rides Again, Cat Ballou, Shanghai Noon).

leaves.label: Musical Western
leaves.defn: A stage or screen musical set on the frontier (Calamity Jane, Oklahoma!, Seven Brides for Seven Brothers).

leaves.label: Revisionist Western
leaves.defn: A western that questions the frontier myth, its violence, heroes, racial and gender order (The Wild Bunch, McCabe & Mrs. Miller, Unforgiven, Meek's Cutoff).
leaves.see: A10-2 Classical Western; A10-7 Acid Western
leaves.axis: by what is revised: the myth itself, the outlaw, race and Native America, frontier women and settlers

leaves.label: Acid Western
leaves.defn: A countercultural, hallucinatory western of the late 1960s and its descendants (The Shooting, El Topo, Dead Man).

leaves.label: Spaghetti Western
leaves.defn: An Italian-produced western of the 1960s–70s cycle, with its operatic violence and its Trinity comic offshoot (A Fistful of Dollars, Django, The Great Silence, They Call Me Trinity).
secs: Zapata Westerns (Sollima, Damiani & the political spaghetti)
leaves.axis: auteur and named sub-cycle

leaves.label: Ostern
leaves.defn: An Eastern Bloc western, East German Indianerfilm or Soviet "red western" (The Sons of Great Bear, Apaches, Nobody Wanted to Die).
leaves.axis: national production tradition

leaves.label: Meat Pie Western
leaves.defn: An Australian western of bushrangers and the outback frontier (The Story of the Kelly Gang, Ned Kelly, The Proposition).

leaves.label: Transnational Western
