leaves.defn: A western whose codes are transposed to another nation's landscape and history, from Manchuria to Patagonia (The Good, the Bad, the Weird, Marlina the Murderer in Four Acts, The Settlers, Bacurau). Italian and Eastern Bloc cycles have their own leaves. Weakly attested umbrella label.

leaves.label: Neo-Western
leaves.defn: A film set in the contemporary American West in which the western's codes of land, law and violence persist (Hud, No Country for Old Men, Hell or High Water, Wind River).

leaves.label: Karl May Western
leaves.defn: The West German (Rialto/CCC) cycle of 1962–1968 adapting Karl May's Winnetou and Old Shatterhand novels, shot in Yugoslavia: noble Apache chief, German blood-brother hero, Martin Böttcher scores (Treasure of Silver Lake, Apache Gold). It preceded and fed the Spaghetti Western boom.

subs.label: Biographical Film
subs.axis: Axis: by the field in which the subject is known: power (royals, politics, war, religion), discovery (exploration, science, business), the arts (visual, literary, music, show business), sport, crime, and private lives last.

leaves.label: Royal Biopic
leaves.defn: A film tracing the life or reign of a monarch, consort or royal favourite (The Private Life of Henry VIII, Sissi, The King's Speech, Spencer). Court intrigue without a single life goes to A8-4.
leaves.see: A8-4 Royal Court Drama; A11-2 Political Biopic
leaves.axis: by dynasty and region: England to the Stuarts, Britain from the Georgians, continental courts, Asian rulers

leaves.label: Political Biopic
leaves.defn: A film tracing the life or career of a statesman, revolutionary, activist or dissident (Gandhi, Malcolm X, Lincoln, Milk). A single political crisis goes to A8-13 Docudrama.
leaves.axis: by role: rulers and statesmen, revolutionaries, civil-rights activists, journalists and whistleblowers

leaves.label: Military Biopic
leaves.defn: A film tracing the life of a soldier, general or war hero, where the person rather than one battle is the subject (Sergeant York, Lawrence of Arabia, El Cid, Napoleon). Battle-centred true stories go to A9.

leaves.label: Religious Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of the life of Jesus, a prophet, saint, reformer or religious leader (The Gospel According to St. Matthew, The Passion of the Christ, Kundun, The Message). Old Testament spectacles go to A8-2.
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Explorer & Adventurer Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of an explorer, mountaineer or solitary adventurer, where the journey into the unknown is the life (Dersu Uzala, Into the Wild, The Lost City of Z, Tenzing).
leaves.see: A11-12 Sports Biopic; A6 Fantasy & Adventure

leaves.label: Science & Medicine Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of a scientist, physician, inventor or astronaut, built on the discovery and its cost (A Beautiful Mind, The Imitation Game, Oppenheimer, First Man).
leaves.axis: by field: science and mathematics, medicine, invention and engineering, space flight

leaves.label: Business Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of an entrepreneur, tycoon or company founding, built on the rise and the deal (The Social Network, The Aviator, The Founder, BlackBerry). Fraudsters go to A11-13.

leaves.label: Artist Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of a painter, sculptor, photographer, fashion designer or dancer, built around the making of the work (Rembrandt, Frida, Mr. Turner, Saint Laurent).
leaves.axis: by medium: painting, photography, fashion and dance

leaves.label: Writer Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of a novelist, poet, playwright or thinker, built around the writing and the life that fed it (Becoming Jane, Capote, Bright Star, Tolkien). Adaptations of a writer's own memoir of ordinary life go to A11-14.
leaves.see: A11-14 Autobiographical & Memoir Film; A11-8 Artist Biopic
leaves.axis: by literary era, children's authors last

leaves.label: Musical Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of a composer, singer, band or performer, with the music performed as part of the story (Amadeus, Ray, Walk the Line, Bohemian Rhapsody).
leaves.see: A14 Musical & Dance Film; A11-11 Show Business Biopic
leaves.axis: by musical tradition: classical, jazz and soul, rock and pop, country and folk, hip hop, chanson and world popular music

leaves.label: Show Business Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of a stage, film or television entertainer, filmmaker or impresario, built on the business of performing (Chaplin, Ed Wood, Judy, Man on the Moon).
leaves.axis: by stage: theatre and vaudeville, Hollywood, television and comedy, world film industries

leaves.label: Sports Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of an athlete, coach or team, built on a career rather than a single match (Ali, Foxcatcher, I, Tonya, The Iron Claw).
leaves.axis: by sport: combat sports, team sports, individual and endurance sports

leaves.label: Crime Biopic
leaves.defn: A film of a real gangster, outlaw, swindler, killer or militant, built on the criminal career (GoodFellas, Catch Me If You Can, Monster, Carlos).
leaves.axis: by kind of crime: organised crime, robbery and fraud, murder cases, political violence

leaves.label: Autobiographical & Memoir Film
leaves.defn: A film adapted from a memoir or tracing the true life of a private person, known for what they lived through rather than a public field (My Left Foot, Angela's Ashes, Girl, Interrupted, Lion). Weakly attested umbrella label.
leaves.axis: by the life experience: family and self-discovery, addiction and mental illness, illness and disability, trauma and survival, teachers, couples

subs.label: Comedy
subs.axis: Axis: by comic mode and engine (what makes the film funny): the clown and stage traditions first, then named national cycles, satire and dark modes, parody and performance forms, situational premises, youth and raunch comedy, crime and action hybrids, and comedy-drama by subject last.

leaves.label: Silent Clown Comedy
leaves.defn: A silent-era comedy (to c. 1930, plus Chaplin's late silents) built on the pantomime and stunt gags of a clown persona or on silent visual farce (The General, Safety Last!, The Kid, The Doll). A sound-era gag film in the same spirit goes to A12-3 Slapstick.
leaves.axis: by clown, the four great silent clowns first in order of their first feature; other clowns and comedies last

leaves.label: Comedian Comedy
leaves.defn: A film built as a vehicle for a solo comedian's established persona, where the performer's routines matter more than the plot (The Bank Dick, The Bellboy, The Gendarme of Saint-Tropez, Wayne's World, Billy Madison). Vehicles for double acts and troupes go to Comedy Team Film; if the film has a stronger premise engine (body swap, heist, parody) it goes there.
leaves.aliases: comedian vehicle; comedy team film; double act (Steve Seidman's 'comedian comedy')
leaves.see: A12-1 Silent Clown Comedy; A12-3 Slapstick; A12-23 Parody & Spoof
leaves.axis: by the kind of comic persona the film is built around: Hollywood star comedian, national comic persona, sketch character, man-child

leaves.label: Comedy Team Film
leaves.breadth: Vehicles for double acts and comedy troupes
leaves.defn: A comedian comedy built around a double act or comedy team whose established partnership is the attraction (Duck Soup, Sons of the Desert, Road to Morocco, Abbott and Costello Meet Dr. Jekyll and Mr. Hyde, Bujang Lapok, Watch Out, We're Mad). Solo comedians' vehicles stay in Comedian Comedy.
leaves.aliases: double act film; comedy duo film; comedy troupe film
leaves.axis: by era: the studio-era teams, the television-era and national duos of 1960–1989, then contemporary teams

leaves.label: Slapstick
leaves.defn: A sound-era comedy whose main engine is physical and visual gag work: pratfalls, chases, destruction and choreographed mishap (Playtime, The Return of the Pink Panther, It's a Mad, Mad, Mad, Mad World, Bean), including the stunt-prank films of the Jackass line. A silent film goes to A12-1 Silent Clown Comedy.
leaves.aliases: physical comedy; visual comedy; gag film; stunt-prank comedy
leaves.see: A12-1 Silent Clown Comedy; A12-2 Comedian Comedy

leaves.label: Screwball Comedy
leaves.defn: A fast, dialogue-driven comedy of the 1930s–40s Hollywood type (and its later pastiches) in which a madcap heroine or eccentric pair upends social decorum, often across class lines (Bringing Up Baby, My Man Godfrey, The Lady Eve, Mr. Deeds Goes to Town). A divorce-and-reunion plot goes to A12-5 Comedy of Remarriage; a modern romantic comedy to A13.
leaves.see: A12-5 Comedy of Remarriage; A13 Romance
leaves.axis: studio-era phase (the field dates the cycle 1934 to the early 1940s)

leaves.label: Comedy of Remarriage
leaves.defn: A screwball-era comedy whose plot is a married or divorced couple driven apart and brought back together (Stanley Cavell's canon: The Awful Truth, His Girl Friday, The Philadelphia Story, My Favorite Wife). Other screwball plots go to A12-4 Screwball Comedy.

leaves.label: Comedy of Manners
leaves.defn: A comedy whose engine is the conversation, codes and hypocrisies of a social milieu, from Wilde and Lubitsch high comedy to modern urban talk comedies (The Importance of Being Earnest, The Women, Metropolitan, Hannah and Her Sisters, Pauline at the Beach). A plot driven by door-slamming mechanics goes to A12-7 Farce; open social attack to A12-15 Social Satire.
leaves.aliases: high comedy; drawing-room comedy; urban neurotic comedy; Comedies and Proverbs
leaves.see: A12-7 Farce; A12-15 Social Satire; A13 Romance
leaves.axis: by milieu and era of the talk: classical high society, contemporary urban circles, the neurotic New York comedy, the conversational moral tale

leaves.label: Farce
leaves.defn: A comedy driven by an accelerating mechanism of deception, mistaken identity, disguise and near-discovery, usually in a confined set (Noises Off..., The Dinner Game, Some Like It Hot, Housefull, Perfect Strangers). Talk-driven social comedy goes to A12-6 Comedy of Manners; bodily slapstick to A12-3 Slapstick.
leaves.aliases: bedroom farce; comédie de boulevard; comedy of errors; chamber comedy; cross-dressing comedy
leaves.see: A12-6 Comedy of Manners; A12-3 Slapstick
leaves.axis: by the farce mechanism: adultery and temptation, boulevard-stage plot, one-room chamber game, mistaken identity and doubles, cross-dressing disguise

leaves.label: Picaresque Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy that follows a roguish or innocent hero through an episodic string of adventures across a society, often a period or literary one (Tom Jones, The Decameron, A Dog's Will, Forrest Gump, Poor Things). A settled ensemble portrait goes to A12-57 Slice-of-Life Comedy-Drama.
leaves.see: A8 Historical & Period Film; A12-57 Slice-of-Life

leaves.label: Ealing Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy from the post-war Ealing Studios cycle (1947–57) of ironic, understated British comedies about little people and institutions (Kind Hearts and Coronets, The Lavender Hill Mob, The Ladykillers).
leaves.see: A12-43 Caper Comedy; A12-15 Social Satire

leaves.label: Commedia all'italiana
leaves.defn: An Italian comedy of the 1958–1980 cycle that laughs bitterly at national vices, sex, family and poverty (Big Deal on Madonna Street, Divorce Italian Style, The Easy Life, We All Loved Each Other So Much).
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Comédia à portuguesa
leaves.defn: A Portuguese popular comedy of the 1930s–40s Lisbon cycle, built on neighbourhood types, fado and city-country contrast (The Courtyard of the Ballads, O Leão da Estrela, Aldeia da Roupa Branca).

leaves.label: Bourekas Film
leaves.defn: An Israeli popular comedy of the 1960s–70s cycle built on Ashkenazi–Mizrahi ethnic stereotypes and mix-ups (Sallah Shabati, Snooker).

leaves.label: Mo lei tau
leaves.defn: Hong Kong nonsense comedy of Stephen Chow's type, mixing absurd non-sequitur, pop-culture spoof and cartoon violence (The God of Cookery, Kung Fu Hustle). A Hong Kong martial-arts action comedy goes to A12-49 Action Comedy.
leaves.see: A12-49 Action Comedy; A12-19 Surreal & Absurdist Comedy

leaves.label: Political Satire
leaves.defn: A comedy whose target is political power: rulers, regimes, campaigns, wars and churches (The Great Dictator, Dr. Strangelove, The Death of Stalin, Wag the Dog, Dogma). Biblical or historical burlesque goes to A12-23 Parody & Spoof. Satire of class, lifestyle or media goes to A12-15 / A12-16 Media & Show-Business Satire.
leaves.aliases: satire of power; war satire; religious satire
leaves.see: A12-15 Social Satire; A12-16 Media & Show-Business Satire; A9 War Film
leaves.axis: by the power under attack: dictators and regimes, campaigns and governments, war and the military, religion

leaves.label: Social Satire
leaves.defn: A comedy whose target is a social order rather than a government: class, suburbia, consumer life, race, custom or the corporation (Life Is a Long Quiet River, American Beauty, Triangle of Sadness, Thank You for Smoking, Dear White People). Satire of media and show business goes to A12-16 Media & Show-Business Satire.
leaves.aliases: class satire; suburban satire; corporate satire
leaves.see: A12-14 Political Satire; A12-16 Media & Show-Business Satire; A12-6 Comedy of Manners
leaves.axis: by the social order under attack: class and wealth, suburbia and lifestyle, race, tradition and custom, corporations and advertising

leaves.label: Media & Show-Business Satire
leaves.defn: A satire whose target is the image industries: Hollywood, television news, celebrity and influencer culture, fashion and the art market (The Player, Network, The King of Comedy, Ingrid Goes West, Official Competition). A non-satirical backstage comedy goes to A12-32 Workplace Comedy; a fake documentary to A12-24 Mockumentary.
leaves.see: A12-32 Workplace Comedy; A12-24 Mockumentary; A12-15 Social Satire
leaves.axis: by the image industry targeted: film business, television and news, celebrity and influencer culture, fashion and art worlds

leaves.label: Black Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy that extracts laughter from death, cruelty, taboo and misfortune, without a political or social target as its main point (Harold and Maude, Happiness, Wild Tales, The Banshees of Inisherin). Comedies whose engine is committing murder go to Murder Comedy; satire of institutions to A12-14 / A12-15 Social Satire.
leaves.see: A12-14 Political Satire; A12-45 Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy; A12-19 Surreal & Absurdist Comedy
leaves.axis: by what the darkness feeds on: death and corpses, misanthropy and taboo, revenge and feuds, escalating nightmare

leaves.label: Murder Comedy
leaves.breadth: Black comedies whose engine is killing: comic murderers, poisoners and bodies to dispose of
leaves.defn: A black comedy built on committing murder — the genteel poisoner, the serial-killing householder, the hapless killer and the body that won't go away, played for laughs (Arsenic and Old Lace, Monsieur Verdoux, Kind Hearts and Coronets, Eating Raoul, Serial Mom, The Green Butchers). Death without a killer stays in Black Comedy; heist-and-crime plots that go wrong to Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy.
leaves.axis: by era: the classic murder comedy to 1979, the 1980s–90s cult and suburban killer comedy, then the 21st century

leaves.label: Camp & Trash Comedy
leaves.defn: A deliberately tasteless, low-budget comedy of outrageous excess, drag and bad taste celebrated as style — the John Waters line and its kin (Pink Flamingos, Female Trouble, Polyester, Pepi, Luci, Bom). Black comedy without the trash aesthetic goes to A12-17 Black Comedy.
leaves.see: A12-17 Black Comedy; A12-23 Parody & Spoof

leaves.label: Surreal & Absurdist Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy built on illogic: absurd premises played straight, dream logic, magical-realist fable or self-reflexive play with the film itself (Deerskin, Songs from the Second Floor, Arizona Dream, Adaptation.). Minimalist straight-faced comedy goes to A12-20 Deadpan.
leaves.aliases: absurdist comedy; surreal humour; metafictional comedy; anti-comedy
leaves.see: A12-20 Deadpan Comedy; A12-13 Mo lei tau; A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde
leaves.axis: by the source of the illogic: absurd premise played straight, surreal or magical-realist fable, metafiction

leaves.label: Deadpan Comedy
leaves.defn: A minimalist comedy of expressionless performance, static framing and laconic timing (Drifting Clouds, Mystery Train, Divine Intervention, Whisky). Whimsical, designed indie quirk goes to A12-21 Quirky Indie Comedy.
leaves.see: A12-21 Quirky Indie Comedy; A12-19 Surreal & Absurdist Comedy
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Quirky Indie Comedy
leaves.defn: An American-indie comedy of whimsical eccentrics, handmade design and wry melancholy, the 'quirky' sensibility of the 2000s (Napoleon Dynamite, Moonrise Kingdom, Lars and the Real Girl, Safety Not Guaranteed).
leaves.see: A12-20 Deadpan Comedy; A12-51 Coming-of-Age Comedy-Drama
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Cringe Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy whose laughter comes from social embarrassment and excruciating awkwardness sustained past comfort (The Foot Fist Way, Shiva Baby, Young Adult, Friendship).

leaves.label: Parody & Spoof
leaves.defn: A comedy that imitates the conventions of a genre, a specific film or franchise, a historical epic or a public persona in order to mock them (Airplane!, Young Frankenstein, Scary Movie, Monty Python and the Holy Grail, Zoolander). Spy spoofs go to A12-50 Spy Comedy; fake documentaries to A12-24 Mockumentary.
leaves.see: A12-50 Spy Comedy; A12-24 Mockumentary; A12-16 Media & Show-Business Satire
leaves.axis: by the target imitated: a whole genre, a specific film or franchise, epic and historical drama, a public persona or milieu, television

leaves.label: Mockumentary
leaves.defn: A fiction comedy formatted as a documentary, or a staged 'real' encounter with a fictional character (This Is Spinal Tap, Best in Show, Borat, Zelig).
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Sketch Film
leaves.defn: A comedy made of separate sketches or self-contained episodes, by one troupe or several directors (Monty Python's And Now for Something Completely Different, The Kentucky Fried Movie, Coffee and Cigarettes, Movie 43, Le Plaisir).
leaves.aliases: film à sketches; comedy anthology film; omnibus
leaves.see: A12-23 Parody & Spoof; A21 Short Film

leaves.label: Stand-Up Comedy Film
leaves.defn: A recorded performance of stand-up or solo comic monologue, released theatrically, on television or streaming (Richard Pryor: Live in Concert, Eddie Murphy: Raw, Hannah Gadsby: Nanette, Bo Burnham: Inside).
leaves.see: B15 Variety & Talk Formats; A19 Documentary
leaves.axis: by format: theatrical concert film, stand-up special, musical comedy special, solo monologue and stage show

leaves.label: Fish-out-of-Water Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy whose engine is a character transplanted into a world whose codes they do not know: country and city, nation and culture, or class (Crocodile Dundee, Welcome to the Sticks, Trading Places, Legally Blonde, Local Hero). A transplant by magic goes to A12-28 Fantasy Comedy.
leaves.aliases: culture-clash comedy; immigrant comedy; rags-to-riches comedy
leaves.see: A12-12 Bourekas Film; A12-28 Fantasy Comedy
leaves.axis: by the border crossed: country and city, nation and culture, class and fortune

leaves.label: Fantasy Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy built on a single supernatural or magical premise whose consequences drive the gags (Groundhog Day, Freaky Friday, Liar Liar, Blithe Spirit, Doctor Dolittle). A technological premise goes to A5-22 Science Fiction Comedy; fantasy adventure to A6.
leaves.aliases: body-swap comedy; high-concept comedy; time-loop comedy; ghost comedy; comic fantasy
leaves.see: A5-22 Science Fiction Comedy; A6 Fantasy & Adventure
leaves.axis: by the magical premise: body swap and transformation, wish curse or magic object, ghosts angels and the afterlife, time loop and time travel, talking animals

leaves.label: Buddy Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy whose engine is a pair or small group of friends or ill-matched partners and their friction (The Odd Couple, Twins, I Love You, Man, Romy and Michele's High School Reunion, The Hangover). A buddy pair of cops goes to A12-48 Buddy Cop Film.
leaves.aliases: odd-couple comedy; bromance; female buddy comedy; bachelor-party comedy
leaves.see: A7-15 Buddy Cop Film; A12-31 Road & Vacation Comedy
leaves.axis: by the bond: ill-matched odd couple, male friendship, female friendship, the bachelor-party pack

leaves.label: Road & Vacation Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy structured by a journey or a holiday away from home, its gags arising from the trip itself (National Lampoon's European Vacation, French Fried Vacation, Flirting with Disaster, Kikujiro).
leaves.aliases: road comedy; vacation comedy; holiday comedy
leaves.see: A12-30 Buddy Comedy; A12-35 Family Comedy
leaves.axis: by the trip: road journey, then holiday resort and vacation

leaves.label: Workplace Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy set in and driven by a workplace and its hierarchy, routines and colleagues (9 to 5, Office Space, Waiting..., Broadcast News, Day for Night). Satire of the corporation as such goes to A12-15 Social Satire; the military to A12-33 Military Comedy.
leaves.aliases: office comedy; backstage comedy; school comedy (teachers)
leaves.see: A12-15 Social Satire; A12-16 Media & Show-Business Satire; A12-33 Military Comedy
leaves.axis: by the workplace: office and corporation, shops restaurants and services, newsroom and broadcasting, school (staff), hospital, show business and the arts

leaves.label: Military Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy of soldiers and military institutions: barracks and boot-camp service comedy, or farce set amid war (Stripes, Private Benjamin, Sgt. Bilko, La Grande Vadrouille). Satire of war itself goes to A12-14 Political Satire.
leaves.see: A12-14 Political Satire; A9 War Film
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Sports Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy built on a sport or competition and the underdog struggle to win it (Caddyshack, Beerfest, The Big Year, The Cup).
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Family Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy whose engine is family life itself: parenting chaos, troublesome kids, in-laws, family gatherings and homes (Mr. Mom, Cheaper by the Dozen, Meet the Parents, Problem Child, The Flintstones). Family comedy-drama goes to A12-52 Family Comedy-Drama; children's films to A17.
leaves.aliases: domestic comedy; in-law comedy; live-action cartoon; kids' comedy
leaves.see: A12-52 Family Comedy-Drama; A17 Children's & Family Film
leaves.axis: by the family engine: parenting, the child, in-laws, the gathering, the house, cartoon families brought to live action

leaves.label: Teen Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy of adolescent social life: high-school hierarchies, school pranks, summer camp and the one wild night (Ferris Bueller's Day Off, Clueless, Mean Girls, Superbad). Teenage sexual initiation goes to A12-38 Teen Sex Comedy; reflective adolescence to A12-51 Coming-of-Age Comedy-Drama.
leaves.aliases: teen movie; high-school comedy; party movie
leaves.see: A12-38 Teen Sex Comedy; A12-51 Coming-of-Age Comedy-Drama; A17 Children's & Family Film
leaves.axis: by the arena: high-school social life, the school as institution, summer camp, the party night

leaves.label: Teen Sex Comedy
leaves.defn: A teen comedy whose plot is the quest to lose virginity or to score (Porky's, Lemon Popsicle, American Pie, Blockers).
leaves.see: A12-37 Teen Comedy; A13-13 Sex Comedy

leaves.label: College & Fraternity Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy of campus life, fraternities and anarchic students versus the dean (National Lampoon's Animal House, Revenge of the Nerds, Old School, Neighbors).

leaves.label: Stoner Film
leaves.defn: A comedy built around cannabis or other drug use and the stoned perspective (Up in Smoke, Dude, Where's My Car?, Harold & Kumar, Pineapple Express).

leaves.label: Slacker Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy of aimless young adults hanging out, talking and avoiding work, including the low-budget mumblecore strand (Slacker, Clerks, Mallrats, Withnail and I).
leaves.see: A12-41 Stoner Film; A12-51 Coming-of-Age Comedy-Drama

leaves.label: Caper Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy organised around a planned theft, swindle or escape, the plan and its unravelling being the engine (A Fish Called Wanda, The Sting, Dirty Rotten Scoundrels, Stir Crazy). Amateurs stumbling into crime go to A12-45 Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy.
leaves.aliases: heist comedy; con-artist comedy; prison comedy
leaves.axis: by the scheme: heist, con, jailbreak and prison

leaves.label: Gangster Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy set among professional criminals — the mob, gangland crews and hitmen (Analyze This, Lock, Stock and Two Smoking Barrels, Snatch, In Bruges). Civilians drawn into crime go to A12-45 Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy; hitman action vehicles to A12-49 Action Comedy.
leaves.aliases: mob comedy; mafia comedy; hitman comedy
leaves.axis: by the criminal world: the mob family, the gangland ensemble, the hitman

leaves.label: Crime-Gone-Wrong Comedy
leaves.defn: A crime comedy in which ordinary people botch a kidnapping, robbery, killing or cover-up, the escalating mess being the engine (Ruthless People, Raising Arizona, Horrible Bosses, Delhi Belly). Planned professional jobs go to A12-43 Caper Comedy.
leaves.see: A12-43 Caper Comedy; A12-17 Black Comedy; A2 Crime
leaves.axis: by how the civilians fall into crime: a kidnapping, a get-rich scheme, a body to hide, being caught up by chance

leaves.label: Comedy Mystery
leaves.defn: A comic whodunit or detective comedy in which a mystery is investigated for laughs (Clue, Fletch, The Big Lebowski, See How They Run).
leaves.see: A3 Thriller & Mystery; A12-47 Cop Comedy

leaves.label: Cop Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy of bungling police, cadets and security guards as an institution, without the action-buddy formula (Police Academy, Super Troopers, Torrente, Paul Blart: Mall Cop).
leaves.see: A7-15 Buddy Cop Film; A12-32 Workplace Comedy

leaves.label: Buddy Cop Comedy
leaves.defn: An action comedy pairing two mismatched partners, at least one a cop, on a case (Beverly Hills Cop, Taxi, The Nice Guys, Let's Be Cops).
leaves.see: A12-49 Action Comedy; A7 Action & Martial Arts

leaves.label: Action Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy whose set pieces are action — chases, fights, shoot-outs, martial arts or sci-fi spectacle — played for laughs (Armour of God, Men in Black, The Hitman's Bodyguard, The Lost City). Cop pairs go to A12-48 Buddy Cop Film; spies to A12-50 Spy Comedy.
leaves.see: A7-15 Buddy Cop Film; A12-50 Spy Comedy; A7 Action & Martial Arts
leaves.axis: by the action engine: adventure and chase, assassins, martial arts, sci-fi spectacle

leaves.label: Spy Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy built on espionage, either spoofing the spy genre or using spy action for comedy (Austin Powers, OSS 117, Johnny English, Charlie's Angels, The Spy Who Dumped Me).
leaves.see: A12-23 Parody & Spoof; A12-49 Action Comedy; A3 Thriller & Mystery
leaves.axis: by stance toward the genre: spoof, then straight action-spy comedy

leaves.label: Coming-of-Age Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: A comedy-drama about growing up, from childhood through the first steps of adulthood (Amarcord, Juno, Frances Ha, Boy, Ghost World). Purely comic teen films go to A12-37 Teen Comedy.
leaves.axis: by age of the protagonist: childhood, adolescence, young adulthood

leaves.label: Family Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: A comedy-drama of a family's tensions and attachments, usually dysfunctional (The Royal Tenenbaums, Parenthood, The Farewell, This Is Where I Leave You). Comic family chaos goes to A12-35 Family Comedy.
leaves.axis: by the family bond in focus: the gathering, parent and adult child, siblings, the whole family in crisis

leaves.label: Marital Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: A comedy-drama of a marriage under strain — affairs, divorce, therapy, the long haul (Bob & Carol & Ted & Alice, Heartburn, This Is 40, Hope Springs). Courtship goes to A13; remarriage plots to A12-5 Comedy of Remarriage.
leaves.see: A12-5 Comedy of Remarriage; A13 Romance
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Midlife Crisis Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy or comedy-drama about middle and later life: the midlife crisis, retirement, ageing and late awakening (City Slickers, Sideways, About Schmidt, Grumpy Old Men, The Best Exotic Marigold Hotel).
leaves.axis: by life stage: midlife crisis, then old age and retirement

leaves.label: Tragicomedy
leaves.defn: A comedy-drama facing illness, grief, addiction or death, whose humour coexists with real loss (Steel Magnolias, 50/50, The Barbarian Invasions, The Bucket List).
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Ensemble Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: A comedy-drama of a group of friends or a community whose interlocking stories carry the film, including the reunion film and the community underdog comedy (The Big Chill, Diner, Short Cuts, The Full Monty, Calendar Girls).
leaves.axis: by what binds the group: friends reunited, a community rallying behind an underdog project

leaves.label: Slice-of-Life Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: A gently comic comedy-drama observing everyday life in a neighbourhood, town or creative milieu, with little plot engine (Marius, Smoke, Happy-Go-Lucky, Cutting It Short, The Horse's Mouth).
leaves.axis: by setting: city and neighbourhood, village and small town, the artist's life

leaves.label: LGBTQ Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy or comedy-drama whose premise is queer identity — coming out, drag, queer family or a gay wedding (The Wedding Banquet, But I'm a Cheerleader, Breakfast on Pluto, Loose Cannons). Cross-dressing as disguise goes to A12-7 Farce.
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Commedia sexy all'italiana
leaves.defn: The Italian erotic comedy cycle of c. 1970–1985: schoolteachers, nurses, policewomen and maids (Edwige Fenech, Gloria Guida, Lino Banfi, Alvaro Vitali) in bawdy, voyeuristic farces descended from the commedia all'italiana and the decamerotici (Malizia, L'insegnante).
leaves.see: A12-10 Commedia all'italiana; A13-13 Sex Comedy

leaves.label: Carry On Film
leaves.defn: The British Carry On series (Peter Rogers and Gerald Thomas, 1958–1978, revived 1992): seaside-postcard innuendo, a stock company (Sid James, Kenneth Williams, Hattie Jacques, Barbara Windsor) and genre and institution parodies (Carry On Nurse, Carry On Up the Khyber).

leaves.label: Chanchada
leaves.defn: The Brazilian popular musical comedy of the 1930s–1950s, above all Atlântida's carnival films with Oscarito and Grande Otelo: samba numbers, burlesque and parodies of Hollywood (Carnaval Atlântida, Nem Sansão Nem Dalila). Its erotic successor is A15-6 Pornochanchada.

subs.label: Romance
subs.axis: Axis: by the love-story engine, what draws the lovers together or keeps them apart; dramatic engines first (obstacle, suffering, obsession, betrayal, the couple itself, war, period, youth, queer love), then the comic engines of the romantic comedy, the romantic fantasy last.

leaves.label: Star-Crossed Romance
leaves.defn: A love story whose engine is an outside force forbidding the match: feuding families, class or caste, religion or ethnicity, custom, state or law (Romeo + Juliet, Bombay, Jungle Fever, Cold War). A comic treatment of the same obstacle goes to the romantic-comedy leaves; a wartime separation goes to A13-6.
leaves.aliases: forbidden love; star-crossed lovers; interracial romance film
leaves.see: A13-6 Wartime Romance; A13-7 Period Romance
leaves.axis: by the force that forbids the match: feuding families, class, faith and ethnicity, custom and state

leaves.label: Romantic Melodrama & Weepie
leaves.defn: A love story built to move the audience to tears through suffering, sacrifice, illness, death or loss (Now, Voyager, Love Story, The Fault in Our Stars, The Notebook). The tearjerker and the woman's film; an obsessive, self-destroying love goes to A13-3.
leaves.aliases: tearjerker; weepie; woman's film; sick-lit romance
leaves.axis: by the source of the tears: sacrifice, illness, grief, lost memory, sentimental small-town romance last

leaves.label: Amour Fou & Obsessive Love
leaves.defn: A love story whose engine is the lovers' own excessive, possessive or self-destroying passion rather than an outside obstacle (Devdas, Leaving Las Vegas, Loulou, Kabir Singh). Where sex itself is the subject the title goes to A15-1.
leaves.aliases: amour fou; mad love; obsessive love; toxic romance
leaves.see: A15-1 Erotic Drama; A3 Thriller & Mystery
leaves.axis: by the form the excess takes: self-destructive devotion, possession and jealousy, lovers outside the law

leaves.label: Adultery Film
leaves.defn: A love story driven by an affair: a brief or unconsummated encounter, a betrayal of marriage, or a temptation resisted (Brief Encounter, In the Mood for Love, Unfaithful, My Night at Maud's). Two rivals for one heart go to Love Triangle Film; a comic affair to the romantic-comedy leaves.
leaves.aliases: infidelity drama; love triangle; affair film
leaves.axis: by what the affair does: the brief or unconsummated encounter, adultery and marital betrayal, the temptation tale

leaves.label: Love Triangle Film
leaves.breadth: Romances of three: two rivals for one heart, or a ménage à trois
leaves.defn: A love story whose engine is a triangle — two lovers competing for one person, or three bound together in a ménage à trois — rather than a single affair against a marriage (Bed and Sofa, Two English Girls, César and Rosalie, Sunday Bloody Sunday, Vicky Cristina Barcelona, Heartbeats). Single affairs stay in Adultery Film.
leaves.aliases: love-triangle romance; ménage à trois film
leaves.axis: by era: the classical triangle, the modernist and New Wave triangle of 1960–1989, then the contemporary triangle

leaves.label: Relationship Drama
leaves.defn: A love story with no outside obstacle whose subject is the courtship of one couple: a chance encounter of a day or a night, a love traced over years, or love kept across distance (Before Sunrise, Past Lives, One Day, Like Crazy). A marriage in crisis or a breakup goes to Marriage Drama; love late in life or across a wide age gap to Late-Life & May–December Romance; an affair or triangle to A13-4.
leaves.aliases: couple drama; brief encounter; long-distance romance; May-December romance
leaves.axis: by the span of the courtship shown: one encounter, years, distance

leaves.label: Marriage Drama
leaves.breadth: dramas of a marriage or long partnership, its crisis and breakup
leaves.defn: A drama of an established couple — a marriage or long partnership followed over time, its crisis, estrangement or breakup (Journey to Italy, Two for the Road, 5x2, Blue Valentine, Before Midnight, The Worst Person in the World).
leaves.aliases: marital drama; breakup film; divorce film
leaves.axis: by era

leaves.label: Late-Life & May–December Romance
leaves.breadth: love stories of old age or across a wide age gap
leaves.defn: A love story whose couple is elderly, or is separated by a wide difference in age (Away from Her, Our Souls at Night, Breezy, White Palace, Elegy).
leaves.aliases: May–December romance; autumn romance; age-gap romance
leaves.axis: by the couple's ages

leaves.label: Wartime Romance
leaves.defn: A love story whose engine is war: lovers met, parted or endangered by a war that stays in the background of the romance (Casablanca, Waterloo Bridge, The English Patient, Dear John). A film about the fighting goes to A9.
leaves.see: A9 War Film; A13-7 Period Romance
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Period Romance
leaves.defn: A love story set in a reconstructed past, where period manners, dress and social codes shape the courtship: classic novel adaptations and original period love stories (Wuthering Heights, Titanic, Far and Away, Lady Chatterley's Lover). Heritage romance; a wartime love story goes to A13-6.
leaves.aliases: historical romance; costume romance; heritage romance
leaves.see: A8 Historical & Period Film; A13-6 Wartime Romance
leaves.axis: by source: adaptation of a literary classic, then original period story

leaves.label: Teen Romance
leaves.defn: A love story whose lovers are adolescents or just past adolescence, built on first love, school and youth (Say Anything..., The Spectacular Now, To All the Boys I've Loved Before, After). Queer teen love goes to A13-9; a teen weepie of illness to A13-2.
leaves.aliases: first love film; high-school romance; new adult romance; teen romantic comedy
leaves.see: A13-9 LGBTQ+ Romance; A17 Children's & Family Film
leaves.axis: by the youth setting and tone: first love, high-school drama, teen comedy, new-adult bad-boy romance

leaves.label: LGBTQ+ Romance
leaves.defn: A love story between lovers of the same sex or across gender identity, where queer desire is the romance (Brokeback Mountain, Carol, Call Me by Your Name, Fire Island). A queer movement film of the early 1990s goes to A1.
leaves.aliases: queer romance; gay romance; lesbian romance; sapphic romance
leaves.see: Movements & Schools (New Queer Cinema); A13-8 Teen Romance
leaves.axis: by the lovers and the tone: gay men, women (incl. trans women), queer first love, queer romantic comedy

leaves.label: Pink Neorealism
leaves.defn: Italian 1950s romantic comedy that keeps neorealism's poor settings and non-star manner but turns them to sentimental courtship (Two Cents Worth of Hope). Neorealismo rosa.

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy of Manners
leaves.defn: A witty, talk-driven romantic comedy whose engine is the social and sexual manners of a milieu, usually urban, sophisticated or literary (Ninotchka, Smiles of a Summer Night, Annie Hall, Bridget Jones's Diary). A farcical screwball goes to A12-4.
leaves.aliases: sophisticated comedy; Lubitsch touch; urban romantic comedy
leaves.axis: by milieu and source: continental sophistication, urban neurosis, Shakespeare and Austen, ensemble roundelay

leaves.label: Sex Comedy
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is sex and the rules of dating: seduction, sexual mores, hook-ups and the failures of the dating market (Pillow Talk, There's Something About Mary, Knocked Up, How to Be Single). A teen sex comedy goes to A12.
leaves.aliases: sex comedy; gross-out romantic comedy; dating comedy; gross-out comedy; raunch comedy
leaves.see: A12 Comedy; A13-17 Friends to Lovers
leaves.axis: by era and register: Hollywood sex comedy, gross-out romantic comedy, hook-up and dating comedy

leaves.label: Meet-Cute Romantic Comedy
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is the contrived or fated first meeting and the near misses that follow, including courtship by letter and the romance of a trip (Sleepless in Seattle, Serendipity, You've Got Mail, French Kiss). The friends who were already there go to A13-17.
leaves.aliases: meet cute; destiny romcom; epistolary romance; holiday romance
leaves.axis: by how the lovers meet: fate and near misses, letters and screens, a journey abroad

leaves.label: Enemies to Lovers
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy whose couple begins in hostility, rivalry or total mismatch and fights its way to love (The Quiet Man, The Ugly Truth, Hum Tum, Anyone But You). Battle-of-the-sexes and opposites-attract comedy; rivals at work go to A13-19.
leaves.aliases: battle of the sexes; opposites attract; bickering couple
leaves.see: A12-4 Screwball Comedy; A13-19 Workplace Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by type

leaves.label: Fake Relationship
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is a pretence: a fake engagement or marriage of convenience, a bet, a disguise or mistaken identity, or a matchmaker's scheme (Green Card, The Proposal, How to Lose a Guy in 10 Days, Hitch). A teen bet comedy goes to A13-8.
leaves.aliases: fake dating; marriage of convenience; romantic deception; Cyrano comedy
leaves.see: A13-15 Enemies to Lovers; A13-20 Wedding Comedy
leaves.axis: by the kind of pretence: fake couple, wager, disguise, matchmaking scheme

leaves.label: Friends to Lovers
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is a friendship that turns, slowly or suddenly, into love, including the friends-with-benefits arrangement (When Harry Met Sally..., Love, Rosie, Jaane Tu... Ya Jaane Na, Friends with Benefits). A dramatic version spanning years goes to A13-5.
leaves.aliases: friends to lovers; friends with benefits; friend zone
leaves.see: A13-5 Relationship Drama; A13-13 Sex Comedy
leaves.axis: by type

leaves.label: Cinderella Story
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy whose engine is a match across wealth or rank in which one lover is raised into the other's world: makeover, royalty, celebrity (Pretty Woman, Roman Holiday, Notting Hill, Maid in Manhattan). A forbidding, tragic class divide goes to A13-1.
leaves.aliases: Cinderella story; rags to riches romance; royal romance
leaves.axis: by the higher world entered: wealth and makeover, royalty and power, celebrity

leaves.label: Workplace Romantic Comedy
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy whose couple meets and spars through a shared job, office or profession (Desk Set, Office Romance, Working Girl, Two Weeks Notice). Career-woman comedy; workplace enemies with no job plot go to A13-15.

leaves.label: Wedding Comedy
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy organised around a wedding: brides and planners, guests and crashers, or the clash of two families and arranged matches (Four Weddings and a Funeral, My Best Friend's Wedding, My Big Fat Greek Wedding, Band Baaja Baaraat). A wedding as one scene only does not count.
leaves.aliases: wedding film; meet-the-parents comedy; arranged-marriage comedy
leaves.axis: by who drives the comedy: the couple and their wedding, the guests, the families

leaves.label: Holiday Romantic Comedy
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy built on a calendar holiday that sets its deadline and mood: Christmas, New Year, Valentine's Day (The Irony of Fate, Valentine's Day, Holidate). Christmas only as backdrop does not count.
leaves.see: A13-12 Romantic Comedy of Manners (Ensemble Roundelay)

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy played half-seriously, from the 1970s on, whose obstacle lies in the lovers' own eccentricity, damage, family burdens or age (Moonstruck, As Good as It Gets, Silver Linings Playbook, Something's Gotta Give, Amélie). The studio-era and other pre-1970 comedy-dramas go to the Classical Romantic Comedy-Drama; the American and English-language independent strand to the Indie Romantic Comedy; a purely dramatic treatment to A13-5.
leaves.axis: by the lovers' burden: eccentricity, damage or illness, children and second chances, age, a homecoming

leaves.label: Classical Romantic Comedy-Drama
leaves.breadth: romantic comedy-dramas of the silent and studio eras, to 1969, across national cinemas
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy-drama of the silent and studio eras, before 1970, in any national cinema — the bittersweet star romance of Hollywood, the European and Soviet lyrical comedy, the Argentine and Mexican comedia romántica, the Asian and Egyptian studio romance (The Strawberry Blonde, Breakfast at Tiffany's, Walking the Streets of Moscow, Arroz con leche, Windfall in Athens). Test: made before 1970; screwball and sophisticated comedy go to their own leaves.
leaves.aliases: classical romantic comedy; studio-era romantic comedy
leaves.axis: by national studio tradition: Hollywood first, then Europe and the Soviet Union, Latin America, and Asia and the Middle East last

leaves.label: Indie Romantic Comedy
leaves.breadth: romantic comedy-dramas of the American and English-language independent cinema
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy-drama made in the American or English-language independent cinema from the 1970s on, deadpan, talky or wounded in tone and outside the studio formula (Minnie and Moskowitz, Chilly Scenes of Winter, Trust, Punch-Drunk Love, Results, The Big Sick, Enough Said). Test: independent production and an off-formula register; studio rom-coms of the same burdens stay in A13-22.
leaves.axis: by the lovers' burden: deadpan and eccentric lovers, then damaged and healing lovers, and age-gap love last

leaves.label: Romantic Fantasy
leaves.defn: A love story, dramatic or comic, whose engine is a fantastic or speculative device: ghosts and afterlife, time travel, supernatural creatures, machines, magic or a time loop (Ghost, Somewhere in Time, Twilight, Her, Palm Springs). Where the device dominates and love is secondary the title goes to A5 or A6.
leaves.aliases: paranormal romance; time-travel romance; supernatural romance; science-fiction romance; fantasy romance
leaves.see: A5 Science Fiction; A6 Fantasy & Adventure
leaves.axis: by the fantastic device: ghost, time travel, creature, machine, magic, loop or parallel life

leaves.label: Telefoni Bianchi
leaves.defn: The Italian sentimental and sophisticated comedies of c. 1932–1943 ('white telephone' films), set among department stores, hotels and Art Deco apartments, after Hollywood and Hungarian models (Mario Camerini, Vittorio De Sica, Mario Soldati): What Scoundrels Men Are!, Il signor Max.

subs.label: Musical & Dance Film
subs.axis: Axis: by how music and dance enter the story: integrated song (book musical, operetta), song as performance (revue, backstage), all-sung forms, rock and pop forms, recorded stage shows, dance, and films about musicians without musical numbers last.

leaves.label: Book Musical
leaves.defn: An American-tradition musical film whose songs and dances arise inside the story and carry plot and character, written for the screen or adapted from the stage (Top Hat, Meet Me in St. Louis, West Side Story, La La Land). Integrated musicals of other national cinemas go to European & World Film Musical; numbers staged as performances to A14-4; an all-sung film to A14-5.
leaves.aliases: integrated musical; film musical; stage-musical adaptation
leaves.see: A14-4 Backstage Musical; A14-5 Opera Film
leaves.axis: by origin and audience: Hollywood studio originals, Broadway adaptations, family musicals, teen musicals, later screen originals, and the Astaire–Rogers cycle

leaves.label: European & World Film Musical
leaves.breadth: Integrated film musicals of national cinemas outside Hollywood
leaves.defn: A book musical — songs and dances carrying the story — made in a national film industry outside Hollywood: René Clair's French musicals, German Tonfilm comedies, the Soviet musical comedies of Aleksandrov and Pyryev, the Egyptian and Lebanese musical, the films of Demy and Honoré (Le Million, Volga-Volga, The Young Girls of Rochefort, Love Songs). Operettas go to Operetta Film; Hindi masala films, rumberas and comedia ranchera to their own leaves.
leaves.axis: by national tradition

leaves.label: Operetta Film
leaves.defn: A musical film in the operetta tradition, light romantic plots in a mythical Ruritania or old Europe told through sung waltzes and duets (The Love Parade, Love Me Tonight, Naughty Marietta, Ulduz).
leaves.see: A14-1 Book Musical; A14-5 Opera Film

leaves.label: Revue Film
leaves.defn: A plotless or nearly plotless film made of separate musical and comic numbers, the screen form of the stage revue (King of Jazz, Ziegfeld Follies).

leaves.label: Backstage Musical
leaves.defn: A musical film about putting on a show, whose numbers are staged as performances within the story (42nd Street, Singin' in the Rain, The Band Wagon, Cabaret). Integrated numbers go to A14-1; a musician's story without numbers goes to A14-13.
leaves.see: A14-1 Book Musical; A14-13 Music Film
leaves.axis: by the stage: Broadway and revue, Hollywood and stardom, cabaret and nightclub

leaves.label: Opera Film & Sung-Through Musical
leaves.defn: A film entirely or almost entirely sung: a filmed or adapted opera, a sung-through screen musical, or a traditional sung music-theatre form (The Tales of Hoffmann, The Umbrellas of Cherbourg, Chunhyang, Annette). A rock opera goes to A14-6.
leaves.aliases: film-opera; opera film; sung-through musical; pansori film
leaves.axis: by type

leaves.label: Rock Opera & Rock Musical
leaves.defn: A musical film set to rock music, a sung rock narrative or stage rock musical (Tommy, Jesus Christ Superstar, The Rocky Horror Picture Show, Hedwig and the Angry Inch). A musical built on existing hits goes to A14-7.
leaves.see: A14-7 Jukebox Musical; A14-5 Opera Film

leaves.label: Jukebox Musical
leaves.defn: A musical film whose numbers are previously released popular songs, often one artist's catalogue (Mamma Mia!, Across the Universe, Moulin Rouge!, Sunshine on Leith). A biopic of the artist goes to A11.
leaves.see: A11 Biographical Film; A14-6 Rock Opera & Rock Musical

leaves.label: Pop Star Vehicle
leaves.defn: A fiction film built to showcase a singer or band playing a version of themselves through their songs (Jailhouse Rock, A Hard Day's Night, Purple Rain, Spice World). A concert record goes to A19.
leaves.aliases: star vehicle; Elvis musical; band film
leaves.see: A19 Documentary (concert film); A14-10 Visual Album

leaves.label: Filmed Stage Musical
leaves.defn: A recording of a stage musical as performed in the theatre, or broadcast live, rather than re-made for the camera (Hamilton, Cats (1998), Grease Live!). Weakly attested label (trade: pro-shot); a screen adaptation goes to A14-1.
leaves.aliases: pro-shot; filmed theatre; live television musical
leaves.see: A14-1 Book Musical; B16 Live Event & Sports Television
leaves.axis: by type

leaves.label: Visual Album
leaves.defn: A feature-length film made to accompany a music album, its songs strung into an impressionistic narrative (Lemonade, Dirty Computer, Black Is King).
leaves.see: A14-8 Pop Star Vehicle; A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde

leaves.label: Dance Film
leaves.defn: A fiction film whose story is carried by dance and dancers, its climaxes danced performances or competitions (The Red Shoes, Saturday Night Fever, Dirty Dancing, Step Up). A sung musical goes to A14-1.
leaves.aliases: dance movie; ballet film; street-dance film
leaves.see: A14-1 Book Musical; A14-4 Backstage Musical
leaves.axis: by the dance form: ballet and concert dance, flamenco, ballroom and social dance, disco and teen dance, street and hip-hop, striptease

leaves.label: Rumberas Film
leaves.defn: Mexican golden-age cabaret melodrama starring a rumba dancer, the rumbera (Victims of Sin).

leaves.label: Music Film
leaves.defn: A fiction film about musicians and music-making whose music is performed in the story but which is not a musical: bands, singers, players, teachers, contests (Whiplash, Once, 8 Mile, Pitch Perfect). A biopic of a real musician goes to A11; a documentary to A19.
leaves.aliases: film about musicians; band film; music-competition film
leaves.see: A11 Biographical Film; A14-4 Backstage Musical
leaves.axis: by the music world: jazz and blues, bands and rock, hip-hop and DJ, singers and stardom, choirs and classical, family, contests last

leaves.label: Comedia Ranchera
leaves.defn: The Mexican ranch musical of the Golden Age (1936–1950s): singing charros (Tito Guízar, Jorge Negrete, Pedro Infante), haciendas, serenades, cockfights and rival suitors (Allá en el Rancho Grande, ¡Ay Jalisco, no te rajes!, Dos tipos de cuidado).
leaves.see: A14-12 Rumberas Film; A10-5 Musical Western

leaves.label: Huangmei Opera Film
leaves.defn: The sung costume romance in Huangmei-opera style, launched in Hong Kong by Li Han-hsiang at Shaw Brothers (1958–1960s) after the mainland Heavenly Match: legendary lovers, cross-dressing heroines, palace and garden sets (The Kingdom and the Beauty, The Love Eterne).

subs.label: Erotic Film
subs.axis: Axis: by how sex drives the film and the production tradition: art-house erotic drama first, erotic thriller, then softcore and exploitation traditions, national erotic cycles last.

leaves.label: Erotic Drama
leaves.defn: A narrative film whose subject is sexual desire, practice or obsession, shown explicitly as the core of the drama (Last Tango in Paris, In the Realm of the Senses, Secretary, Fifty Shades of Grey). A love story with sex scenes goes to A13; a suspense plot to A3-9.
leaves.see: A13-3 Amour Fou; A3-9 Erotic Thriller
leaves.axis: by the erotic engine: awakening, obsession and transgression, sadomasochism, unsimulated sex, bestseller erotic romance

leaves.label: Softcore Film
leaves.defn: A film of simulated sex made for erotic display, often in the European erotic tradition (Immoral Tales, Vampyros Lesbos, Delta of Venus).
leaves.axis: school / national tradition

leaves.label: Sexploitation
leaves.defn: A low-budget independent film made to exploit sex and nudity, from roadshow sex-hygiene films to Russ Meyer and nunsploitation (Mom and Dad, Faster, Pussycat! Kill! Kill!, Ilsa, the Wicked Warden).
leaves.see: A18 Popular Cinema Modes; A4 Horror
leaves.axis: named exploitation cycle

leaves.label: Pink Film
leaves.defn: Japanese theatrical softcore cinema (pinku eiga) of the independent studios and Nikkatsu's Roman Porno line. Kept as an attested canon although no title in the present corpus belongs here.
leaves.aliases: pinku eiga; Roman Porno; Nikkatsu Roman Porno
leaves.axis: by cycle and studio, in order of emergence: the first independent wave, Nikkatsu Roman Porno, the Pink Shitennō and Seven Lucky Gods directors, the Roman Porno reboot

leaves.label: Pornochanchada
leaves.defn: Brazilian erotic comedy and drama of the 1970s–80s made around São Paulo's Boca do Lixo (A Dama do Lotação).

leaves.label: Hong Kong Category III Film
leaves.defn: A Hong Kong film of the adults-only Category III rating cycle (1988 onward, peaking in the early 1990s): sex-and-violence exploitation, erotic costume romps (Sex and Zen) and lurid true-crime shockers (The Untold Story, Ebola Syndrome). Defined by the named Hong Kong cycle rather than one plot type.
leaves.see: A4 Horror; A7-10 Hong Kong Action Cinema
leaves.axis: strand of the cycle

subs.label: Drama
subs.axis: Axis: by the dramatic engine — the bond, inner state, social condition, institution, contest or journey the drama turns on: family and home first, then the self, youth, society and its institutions, faith, sport, and journeys and animals last.

leaves.label: Shomingeki (Shoshimin-eiga)
leaves.defn: A Japanese studio drama of ordinary lower-middle-class urban life: salarymen, households, marriages arranged and parents left behind, told at the scale of the home (Tokyo Story, Late Spring, I Was Born, But...). Non-Japanese family dramas go to A16-3 or A16-4.
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Family Saga
leaves.defn: A drama that follows one family across generations or decades, the passing of time and inheritance of fortune being the engine (The Magnificent Ambersons, Giant, Fanny and Alexander, The Best of Youth). A drama confined to one crisis in one generation goes to A16-3 or A16-4.
leaves.see: A16-3 Family Drama; A8 Historical & Period Film
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Family Drama
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is the family as a group rather than one parent–child pair or one sibling bond: the household, the family gathered for a holiday or funeral, the inheritance, the home after a death (Still Walking, Rachel Getting Married, Summer Hours, Ordinary People). Siblings go to Sibling Drama; foster, adoptive and chosen families to Found Family Film; one parent and child to A16-4; a couple to A16-5.
leaves.see: Parent–Child Drama; A16-5 Domestic Drama; A16-2 Family Saga
leaves.axis: by the family occasion: the household, then the gathered family, the inheritance, and the bereaved home last

leaves.label: Sibling Drama
leaves.breadth: Dramas of sisters, brothers and brother–sister bonds
leaves.defn: A family drama centred on siblings — sisters, brothers, or a brother and sister — their rivalry, devotion or estrangement (Rocco and His Brothers, The Makioka Sisters, You Can Count on Me, Our Little Sister, Frère et soeur). A drama of the whole family goes to Family Drama.
leaves.axis: by the sibling bond: sisters, brothers, then brother and sister and mixed sibling groups

leaves.label: Found Family Film
leaves.breadth: Dramas of foster, adoptive and chosen families
leaves.defn: A family drama whose family is made rather than born: the foster home and the orphan taken in, adoption and the search for birth origins, the chosen family of strangers (The Kid with a Bike, Secrets & Lies, Shoplifters, The Quiet Girl, Return to Seoul).
leaves.aliases: chosen family; foster family drama; adoption drama
leaves.axis: by how the family is made: fostering and orphans, adoption and birth origins, then chosen families

leaves.label: Father–Child Drama
leaves.defn: A drama centred on a father and his child — the father–son or father–daughter bond strained, broken or repaired, into the father's old age (The Return, Aftersun, Fences, On Golden Pond, Like Father, Like Son). A mother and child goes to Mother–Child Drama; a drama of the whole family to A16-3; Japanese shomingeki to A16-1.
leaves.see: A16-3 Family Drama; A16-13 Coming-of-Age Film
leaves.axis: by the child and the stage of life: fathers and sons, fathers and daughters, then ageing fathers (and parents) with their adult children

leaves.label: Mother–Child Drama
leaves.breadth: Dramas of a mother and her daughter or son
leaves.defn: A drama centred on a mother and her child — the mother–daughter or mother–son bond, from childhood to the mother's old age (Autumn Sonata, Terms of Endearment, Mommy, I Killed My Mother, Room). A father and child goes to Father–Child Drama; a drama of the whole family to A16-3.
leaves.axis: by the child and the stage of life: mothers and daughters, mothers and sons, then ageing mothers (and grandmothers) with their adult children

leaves.label: Domestic Drama
leaves.defn: A drama of the married couple at home — the marriage worn down, betrayed or dissolved (Scenes from a Marriage, Revolutionary Road, Kramer vs. Kramer, Marriage Story). A romance that ends in marriage goes to A13; the wider family to A16-3.
leaves.see: A13 Romance; A16-3 Family Drama; A16-6 Melodrama
leaves.axis: by the state of the marriage: the marriage in crisis, adultery, then divorce and custody

leaves.label: Melodrama
leaves.defn: A drama in the melodramatic mode — heightened emotion, sacrifice and fate carried by music and mise-en-scène — whose sacrifice is made for a child or a family, or to illness (Stella Dallas, Imitation of Life, Written on the Wind, Dark Victory, All About My Mother). The melodrama of the fallen, desiring or self-sacrificing woman in love goes to the Woman's Film; realist family dramas to A16-3 to A16-5.
leaves.axis: by the sacrifice at the core: maternal sacrifice first, then the family melodrama, the illness tearjerker, and Sirk's non-melodrama studio pictures last

leaves.label: Woman's Film
leaves.breadth: melodramas of the fallen, desiring or self-sacrificing woman, across national studio traditions
leaves.defn: A melodrama centred on a woman's desire, fall or sacrifice in love, marriage or work, made for and around a female star or a woman's point of view (The Cheat, Pandora's Box, Back Street, All That Heaven Allows, When a Woman Ascends the Stairs, Far from Heaven). Test: the heroine's own passion or fall is the engine; sacrifice for a child or a family stays in A16-6.
leaves.aliases: woman's picture; women's film; fallen-woman melodrama; josei eiga
leaves.axis: by era and national studio tradition: the silent vamp and fallen woman first, then the Hollywood woman's film, the European, Japanese, Chinese-Korean-Indian and Latin American traditions, and the modern revisionist woman's film last

leaves.label: Psychological Drama
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is one person's inner state of trauma, guilt or obsession, rendered from inside (Peppermint Candy, Affliction, Death in Venice, The Master). A drama of mourning goes to Grief Drama, one of madness and mental illness to Mental Illness Drama; where suspense drives it, see A3; where the crisis is existential rather than psychological, A16-8.
leaves.see: A16-8 Existentialist Film; A3 Thriller & Mystery; A16-26 Medical Drama
leaves.axis: by the inner condition: trauma and abuse first, then guilt and atonement, and obsession last

leaves.label: Grief Drama
leaves.breadth: Dramas of mourning: the bereaved spouse, parent or friend living through a death
leaves.defn: A drama whose subject is grief itself — a widow, widower, parent or friend living through loss, often in the long aftermath of a death (Three Colors: Blue, Maborosi, Manchester by the Sea, Drive My Car). A family collectively bereaved goes to Family Drama; a grief that becomes breakdown, to Mental Illness Drama.
leaves.axis: by era

leaves.label: Mental Illness Drama
leaves.breadth: Dramas of madness, breakdown, psychosis and the asylum
leaves.defn: A drama of a mind coming apart — schizophrenia, psychosis, depression, dissociation, breakdown — or of life in the asylum and clinic (Through a Glass Darkly, The Cobweb, Clean, Shaven, Spider, Take Shelter). A psychological thriller goes to A3; a grief drama to Grief Drama.
leaves.aliases: madness film; asylum drama; mental illness in film
leaves.axis: by era: the studio-era psychiatric drama, the anti-psychiatry and modernist decades, then the contemporary independent character study

leaves.label: Existentialist Film
leaves.defn: An art-film character study whose engine is a crisis of meaning in the present tense — alienation, ennui, or a self disguised or doubled (La Dolce Vita, The Silence, Lost in Translation, The Passenger, The Double Life of Véronique). A life weighed up at its middle or end goes to the Midlife Crisis Film; a clinical inner state to A16-7; a quiet everyday portrait to A16-9.
leaves.see: A16-7 Psychological Drama; A16-9 Slice of Life; Movements & Schools
leaves.axis: by the shape of the crisis: alienation first, divided by era (the postwar modernist wave to 1979, its late-modernist continuation in the 1980s–90s, the contemporary festival film), then the ennui of the affluent, and double lives and masks last

leaves.label: Midlife Crisis Film
leaves.breadth: existential dramas of a life weighed up — at its middle, in old age, or reviewed whole from rise to fall
leaves.defn: A drama whose crisis of meaning comes from taking stock of a life already lived: the midlife crisis, the reckoning of old age, or a whole life reviewed in its rise and fall (Dodsworth, Save the Tiger, Husbands, Citizen Kane, Death of a Salesman, Youth, Gran Torino). Test: the film's engine is the review of a life's course rather than a present-tense alienation (A16-8) or a clinical breakdown (A16-7).
leaves.aliases: midlife-crisis drama; late-life drama; life-review film
leaves.axis: by where the life is weighed up: the whole life reviewed in its rise and fall first, then the crisis at midlife, and old age and last reckonings last

leaves.label: Slice of Life
leaves.defn: A drama with no plot engine beyond a settled daily life observed — routines, rituals, small encounters and the passing days of people at home in their place (Paterson, Perfect Days, Café Lumière, The Scent of Green Papaya). A life adrift goes to the Drifter Film; a crisis of meaning to A16-8; a journey to A16-36.
leaves.see: A16-8 Existentialist Film; A16-36 Road Movie
secs: Eastern Europe, the Caucasus & Central Asia
Middle East, Africa, South & Southeast Asia, Oceania
leaves.axis: by national and regional tradition, as festival everyday cinema is grouped: East Asia first (the Japanese, Korean, Chinese and Taiwanese quotidian film), then Western Europe, Eastern Europe and Central Asia, North America, Latin America, and the rest of the world last

leaves.label: Drifter Film
leaves.breadth: dramas of loners and drifters without settled place or purpose
leaves.defn: A drama of observed days whose protagonist is adrift — a loner, wanderer or young person between jobs, homes and attachments, followed without a plot engine (Wanda, Wendy and Lucy, Naked, Millennium Mambo, Morvern Callar, Old Joy). Test: the life is unsettled and the drift is the subject; a journey with a destination goes to A16-36, a settled daily routine stays in A16-9.
secs: Eastern Europe, the Caucasus & Central Asia
Middle East, Africa, South & Southeast Asia, Oceania
leaves.axis: by national and regional tradition: East Asia first, then Western Europe, Eastern Europe and Central Asia, North America, Latin America, and the rest of the world last

leaves.label: Chamber Drama (Kammerspiel)
leaves.defn: A drama confined to a few characters in one space or one conversation, the dialogue being the action (My Dinner with Andre, Tape, The Sunset Limited, Locke). A filmed stage production goes to A16-12 when it is about performers.
leaves.see: A16-12 Artist Film; A16-5 Domestic Drama
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Hyperlink Cinema
leaves.defn: An ensemble drama of several separate storylines linked by chance, place or a shared event (Magnolia, 21 Grams, Babel, Crash). A single family's ensemble goes to A16-3.
leaves.see: A16-3 Family Drama; A16-19 Social Realism
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Artist Film (Künstlerroman)
leaves.defn: A drama of a fictional performer, musician, writer or painter whose art or career is the engine — the artist at work and in crisis (All About Eve, Opening Night, Tár, La belle noiseuse). Films about making films go to Film about Filmmaking; real artists' lives to A11; musicals to A14.
leaves.see: A11 Biographical Film; A14 Musical & Dance Film
leaves.axis: by the art: stage, then screen and show-business performers, musicians, writers, and painters and visual artists last

leaves.label: Film about Filmmaking
leaves.breadth: Fiction films set in the film world: a director, crew or production in crisis
leaves.defn: A fiction film whose subject is the making of films — a director's creative crisis, a troubled shoot, the studio or the film world, often self-reflexive (8½, The Bad and the Beautiful, Passion, The State of Things, Day for Night, Pain and Glory, The Fabelmans). Stage and screen performers' careers stay in Artist Film; documentaries on film production go to Making-of Documentary.
leaves.aliases: film within a film; metafilm; films about filmmaking; Hollywood-on-Hollywood film
leaves.axis: by era: classical and modernist films about filmmaking, the late-modern and festival-auteur decades, then the 2010s onward

leaves.label: Coming-of-Age Film
leaves.defn: A drama of a child's or young adolescent's passage toward understanding, told from the child's side, in the ordinary settings of home, city or village (My Life as a Dog, The Long Day Closes, Boyhood, Ratcatcher, Close). Childhood under war or dictatorship goes to the War-Childhood Film; the summer away to the Summer Coming-of-Age Film; school and boarding school to the School Story Film; high-school teen life to A16-14; delinquency to A16-15.
leaves.see: A16-14 Teen Film; A16-15 Juvenile Delinquency Film; A17 Children's & Family Film
leaves.axis: by the setting of the childhood: home and family first, then city streets, and village and countryside last

leaves.label: War-Childhood Film
leaves.breadth: coming-of-age dramas of children under war, occupation or dictatorship
leaves.defn: A coming-of-age drama told from the side of a child growing up under war, occupation or dictatorship, where the historical violence shapes the passage (The Spirit of the Beehive, Cría Cuervos, In the Heat of the Sun, West Beirut, Kamchatka, Clandestine Childhood). Test: a child's-eye coming of age with war or repression as its condition; a combat film with child soldiers goes to A9.
leaves.aliases: childhood war film; children-in-war film; child's-eye war film

leaves.label: Summer Coming-of-Age Film
leaves.breadth: coming-of-age dramas of the summer holiday away from routine
leaves.defn: A coming-of-age drama set in the suspended time of a summer holiday — the trip, the camp, the summer house, the gang's adventure — whose end marks the passage (Stand by Me, My Father's Glory, The Sandlot, Summer 1993, The Way Way Back). Test: the summer away is the frame; school-year childhoods stay in A16-13.

leaves.label: School Story Film
leaves.breadth: childhood dramas set in the classroom or boarding school
leaves.defn: A childhood drama whose world is the school — the boarding school, the classroom and its teacher, exams and school tyranny — told from the pupils' side (Zéro de conduite, Evil, Son of Rambow, Our Twisted Hero, Playground, Monster). Test: pre-teen or early-adolescent pupils and their school; the high school goes to A16-14, college to A16-16, the teacher's own story to A16-17.

leaves.label: Teen Film
leaves.defn: A drama of teenage life in its own institutions — high school, cliques, first love and sexual awakening (The Breakfast Club, Lady Bird, Eighth Grade, Murmur of the Heart). Rebellion and crisis go to A16-15; teen comedies to A12; teen romance to A13.
leaves.see: A16-13 Coming-of-Age Film; A16-15 Juvenile Delinquency Film; A13 Romance
leaves.axis: by the arena of adolescence: school and cliques, friendship and teenage summers, home and hardship, then first love and sexual awakening

leaves.label: Juvenile Delinquency Film
leaves.defn: A drama of youth in revolt or in danger — gangs, rebels, subcultures and teenagers in crisis (Rebel Without a Cause, The Outsiders, This Is England, Thirteen); includes the Japanese taiyōzoku cycle (Crazed Fruit). Crime-driven youth gangs go to A2.
leaves.aliases: JD film; rebel youth film; taiyōzoku film
leaves.axis: by the form of revolt: street gangs, rebels and runaways, youth subcultures, then teenagers in crisis

leaves.label: Campus Film
leaves.defn: A drama set in a college or university, or among its just-graduated (Starter for 10, Higher Learning, St. Elmo's Fire). High school goes to A16-14; campus comedy to A12.
leaves.see: A16-14 Teen Film; A16-17 Teacher Film

leaves.label: Teacher Film
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is a teacher and a class — the inspirational, embattled or failing educator (To Sir, with Love, Dead Poets Society, The Class, The Teachers' Lounge). Pupils' own stories go to A16-13 or A16-14.
leaves.see: A16-14 Teen Film; A16-16 Campus Film
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: LGBTQ Film
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is queer identity — coming out, queer love and community, or trans life (Beautiful Thing, Moonlight, The Boys in the Band, A Fantastic Woman). A queer love story foregrounding romance goes to A13; the 1990s movement to A1.
leaves.aliases: queer cinema; gay and lesbian film; coming-out film
leaves.see: Movements & Schools; A13 Romance; A16-14 Teen Film
leaves.axis: by the queer experience: coming out, queer love and desire, community, AIDS and society, then trans and intersex lives

leaves.label: Social Realism
leaves.defn: A drama of ordinary poor people shown in their material conditions — poverty, unemployment, precarity, the street and the slum (Rosetta, I, Daniel Blake, Salaam Bombay!, Accattone). Films centred on work and labour struggle go to Labour Film; peasant and village life to Rural Drama; a drama built around one named social issue goes to A16-22; Italian neorealism and kitchen-sink realism are movements with their own leaves.
leaves.aliases: working-class film; kitchen-sink drama; social drama
leaves.see: Movements & Schools; A16-22 Social Problem Film; A16-21 Immigrant Film
leaves.axis: by where the hardship falls (poverty and precarity, then the street and slum), each by era

leaves.label: Labour Film
leaves.breadth: realist dramas of work, the workplace, strikes and unions
leaves.defn: A realist drama whose subject is work itself — the factory, mine, dock, office or service job, the strike and the union, the dignity or exploitation of labour (Salt of the Earth, Norma Rae, The Working Class Goes to Heaven, Two Days, One Night, Sorry We Missed You).
leaves.aliases: labor film; workers' film; working-class film; strike film; proletarian film
leaves.axis: by era

leaves.label: Rural Drama
leaves.breadth: realist dramas of peasant, farming and village life
leaves.defn: A realist drama of peasants, farmers, fishers and herders and the hardship of village life on the land (The Grapes of Wrath, The Ballad of Narayama, The Story of Qiu Ju, Ixcanul, Happy as Lazzaro). The idealised German homeland film goes to Heimatfilm.
leaves.aliases: peasant film; village film; rural realism
leaves.axis: by era

leaves.label: Banlieue Film
leaves.defn: A French drama of the multi-ethnic housing estates of the urban periphery, youth and police at its centre (La Haine, Girlhood, Les Misérables). Non-French urban dramas go to A16-19.
leaves.see: A16-19 Social Realism; A16-15 Juvenile Delinquency Film

leaves.label: Immigrant Film
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is migration — the crossing, the arrival in a new country, or the second generation between cultures (El Norte, Minari, My Beautiful Laundrette, Io Capitano). Migration as backdrop to a crime goes to A2.
leaves.aliases: migrant cinema; diaspora film; accented cinema
leaves.see: A16-19 Social Realism; A16-36 Road Movie
leaves.axis: by the stage of migration: the arrival and new life, the second generation, then the crossing and the refugee

leaves.label: Social Problem Film
leaves.defn: A drama built to expose one named social ill of prejudice, violence or patriarchy — racism and caste, youth violence and its institutions, sexual violence and reproductive rights, the oppression of women (Gentleman's Agreement, Within Our Gates, Never Rarely Sometimes Always, Moolaadé). Addiction goes to the Addiction Drama; prostitution and trafficking to the Prostitution Film; diffuse working-class hardship to A16-19; the courtroom to A16-25.
leaves.aliases: problem picture; message film; issue film
leaves.see: A16-19 Social Realism; A16-25 Legal Drama; A16-23 Political Drama
leaves.axis: by the social ill: race and caste first, then youth violence and reform schools, sexual violence and reproductive rights, and the oppression of women last

leaves.label: Addiction Drama
leaves.breadth: social-problem dramas of drink, drugs and gambling
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is one person's or one milieu's addiction — to alcohol, drugs or gambling — followed through craving, collapse and (sometimes) recovery (The Lost Weekend, Days of Wine and Roses, The Man with the Golden Arm, Requiem for a Dream, The Gambler). Test: the addiction itself is the subject, not a backdrop to crime (A2) or a psychological portrait (A16-7).
leaves.aliases: drug film; alcoholism film; addiction film
leaves.axis: by the substance: drink first, then drugs, and gambling last

leaves.label: Prostitution Film
leaves.breadth: dramas of sex work, the fallen woman and trafficking
leaves.defn: A drama whose subject is prostitution as a social condition — the fallen woman of the silent and studio eras, the brothel and the red-light district, the street, and modern trafficking (Diary of a Lost Girl, Street of Shame, Nights of Cabiria, Mamma Roma, Lilya 4-Ever, Much Loved). Test: selling sex is the protagonist's situation and the film's subject; an erotic treatment goes to A15.
leaves.aliases: fallen-woman film; sex-work drama; trafficking drama
leaves.axis: by era, as the field divides it: the fallen-woman film of the silent and early sound eras, the postwar brothel and red-light film, then the modern sex-work and trafficking drama

leaves.label: Political Drama
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is political power — winning and abusing office, or living under it, or communities torn by political conflict (Mr. Smith Goes to Washington, The Candidate, Yol, Leviathan). Films of militant struggle and revolution go to Revolutionary Film; political thrillers to A3; war to A9.
leaves.see: A3 Thriller & Mystery; A16-24 Journalism Film; A9 War Film
leaves.axis: by the relation to power: holding and seeking office, life under repression, then communal conflict and extremism

leaves.label: Revolutionary Film
leaves.breadth: Dramas of militants, uprisings, strikes and revolutionary movements
leaves.defn: A drama whose subject is the making of revolution or militant struggle — the activist cell, the uprising, the strike, the liberation movement, often itself made as militant cinema (Wind from the East, Ice, Milestones, Finye, Good Morning, Night, Rang De Basanti). Films of life under a regime without organised resistance stay in Political Drama.
leaves.aliases: militant cinema; cinéma militant; revolutionary cinema
leaves.axis: by era of the struggle: socialist-realist and early revolutionary films, the 1967–79 militant-cinema wave, then post-1980 activism and uprising

leaves.label: Journalism Film
leaves.defn: A drama of reporters and the press, the getting or abusing of a story being the engine (Ace in the Hole, Good Night, and Good Luck., She Said). Newspaper thrillers go to A3.
leaves.see: A16-23 Political Drama; A3 Thriller & Mystery

leaves.label: Legal Drama
leaves.defn: A drama of the law in action — the trial, the lawyer's case, the wrongful conviction (12 Angry Men, To Kill a Mockingbird, Anatomy of a Murder, Anatomy of a Fall). A whodunit with a courtroom climax goes to A3.
leaves.aliases: courtroom drama; trial film; legal thriller
leaves.see: A3 Thriller & Mystery; A16-22 Social Problem Film
leaves.axis: by the kind of proceeding: the criminal trial, political and war-crimes trials, courts-martial, wrongful conviction and the death penalty, then the lawyer's civil case

leaves.label: Medical Drama
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is illness, disability or medicine — the dying patient, the disabled life, dementia, the doctor's work (Ikiru, The Father, Scent of a Woman, Bringing Out the Dead). Mental illness as inner state goes to A16-7.
leaves.axis: by the condition: doctors and carers, terminal illness, disability, then dementia

leaves.label: Religious Drama
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is faith — the priest's or nun's vocation, doubt, conversion or fanaticism (Diary of a Country Priest, Winter Light, Ida, First Reformed). Evangelical industry films go to A16-28; biblical epics to A8.
leaves.aliases: faith drama; spiritual film; transcendental style
leaves.see: A16-28 Christian Film; A8 Historical & Period Film
leaves.axis: by who carries the faith: priests and pastors, nuns and convents, then lay believers and seekers

leaves.label: Christian Film
leaves.defn: A film made by or for the evangelical Christian film industry, whose plot affirms faith (Fireproof, God's Not Dead, The Shack); includes the early race-film religious dramas (The Blood of Jesus). Art-house faith dramas go to A16-27.

leaves.label: Sports Film
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is athletic contest outside the sports given their own leaves — ice and snow, field games, golf and racket sports, athletics, gymnastics, boards, racing animals and bicycles, cue games and combat sports (Chariots of Fire, The Hustler, Miracle, Lagaan). Boxing, baseball, American football, basketball, football and motor racing have leaves A16-30 to A16-35.
leaves.axis: by the sport: ice and snow first, then field games, golf and racket sports, running and swimming, gymnastics and cheer, board sports, horse and bicycle racing, cue and table games, and combat sports last

leaves.label: Boxing Film
leaves.defn: A sports drama of the prizefighter and the ring, including cage fighting (Rocky, Fat City, Million Dollar Baby, Creed).
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Baseball Film
leaves.defn: A sports drama of baseball (The Pride of the Yankees, The Natural, Bull Durham, Moneyball).

leaves.label: American Football Film
