leaves.defn: A sports drama of American (gridiron) football (Rudy, Remember the Titans, Friday Night Lights, Any Given Sunday).

leaves.label: Basketball Film
leaves.defn: A sports drama of basketball (Hoosiers, He Got Game, Coach Carter, Love & Basketball).

leaves.label: Association Football Film
leaves.defn: A sports drama of association football (Victory, Bend It Like Beckham, Goal! The Dream Begins, Next Goal Wins).

leaves.label: Auto Racing Film
leaves.defn: A sports drama of motor racing (Grand Prix, Le Mans, Rush, Ford v Ferrari).
leaves.see: A16-29 Sports Film; A7 Action & Martial Arts

leaves.label: Road Movie
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is the journey itself — leaving home, the open road and what it changes (Wild Strawberries, Thelma & Louise, The Straight Story, Nomadland). A journey driven by the bond of two friends goes to A16-37; migrant crossings to A16-21.
leaves.see: A16-37 Buddy Film; A16-21 Immigrant Film
leaves.axis: by who travels and why: the family trip, lovers and outlaws on the run, motorcycle journeys, pilgrimages on foot, quests of search and memory, errands and funeral journeys, then drifters and nomads

leaves.label: Buddy Film
leaves.defn: A film whose engine is the friendship of two (or a small band of) companions, here mostly on a trip together (Planes, Trains & Automobiles, Rain Man, Y tu mamá también, The Trip). Cop-buddy action goes to A7; pure road comedy also to A12.
leaves.aliases: buddy road movie; female buddy film
leaves.see: A16-36 Road Movie; A12 Comedy; A7 Action & Martial Arts
leaves.axis: by the pairing: male friends, female friends, mismatched pairs, then groups of friends

leaves.label: Animal Film
leaves.defn: A drama whose engine is the bond between people and an animal, or an animal's own odyssey (Lassie Come Home, The Black Stallion, Au hasard Balthazar, Hachi: A Dog's Tale). Animated talking-animal films go to C12; wildlife documentary to A19.
leaves.see: A17 Children's & Family Film; A19 Documentary
leaves.axis: by the animal: dogs first, then horses, then wild and farm animals

leaves.label: Pre-Code Hollywood Film
leaves.defn: The Hollywood dramas of c. 1929–1934, between the coming of sound and strict enforcement of the Production Code, that treated sex, adultery, prostitution, crime and Depression misery with a frankness later forbidden (Baby Face, Red-Headed Woman, Heroes for Sale). Pre-Code gangster, horror and musical films stay in their genres.
leaves.axis: the era's own cycles

leaves.label: Brat Pack Film
leaves.defn: The mid-1980s American youth films starring the 'Brat Pack' (Emilio Estevez, Molly Ringwald, Judd Nelson, Ally Sheedy, Andrew McCarthy, Rob Lowe, Demi Moore, Anthony Michael Hall), above all John Hughes's teen films and Joel Schumacher's post-college ensemble (The Breakfast Club, St. Elmo's Fire).
leaves.see: A16-14 Teen Film; A12-37 Teen Comedy

leaves.label: Heimatfilm
leaves.defn: The German and Austrian homeland film, dominant c. 1947–1960s: Alpine, Black Forest and heath landscapes, foresters, dirndls, folk song and reconciled village communities (Black Forest Girl, Grün ist die Heide), and the critical Neuer or Anti-Heimatfilm of the late 1960s–70s that inverted it.
leaves.axis: phase

leaves.label: Rubble Film (Trümmerfilm)
leaves.defn: The German films of 1946–1949 shot among the bombed ruins, about guilt, returning soldiers, black markets and survival in the immediate post-war (The Murderers Are Among Us, In Those Days).

subs.label: Children's & Family Film
subs.axis: Axis: by the family-film engine: fantasy and animals first, then children's adventure, drama and comedy, then the teen television film, then the Christmas film by mode.

leaves.label: Children's Fantasy Film
leaves.defn: A fantasy made first for children, in which magic, a magical nanny, a creature friend or a spooky night enters a child's world (Mary Poppins, Willy Wonka & the Chocolate Factory, Pete's Dragon, The Witches). A wizarding-school saga goes to A6-6; a Disney Channel television film to A17-6.
leaves.see: A6-4 Portal Fantasy; A6-6 Contemporary Fantasy; A17-6 Disney Channel Original Movie
leaves.axis: by the magic's form: musical and magical-nanny fantasy, storybook adaptations, creature and magic-friend fantasy, then Halloween and spooky fantasy

leaves.label: Animal Adventure Film
leaves.defn: A family film whose hero is an animal: a dog, horse, whale or talking creature, live or computer-generated (Homeward Bound: The Incredible Journey, Babe, Free Willy, Paddington). An animated feature goes to C12.
leaves.aliases: animal film; dog film; talking-animal film
leaves.see: C12 Animated Feature; A12-35 Family Comedy
leaves.axis: by the animal: dog films, talking-animal and CGI-hybrid films, then wild-animal and horse stories

leaves.label: Children's Adventure Film
leaves.defn: A family adventure in which a gang of children or a child hero goes treasure-hunting, on the run, or undercover as a kid spy (The Goonies, Holes, Spy Kids: Armageddon, Agent Cody Banks). A child alone at home at Christmas goes to A17-9.
leaves.see: A6-20 Treasure-Hunt Adventure; A12-35 Family Comedy
leaves.axis: by the children's mission: gang and treasure adventures, then kid spies and kid capers

leaves.label: Children's Drama
leaves.defn: A serious film for and about children: a classic children's novel or a contemporary story of a child facing illness, difference, grief or loneliness (The Secret Garden 1993, A Little Princess, Like Stars on Earth, Wonder). A coming-of-age drama for adults goes to A16.
leaves.axis: by source: classic children's novels first, then contemporary and world children's dramas

leaves.label: Disney Channel Original Movie
leaves.defn: A made-for-television feature of the Disney Channel tradition for tweens and teens: musicals, magic-and-monster comedies and school or sports stories (High School Musical, Halloweentown, Descendants, Cadet Kelly). A theatrical family comedy goes to A12-35.
leaves.see: A12-35 Family Comedy; A14 Musical & Dance Film; B10 Children's Series
leaves.axis: by the engine: tween musicals, magic and monster comedies, then tween comedy and sports films

leaves.label: Christmas Carol Adaptation
leaves.defn: A film adapting Dickens's A Christmas Carol: a miser visited by ghosts of Christmas past, present and future, straight or updated (A Christmas Carol 1951, Scrooge, Scrooged, The Muppet Christmas Carol).

leaves.label: Christmas Fantasy Film
leaves.defn: A Christmas film whose engine is the holiday's magic: Santa Claus and his workshop, an angel or Christmas miracle, or Santa turned action hero (Miracle on 34th Street, It's a Wonderful Life, Elf, The Santa Clause). Dickens's ghosts go to A17-7.
leaves.aliases: Santa Claus film; Christmas miracle film
leaves.see: A17-7 Christmas Carol Adaptation; A12-28 Fantasy Comedy
leaves.axis: by the holiday magic: Santa Claus films, angels and Christmas miracles, then Christmas action and horror

leaves.label: Christmas Family Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy whose engine is the Christmas season itself: a child left home alone, the family gathering, the office party, the pageant (Home Alone, A Christmas Story, National Lampoon's Christmas Vacation, Bad Santa). A Christmas love story goes to A17-10.
leaves.see: A17-10 Christmas Romantic Comedy; A12 Comedy
leaves.axis: by the Christmas set-up: kids at Christmas, family gatherings, adult and raunchy comedy, specials and musical revues, then Christmas comedy beyond Hollywood

leaves.label: Christmas Romantic Comedy
leaves.defn: A romantic comedy timed to and powered by the Christmas season: a holiday meet-cute, a fake date home for Christmas, a snowed-in prince (The Shop Around the Corner, The Holiday, A Christmas Prince, Happiest Season). A non-seasonal rom-com goes to A13.
leaves.see: A13 Romance; A17-9 Christmas Family Comedy
leaves.axis: by the romance: classic Hollywood Christmas romance, royal and fairy-tale Christmas romance, then the contemporary holiday rom-com

subs.label: Popular Cinema Modes
subs.axis: Axis: by popular industry and its named mode: Indian masala by language industry first, then the other South Asian, African and Turkish popular cinemas.

leaves.label: Golden Age of Hindi Cinema
leaves.defn: A Hindi studio-era film of the classical Bombay industry (c. 1946 to the early 1970s): song-and-dance melodrama, romance and social drama built around playback songs and stars such as Raj Kapoor, Dilip Kumar, Dev Anand and Nargis, by directors such as Raj Kapoor, Mehboob Khan, Bimal Roy, Vijay Anand, V. Shantaram and Shakti Samanta (Awaara, Shree 420, Devdas, Madhumati, Guide, Pakeezah). Later star masala from c. 1973 goes to A18-1; the art-house strand to A1-6.

leaves.label: Bollywood Masala
leaves.defn: A Hindi popular film in the masala mode: action, romance, comedy, family melodrama and song-and-dance combined around a star (Sholay, Dilwale Dulhania Le Jayenge, Dabangg, Jawan). A big-budget multilingual South Indian release goes to A18-4.
leaves.see: A18-4 Pan-Indian Film; A13 Romance; A14 Musical & Dance Film
leaves.axis: era (the field's own periodisation of Hindi masala)

leaves.label: Tamil Masala
leaves.defn: A Tamil-language popular film in the masala mode built around a mass hero, punch dialogues, songs and social messages (Baasha, Sivaji, Ghilli, Vikram). A pan-Indian multilingual epic goes to A18-4.
leaves.see: A18-3 Telugu Masala; A18-4 Pan-Indian Film
leaves.axis: by star and maker: superstar vehicles, Vijay and Ajith mass films, Shankar's vigilante spectacles, the Lokesh Cinematic Universe, then new Tamil mass cinema

leaves.label: Telugu Masala
leaves.defn: A Telugu-language popular film in the masala mode: a mass hero, family sentiment, comedy and action set pieces (Pokiri, Magadheera, Ala Vaikunthapurramuloo, Dasara). A pan-Indian multilingual epic goes to A18-4.
leaves.see: A18-2 Tamil Masala; A18-4 Pan-Indian Film

leaves.label: Pan-Indian Film
leaves.defn: A South Indian big-budget spectacle made and released simultaneously in several Indian languages for a national market (Baahubali: The Beginning, K.G.F: Chapter 1, RRR, Pushpa: The Rise - Part 1).
leaves.see: A18-1 Bollywood Masala; A18-3 Telugu Masala; A6-11 Mythological Fantasy

leaves.label: Malayalam Mass Film
leaves.defn: A Malayalam-language star action film in the mass mode, from political-gangster sagas to ensemble fight films (Lucifer, King of Kotha, RDX: Robert Dony Xavier, Rifle Club).
leaves.see: A18-2 Tamil Masala; A18-4 Pan-Indian Film

leaves.label: Dhallywood & Lollywood Masala
leaves.defn: A masala film from the Bengali, Bangladeshi, Pakistani or Sri Lankan popular industries (Toofan, Taandob, The Legend of Maula Jatt, Teefa In Trouble).

leaves.label: Nollywood
leaves.defn: A Nigerian popular feature of the Lagos-centred industry, from video-era melodrama to New Nollywood comedies and crime films (Osuofia in London, The Wedding Party, King of Boys, The Black Book).
leaves.axis: era of the Nigerian industry

leaves.label: Yeşilçam
leaves.defn: A Turkish popular film of the Istanbul studio era (c. 1950–1990): melodramas, school comedies and historical adventures (The Chaos Class, Tosun Pasha, My Dear Brother, The Girl with the Red Scarf).
leaves.axis: popular genre cycle of the Yeşilçam studio era

leaves.label: Wakaliwood
leaves.defn: An ultra-low-budget action film from Wakaliga, Kampala, made by Ramon Film Productions with homemade effects and a live 'video joker' narration (Who Killed Captain Alex?, Bad Black, Crazy World).
leaves.see: A7-17 Exploitation Action Film; A18-7 Nollywood

leaves.label: Ozploitation
leaves.defn: The Australian low-budget exploitation boom of c. 1971–1990 under the 10BA tax concession: ocker sex comedies, bikie films, outback horror, kung-fu and car-crash action (Stone, Alvin Purple, Patrick, Turkey Shoot, Dead End Drive-In).
leaves.see: A1-23 Australian New Wave; A10-10 Meat Pie Western

subs.label: Documentary
subs.axis: Axis: by documentary mode first (observational, ethnographic, poetic, essay, personal, archival, hybrid, propaganda), then by subject (politics, investigation, crime, war, history, people, art, cinema, music, sport, travel, nature); mondo last.

leaves.label: Direct Cinema & Cinéma Vérité
leaves.defn: A documentary of the 1960s–80s observational movements, or by their founding filmmakers, made by watching events as they happen with lightweight sync-sound cameras, no narration and minimal intervention (Primary, Chronicle of a Summer, Titicut Follies, Salesman, Grey Gardens). Later observational films go to Institutional, Work & Labour, Family or Observational Documentary; a first-person or reflexive film goes to A19-5; a staged film to A19-7.
leaves.axis: by national school, with Frederick Wiseman as his own section

leaves.label: Institutional Documentary
leaves.breadth: Observational documentaries (1990–) set inside a single institution: schools, hospitals, courts, prisons, parliaments, museums.
leaves.defn: An observational documentary made since 1990 that watches the daily working of one institution — a school, hospital, court, prison, campaign or museum — from inside (To Be and to Have, The Waiting Room, Starless Dreams, Boys State, De humani corporis fabrica).
leaves.axis: by kind of institution

leaves.label: Work & Labour Documentary
leaves.breadth: Observational documentaries (1990–) of work: factories, mines, farms, fishing, trades and offices.
leaves.defn: An observational documentary made since 1990 that follows people at work — in factories, mines, fields, kitchens or offices (Workingman's Death, Our Daily Bread, Machines, Honeyland, American Factory).
leaves.axis: by era

leaves.label: Family Documentary
leaves.breadth: Observational documentaries (1990–) of families, couples and private lives, often followed over years.
leaves.defn: An observational documentary made since 1990 that follows a family, a couple or a private life at close range, often over years (Love and Diane, Last Train Home, Three Sisters, The Wolfpack, Time).
leaves.axis: by era

leaves.label: Observational Documentary
leaves.breadth: Observational documentaries (1990–) of communities, neighbourhoods, borders and places.
leaves.defn: An observational documentary made since 1990 that watches a community, neighbourhood or place without narration or interview (Bread Day, En Construcción, 45365, Sacro GRA, Fire at Sea, Hale County This Morning, This Evening). Films centred on one institution, on work or on a family have their own leaves.
leaves.axis: by era

leaves.label: Ethnographic Film
leaves.defn: A documentary that records and interprets a culture or way of life, from Flaherty to sensory ethnography (Nanook of the North, Dead Birds, Leviathan, Manakamana).
leaves.see: A19-1 Direct Cinema & Cinéma Vérité; A19-7 Docufiction
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: City Symphony
leaves.defn: A feature-length silent-era documentary portraying a city's day as a rhythmic montage (Berlin: Symphony of a Metropolis, Man with a Movie Camera). City-symphony shorts sit in A21-12.
leaves.see: A21-12 Documentary Short; A20-5 Non-Narrative Film

leaves.label: Essay Film
leaves.defn: A documentary that argues or meditates in a personal voice, usually through first-person narration over assembled images, here about images and cinema themselves, art and thought, or identity and the body (F for Fake, Histoire(s) du cinéma, Los Angeles Plays Itself, Tongues Untied, Blue). Essays on history and politics go to Political Essay Film; on place, cities and travel to Landscape Film; on the filmmaker's own life to A19-5.
leaves.see: A19-5 Diary Film; A19-6 Compilation Film
secs: Essays on Cinema & the Moving Image
leaves.axis: by the essay's object: cinema and images, art and thought, then identity and the body

leaves.label: Political Essay Film
leaves.breadth: essay films on history, politics and society
leaves.defn: An essay film whose object is history, politics or society, argued in a personal voice over assembled or found images — the militant essays of Marker and the Dziga Vertov Group, and their heirs in Farocki, Akomfrah, Curtis and Peck (A Grin Without a Cat, Ici et ailleurs, Handsworth Songs, Nostalgia for the Light, I Am Not Your Negro).
leaves.aliases: historical essay film; militant essay film; film-tract
leaves.axis: by era

leaves.label: Landscape Film
leaves.breadth: essay films about places, cities, landscapes and journeys
leaves.defn: An essay film that meditates on a place — a city, landscape, territory or journey — through observation and voice, including psychogeographic and travel essays (Sans Soleil, News from Home, London, My Winnipeg, Of Time and the City).
leaves.aliases: city essay; travel essay film; psychogeographic film
leaves.axis: by era

leaves.label: Diary Film
leaves.defn: A first-person documentary whose subject is the filmmaker's own life as it is lived and recorded — the film diary, the home movie, the video or digital self-portrait, the chronicle of illness, exile or confinement (Reminiscences of a Journey to Lithuania, Sherman's March, Tarnation, Dear Diary, This Is Not a Film). A film that turns the camera on the filmmaker's parents, siblings or family history goes to the Family Documentary.
leaves.aliases: personal documentary, autobiographical documentary, first-person documentary
secs: Film Diaries of the New American Cinema & After
leaves.axis: by the diary's form and occasion: home movies first, the New American Cinema film diary and the essayistic life-diary, auteurs' diaries and self-portraits, then diaries of illness, exile and political confinement, and the video and digital diary last

leaves.label: Compilation Film
leaves.defn: A documentary built mainly from pre-existing archival footage, edited without new interviews (The Atomic Cafe, Apollo 11, They Shall Not Grow Old, State Funeral). Artist appropriation of footage goes to A20-4.
leaves.see: A20-4 Found-Footage Film; A19-13 Historical Documentary
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Docufiction
leaves.defn: A film that blends documentary and fiction: staged or re-enacted scenes with real people, real people performing scripted or semi-scripted fictions, or fiction shot as documentary (Fires Were Started, Caesar Must Die, Four Daughters, The Arbor). Includes mockumentary features. Docufictions in which a community enacts its own culture go to Ethnofiction.
leaves.see: A19-1 Direct Cinema & Cinéma Vérité; A19-2 Ethnographic Film
leaves.axis: by how fact and fiction are joined: the staged story documentary, re-enactment, the fake documentary, hybrid fiction with non-actors, then the self-reflexive docufiction

leaves.label: Ethnofiction
leaves.breadth: Docufiction in which a community plays itself within its own culture
leaves.defn: A docufiction in which members of a people or community — often indigenous, rural, nomadic or colonised — act out stories in their own setting, language and customs, so that the fiction serves as ethnography (Chang, Louisiana Story, Jaguar, Farrebique, Alamar, The Dead and the Others). Staged films about urban or institutional subjects stay in Docufiction; non-staged fieldwork goes to Ethnographic Film.
leaves.axis: by era: the silent and classical staged-ethnography film, Rouch and the ethnofiction of 1960–1999, then contemporary ethnofiction

leaves.label: Propaganda Film
leaves.defn: A documentary made by or for a state or cause to persuade a mass audience (Triumph of the Will, Why We Fight, The Negro Soldier). Wartime sponsored shorts go to A21-14.
leaves.see: A21-14 Sponsored Film; A19-12 War Documentary
leaves.axis: state / political tradition

leaves.label: Political Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary that takes a side on a public issue or follows a political movement, campaign or politician (Roger & Me, Harlan County U.S.A., 13th, The Square). Environmental causes go to Environmental Documentary, films made inside 1957–1990 militant movements to Militant Cinema, LGBTQ liberation and rights to LGBTQ Documentary; exposés of hidden wrongdoing to A19-10.
leaves.aliases: advocacy documentary, activist documentary, social-issue documentary
leaves.see: A19-10 Investigative Documentary; A19-8 Propaganda Film
leaves.axis: by the cause: first-person polemic, labour, civil and human rights, women's movements, elections and politicians, then protest and uprisings

leaves.label: Environmental Documentary
leaves.breadth: Documentaries of ecological causes: pollution, climate, food and animals, land defence
leaves.defn: A documentary that argues an ecological cause — industrial pollution and nuclear risk, climate change, the food system and animal welfare, or a community's defence of its land and water (Minamata, An Inconvenient Truth, Food, Inc., The Cove, Virunga). A nature film without an argument goes to Nature Documentary.
leaves.axis: by the cause: pollution and disaster, climate and the planet, food and animals, then land, water and indigenous defence

leaves.label: Militant Cinema
leaves.breadth: Documentaries made inside a movement as its weapon, 1957–1990: collectives, Newsreel, Third Cinema
leaves.defn: A documentary made from inside a struggle by its participants or a film collective, as an instrument of the movement rather than a report on it, in the cycle from the late 1950s to 1990 (The Battle of Chile, Summer in Narita, Finally Got the News…, The Nightcleaners, Patu!). Later activist films stay in Political Documentary.
leaves.aliases: cinéma militant; Third Cinema; Newsreel; collective documentary
secs: North American Newsreel & Black Radical Cinema
leaves.axis: by national movement: Japanese collectives, Latin American Third Cinema, European militant collectives, North American Newsreel and Black radical cinema, then Asia, Africa and Oceania

leaves.label: LGBTQ Documentary
leaves.breadth: Documentaries of gay, lesbian and trans liberation, AIDS activism and LGBTQ rights
leaves.defn: A documentary about LGBTQ people as a political community — gay liberation and its histories, AIDS activism, trans lives and the global fight for LGBTQ rights (Word Is Out, The Times of Harvey Milk, How to Survive a Plague, Kokomo City). A portrait of one queer artist goes to Biographical Documentary.
leaves.aliases: queer documentary; gay and lesbian documentary
leaves.axis: by the cause: liberation and queer histories, AIDS activism, then trans lives and LGBTQ rights worldwide

leaves.label: Investigative Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary that uncovers concealed wrongdoing through journalistic investigation (Inside Job, Citizenfour, Going Clear, Collective). A criminal case goes to A19-11.
leaves.see: A19-11 True Crime Documentary; A19-9 Political Documentary
leaves.axis: by the target of the investigation: corporations, the state, cults and belief, disasters, then media and technology

leaves.label: True Crime Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary reconstructing a specific crime, its investigation or trial (The Thin Blue Line, Paradise Lost, Capturing the Friedmans, The Tinder Swindler).
leaves.axis: by the kind of case: murder and violent crime, trials and wrongful convictions, fraud and hoaxes, then abuse and exploitation

leaves.label: War Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary filmed in or about a war or armed conflict, often from the front line (Restrepo, For Sama, 20 Days in Mariupol, Hearts and Minds). Archival war compilations go to A19-6; wartime state films to A19-8.
leaves.see: A19-8 Propaganda Film; A9 War Film
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Historical Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary reconstructing a past event or period through testimony and research (Shoah, The Act of Killing, Freedom Riders, The Fog of War).
leaves.see: A19-6 Compilation Film; A19-12 War Documentary
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Biographical Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary portrait of one famous or public person — an entertainer, politician, activist, writer, thinker or scientist — other than a musician, artist, filmmaker or athlete (Won't You Be My Neighbor?, RBG, Joan Didion: The Center Will Not Hold, The Unknown Known). Portraits of private, unknown people go to Portrait Documentary; of a subculture or community to Subculture Documentary.
leaves.see: A19-15 Art Documentary; A19-17 Rockumentary; A11 Biographical Film
leaves.axis: by the subject's public sphere: entertainment, public life, then letters and ideas

leaves.label: Portrait Documentary
leaves.breadth: documentary portraits of private, unknown or eccentric people
leaves.defn: A documentary portrait of a private person or a few ordinary people — an eccentric, an obsessive, a life at the margins, or a life followed over years — whose interest lies in the person, not their fame (Portrait of Jason, Gates of Heaven, American Movie, Grizzly Man, Stevie, the Up series).
leaves.aliases: documentary portrait; character documentary; portrait film
leaves.axis: by era of making

leaves.label: Subculture Documentary
leaves.breadth: documentaries portraying a subculture, scene or community of enthusiasts
leaves.defn: A documentary portrait of a group defined by a shared identity, scene or passion — drag and queer communities, youth and outlaw subcultures, hobbyists, fans and believers (Paris Is Burning, The Cockettes, Hell's Angels Forever, Wordplay, Indie Game: The Movie).
leaves.axis: by the kind of subculture

leaves.label: Art Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary about a visual artist, designer, architect, dancer or fashion house and their work (Crumb, Pina, Finding Vivian Maier, Exit Through the Gift Shop).
leaves.see: A19-14 Biographical Documentary; Making-of & Film History Documentary
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Making-of Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary about the making of a particular film, series or stage production: the shoot, the rehearsal, the troubled or abandoned project, or the production looked back on (Hearts of Darkness, Burden of Dreams, Lost in La Mancha, Jodorowsky's Dune). Portraits of filmmakers and actors go to Filmmaker Portrait Documentary; histories of cinema to Film History Documentary.
leaves.see: A19-4 Essay Film; A19-15 Art Documentary
leaves.axis: by the production's fate and the film's stance: the on-set record, the troubled or unmade production, the retrospective making-of, then the rehearsal film

leaves.label: Filmmaker Portrait Documentary
leaves.breadth: Documentary portraits of directors, actors and other film people
leaves.defn: A documentary portrait of a person of the cinema — a director, actor, star or craftsperson — built on interviews, archive and the subject's films (Directed by John Ford, Cinéastes de notre temps, Marlene, My Best Fiend, Life Itself, De Palma). The making of one production goes to Making-of Documentary.
leaves.aliases: film-director portrait; actor documentary; Cinéastes de notre temps
leaves.axis: by the sitter: directors first, then actors and stars, then crew, critics, programmers and archivists

leaves.label: Film History Documentary
leaves.breadth: Documentaries on the history, genres, crafts and criticism of cinema
leaves.defn: A documentary that tells the history of cinema or a part of it — a national cinema, studio or era, a genre or cult, the screen image of a group, or a craft or way of watching (The Celluloid Closet, Visions of Light, A Personal Journey with Martin Scorsese Through American Movies, Not Quite Hollywood).
leaves.aliases: documentary on film history; cinema history documentary
leaves.axis: by the history told: national, studio and industry histories, genre and cult histories, representation on screen, then craft, criticism and cinephilia

leaves.label: Rockumentary
leaves.defn: A documentary about rock and pop musicians or their music, built on interviews, archive and backstage footage rather than a complete performance (Dont Look Back, Amy, Searching for Sugar Man, The Decline of Western Civilization). Jazz, blues, roots and world music go to Jazz, Blues & Roots Music Documentary; hip-hop to Hip-Hop Documentary; classical, electronic and experimental music to Classical & Art Music Documentary; a film of a performance to A19-18.
leaves.see: A19-18 Concert Film; Musical & Dance Film
leaves.axis: by subject: an artist's life, a star's self-portrait or tour, a band or recording, then scenes and movements

leaves.label: Jazz, Blues & Roots Music Documentary
leaves.breadth: Documentaries of jazz, blues, gospel, folk-roots and world music traditions
leaves.defn: A music documentary about jazz, the blues and gospel, American roots music, or a traditional or world-music culture (Thelonious Monk: Straight, No Chaser, Let's Get Lost, Always for Pleasure, Say Amen, Somebody, Buena Vista Social Club). Rock and pop go to Rockumentary.
leaves.aliases: jazz documentary; roots music documentary; world music documentary
leaves.axis: by tradition: jazz, then blues, gospel and American roots, then world and traditional music

leaves.label: Hip-Hop Documentary
leaves.breadth: Documentaries of rappers, DJs, crews and hip-hop culture
leaves.defn: A music documentary about hip-hop — a rapper's life, a crew or label, the history of MCing, DJing and breaking, or a national hip-hop scene (Rhyme & Reason, Scratch, Beats, Rhymes & Life, Time is Illmatic, Slingshot Hip Hop).
leaves.axis: by subject: artist portraits, crews and hip-hop history, then hip-hop outside the United States

leaves.label: Classical & Art Music Documentary
leaves.breadth: Documentaries of composers, classical performers, and electronic and experimental music
leaves.defn: A music documentary about art music — a composer, a classical performer or conductor, or the pioneers of electronic and experimental sound (A Stravinsky Portrait, Glass: A Portrait of Philip in Twelve Parts, Seymour: An Introduction, Ennio, Theremin: An Electronic Odyssey). A filmed opera or concert goes to A19-18.
leaves.axis: by subject: composers, performers and conductors, then electronic and experimental music

leaves.label: Concert Film
leaves.defn: A film whose substance is a recorded live performance, concert, tour show or festival (Monterey Pop, The Last Waltz, Stop Making Sense, Taylor Swift: The Eras Tour).
leaves.see: A19-17 Rockumentary; Live Event & Sports Television
leaves.axis: by the performance: festivals, rock and soul concerts, pop arena tours, then stage and studio performances

leaves.label: Sports Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary about an athlete, team, match or competition (When We Were Kings, Senna, Hoop Dreams, The King of Kong). Official Olympic films go to A19-20.
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Olympic Film
leaves.defn: An official or authorised feature film of an Olympic Games (Olympia, Tokyo Olympiad, Visions of Eight, 16 Days of Glory).
leaves.axis: by era of the Olympic film: interwar, postwar national and auteur films, then the Greenspan and later era

leaves.label: Travelogue Film
leaves.defn: A documentary organised as a journey through places, recording what the traveller sees (This Is Cinerama, Calcutta, ¡Vivan las antípodas!).

leaves.label: Mountaineering & Expedition Film
leaves.defn: A documentary of an expedition or feat of endurance in mountains, ice, ocean or wilderness (Kon-Tiki, Touching the Void, Free Solo, The Rescue).
leaves.aliases: mountain film, adventure documentary, expedition film
leaves.see: A19-21 Travelogue Film; A19-19 Sports Documentary
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Nature Documentary
leaves.defn: A documentary about animals, plants or the natural world (The Silent World, March of the Penguins, Microcosmos, My Octopus Teacher).
leaves.see: A19-9 Political Documentary; A21-13 Scientific Film
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Mondo Film
leaves.defn: A shock documentary of real or staged death, cruelty and taboo customs (Faces of Death, Orozco the Embalmer).

subs.label: Experimental & Avant-Garde
subs.axis: Axis: by avant-garde strategy for feature-length work: dream logic, underground, system, appropriation, tone poem, altered state, then avant-garde narrative.

leaves.label: Surrealist Film
leaves.defn: A film built on Surrealist dream logic, irrational juxtaposition and the disruption of bourgeois order (L'Age d'Or, The Exterminating Angel, The Holy Mountain, Eraserhead). Surrealist shorts sit in A21-15.
leaves.see: A21-15 Avant-Garde Short; A20-6 Psychedelic Film

leaves.label: Underground Film
leaves.defn: A low-budget, self-distributed avant-garde feature made outside the industry, often transgressive or camp (Flaming Creatures, Chelsea Girls, Pink Narcissus, Trash Humpers).
leaves.see: A1-19 New American Cinema; A1-22 No Wave Cinema
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Cinema Marginal
leaves.defn: A Brazilian underground film of the late 1960s, a trash-aesthetic, anarchic reply to Cinema Novo (The Red Light Bandit).
leaves.aliases: Cinema de Boca do Lixo, udigrudi
leaves.see: A1-16 Cinema Novo; A20-2 Underground Film
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Structural Film
leaves.defn: An experimental film whose shape is a predetermined system: fixed camera, duration, repetition or rule (Wavelength, Zorns Lemma, Empire, 13 Lakes).
leaves.see: A1-39 Slow Cinema; A21-15 Avant-Garde Short
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Found-Footage Film
leaves.defn: An experimental feature made by re-editing appropriated film material (Decasia, Star Spangled to Death, The Clock). Archival documentary goes to A19-6.
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Non-Narrative Film
leaves.defn: A feature without plot or characters, built as an audiovisual tone poem of images and music (Koyaanisqatsi, Baraka, Samsara).
leaves.see: A19-3 City Symphony; A19-23 Nature Documentary
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Psychedelic Film
leaves.defn: An experimental feature that simulates altered states through strobing colour, sound and disorientation (Head, Enter the Void, Lux Æterna).

leaves.label: Art Film
leaves.defn: A narrative feature whose avant-garde form (tableau, recitation, fragmentation, dream logic, anti-illusion) is its defining element (A Page of Madness, Limit, The Color of Pomegranates, Russian Ark, Holy Motors). The political-modernist 'counter-cinema' of Duras, Straub–Huillet, Godard and Rainer goes to Counter-Cinema; films made by gallery artists or for installation to Artists' Film & Video Installation; duration-based art films to A1-39 Slow Cinema.
leaves.axis: by era: the silent and interwar avant-garde feature, the poetic cinema of the 1960s–80s, then the later art-house avant-garde by period

leaves.label: Counter-Cinema
leaves.breadth: Political-modernist narrative features of the 1960s–80s that dismantle illusion: text, recitation, distanciation
leaves.defn: A narrative feature in the political-modernist tradition Peter Wollen named 'counter-cinema': estrangement over identification, text and recitation over drama, the soundtrack split from the image, the narrative opened to theory (India Song, From the Clouds to the Resistance, Riddles of the Sphinx, Film About a Woman Who..., Salomé). Its core is 1968–1990, with its auteurs' later work; dream and tableau art films without that programme stay in Art Film.
leaves.aliases: political modernism; cinéma de la modernité; Brechtian cinema
leaves.axis: by national tradition: France and Belgium; Italy, Iberia and Greece; the German-speaking and Central European wing; the Anglo-American feminist wing; the Third Cinema wing

leaves.label: Artists' Film & Video Installation
leaves.breadth: Narrative and quasi-narrative works by gallery artists, and moving-image installations
leaves.defn: A moving-image work made by a visual artist from the gallery world, shown as a feature, a cycle or a multi-screen installation (Cremaster 3, Rape, Manifesto, Inconsolable Memories, Primitive). Underground and experimental filmmakers outside the art world stay in Art Film or their own leaves.
leaves.aliases: artists' cinema; gallery film; moving-image installation
leaves.axis: by form and period: installations and exhibitions, then artists' features before and after 2010

leaves.label: Lettrist & Situationist Cinema
leaves.defn: The Paris avant-garde of Isidore Isou's Lettrists (1951–1952) and Guy Debord's Situationist International: 'discrepant' and anti-films that separate sound from image, scratch and blank the film strip, and détourn found images against the spectacle (Venom and Eternity, Howlings in Favour of de Sade, The Society of the Spectacle).
leaves.see: A19-4 Essay Film; A20-4 Found-Footage Film

subs.label: Short Film
subs.axis: Axis: by short-film mode: early cinema forms first, then fiction shorts by genre, then nonfiction shorts by purpose, avant-garde shorts last.

leaves.label: Actuality Film
leaves.defn: A pre-1910 single-shot or few-shot nonfiction film recording a real scene (Workers Leaving the Factory, The Arrival of a Train, Roundhay Garden Scene).
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Newsreel
leaves.defn: A short topical news film for theatrical release (Hindenburg Disaster Newsreel Footage, Tacoma Narrows Bridge Collapse, Faces of November).
leaves.see: A21-1 Actuality Film; A21-12 Documentary Short

leaves.label: Free Cinema
leaves.defn: The British documentary movement of 1956–1959 (Lindsay Anderson, Karel Reisz, Tony Richardson, Lorenza Mazzetti) whose six National Film Theatre programmes showed unscripted, personal films of working-class leisure and labour (O Dreamland, Every Day Except Christmas). Its directors went on to the British New Wave (A1-10).

leaves.label: Trick Film
leaves.defn: An early short built on camera tricks (stop substitution, multiple exposure) for magical effect (A Trip to the Moon, The India Rubber Head, Dream of a Rarebit Fiend).
leaves.axis: by country of production, largest first; other countries last

leaves.label: One-Reeler
leaves.defn: A silent narrative short of one reel or less, the story film of the nickelodeon era (The Great Train Robbery, A Corner in Wheat, The Musketeers of Pig Alley). Silent comedy shorts go to A21-5.
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Slapstick Short
leaves.defn: A silent or early-sound comedy short of physical gags, typically a one- or two-reeler (The Immigrant, One Week, The Music Box).
leaves.see: A21-8 Comedy Short Film; A12 Comedy
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Musical Short
leaves.defn: A short whose substance is a song or musical number: early sound musical shorts, soundies and long-form music videos (Black and Tan, Jammin' the Blues, Runaway, Anima).
leaves.see: A19-18 Concert Film; Musical & Dance Film
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Drama Short Film
leaves.defn: A live-action fiction short whose engine is realist drama — social circumstance, childhood, relationships, crime or war — rather than comedy or genre (The Lunch Date, Wasp, The Present, Two Cars, One Night). Poetic, literary and auteurist shorts go to Art-House Short Film.
leaves.see: A21-8 Comedy Short Film; A16 Drama
leaves.axis: by the dramatic engine: social realism, childhood, relationships, crime, then war

leaves.label: Art-House Short Film
leaves.breadth: poetic, literary and auteurist fiction shorts
leaves.defn: A live-action fiction short made in the art-film manner — a literary adaptation, a poetic or formally experimental narrative, or a short by an established auteur (A Day in the Country, Pull My Daisy, Machorka-Muff, The Human Voice, The Wonderful Story of Henry Sugar).
leaves.aliases: art film short; auteur short; literary short film
leaves.axis: by era

leaves.label: Comedy Short Film
leaves.defn: A sound-era live-action comedy short (Bottle Rocket, Six Shooter, Coffee and Cigarettes, An Irish Goodbye). Silent and early-sound slapstick goes to A21-5.
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Horror Short Film
leaves.defn: A live-action horror short (Lights Out, Saw, Tarantella, Frankenweenie).
leaves.see: A4 Horror; Science Fiction & Fantasy Short Film
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Science Fiction & Fantasy Short Film
leaves.defn: A live-action science-fiction or fantasy short (La Jetée, The Red Balloon, Electronic Labyrinth THX 1138 4EB, Rakka).
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Tie-In Short Film
leaves.defn: A short made to extend or promote an existing property or brand: studio one-shots, fan films, fake trailers, commissioned branded shorts (Marvel One-Shot: Agent Carter, Team Thor, Power Rangers, Castello Cavalcanti).
leaves.axis: by who made it and why: studio tie-ins, unofficial fan films, then commissioned branded shorts

leaves.label: Documentary Short
leaves.defn: A nonfiction short of the sound era observing people, work and social life at first hand — portraits, social observation and sport — not made as sponsored, scientific, political, poetic, essay, arts or ethnographic film (Le Sang des bêtes, Les Raquetteurs, Seven Up!, Talking Heads).
leaves.axis: by era for portrait and social shorts, then sport

leaves.label: Political Documentary Short
leaves.breadth: Short militant, activist and social-issue documentaries.
leaves.defn: A documentary short made to argue, mobilise or bear witness on a political or social cause — militant and revolutionary newsreels, anticolonial and activist films, war and social-issue reportage (Misère au Borinage, Afrique 50, Now, Hanoi Tuesday 13th, The White Helmets).
leaves.aliases: militant film; activist documentary short; social-issue documentary short
leaves.axis: by era: interwar and postwar militant film, the 1960s revolutionary and Third Cinema shorts, the 1970s collectives, then later activism

leaves.label: Poetic Documentary Short
leaves.breadth: Short documentaries organised by rhythm, image and mood rather than argument: city symphonies and lyrical studies of place and labour.
leaves.defn: A documentary short shaped by visual rhythm, montage and mood instead of exposition — city symphonies, lyrical studies of landscape, seasons and work (Manhatta, Rain, À propos de Nice, Islands of Fire, Beginning).
leaves.axis: city symphonies first, then poetic documentary by era

leaves.label: Essay Film Short
leaves.breadth: Short first-person and reflective nonfiction films that think through images, memory and history.
leaves.defn: A nonfiction short that reflects in a personal, argumentative voice, working through memory, history and images themselves (Night and Fog, The House Is Black, Reassemblage, Isle of Flowers, History and Memory).
leaves.aliases: short essay film; video essay; film essay
leaves.axis: by era

leaves.label: Arts Documentary Short
leaves.breadth: Short documentaries about artists, writers, filmmakers, musicians and dancers and their work.
leaves.defn: A documentary short whose subject is an art, an artist or a performance — painting and sculpture, writers, cinema and filmmakers, music and dance (Henri Matisse, Guernica, Jazz Dance, Werner Herzog Eats His Shoe, Kazuo Ohno).
leaves.aliases: art documentary short; music documentary short; dance documentary
leaves.axis: by art form

leaves.label: Ethnographic Short
leaves.breadth: Short fieldwork and ethnographic documentaries of ritual, craft and community life.
leaves.defn: A documentary short recording the ritual, craft or daily life of a community as ethnographic fieldwork (Trance and Dance in Bali, Les Maîtres fous, The Ax Fight, Gestes du repas).
leaves.aliases: ethnographic documentary short; visual anthropology short
leaves.axis: by era of fieldwork

leaves.label: Scientific Film
leaves.defn: A short that films natural or laboratory phenomena for science, often through microcinematography (The Sea Horse, The Vampire, The Love Life of the Octopus).
leaves.see: A19-23 Nature Documentary; A21-14 Sponsored Film

leaves.label: Sponsored Film
leaves.defn: A short commissioned by a government, company or institution to inform, instruct or promote (The Plow That Broke the Plains, Listen to Britain, Duck and Cover, Glass).
leaves.aliases: industrial film, educational film, government film
leaves.see: A19-8 Propaganda Film; A21-12 Documentary Short
leaves.axis: by sponsor: governments and wartime ministries, industry, then educational bodies

leaves.label: Avant-Garde Short
leaves.defn: A short of the first and postwar avant-garde built on dream, ritual, rhythm or the plastic image rather than story: Dada and cinéma pur, surrealist, trance and psychodrama, mythopoeic and underground films (Ballet Mécanique, Un Chien andalou, Meshes of the Afternoon, Scorpio Rising). Lyrical, landscape, structural, found-footage and video works have their own leaves.
leaves.axis: by avant-garde movement in historical order: Dada and cinéma pur, surrealism, the trance film, the mythopoeic and underground film, then later dream shorts

leaves.label: Lyrical Film
leaves.breadth: Personal, first-person avant-garde shorts in the Brakhage line: the camera as the maker's eye, body and memory.
leaves.defn: An avant-garde short in which the camera renders the filmmaker's own seeing, body, household or devotion, with handheld, rhythmic or painted imagery and no story (Anticipation of the Night, Window Water Baby Moving, Fuses, Notebook, Pneuma). A film observing a place goes to Landscape Film.
leaves.axis: by era, with Stan Brakhage's large body of work as its own section

leaves.label: Landscape Film (short)
leaves.breadth: Avant-garde shorts devoted to place: cities, land, water, weather and light observed through the camera.
leaves.defn: An avant-garde short whose subject is a place — a city, a stretch of land or water, the weather or light over time — observed rather than narrated (Fog Line, New York Portrait, Study of a River, Altiplano, Night Without Distance).
leaves.axis: by kind of place and method: city films, structural and durational landscapes, then land, water and light by era

leaves.label: Structural Short
leaves.breadth: Avant-garde shorts whose shape is set by a predetermined system or by the film material itself.
leaves.defn: An avant-garde short whose form is a predetermined structure or an exposure of the film material and apparatus — fixed frame, flicker, loop printing, rephotography, metric montage (Arnulf Rainer, The Flicker, Serene Velocity, Zorns Lemma, Berlin Horse).
leaves.aliases: structural-materialist film; metric film; flicker film
leaves.axis: by school: Austrian formal film, Warhol, American structural film, British and European structural-materialist film, Owen Land's parodies, then contemporary analog work

leaves.label: Found-Footage Short
leaves.breadth: Avant-garde shorts made by re-editing, reprinting or manipulating footage shot by others.
leaves.defn: An avant-garde short assembled from appropriated footage — newsreels, Hollywood films, home movies, archives — re-edited, optically reprinted or physically altered (Rose Hobart, A Movie, Free Fall, Passage à l'acte, Outer Space).
leaves.axis: by era

leaves.label: Video Art & Expanded Cinema
leaves.breadth: Artists' video, gallery moving-image works and expanded-cinema pieces.
leaves.defn: A short moving-image artwork made on video or for the gallery, or an expanded-cinema piece that works with projection, performance or installation (Vertical Roll, Global Groove, Line Describing a Cone, Semiotics of the Kitchen, How Not to Be Seen).
leaves.aliases: artists' video; artists' moving image; gallery film
leaves.axis: by era

leaves.label: Cinema of Transgression
leaves.defn: Nick Zedd's 1985 name for the New York Lower East Side Super-8 underground (Zedd, Richard Kern, Lydia Lunch, Tessa Hughes-Freeland) of deliberately shocking, punk, sexually and violently taboo films (Fingered, They Eat Scum).
leaves.see: A1-22 No Wave Cinema; A20-2 Underground Film

fams.label: Television
fams.test: a series, serial, programme or live broadcast made for television or subscription streaming: scripted series and miniseries (B1–B11), the long-running serial traditions (B12), unscripted formats (B13–B15) and live event and sports television (B16). Internet-native series — web series, online video channels, app micro-dramas — are not here: they belong to the future Interactive Entertainment Taxonomy.
key: B1 Drama Series — by the dramatic premise that drives the series, from home and the self (prestige, family, everyday life, social realism, identity, youth, romance) through the professions and institutions (medicine, law, politics, work, music, sport, the military) to history and genre (war, Western, historical, costume, heritage, period, adventure, disaster), then the real and the formal (docudrama, biography, literary adaptation, anthology).

B2 Korean Drama — by the genre the Korean industry and fandom name: romance forms first (rom-com, office, chaebol, melodrama), then the serial forms (makjang, revenge, family), the historical sageuk, professional and thriller genres, fantasy romance, and school and youth drama last

B3 Japanese Television Drama — by the genre or slot tradition Japanese broadcasting names: NHK serial forms first (asadora, taiga), then romance forms (trendy/getsuku, jun'ai, rom-com, office, school romance), then school, home and workplace dramas, gourmet and slice-of-life, and suspense and fantasy last

B4 Chinese-Language Drama — by genre tradition, costume and mythic genres first (epic, palace, intrigue, case, romance, time travel, wuxia, xianxia, xuanhuan, shenmo), then the Republican and state genres, then modern romance traditions, TVB last
B5 Boys' Love & Girls' Love Drama — by national tradition, Thai BL subdivided by its narrative engine, GL last
B6 Lakorn — by lakorn genre: melodrama, comedy, period and fantasy, remake, teen series

B7 Crime & Thriller Series — by the series' engine, from who investigates (police, detectives, sleuths, lawyers), to who commits the crime (gangs, dealers, crews, antiheroes, real criminals), to what threatens the protagonist (killers, minds, households, avengers, agents, states, games)

B8 Comedy Series — by comic engine and form: the domestic and workplace sitcom first, then friends, romance, youth and place, character and embarrassment, documentary and absurd forms, sketch, satire and parody, music and sport, the fantastic genres, crime and darkness; comedy-drama and tragicomedy last

B9 Speculative Series — by speculative premise — science-fiction premises first (space, aliens, time, technology, society's end), then costumed heroes, then fantasy worlds, then the supernatural among us, then horror; comic and anthology forms at the edges of each run.
B10 Children's Series — by age and mode: preschool first, then educational, sketch, sitcom and drama for older children, realistic and fantastic adventure; the seasonal Christmas calendar last
B11 Documentary Series — by subject: the natural world and science first, then history and war, lives, music, sport and the arts, travel and food, investigation; true crime and the paranormal last

B12 Serial Drama Traditions — by the named national or regional long-form serial tradition, Latin American telenovela first, then the Anglo-European soap opera, the Turkish dizi, South Asian serials, the Arabic musalsal, the Philippine teleserye last.
B13 Competition Formats — by what contestants are judged on — performance first (talent, singing, idol debut), then survival in a social game, then a craft, then knowledge, luck or play.
B14 Factual Entertainment Formats — by the real situation the camera arranges — courtship, everyday lives, an experiment, a transformation, a trick, a ghost hunt, a journey, a lesson, a ruling.
B15 Variety & Talk Formats — by what the host-led show presents — a revue of acts, cast members at play, conversation, comedy panels, clips, a single performance broadcast.

B16 Live Event & Sports Television — by the kind of live event the broadcast carries: sporting competition (by sport, then multi-sport and anthology), professional wrestling, then ceremonies, contests and pageants, civic and state occasions, fund-raising broadcasts, and stage performances (concert, theatre, circus, stand-up)

subs.label: Drama Series
subs.axis: Axis: by the dramatic premise that drives the series, from home and the self (prestige, family, everyday life, social realism, identity, youth, romance) through the professions and institutions (medicine, law, politics, work, music, sport, the military) to history and genre (war, Western, historical, costume, heritage, period, adventure, disaster), then the real and the formal (docudrama, biography, literary adaptation, anthology).

leaves.label: Prestige Drama
leaves.defn: A long-arc auteur drama whose engine is a morally compromised protagonist or a family/institution observed with novelistic ambition, made under the post-2000 cable "quality TV" banner (Mad Men, Six Feet Under, Billions, The Leftovers). A prestige crime saga goes to B7; a prestige family-business saga with succession at its centre goes to B1-3.
leaves.see: B1-3 Family Drama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series
leaves.axis: era of the prestige-TV cycle

leaves.label: Family Saga
leaves.defn: A serial that follows one family (or a few linked families) across generations or decades, so that historical time is the plot (Roots, Heimat, Pachinko, When Life Gives You Tangerines). A family drama set in one present moment goes to B1-3; a dynasty soap of wealth and scheming goes to B12-5.
leaves.see: B1-3 Family Drama; B1-22 Period Drama; B12-5 Prime-Time Soap Opera

leaves.label: Family Drama
leaves.defn: A series whose engine is the everyday bonds, conflicts and crises of one household or kin group in roughly its own present (Parenthood, This Is Us, The Waltons, Succession). A family followed across generations goes to B1-2; a family-revenge melodrama of the prime-time kind goes to B12-5.
leaves.aliases: domestic drama; family drama series; weekend drama (jumal deurama)
leaves.see: B1-2 Family Saga; B12-5 Prime-Time Soap Opera; B2 Korean Drama
leaves.axis: by what the family drama turns on, ensemble household first, then setting, wealth and marriage, the long broadcast family serial last

leaves.label: Slice-of-Life Drama
leaves.defn: A low-plot drama of ordinary lives, friendships and recoveries in which the texture of daily living, not an event, carries the series (thirtysomething, My Mister, Ode to Joy, Dear My Friends). Social-problem realism goes to B1-5; a romance-driven series goes to B1-9.
leaves.aliases: healing drama (hilling deurama); urban drama (dushi ju); ensemble drama
leaves.see: B1-5 Social Realist Drama; B1-9 Romantic Drama; C6 Slice of Life & Iyashikei Anime
leaves.axis: by whose daily life is observed: friends and young adults, the wounded and healing, women in the city, then older people and whole communities

leaves.label: Social Realist Drama
leaves.defn: A drama that renders a social condition (class, work, abuse, faith, migration) with documentary-leaning realism and makes that condition the subject (Boys from the Blackstuff, This Is England '86, I May Destroy You, Unorthodox). A dramatisation of a real public case goes to B1-26.
leaves.aliases: kitchen sink realism; social problem drama; issue drama
leaves.see: B1-4 Slice-of-Life Drama; B1-26 Docudrama; B1-29 Anthology Drama
leaves.axis: by the social condition examined: working-class and community life, personal trauma and social issues, faith communities, migrants last

leaves.label: LGBTQ Drama
leaves.defn: A series whose central lives, community and conflicts are those of gay, lesbian, bisexual or trans characters (Queer as Folk, The L Word, POSE, It's a Sin). A teen coming-out romance stays in B1-7; East and Southeast Asian BL/GL series go to B5.
leaves.aliases: queer television; gay drama; lesbian drama
leaves.see: B5 Boys' Love & Girls' Love Drama; B1-7 Teen Drama; B1-9 Romantic Drama

leaves.label: Teen Drama
leaves.defn: A drama centred on adolescents of secondary-school age and their school, friendships, first loves and coming of age (Beverly Hills, 90210, Degrassi, Skins, Euphoria). College and exam-coaching students go to B1-8; children's series for under-twelves go to B10.
leaves.aliases: high-school drama; teen soap; school drama (hakgyo deurama); seishun drama; tween drama; children's drama
leaves.see: B1-8 Campus Drama; B10 Children's Series; B5 Boys' Love & Girls' Love Drama
leaves.axis: by the teen engine: the glossy teen soap first, then issue drama, the school and its teachers, performing-arts schools, school violence, teen romance last

leaves.label: Campus Drama
leaves.defn: A drama of university students or exam aspirants in which the college or coaching institution is the world of the series (Felicity, Kota Factory, Aspirants, Hellcats). Secondary-school life goes to B1-7.
leaves.aliases: college drama; university drama; coaching-centre drama
leaves.see: B1-7 Teen Drama; B1-4 Slice-of-Life Drama

leaves.label: Romantic Drama
leaves.defn: A series whose main engine is a love story or the course of a relationship, played for feeling rather than laughs (Normal People, Virgin River, The Affair, Little Birds). A romantic comedy series goes to B8; a period romance in costume goes to B1-20; erotic film goes to A15.
leaves.aliases: romance series; love story; erotic drama
leaves.see: B1-20 Costume Drama; B8 Comedy Series; A15 Erotic Film
leaves.axis: by the romantic engine: contemporary love story first, literary and young-adult romance, small-town romance, then the affair and the frankly erotic last

leaves.label: Medical Drama
leaves.defn: A series set among doctors, nurses and patients in which treating illness and the life of the hospital or practice drive the episodes (ER, Grey's Anatomy, House, Doctor X). A medical-crime investigation goes to B7.
leaves.see: B1-13 Workplace Drama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series
leaves.axis: by where the medicine happens and who practises it: the hospital ensemble first, star doctors, emergency medicine, country doctors, nurses and allied staff, period medicine last

leaves.label: Legal Drama
leaves.defn: A series in which lawyers, prosecutors, judges or juries and their cases are the engine (L.A. Law, The Good Wife, Suits, Extraordinary Attorney Woo). A police procedural goes to B7; a courtroom docudrama goes to B1-26.
leaves.aliases: courtroom drama; lawyer drama; hōtei drama
leaves.see: B7 Crime & Thriller Series; B1-26 Docudrama
leaves.axis: by which side of the law carries the series: the firm, the defence case, the prosecutor, the bench and jury, then comic and thriller treatments

leaves.label: Political Drama
leaves.defn: A series about the getting and use of political power by presidents, ministers, legislators and their staffs (The West Wing, Borgen, House of Cards, The Diplomat). An espionage thriller goes to B7; a dramatised real scandal goes to B1-26.
leaves.see: B1-26 Docudrama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series
leaves.axis: by the seat of power: head of state and executive first, parliament and party, city and campaign politics, diplomacy and the security state last

leaves.label: Workplace Drama
leaves.defn: A series whose engine is the work and rivalries of one non-medical, non-legal profession or company (The Newsroom, Chicago Fire, Misaeng: Incomplete Life, The Bear). Hospitals go to B1-10, law to B1-11, the military to B1-16; a workplace sitcom goes to B8.
leaves.aliases: professional drama; office drama (opisu deurama); procedural drama
leaves.see: B1-10 Medical Drama; B1-11 Legal Drama; B8 Comedy Series
leaves.axis: by the trade: newsrooms and media, first responders, offices and business, kitchens and hotels and trades, show business, then the caring professions

leaves.label: Musical Drama Series
leaves.defn: A drama whose world is the making of music or dance performance, with performances carrying story and feeling (Nashville, Smash, Daisy Jones & the Six, The Singing Detective). A performing-arts high school goes to B1-7; a music competition show goes to B13.
leaves.aliases: backstage musical; music drama; music-industry drama
leaves.see: B1-7 Teen Drama; A14 Musical & Dance Film; B13 Competition Formats

leaves.label: Sports Drama
leaves.defn: A series in which training for and competing in a sport or game is the spine of the story (Friday Night Lights, Cobra Kai, Racket Boys, Hikaru no Go). Sports anime goes to C7; live sport goes to B16.
leaves.see: C7 Sports & Game Anime; B16 Live Event & Sports Television
leaves.axis: by the kind of contest: team sports first, combat sports, individual and racing sports, mind sports and esports last

leaves.label: Military Drama
leaves.defn: A series about serving soldiers, sailors or special forces and their units in peacetime or present-day deployments, where service life is the engine (SEAL Team, The Unit, Sea Patrol, D.P.). A historical war goes to B1-17.
leaves.see: B1-17 War Drama; B1-13 Workplace Drama

leaves.label: War Drama
leaves.defn: A series set inside a historical war, on the front or behind it, in which the war itself drives the story (Band of Brothers, Das Boot, Generation War, Tour of Duty). Present-day service life goes to B1-16; war film goes to A9.
leaves.see: B1-16 Military Drama; A9 War Film; B1-22 Period Drama
leaves.axis: by the war, the Second World War first, then earlier wars, partisan and resistance cycles, later wars, home fronts and war nursing last

leaves.label: Television Western
leaves.defn: A series set on the American (or a comparable) frontier whose codes of gun, horse, land and law shape the story (Gunsmoke, Bonanza, Deadwood, Yellowstone). Western film goes to A10.
leaves.axis: by kind of Western: the classic episodic Western first, frontier and pioneer drama, epic miniseries, the revisionist Western, the neo-Western last

leaves.label: Historical Drama
leaves.defn: A series that dramatises the great events and rulers of a pre-twentieth-century age, its wars, courts and faiths (I, Claudius, The Tudors, Vikings, The Crown). Ottoman historical dizi go to B12-6; Chinese and Korean court drama go to B4 and B2; a novel adaptation in period dress goes to B1-20.
leaves.see: B1-20 Costume Drama; B12-6 Dizi; B4 Chinese-Language Drama; B2 Korean Drama
leaves.axis: by age and power: the ancient world first, biblical and religious epics, medieval and Renaissance, royal courts, colonial and slavery-era America, national and imperial epics last

leaves.label: Costume Drama
leaves.defn: A series adapted from (or modelled on) a pre-1900 novel, whose period manners, marriages and class are the drama (Pride and Prejudice, Bleak House, Anne of Green Gables, Bridgerton). Real rulers and battles go to B1-19; Edwardian country-house and shop sagas go to B1-21.
leaves.aliases: classic serial; period adaptation; bonnet drama
leaves.see: B1-19 Historical Drama; B1-21 Heritage Drama; B1-9 Romantic Drama
leaves.axis: by literary source, Austen and the Regency first, the Victorian novel, continental classics, gothic and sensation fiction, classic girls' and school stories, then original costume romance

leaves.label: Heritage Drama
leaves.defn: A series that lovingly recreates late-Victorian to interwar British (and kindred) society through a great house, shop or village and the classes inside it (Upstairs, Downstairs, Downton Abbey, Mr Selfridge, The Jewel in the Crown). Novel adaptations of the 19th century go to B1-20.
leaves.see: B1-20 Costume Drama; B1-22 Period Drama
leaves.axis: by the institution that holds the classes together: the country house, the shop or hotel, the village, then empire and Raj

leaves.label: Period Drama
leaves.defn: A series set in a recent past of the twentieth century (roughly 1918–1999) whose era, its manners and its changes are the drama (Pan Am, The Queen's Gambit, Cable Girls, Blossoms Shanghai). A series set within a war goes to B1-17; a multi-generation chronicle goes to B1-2.
leaves.aliases: period piece; era drama (niandai ju); nostalgia drama
leaves.see: B1-2 Family Saga; B1-17 War Drama; B1-21 Heritage Drama
leaves.axis: by decade, earliest first: interwar, the 1940s, the postwar and 1950s, the 1960s–70s, the 1980s–90s

leaves.label: Swashbuckler
leaves.defn: An episodic or serial adventure of swordplay, outlaw heroes, musketeers and pirates in a romanticised past (The Adventures of Robin Hood, Zorro, The Musketeers, Black Sails). Grounded medieval epics go to B1-19; martial-arts adventure goes to A7.
leaves.see: B1-19 Historical Drama; B1-24 Action-Adventure; A6 Fantasy & Adventure

leaves.label: Action-Adventure
leaves.defn: A series built on quests, voyages, treasure hunts or a weekly hero-in-action format (Knight Rider, MacGyver, The Lost Tomb, Michael Strogoff). Swordplay romances go to B1-23; spy and crime action go to B7; superpowered heroes go to B9.
leaves.see: B1-23 Swashbuckler; B7 Crime & Thriller Series; B9 Speculative Series
leaves.axis: by the adventure engine: literary adventure and voyages first, treasure hunts and tomb raiding, the weekly action hero, martial arts and street fighting last

leaves.label: Disaster Miniseries
leaves.defn: A miniseries whose story is an earthquake, eruption, impact or shipwreck and the struggle to survive it (10.5, Category 7: The End of the World, La Palma, Titanic). A dramatisation of a specific real disaster told as public record goes to B1-26.

leaves.label: Docudrama
leaves.defn: A drama that reconstructs a real event, case or institution with documentary fidelity, often naming the real people (Chernobyl, When They See Us, Mr Bates vs The Post Office, Dopesick). A dramatised life story goes to B1-27; a documentary series goes to B11.
leaves.see: B1-27 Biographical Miniseries; B11 Documentary Series; B7 Crime & Thriller Series
leaves.axis: by the kind of real event: reenactment-led docudrama first, disasters, political scandal, injustice cases, terror and siege, corporate and public-health scandal, exploration and science last

leaves.label: Biographical Miniseries
leaves.defn: A miniseries or series that tells the life (or a defining stretch of it) of a real modern person (Fosse/Verdon, Elvis, Genius, The Kennedys). A pre-modern ruler goes to B1-19; biographical film goes to A11.
leaves.see: A11 Biographical Film; B1-26 Docudrama; B1-19 Historical Drama
leaves.axis: by the sphere of the life: politics and royalty first, musicians, show business and fashion, sport, then science, enterprise and faith

leaves.label: Literary Adaptation
leaves.defn: A limited series adapted from a modern literary novel or story, set in its author's present, where the book's voice shapes the drama (Olive Kitteridge, My Brilliant Friend, Patrick Melrose, The Slap). Pre-1900 novels go to B1-20; a literary romance goes to B1-9.
leaves.aliases: limited series; literary miniseries; prestige adaptation
leaves.see: B1-20 Costume Drama; B1-9 Romantic Drama; B1-1 Prestige Drama

leaves.label: Anthology Drama
leaves.defn: A series of self-contained plays or stories with new casts and stories per episode or season (Play for Today, Playhouse 90, Alfred Hitchcock Presents, Modern Love). Horror anthologies of the uncanny go to B9 when the supernatural is the engine.
leaves.aliases: anthology series; single play; omnibus drama
leaves.see: B9 Speculative Series; B7 Crime & Thriller Series
leaves.axis: by the anthology unit: the live and single play first, suspense and crime tales, omnibus and linked-story series, then the themed modern anthology

leaves.label: Golden Age Anthology Drama
leaves.defn: A sponsor-titled American anthology drama of the first Golden Age of Television (c. 1947–1961): a new self-contained teleplay each week, broadcast live from New York or Hollywood (Kraft Television Theatre, Studio One, The Philco Television Playhouse, Playhouse 90) or, later in the decade, filmed in Hollywood (General Electric Theater, Schlitz Playhouse). Later anthologies stay in B1-29 Anthology Drama.
leaves.aliases: live anthology drama; Golden Age of Television
leaves.axis: production mode

subs.label: Korean Drama
subs.axis: Axis: by the genre the Korean industry and fandom name: romance forms first (rom-com, office, chaebol, melodrama), then the serial forms (makjang, revenge, family), the historical sageuk, professional and thriller genres, fantasy romance, and school and youth drama last

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy (rom-com)
leaves.defn: A Korean romance series whose engine is comic: mismatched leads, a contrived premise that forces them together, and a happy ending (Coffee Prince, Because This Is My First Life, Hometown Cha-Cha-Cha). A romance set mainly at work goes to B2-2; a rich-heir and poor-heroine romance goes to B2-3; a supernatural premise goes to B2-12.
leaves.see: B2-2 Office Romance; B2-3 Chaebol Romance; B2-12 Fantasy Romance
leaves.axis: by the premise that throws the couple together: contract and fake relationships first, then cohabitation, disguise, showbiz, mature second chances, small-town healing; genre-hybrid rom-coms last

leaves.label: Office Romance
leaves.defn: A Korean romance series set inside a workplace, where the job, hierarchy and colleagues drive the love story (What's Wrong with Secretary Kim, Business Proposal, Pasta, Romance Is a Bonus Book). A series about a profession first and foremost (hospital, court) goes to B2-9 or B2-10.
leaves.see: B2-1 Romantic Comedy; Medical Drama; Legal Drama
leaves.axis: by the workplace: boss-and-secretary hierarchies first, then company ensembles, kitchens and shops, media and creative industries

leaves.label: Chaebol Romance
leaves.defn: A Korean romance built on the class gap between a chaebol (conglomerate) heir or heiress and a poor partner, the "Candy" Cinderella formula (Boys over Flowers, Lovers in Paris, The Heirs, Queen of Tears). Chaebol family intrigue with birth secrets and revenge goes to B2-5 Makjang.
leaves.aliases: Cinderella story; Candy-girl romance; jaebeol romance
leaves.see: B2-1 Romantic Comedy; B2-5 Makjang Drama
leaves.axis: by who is rich: the Cinderella form (poor heroine, rich heir) first, then the reverse (heiress and poor man), then royals of an imagined constitutional monarchy

leaves.label: Korean Melodrama
leaves.defn: A Korean romance played for tears or emotional realism rather than laughs: fated or doomed love, illness, love triangles, adultery, or the quiet realism of adult relationships (Winter Sonata, Autumn in My Heart, Something in the Rain, Secret Love Affair). Melodrama of birth secrets, affairs and outrageous plotting goes to B2-5 Makjang.
leaves.see: B2-5 Makjang Drama; B2-1 Romantic Comedy
secs: Hallyu Tearjerkers: Fate, First Love & Illness
leaves.axis: by emotional mode, in the order the forms arose: early trendy dramas first, then Hallyu tearjerkers of fate and illness, adult and affair melodramas, the realist and healing romances of the 2010s, and music and arts melodramas last

leaves.label: Makjang Drama
leaves.defn: A Korean serial built on deliberately outrageous plotting: birth secrets, adultery, amnesia, chaebol family feuds and revenge escalating beyond plausibility (The Penthouse: War in Life, The World of the Married, East of Eden, Money Flower). A weekend family drama without the excess goes to B2-7.
leaves.see: B2-6 Revenge Drama; B2-7 Family Drama
leaves.axis: by the engine of the excess: birth-secret and family-feud serials first, then adultery and marriage makjang, then revenge and chaebol-intrigue makjang

leaves.label: Revenge Drama
leaves.defn: A Korean series whose spine is a protagonist's long-planned vengeance, usually wrapped in a romance or melodrama (Green Rose, Don't Look Back: The Legend of Orpheus, Goodbye Mr. Black, Call It Love). Revenge inside an outrageous family serial goes to B2-5 Makjang.
leaves.see: B2-5 Makjang Drama; B2-11 Thriller & Mystery Drama

leaves.label: Family Drama (gajok deurama)
leaves.defn: A Korean series centred on an extended family across generations, typically the long-running weekend family drama or the evening daily drama (My Golden Life, Young Lady and Gentleman, Homemade Love Story). Family serials driven by birth secrets and revenge go to B2-5 Makjang.
leaves.aliases: weekend drama (jumal deurama); daily drama (ilil deurama); home drama
leaves.see: B2-5 Makjang Drama; B2-4 Korean Melodrama

leaves.label: Sageuk (historical drama)
leaves.defn: A Korean historical drama set in the Joseon, Goryeo or Three Kingdoms periods, or a modern-era period drama of the Korean Empire, the colonial era and the later twentieth century (Jewel in the Palace, Jumong, Moon Embracing the Sun, Mr. Sunshine). A present-day romance with a brief slip into the past goes to B2-12.
leaves.aliases: sageuk; jeong-geuk (orthodox sageuk); fusion sageuk; daeha drama; sidae-geuk
leaves.see: B2-12 Fantasy Romance; A8 Historical & Period Film
leaves.axis: by mode, from historical fidelity to invention: orthodox jeong-geuk and dynastic epics first, then fusion sageuk of adventure, mystery and comedy, sageuk romance, fantasy, time-slip and horror sageuk, and modern-era period dramas last

leaves.label: Korean Medical Drama
leaves.defn: A Korean series set among doctors and hospitals, whose cases and careers drive the story even when a romance runs alongside (Descendants of the Sun, Emergency Couple, Doctor Slump). A psychiatric healing melodrama goes to B2-4.
leaves.see: B2-2 Office Romance; B2-4 Korean Melodrama

leaves.label: Korean Legal Drama
leaves.defn: A Korean series set among lawyers, prosecutors and judges, with cases framing the plot (I Hear Your Voice, Suspicious Partner, While You Were Sleeping). A Joseon-era lawyer goes to B2-8 Sageuk.
leaves.see: Medical Drama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Thriller & Mystery Drama
leaves.defn: A Korean series driven by a crime, a mystery or a threat, usually entwined with a love story (The Smile Has Left Your Eyes, When the Phone Rings, The Trunk). A revenge plan as spine goes to B2-6; a police procedural without romance belongs in B7.
leaves.see: B2-6 Revenge Drama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Fantasy Romance
leaves.defn: A Korean romance series whose premise is supernatural or speculative: time slips, immortal beings (goblin, gumiho, grim reaper), body swaps, ghosts, superpowers or a fictional world (Guardian: The Lonely and Great God, My Love from the Star, Lovely Runner, W). A historical drama with fantasy elements goes to B2-8 section 4.
leaves.aliases: fantasy rom-com; time-slip drama; gumiho drama
leaves.axis: by the supernatural device: time-slip, time-loop and reincarnation first, then mythical and immortal beings, body swaps and possession, ghosts and the afterlife, superpowers and science-fiction devices, and fictional or webtoon worlds last

leaves.label: School & Youth Drama
leaves.defn: A Korean series about teenagers or people in their early twenties, set in high school, university, idol training or sport, where growing up is the subject (Playful Kiss, Cheese in the Trap, Weightlifting Fairy Kim Bok-joo, Twenty-Five Twenty-One). A rich-heir high-school romance goes to B2-3.
leaves.aliases: teen drama; hakgyo drama; campus drama; cheongchun drama
leaves.see: B2-3 Chaebol Romance; B2-1 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by the youth setting: high school first, then university and twenty-something life, idol and music, and sport last

subs.label: Japanese Television Drama
subs.axis: Axis: by the genre or slot tradition Japanese broadcasting names: NHK serial forms first (asadora, taiga), then romance forms (trendy/getsuku, jun'ai, rom-com, office, school romance), then school, home and workplace dramas, gourmet and slice-of-life, and suspense and fantasy last

leaves.label: Asadora (Renzoku Terebi Shōsetsu)
leaves.defn: An NHK morning serial: some 150 fifteen-minute episodes over six months following a heroine's life, often across decades (Oshin, Amachan, Massan). A family drama in other slots goes to B3-9.
leaves.aliases: asadora; morning drama; renzoku terebi shosetsu
leaves.see: B3-2 Taiga Drama; B3-9 Home Drama

leaves.label: Taiga Drama
leaves.defn: NHK's year-long Sunday historical epic, one historical figure or era per year (Atsu Hime, Taira no Kiyomori, What Will You Do, Ieyasu?). Other period dramas belong in A8 or B1.
leaves.see: B3-1 Asadora; A8 Historical & Period Film

leaves.label: Trendy Drama & Getsuku
leaves.defn: A Japanese prime-time romance in the trendy-drama tradition: urban young professionals in love, star casts and theme songs, most famously Fuji TV's Monday 9 pm "getsuku" slot (Tokyo Love Story, Long Vacation, Beautiful Life, Rich Man, Poor Woman). A late-night or streaming romance goes to B3-4 or B3-5.
leaves.see: B3-4 Jun'ai & Romantic Melodrama; B3-5 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by phase of the cycle: bubble-era trendy dramas first, then the getsuku peak, then later getsuku and prime-time romances

leaves.label: Jun'ai & Romantic Melodrama
leaves.defn: A Japanese romance played for tears or for dark adult emotion: pure love against illness or death (jun'ai), forbidden or adulterous love (furin), obsessive love (Crying Out Love, in the Center of the World, Silent, Hirugao, Last Friends). A prime-time trendy romance goes to B3-3.
leaves.see: B3-3 Trendy Drama & Getsuku; B3-5 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by the obstacle to love: illness, death and pure love first, then adultery and forbidden love, then obsessive and dark romance

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy (ren'ai komedi)
leaves.defn: A Japanese romance series whose engine is comic: a contrived arrangement, a marriage hunt, a cohabitation or an oddball heroine, often adapted from josei or TL manga (Tokyo Tarareba Girls, Princess Jellyfish, Densha Otoko, Busu no Hitomi ni Koishiteru). An office love story goes to B3-6; a school romance goes to B3-7.
leaves.see: B3-6 Office Romance; B3-7 School Romance
leaves.axis: by the comic premise: contract and fake marriages first, then marriage-hunting and single life, cohabitation and housekeepers, makeovers and otaku heroines, rich-man Cinderella stories, and Teens' Love late-night romances last

leaves.label: Office Romance (shanai ren'ai)
leaves.defn: A Japanese romance set inside a company or workplace, between boss and subordinate or colleagues (Hotaru no Hikari, Oh My Boss! Love Not Included, Kissing the Ring Finger). A drama about the work itself goes to B3-10 Oshigoto Drama.
leaves.see: B3-10 Oshigoto Drama; B3-5 Romantic Comedy

leaves.label: School Romance (gakuen ren'ai)
leaves.defn: A Japanese romance among students, mostly live-action adaptations of shōjo manga, set in high school or college (Hana Yori Dango, Itazura na Kiss, Good Morning Call, Ao Haru Ride). A school drama about teachers, delinquents or clubs goes to B3-8.
leaves.see: B3-8 School Drama; B3-5 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by age and pairing: high-school romances first, then campus and young-adult romances, then teacher-student romances

leaves.label: School Drama (gakuen dorama)
leaves.defn: A Japanese series set in a school whose subject is the institution itself: the crusading teacher, the delinquent class, bullying, or the school club (GTO, Gokusen, The Queen's Classroom, Rookies). A love story between students goes to B3-7.
leaves.aliases: gakuen dorama; teacher drama; yankii drama; bukatsu drama
leaves.see: B3-7 School Romance; B10 Children's Series
leaves.axis: by the engine of the school story: teacher dramas first, then delinquent (yankii) dramas, bullying and dark classroom dramas, school-club and sports dramas, and school comedies last

leaves.label: Home Drama (hōmu dorama)
