leaves.defn: A Japanese series about a household: siblings, parents and children, single fathers, a family's illness or hardship (Hitotsu Yane no Shita, Tonbi, One Liter of Tears, Mother). A comedy of everyday eccentricity goes to B3-12.
leaves.aliases: hōmu dorama; kazoku dorama; Showa home drama
leaves.axis: by what tests the family: family ensembles first, then parenting and single parents, then illness, disability and hardship

leaves.label: Oshigoto Drama (workplace drama)
leaves.defn: A Japanese series about a job: the company, the trade, the profession or the industry is the subject (Naoki Hanzawa, Shomuni, The Pride of the Temp, Downtown Rocket). A romance at work goes to B3-6; a cooking or restaurant drama goes to B3-11.
leaves.aliases: oshigoto dorama; work drama; business drama
leaves.see: B3-6 Office Romance; B3-11 Gourmet Drama
leaves.axis: by the kind of work: corporate and finance first, then office comedies and temps, trades and service professions, media, publishing and entertainment, and medical, legal, care and rescue professions last

leaves.label: Gourmet Drama (gurume dorama)
leaves.defn: A Japanese series in which food, cooking and eating are the subject, often episodic around one dish per episode (Solitary Gourmet, Midnight Diner, The Makanai: Cooking for the Maiko House). A romance between cooks goes to B3-5 or B3-6.
leaves.aliases: gurume dorama; meshi-tero drama; food drama
leaves.see: B3-10 Oshigoto Drama; B3-12 Slice-of-Life Drama

leaves.label: Slice-of-Life Drama (nichijō)
leaves.defn: A Japanese series of everyday life with no strong romantic or professional engine: healing (iyashi) rhythms or eccentric small-group comedy (Yuru Camp, Barakamon, Kisarazu Cat's Eye, Tiger and Dragon). A food-centred series goes to B3-11.
leaves.see: B3-11 Gourmet Drama; C6 Slice of Life & Iyashikei Anime
leaves.axis: by tone: healing (iyashi) slice of life first, then eccentric-ensemble comedy-drama

leaves.label: Suspense Drama (sasupensu)
leaves.defn: A Japanese series driven by a secret, crime or threat, often a domestic or romantic mystery (I Am Mita, Your Housekeeper, Quartet, Perfect Crime). A detective or police procedural belongs in B7.
leaves.see: B3-4 Jun'ai & Romantic Melodrama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Fantasy & Supernatural Drama
leaves.defn: A Japanese series whose premise is supernatural or science-fictional, usually framing a romance: a robot or alien lover, a ghost, a time slip, a body swap (Zettai Kareshi, Ima, Ai ni Yukimasu, Q10). Tokusatsu hero shows belong in B9.
leaves.aliases: fantasy romance; SF drama; tokusatsu-adjacent drama
leaves.see: B9 Speculative Series; B3-5 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by what the premise serves: fantasy-premise romances first, then supernatural and science-fiction dramas without a central romance

subs.label: Chinese-Language Drama
subs.axis: Axis: by genre tradition, costume and mythic genres first (epic, palace, intrigue, case, romance, time travel, wuxia, xianxia, xuanhuan, shenmo), then the Republican and state genres, then modern romance traditions, TVB last

leaves.label: Historical Epic Drama
leaves.defn: A serial that dramatises recorded dynastic history or a classic of Chinese literature at epic scale, statecraft and great events foremost and invented romance secondary (Romance of the Three Kingdoms, The Qin Empire, Ming Dynasty in 1566, A Dream of Red Mansions). A fictional court with romantic leads goes to B4-5; schemers in a fictional court go to B4-3.
leaves.aliases: lishi zhengju (orthodox historical drama); classic-novel adaptation
leaves.see: B4-3 Court Intrigue Drama; A8 Historical & Period Film

leaves.label: Palace Drama
leaves.defn: A costume serial whose engine is the rivalry of consorts, empresses and palace women in the imperial harem, rising through scheming and survival (Empresses in the Palace, Story of Yanxi Palace, Ruyi's Royal Love in the Palace, Legend of Mi Yue). Male ministers and princes plotting for the throne go to B4-3.
leaves.see: B4-3 Court Intrigue Drama; B4-5 Costume Romance; B4-21 TVB Drama

leaves.label: Court Intrigue Drama
leaves.defn: A costume serial driven by political scheming for power, succession or revenge at court, with a strategist hero at its centre (Nirvana in Fire, The Advisors Alliance, Joy of Life, The Longest Day in Chang'an). Harem rivalry among women goes to B4-2; romance first goes to B4-5.
leaves.see: B4-2 Palace Drama; B4-1 Historical Epic Drama

leaves.label: Gong'an & Costume Detective Drama
leaves.defn: A costume serial built on cases solved by a magistrate, coroner or detective in imperial China, one or several cases per arc (Justice Bao, The Imperial Coroner, Strange Tales of Tang Dynasty, Luoyang). A jianghu swordsman solving mysteries goes to B4-7.
leaves.aliases: gong'an fiction; costume mystery; ancient detective drama
leaves.see: B4-3 Court Intrigue Drama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Costume Romance
leaves.defn: A guzhuang serial set in imperial or invented dynastic China whose engine is the central love story, intrigue and history serving it (Love Like the Galaxy: Part 1, The Story of Ming Lan, Blossoms in Adversity, Dawn Is Breaking). Immortals and cultivation go to B4-8; a modern heroine thrown into the past goes to B4-6.
leaves.aliases: guzhuang yanqing ju; costume drama; period romance
leaves.see: B4-2 Palace Drama; B4-6 Time-Travel Drama; B4-8 Xianxia Drama
leaves.axis: by the engine of the love story: court romance, household rivalry, rebirth and revenge, the general and the frontier, the heroine's enterprise, comedy last

leaves.label: Time-Travel Drama
leaves.defn: A serial whose premise is a protagonist displaced in time or into a fictional world, the gap between eras or texts being the engine (Scarlet Heart, Go Princess, Go!, Romance of a Twin Flower, Back to Seventeen). Supernatural lovers without displacement go to B4-20.
leaves.aliases: chuanyue (crossing over); chuanshu (transmigration into a book); time-slip
leaves.see: B4-5 Costume Romance; B4-20 Romantic Fantasy Drama
leaves.axis: by where the traveller lands: inside a novel or game, the dynastic past, a younger self in modern times

leaves.label: Wuxia Drama
leaves.defn: A serial of martial heroes in the jianghu, the world of sects, swordsmen and codes of honour, with martial skill realistic rather than magical (The Legend of the Condor Heroes, Laughing in the Wind, Legend of Fei, Mysterious Lotus Casebook). Immortals and cultivation go to B4-8.
leaves.see: B4-8 Xianxia Drama; A7 Action & Martial Arts
leaves.axis: by source: Jin Yong canon first, other classic authors, jianghu romance, original wuxia adventure last

leaves.label: Xianxia Drama
leaves.defn: A serial of immortals, gods, demons and cultivators in a Daoist-mythic cosmos, often across several lifetimes (Eternal Love, Ashes of Love, Love between Fairy and Devil, Till the End of the Moon). Secondary-world empires without Daoist cosmology go to B4-9; the Journey-to-the-West mythology goes to B4-10.
leaves.see: B4-9 Xuanhuan Drama; B4-10 Shenmo Drama; B5-10 Danmei Drama
leaves.axis: by engine: immortal romance across lives, cultivation and sect adventure, demon and spirit romance, comedy last

leaves.label: Xuanhuan Drama
leaves.defn: A serial set in an invented secondary world of magic, races and empires, high fantasy not bound to Daoist cosmology (Novoland: Eagle Flag, Ice Fantasy, Ever Night, Douluo Continent). Immortals and heavens go to B4-8.
leaves.see: B4-8 Xianxia Drama; B9 Speculative Series

leaves.label: Shenmo Drama
leaves.defn: A serial adapting the gods-and-demons classics and folk legends of China (Journey to the West, Feng Shen Bang, The Legend of White Snake, Butterfly Lovers). Original immortal romances go to B4-8.

leaves.label: Republican-Era Drama
leaves.defn: A serial set in the Republic of China (1912–1949) whose engine is the period itself: warlords, Shanghai glamour, opera troupes and adventure (Winter Begonia, The Mystic Nine, Siege in Fog, White Deer Plain). Spies of the period go to B4-12.
leaves.see: B4-12 Spy Drama; B4-13 Main-Melody Drama
leaves.axis: by engine: literary saga, romance, mystery and adventure

leaves.label: Spy Drama
leaves.defn: A serial of undercover agents in the Republican and anti-Japanese war years, the double life and its unmasking the engine (Lurk, Rookie Agent Rouge, All Quiet in Peking, Silent Honor). A war-front epic goes to B4-13.
leaves.see: B4-11 Republican-Era Drama; B4-13 Main-Melody Drama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Main-Melody Drama
leaves.defn: A state-endorsed serial celebrating the Party, the revolution, the army or a national achievement (Awakening Age, Minning Town, Across the Yalu River, Ace Troops). Spies go to B4-12; Republican romance goes to B4-11.
leaves.see: B4-12 Spy Drama; B4-1 Historical Epic Drama
leaves.axis: by subject: revolutionary history and leaders, war, the army today, reform and national achievement

leaves.label: Qiong Yao Drama
leaves.defn: A serial adapted from or produced by the novelist Qiong Yao, the canon of tearful romance and its comic costume offshoots (Princess Pearl, Romance in the Rain, Love in the Rain). Later Taiwanese idol drama goes to B4-15.

leaves.label: Taiwanese Idol Drama
leaves.defn: A Taiwanese romance serial of the idol-drama tradition, young pop-star leads in a glossy love story often adapted from manga (Meteor Garden, It Started with a Kiss, Hana Kimi, In Time with You). Taiwanese BL goes to B5-9.
leaves.see: B4-16 Idol Drama; B2 Korean Drama; B3 Japanese Television Drama
leaves.axis: by engine, idol era first: manga and remake idol drama, romantic comedy, melodrama, idol fantasy, post-idol romance last

leaves.label: Idol Drama
leaves.defn: A mainland romance serial of the idol-drama mode, young leads in a sweet, low-conflict love story (Well-Intended Love, Boss & Me, Hello Mr. Right). Adult workplace and marriage dramas go to B4-17; school settings go to B4-18.
leaves.aliases: ouxiang ju; tianchong (sweet pet drama); C-drama romance
leaves.see: B4-15 Taiwanese Idol Drama; B4-17 Urban Romance Drama; B4-18 Youth Drama
leaves.axis: by premise: pure sweet romance first, the domineering CEO, contract and hidden identity, entertainment industry

leaves.label: Urban Romance Drama
leaves.defn: A mainland serial of adult lives in the city, love bound up with career, profession, marriage or family (The Rational Life, You Are My Hero, Best Choice Ever, Love in the Edge of Divorce). Young sweet romance goes to B4-16.
leaves.aliases: dushi qinggan ju (urban emotional drama); urban drama
leaves.see: B4-16 Idol Drama; B1 Drama Series
leaves.axis: by the second engine beside love: the office, a profession, marriage and family

leaves.label: Youth Drama
leaves.defn: A mainland coming-of-age serial of school or university years, first love and friendship before adulthood (A Love So Beautiful, With You, When I Fly Towards You, Hidden Love). Sports-team stories go to B4-19.
leaves.see: B4-16 Idol Drama; B4-19 Sports & Esports Drama
leaves.axis: by setting: high school, college

leaves.label: Sports & Esports Drama
leaves.defn: A serial whose engine is competition in a sport or a video game, romance and rivalry riding on training and tournaments (The Whirlwind Girl, Skate Into Love, Gank Your Heart, Love O2O). Campus life without competition goes to B4-18.
leaves.see: B4-18 Youth Drama; B4-16 Idol Drama
leaves.axis: by arena: physical sport, esports and online gaming

leaves.label: Romantic Fantasy Drama
leaves.defn: A modern-day mainland romance with one supernatural element, a spirit, alien, mermaid or curse, at its centre (My Girlfriend Is an Alien, I Cannot Hug You, The Fox's Summer, Love Me in Three Days). Displacement in time goes to B4-6; immortals in mythic worlds go to B4-8.
leaves.see: B4-6 Time-Travel Drama; B9 Speculative Series

leaves.label: TVB Drama
leaves.defn: A Hong Kong serial in the house tradition of Television Broadcasts Limited, the 20-to-30-episode Cantonese drama of cops, professionals and family empires (Line Walker, Forensic Heroes, Moonlight Resonance, War and Beauty). TVB wuxia goes to B4-7.
leaves.aliases: Hong Kong drama; HK drama; Cantonese drama
leaves.see: B4-7 Wuxia Drama; B7 Crime & Thriller Series
leaves.axis: by house genre: police and crime, professional drama, family and business saga, costume drama, supernatural and comedy last

subs.label: Boys' Love & Girls' Love Drama
subs.axis: Axis: by national tradition, Thai BL subdivided by its narrative engine, GL last

leaves.label: Thai Campus BL
leaves.defn: A Thai BL (Y series) love story set among students, the faculty, the hazing senior and the dorm its stage (SOTUS, 2gether, Bad Buddy, I Told Sunset about You). Thai BL among working adults goes to B5-2.
leaves.aliases: Y series; Thai university BL; campus BL
leaves.see: B5-2 Thai Workplace & Adult BL; B5-7 Korean BL Drama
leaves.axis: by school level: university first, high school, campus sports and bands

leaves.label: Thai Workplace & Adult BL
leaves.defn: A Thai BL series about working adults, love tied to the office, a profession, showbiz, a shop or a contract (Lovely Writer, Step by Step, Moonlight Chicken, Last Twilight). Students go to B5-1; gangsters go to B5-3.
leaves.see: B5-1 Thai Campus BL; B5-6 Japanese BL Drama
leaves.axis: by the world the lovers work in: office, profession, showbiz and creative work, food and shop, contract and fake relationship, adult romance last

leaves.label: Mafia & Action BL
leaves.defn: A Thai BL series built on gangs, bodyguards, mafia families or fighters, violence and loyalty driving the romance (KinnPorsche, Never Let Me Go, The Heart Killers, Not Me). Murder mysteries go to B5-4.
leaves.see: B5-4 BL Thriller & Horror; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: BL Thriller & Horror
leaves.defn: A Thai BL series whose engine is a murder case, a killer or a horror, the romance inside a suspense plot (Manner of Death, Dead Friend Forever - DFF, Khemjira, The Effect). Ghost romance without dread goes to B5-5.
leaves.see: B5-3 Mafia & Action BL; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Fantasy & Period BL
leaves.defn: A Thai BL series with a supernatural, time-crossing or historical premise (Until We Meet Again, Be My Favorite, Love in the Moonlight, OMG! Vampire). Horror goes to B5-4.
leaves.see: B5-4 BL Thriller & Horror; B9 Speculative Series
leaves.axis: by premise: ghosts and the supernatural, time and reincarnation, period and royal settings, creatures and omegaverse

leaves.label: Japanese BL Drama
leaves.defn: A Japanese boys' love television drama, usually a late-night adaptation of BL manga (Ossan's Love, Cherry Magic! Thirty Years of Virginity Can Make You a Wizard?!, My Beautiful Man, What Did You Eat Yesterday?). Japanese GL goes to B5-11.
leaves.see: B3 Japanese Television Drama; B5-11 GL Series
leaves.axis: by setting: office and adult life first, school and youth, fantasy, BL parody, yakuza and crime last

leaves.label: Korean BL Drama
leaves.defn: A Korean boys' love series, mostly short web-born drama adapted from webtoons and web novels (Semantic Error, To My Star, Light on Me, Painter of the Night). Korean GL goes to B5-11.
leaves.see: B2 Korean Drama; B5-6 Japanese BL Drama
leaves.axis: by setting: school and campus first, office and adult life, fantasy, sageuk last

leaves.label: Taiwanese & Hong Kong BL
leaves.defn: A boys' love series from Taiwan, Hong Kong or Singapore, the HIStory anthologies and their successors (HIStory, We Best Love: No. 1 For You, Kiseki: Dear to Me, I'm a Fool for You). Mainland danmei goes to B5-10.
leaves.see: B5-10 Danmei Drama; B4-15 Taiwanese Idol Drama
leaves.axis: by tradition and engine: Taiwanese campus BL, Taiwanese adult romance, queer family and literary drama, Hong Kong BL, Singapore BL

leaves.label: Filipino BL
leaves.defn: A Philippine boys' love series, the Pinoy BL wave that began with the lockdown productions of 2020 (Gameboys, Hello Stranger, Gameboys 2, Love at First Spike). Filipino GL goes to B5-11.
leaves.axis: by production wave: the 2020–21 lockdown wave, later Pinoy BL

leaves.label: Danmei Drama
leaves.defn: A mainland Chinese drama from the danmei tradition, uncensored early web BL or censored 'bromance' adaptations of danmei novels (Addicted, The Untamed, Word of Honor, Guardian). Taiwanese BL goes to B5-8.
leaves.see: B4-7 Wuxia Drama; B4-8 Xianxia Drama
leaves.axis: by period and censorship: uncensored web BL, censored danmei adaptation, later modern-day BL

leaves.label: GL Series
leaves.defn: A girls' love series, a romance between women in the GL/yuri tradition (GAP, Blank, Ayaka Is in Love with Hiroko!, Lulu). Mixed BL and GL anthologies stay with their BL tradition.
leaves.see: B5-1 Thai Campus BL; B5-6 Japanese BL Drama
leaves.axis: by tradition: Thai GL, Japanese GL, other GL traditions

subs.label: Lakorn
subs.axis: Axis: by lakorn genre: melodrama, comedy, period and fantasy, remake, teen series

leaves.label: Nam Nao Lakorn
leaves.defn: A prime-time Thai melodrama of passion, rivalry and revenge, often with the forced 'slap-kiss' romance (Sawan Biang, Leh Ratree, Game Sanaeha, So Wayree). Comic romance goes to B6-2.
leaves.aliases: lakorn nam nao ("rotten water"); lakorn tob jub (slap-kiss); revenge lakorn
leaves.see: B6-2 Romantic Comedy Lakorn; B12 Serial Drama Traditions

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy Lakorn
leaves.defn: A Thai romance serial played for comedy, bickering couples and contrived arrangements (Love at First Hate, Boy for Rent, My Husband in Law, My Secret Bride). Melodrama goes to B6-1.
leaves.see: B6-1 Nam Nao Lakorn; B6-5 Thai Teen Drama

leaves.label: Period & Fantasy Lakorn
leaves.defn: A lakorn with a period setting or a supernatural premise, ghosts, time-slip or magic (Love Destiny, Happy Birthday, My Cherie Amour, 55:15 Never Too Late). Thai BL with such premises goes to B5-5.
leaves.aliases: lakorn boran; lakorn phi (ghost lakorn); jak-jak wong-wong
leaves.see: B6-4 Thai Remake Drama; B5-5 Fantasy & Period BL

leaves.label: Thai Remake Drama
leaves.defn: A Thai serial remaking a Korean, Taiwanese, Chinese or Japanese drama (Full House, F4 Thailand: Boys over Flowers, Princess Hours, Kiss Me). Original lakorn go to B6-1 to B6-3.
leaves.see: B2 Korean Drama; B4-15 Taiwanese Idol Drama

leaves.label: Thai Teen Drama
leaves.defn: A Thai series of teenagers and students, school, sport and first love, mostly from GMMTV and GTH (Hormones, U-Prince: Brian, Project S: Skate Our Souls, Kiss). Teen BL goes to B5-1.
leaves.see: B5-1 Thai Campus BL; B10 Children's Series

subs.label: Crime & Thriller Series
subs.axis: Axis: by the series' engine, from who investigates (police, detectives, sleuths, lawyers), to who commits the crime (gangs, dealers, crews, antiheroes, real criminals), to what threatens the protagonist (killers, minds, households, avengers, agents, states, games)

leaves.label: Police Procedural
leaves.defn: A series whose engine is the investigation itself: detectives, agents or a specialist unit work cases through interviews, evidence and chain of command, usually one case per episode (Law & Order, NCIS, Criminal Minds, Cold Case). A series about the lives of uniformed cops or of bent and undercover officers goes to B7-2; a two-hander built on the partnership to B7-3; a lab-led show to B7-4; a single literary detective to B7-9; a serialised single murder to B7-8.
leaves.aliases: cop show; police drama; keiji dorama
leaves.see: B7-2 Police Drama; B7-3 Buddy Cop Series; B7-4 Forensic Procedural; B7-8 Whodunit
leaves.axis: by the unit the series follows: detective squads, federal and specialist units, profilers, cold-case teams, then fantastic-premise procedurals last

leaves.label: Police Drama
leaves.defn: A series about the working lives of police officers themselves, the shift, the station, the street and the temptations of the badge, rather than about solving a case (Hill Street Blues, The Bill, The Shield, Line of Duty). A case-driven investigation series goes to B7-1.
leaves.see: B7-1 Police Procedural; B7-3 Buddy Cop Series
leaves.axis: by the officers' world: patrol and precinct ensembles, then undercover and police-corruption dramas

leaves.label: Buddy Cop Series
leaves.defn: A police or law-enforcement series whose engine is a mismatched pair of partners whose friction drives the cases (Starsky & Hutch, Miami Vice, Castle, Rizzoli & Isles). An ensemble squad goes to B7-1; a sitcom about cops goes to B8.
leaves.see: B7-1 Police Procedural; B7-13 Amateur Sleuth; B8 Comedy Series
leaves.axis: by who makes up the pair: two cops, a cop and a civilian or animal, then comic buddy cops

leaves.label: Forensic Procedural
leaves.defn: A crime series in which the lab, autopsy table or crime scene is the investigative engine and the leads are scientists, pathologists or coroners (CSI: Crime Scene Investigation, Quincy, M.E., Silent Witness, Unnatural). A squad drama that merely uses forensics stays in B7-1.
leaves.axis: by the forensic seat: crime-scene labs, then pathologists and coroners

leaves.label: Country Noir
leaves.defn: A crime series set in a rural, small-town, frontier or outback community where the land, isolation and local kinship shape the crime and the lawman (Justified, Longmire, Mystery Road, Happy Valley). A Scandinavian series goes to B7-6; a Scottish one to B7-7.
leaves.aliases: rural noir; outback noir; neo-Western crime
leaves.see: B7-6 Nordic Noir; B7-7 Tartan Noir; A10 Western
leaves.axis: by the terrain: American backcountry and frontier, outback and antipodean bush, then British, Irish and European countryside

leaves.label: Nordic Noir
leaves.defn: Scandinavian and Nordic crime drama in the bleak, socially critical register named for the cycle that followed The Killing and The Bridge: slow serialised investigations, damaged detectives, wintry landscapes (Wallander, Trapped, Deadwind). Remakes and imitations set elsewhere stay with B7-1 or B7-8.
leaves.see: B7-7 Tartan Noir; B7-5 Country Noir
leaves.axis: by the shape of the investigation: serialised single-case runs, then recurring detectives with many cases

leaves.label: Tartan Noir
leaves.defn: Scottish crime drama in the Tartan noir tradition of Ian Rankin and Val McDermid: hard-edged detectives in Edinburgh, Glasgow or the islands (Rebus, Shetland, Karen Pirie). An English village mystery goes to B7-11.
leaves.see: B7-6 Nordic Noir; B7-9 Detective Drama

leaves.label: Whodunit
leaves.defn: A serialised mystery in which a single murder or disappearance, and the circle of suspects around it, sustains a whole season and the question who did it is the engine (Broadchurch, Mare of Easttown, And Then There Were None, Magpie Murders). A recurring detective solving a new case each story goes to B7-9.
leaves.see: B7-9 Detective Drama; B7-23 Psychological Thriller
leaves.axis: by who carries the mystery: police-led serialised investigations, then closed-circle and Golden Age adaptations, then ensemble and anthology whodunits

leaves.label: Detective Drama
leaves.defn: A series built around a single named star detective, police or private and often of literary pedigree, who solves a self-contained case each story through deduction and character (Agatha Christie's Poirot, Inspector Morse, Sherlock, Kindaichi Shonen no Jikenbo). A squad procedural goes to B7-1; a cosy village mystery to B7-11; a period-set detective to B7-12.
leaves.see: B7-11 Cozy Mystery; B7-12 Historical Mystery; B7-13 Amateur Sleuth
leaves.axis: by the detective's lineage: Sherlock Holmes and Holmesian geniuses, Golden Age sleuths, star police inspectors, then puzzle-mystery (honkaku) series

leaves.label: Inverted Detective Story
leaves.defn: A mystery series in which the audience sees the crime and culprit first and the pleasure is watching the detective work it out (Columbo, Poker Face, Elsbeth).

leaves.label: Cozy Mystery
leaves.defn: A gentle murder mystery set in a village, resort or closed community where violence happens offstage and charm, humour and a returning cast matter as much as the puzzle (Midsomer Murders, Murder, She Wrote, Death in Paradise, Father Brown). A period setting first goes to B7-12.
leaves.see: B7-12 Historical Mystery; B7-13 Amateur Sleuth
leaves.axis: by who solves the murders: village and island police, then amateur and clerical sleuths

leaves.label: Historical Mystery
leaves.defn: A detective or police series whose cases are set in a past era that shapes method and motive (Cadfael, Murdoch Mysteries, Foyle's War, Babylon Berlin). Period gangland sagas go to B7-16.
leaves.see: B7-9 Detective Drama; B7-11 Cozy Mystery; A8 Historical & Period Film
leaves.axis: by era: medieval to Victorian, then the Edwardian and interwar years, then wartime and postwar decades

leaves.label: Amateur Sleuth
leaves.defn: A series in which a non-police investigator, a consultant, academic, doctor, writer or hobbyist, solves crimes through a special gift, usually alongside the police (Monk, Psych, The Mentalist, Only Murders in the Building). Licensed private investigators go to B7-14.
leaves.see: B7-14 Private Eye; B7-3 Buddy Cop Series
leaves.axis: by the sleuth's gift: specialist consultants to the police, then hobbyists and accidental sleuths, then comic sleuthing

leaves.label: Private Eye
leaves.defn: A series following a licensed private investigator or agency taking clients' cases, from hardboiled loners to glamorous agency teams (The Rockford Files, Magnum, P.I., Strike, Jack Irish).
leaves.axis: by the eye's register: hardboiled loners, then glamour and action agencies

leaves.label: Legal Thriller
leaves.defn: A series in which a criminal trial, defence or prosecution is the suspense engine: lawyers, defendants and judges racing to the verdict (Perry Mason, The Night Of, How to Get Away with Murder, Presumed Innocent). Workplace legal dramas without the crime engine go to B1.
leaves.see: B1 Drama Series; B7-1 Police Procedural
leaves.axis: by whose side the story takes: defence lawyers, then the accused and their families, then judges and prosecutors

leaves.label: Gangster Drama
leaves.defn: A saga told from inside a criminal organisation, mob family or gang, its loyalties, succession and turf wars (The Sopranos, Peaky Blinders, Gomorrah, Sons of Anarchy). A series about the drug trade itself goes to B7-17.
leaves.aliases: mob drama; mafia saga; yakuza drama
leaves.see: B7-17 Narco Series; B7-21 True Crime Drama
leaves.axis: by the organisation: Mafia and mob families, period gangland, modern city syndicates and crews, outlaw biker clubs, then yakuza and Asian syndicates

leaves.label: Narco Series
leaves.defn: A series about the drug trade as an economy: cooks, dealers, cartels, smugglers and the agents chasing them (Breaking Bad, Snowfall, Queen of the South, ZeroZeroZero). A mob saga where drugs are one racket goes to B7-16; a dramatised real kingpin to B7-21.
leaves.see: B7-16 Gangster Drama; B7-21 True Crime Drama
leaves.axis: by the rung of the trade: cartels and trafficking routes, then street dealing and urban drug wars, then outsiders who become dealers

leaves.label: Heist & Caper
leaves.defn: A series whose engine is the plan: a crew assembled for a robbery, a con or a theft, with the pleasure in the scheme and the double-cross (Money Heist, Hustle, Leverage, Lupin).
leaves.aliases: heist series; con-artist drama; grifter show
leaves.axis: by the scheme: robbery heists, then cons and grifts, then gentleman thieves, then gambling

leaves.label: Neo-Noir
leaves.defn: A crime series told from the side of the morally compromised: fixers, hitmen, small-time crooks and ordinary people who slide into crime, in the fatalistic noir register (Better Call Saul, Ray Donovan, Good Girls, Mr Inbetween). An organised family saga goes to B7-16; a drug saga to B7-17.
leaves.see: B7-16 Gangster Drama; B7-17 Narco Series; B7-5 Country Noir
leaves.axis: by the antihero: ordinary people turned criminal, then fixers, lawyers and middlemen, then hitmen and assassins, then social-realist and anthology noir

leaves.label: Prison Drama
leaves.defn: A series set inside a prison, where incarceration, inmate hierarchies and escape are the engine (Oz, Wentworth, El marginal, Locked Up).

leaves.label: True Crime Drama
leaves.defn: A scripted dramatisation of a real crime, case or criminal, told with named real people (American Crime Story, Des, Narcos, Scam 1992). Documentary series go to B11.
leaves.see: B11 Documentary Series; B7-22 Serial-Killer Thriller
leaves.axis: by the crime: murders and serial killers, then fraud and scandal, then robbery, then gangsters and drug lords, then terror and state crimes, then wrongful accusation and justice

leaves.label: Serial-Killer Thriller
leaves.defn: A series organised around a serial killer, whether hunted across a season or followed from the inside (Dexter, The Following, You, The Fall). Episodic profiler units go to B7-1; real killers to B7-21.
leaves.see: B7-1 Police Procedural; B7-21 True Crime Drama; B7-23 Psychological Thriller
leaves.axis: by point of view: the killer's own story, then the hunt for the killer

leaves.label: Psychological Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose suspense lies in the mind: obsession, manipulation, unreliable memory, a missing person or a community's hidden secret, rather than in action (Fool Me Once, Behind Her Eyes, The Missing, Sharp Objects). A thriller of marriage and household goes to B7-24.
leaves.see: B7-24 Domestic Noir; B7-8 Whodunit; B7-22 Serial-Killer Thriller
leaves.axis: by the source of dread: a missing person or abduction, obsession and manipulation, identity and memory, a small community's buried secret, then time-slip and uncanny thrillers last

leaves.label: Domestic Noir
leaves.defn: A thriller set in marriage, family and the home, where the danger is a spouse, a lover, a neighbour or one's own household (Big Little Lies, The Undoing, Doctor Foster, Mine). An affair thriller led by sex goes to B7-25.
leaves.see: B7-25 Erotic Thriller; B7-23 Psychological Thriller; B1 Drama Series
leaves.axis: by where the threat sits: the spouse, then the family and its heirs, then the social clique, then neighbours and strangers in the home

leaves.label: Erotic Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller in which sexual obsession or seduction drives the danger (Fatal Attraction, Dark Desire, Toy Boy). A marriage thriller without the erotic engine goes to B7-24.
leaves.see: B7-24 Domestic Noir; A15 Erotic Film

leaves.label: Revenge & Vigilante Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller whose engine is justice taken outside the law: a wronged person's long revenge or a vigilante crew punishing those the system lets go (The Glory, Taxi Driver, Revenge of Others, Vigilante).
leaves.see: B7-27 Action Thriller; B2 Korean Drama
leaves.axis: by who takes justice: vigilantes and avengers-for-hire, then a single wronged person's revenge

leaves.label: Action Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller driven by pursuit, combat and the ticking clock: counter-terror agents, lone ex-soldiers, bodyguards, hijacks and fugitives (24, Reacher, Bodyguard, The Fugitive). A spy story goes to B7-28.
leaves.see: B7-28 Espionage; B7-26 Revenge & Vigilante Thriller; A7 Action & Martial Arts
leaves.axis: by the mission: counter-terror and the ticking clock, lone heroes and ex-soldiers, bodyguards and protectors, hijacks hostages and sieges, then fugitives on the run

leaves.label: Espionage
leaves.defn: A series about spies, intelligence agencies, double agents and covert operations (Tinker Tailor Soldier Spy, The Americans, Homeland, Slow Horses). Counter-terror action without tradecraft goes to B7-27.
leaves.see: B7-27 Action Thriller; B7-29 Political Thriller
leaves.axis: by the spy's world: Cold War tradecraft, period and wartime espionage, present-day agencies and counter-terror, gadget spy-fi, action spies and assassins, then spy comedy and secret double lives

leaves.label: Political Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller set in the machinery of state: governments, coups, diplomats, scandals and the press that exposes them (A Very British Coup, State of Play, Occupied, The Diplomat). A plot by hidden powers outside the state goes to B7-30.

leaves.label: Conspiracy Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller in which an ordinary person or a small group uncovers a hidden plot by corporations, cults or shadow powers (Rubicon, Utopia, Edge of Darkness, Hunters).
leaves.axis: by the hidden power: corporations and finance, then the state and its security services, then cults and secret societies, then science and medicine

leaves.label: Death Game
leaves.defn: A thriller in which participants are forced into a deadly or ruinous game with prizes and eliminations (Squid Game, Alice in Borderland, Liar Game, Kakegurui).
leaves.see: B7-18 Heist & Caper; B9 Speculative Series

leaves.label: Teen Noir
leaves.defn: A mystery or thriller centred on teenagers, schools and campuses, where adolescent secrets, cliques and a death drive the plot (Pretty Little Liars, Veronica Mars, Riverdale, Girl from Nowhere).
leaves.see: B1 Drama Series; B7-23 Psychological Thriller
leaves.axis: by the setting: high-school secrets and murders, then classroom and teacher thrillers, then boarding-school and campus mysteries

leaves.label: Survival Thriller
leaves.defn: A thriller in which characters are stranded, trapped or hunted in a hostile place and must survive while a mystery unfolds (The Wilds, The Stranded, Persons Unknown, Jirisan).
leaves.see: B7-32 Death Game; B9 Speculative Series

subs.label: Comedy Series
subs.axis: Axis: by comic engine and form: the domestic and workplace sitcom first, then friends, romance, youth and place, character and embarrassment, documentary and absurd forms, sketch, satire and parody, music and sport, the fantastic genres, crime and darkness; comedy-drama and tragicomedy last

leaves.label: Family Sitcom
leaves.defn: A studio (multi-camera, audience or laugh-track) sitcom whose comic engine is the family household: parents, children and relatives colliding at home (Father Knows Best, All in the Family, The Cosby Show, Everybody Loves Raymond). A single-camera family comedy goes to B8-2; a family comedy-drama goes to B8-24.
leaves.aliases: domestic sitcom; family sitcom; multi-camera family sitcom
leaves.see: B8-2 Single-Camera Family Comedy; B8-24 Comedy-Drama; B10-4 Teen Sitcom
leaves.axis: era of the network sitcom, by national tradition (start year)

leaves.label: Single-Camera Family Comedy
leaves.defn: A family sitcom shot single-camera without audience or laugh track, playing family life with filmic cutaways, narration or deadpan (Malcolm in the Middle, The Middle, Friday Night Dinner, Fresh Off the Boat). A studio family sitcom goes to B8-1; a family mockumentary such as Modern Family goes to B8-11.
leaves.see: B8-1 Family Sitcom; B8-11 Mockumentary; B8-24 Comedy-Drama
leaves.axis: by the family at the centre: the nuclear household first, then class, family shape and generations; period nostalgia last

leaves.label: Workplace Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series whose comic engine is a workplace and its colleagues, the job supplying the situation and the hierarchy the conflict (The Mary Tyler Moore Show, Cheers, The IT Crowd, Superstore). A workplace mockumentary goes to B8-11; a military unit to B8-4; a political office to B8-15.
leaves.see: B8-4 Military Comedy; B8-11 Mockumentary; B8-15 Political Satire
secs: US early network and classic eras (1947–1969)
leaves.axis: era of the workplace sitcom, by national tradition (start year)

leaves.label: Military Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series set in an army unit, camp or wartime posting, its humour drawn from rank, drill and the absurdities of war (Dad's Army, Hogan's Heroes, M*A*S*H, Bluestone 42). A satire of the military establishment as policy goes to B8-15.
leaves.see: B8-3 Workplace Comedy; A9 War Film

leaves.label: Hangout Sitcom
leaves.defn: A comedy series whose engine is a group of friends, flatmates or neighbours simply spending time together, plot subordinate to banter (Seinfeld, Friends, How I Met Your Mother, The Golden Girls). A group defined by a job goes to B8-3; one built around a romance to B8-6.
leaves.aliases: friends sitcom; ensemble sitcom; hangout comedy
leaves.see: B8-3 Workplace Comedy; B8-6 Romantic Comedy Series
leaves.axis: era of the sitcom, by national tradition (start year)

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy Series
leaves.defn: A comedy series whose engine is a couple or the search for love: courtship, cohabitation, dating and break-ups (Mad About You, Catastrophe, The Mindy Project, Nobody Wants This). A marriage played as family life goes to B8-1/B8-2; a romance-led drama to B1.
leaves.see: B8-1 Family Sitcom; B8-5 Hangout Sitcom; A13 Romance
leaves.axis: by the stage of love: established couples first, then dating and singles; anthologies of love stories last

leaves.label: Teen Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series about adolescents or students made for a general or adult audience, built on school, sex and growing up (The Inbetweeners, Derry Girls, PEN15, Community). A teen sitcom made for children's networks goes to B10-4.
leaves.aliases: high-school comedy; college comedy; coming-of-age comedy
leaves.see: B10-4 Teen Sitcom; B1-7 Teen Drama; B8-24 Comedy-Drama
leaves.axis: by the institution: high school first, college and university second

leaves.label: Rural Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series whose engine is country or small-town life, often with the rube-versus-city contrast (The Andy Griffith Show, Green Acres, Corner Gas, Letterkenny). A small-town comedy-drama goes to B8-24.
leaves.aliases: rural sitcom; rube sitcom; village comedy

leaves.label: Character Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series built on one grotesque, deluded or hapless central character whose flaw drives every plot (Fawlty Towers, Keeping Up Appearances, Mr. Bean, One Foot in the Grave). Where the comedy is the audience's embarrassment rather than the character, see B8-10.
leaves.see: B8-10 Cringe Comedy; B8-13 Sketch Comedy
leaves.axis: era of the sitcom, by national tradition (start year)

leaves.label: Cringe Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series whose engine is social embarrassment, the awkward pause and the faux pas, often with the star playing a version of himself (Curb Your Enthusiasm, Peep Show, Extras, I'm Alan Partridge). A documentary-style cringe comedy goes to B8-11.

leaves.label: Mockumentary
leaves.defn: A scripted comedy series shot as if it were a documentary or reality show, with talking heads and camera awareness (The Office, Parks and Recreation, Summer Heights High, What We Do in the Shadows).
leaves.see: B8-3 Workplace Comedy; B8-16 Parody Series
leaves.axis: by the documentary subject: the workplace first, then a character or celebrity, a pastiche of documentary and reality TV; family and community last

leaves.label: Surreal & Absurdist Comedy
leaves.defn: A narrative comedy series whose engine is the illogical, dreamlike or anti-comic, breaking realism rather than embarrassing anyone (The Young Ones, The Mighty Boosh, Get a Life, Joe Pera Talks With You). A surreal sketch show goes to B8-13.
leaves.see: B8-13 Sketch Comedy; B8-19 Fantasy Sitcom
leaves.axis: by the break with realism: British alternative comedy first, then absurdist narrative comedy; anti-comedy last

leaves.label: Sketch Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series made of short unrelated sketches, with recurring characters but no running plot (Monty Python's Flying Circus, Saturday Night Live, The Fast Show, Key & Peele). A sketch series for children goes to B10-3.
leaves.see: B8-12 Surreal & Absurdist Comedy; B15 Variety & Talk Formats; B10-3 Children's Sketch & Puppet Comedy
leaves.axis: by the format: the variety-sketch show first, then live ensembles, troupes, character showcases, star vehicles, topical satire; prank, puppet and riffing shows last

leaves.label: Ramadan Comedy
leaves.defn: An Arabic-language comedy series made for the Ramadan prime-time season, typically thirty episodes, often social satire (Maraya, Tash ma Tash, Choufli Hal, El Kebeer Awi). Ramadan drama goes to B12.
leaves.see: B12 Serial Drama Traditions; B8-15 Political Satire

leaves.label: Political Satire
leaves.defn: A comedy series that ridicules power: governments, politicians, news media, bureaucracy, monarchy or the rich (Yes Minister, The Thick of It, Veep, Brass Eye).
leaves.see: B8-16 Parody Series; B8-13 Sketch Comedy; B15 Variety & Talk Formats
leaves.axis: by the target: government first, then the news media, bureaucracy and corporations, monarchy and history; society at large last

leaves.label: Parody Series
leaves.defn: A comedy series that imitates and mocks a specific genre or programme (Police Squad!, Sledge Hammer!, Childrens Hospital, Garth Marenghi's Darkplace). A documentary-form parody goes to B8-11.
leaves.axis: by the genre mocked: cop shows first, then spy, action and superhero, fantasy and horror, soaps and melodrama; film and media spoofs last

leaves.label: Musical Comedy Series
leaves.defn: A comedy series in which characters perform songs as part of the story (Flight of the Conchords, Glee, Crazy Ex-Girlfriend, Schmigadoon!).
leaves.see: A14 Musical & Dance Film; B8-24 Comedy-Drama

leaves.label: Sports Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series set around a team, athlete or sport, built on competition and locker-room egos (Coach, Eastbound & Down, Ted Lasso, Shoresy).
leaves.see: B8-3 Workplace Comedy; B11-7 Sports Documentary Series

leaves.label: Fantasy Sitcom
leaves.defn: A comedy series whose premise is a magical, supernatural or impossible element placed in everyday life (Bewitched, ALF, 3rd Rock from the Sun, The Good Place). Spaceships and future worlds go to B8-20; ghosts and monsters played for scares to B8-21.
leaves.see: B8-20 Science Fiction Comedy; B8-21 Horror Comedy; B9 Speculative Series
leaves.axis: by the impossible element: magic and supernatural beings first, then aliens, robots and creatures, afterlife and high-concept premises; body-swap and time-slip last

leaves.label: Science Fiction Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series set in space, the future or a technological world (Hyperdrive, Avenue 5, Upload, The Last Man on Earth).
leaves.see: B8-19 Fantasy Sitcom; B9 Speculative Series

leaves.label: Horror Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series built on horror premises (ghosts, vampires, zombies, slashers) played for laughs (Santa Clarita Diet, Ghosts, Scream Queens, Stan Against Evil).
leaves.see: B8-19 Fantasy Sitcom; B9 Speculative Series; A4 Horror

leaves.label: Crime Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series whose engine is crime: criminals, cons, heists, comic cops or murder mysteries played for laughs (Porridge, Weeds, Los simuladores, The Afterparty). A parody of cop shows goes to B8-16; a crime drama to B7.
leaves.see: B7 Crime & Thriller Series; B8-23 Black Comedy; B8-16 Parody Series
leaves.axis: by the side of the law: criminals, cons and heists first, then comic detectives and police; comic murder mysteries last

leaves.label: Black Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series that finds humour in death, cruelty, despair or taboo, inviting laughter at the dreadful (Nighty Night, Inside No. 9, Barry, Dead to Me).

leaves.label: Comedy-Drama
leaves.defn: A series that balances comedy with dramatic stakes and serialized character arcs, usually single-camera and hour or half-hour (Northern Exposure, Gilmore Girls, Sex and the City, Atlanta). Comedy built on illness, grief or crisis goes to B8-25; a drama with light touches to B1.
leaves.see: B8-25 Tragicomedy; B1 Drama Series; B8-6 Romantic Comedy Series
leaves.axis: by the subject: family first, then small towns, professions, workplaces and the arts, women's ensembles, the comedian's own life; anthologies last

leaves.label: Tragicomedy
leaves.defn: A comedy-drama whose comedy is wrung from a wound: terminal illness, bereavement, addiction, mental illness or midlife collapse (The Big C, After Life, Kidding, Mom).
leaves.axis: by the wound: illness and dying first, then grief, addiction and mental health; divorce and midlife crisis last

subs.label: Speculative Series
subs.axis: Axis: by speculative premise — science-fiction premises first (space, aliens, time, technology, society's end), then costumed heroes, then fantasy worlds, then the supernatural among us, then horror; comic and anthology forms at the edges of each run.

leaves.label: Space Opera
leaves.defn: A series whose drama plays out among starships, space stations and interplanetary polities (Star Trek, Babylon 5, The Expanse, The Mandalorian). Earth-bound alien drama goes to B9-2; a comic space series to B9-11.
leaves.see: B9-2 Alien Invasion; B9-11 Comic Science Fiction
leaves.axis: by franchise first, then by mode: Star Trek, Star Wars, Stargate, Battlestar Galactica and military space opera, space westerns and adventure operas, exploration and colony dramas

leaves.label: Alien Invasion
leaves.defn: A series whose engine is extraterrestrials arriving on Earth — as conquerors, hidden infiltrators, first contacts or neighbours (V, Falling Skies, 3 Body Problem, Roswell). Star-faring drama goes to B9-1.
leaves.see: B9-1 Space Opera; B9-22 Occult Detective Fiction
leaves.axis: by the shape of the contact: open invasion, hidden conspiracy, first contact, aliens living among us

leaves.label: Time Travel
leaves.defn: A series whose premise is movement through time — travellers, slips, rewrites or loops (Doctor Who, Quantum Leap, 12 Monkeys, JIN). Time-slip romance with rebirth goes to B9-19.
leaves.see: B9-19 Magic Realism; B9-4 Mystery Box
leaves.axis: by what the traveller does with time: roams it, changes it, slips into the past, repeats a day

leaves.label: Mystery Box
leaves.defn: A serial built on a withheld central enigma that the audience decodes over seasons — an island, a vanished flight, a town no one can leave (Lost, Dark, Manifest, The OA). If the enigma is solved weekly by investigators, B9-22.
leaves.see: B9-3 Time Travel; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Techno-thriller
leaves.defn: A science-fiction thriller whose threat is a near-present technology or experiment — clones, enhancements, fringe science (Orphan Black, Fringe, Limitless, Kyle XY). Machines that think go to B9-6; costumed powers to B9-12.
leaves.see: B9-6 Artificial Intelligence in Fiction; B9-12 Superhero Fiction
leaves.axis: by the technology at stake: genetics and cloning, human enhancement, fringe science and conspiracy

leaves.label: Artificial Intelligence in Fiction
leaves.defn: A series whose premise is a thinking machine or a simulated world — androids, AI, virtual reality, cyberpunk cities (Westworld, Humans, Altered Carbon, Memories of the Alhambra).
leaves.axis: by where the artificial mind lives: robot bodies, simulated worlds, cyberpunk society

leaves.label: Dystopian Fiction
leaves.defn: A series set in an oppressive engineered society, or a contest that society stages for survival (The Handmaid's Tale, 3%, Severance, Alice in Borderland). A world after a catastrophe goes to B9-9.
leaves.see: Apocalyptic & Post-Apocalyptic Fiction; B9-8 Alternate History
leaves.axis: by what oppresses: the state, technology or the corporation, a selection or survival game

leaves.label: Alternate History
leaves.defn: A series set in a history that diverged at a known point (The Man in the High Castle, For All Mankind, SS-GB). A traveller who changes history goes to B9-3.
leaves.see: B9-3 Time Travel; B9-7 Dystopian Fiction

leaves.label: Apocalyptic and Post-Apocalyptic Fiction
leaves.defn: A series about the end of civilisation — the plague, collapse or impact, or the world that survives it (Station Eleven, Jericho, The 100, Fallout). Zombie apocalypses go to B9-28.
leaves.see: B9-28 Zombie Apocalypse; B9-7 Dystopian Fiction
leaves.axis: by the stage of the end: pandemic and extinction, wasteland after collapse, catastrophe still coming

leaves.label: Anthology Series
leaves.defn: A science-fiction or fantasy series telling a self-contained story with new characters each episode (The Twilight Zone, Black Mirror, The Outer Limits, Amazing Stories). Horror anthologies go to B9-26.

leaves.label: Comic Science Fiction & Comic Fantasy
leaves.defn: A series that plays a science-fiction or fantasy premise chiefly for laughs (Red Dwarf, The Hitchhiker's Guide to the Galaxy, Good Omens, The Watch). A sitcom with a light fantastic touch stays in B8.
leaves.see: B8 Comedy Series; B9-1 Space Opera
leaves.axis: by the premise mocked: science fiction, then fantasy

leaves.label: Superhero Fiction
leaves.defn: A series about costumed or superpowered heroes and their villains (Smallville, Daredevil, The Boys, Moving). Japanese henshin heroes go to B9-13.
leaves.axis: by source and tradition: DC Comics, Marvel Comics, creator-owned and original heroes, ensemble superpower dramas, Asian superhero series

leaves.label: Tokusatsu
leaves.defn: A Japanese special-effects hero series built on transformation (henshin), suit actors and miniature monsters, and its adaptations (Kamen Rider, Himitsu Sentai Goranger, Ultraman, Power Rangers).
leaves.see: B9-12 Superhero Fiction; C1 Action & Battle Anime
leaves.axis: by franchise: Super Sentai, Kamen Rider, Ultra Series, Metal Heroes and other henshin heroes, Power Rangers adaptations last

leaves.label: High Fantasy
leaves.defn: A series set wholly in an invented secondary world of magic, kingdoms and quests (Game of Thrones, The Wheel of Time, The Witcher, Alchemy of Souls). Myth and legend retold go to B9-15.
leaves.see: B9-15 Mythic Fiction; B4 Chinese-Language Drama
leaves.axis: by world-building scale: epic invented worlds, East Asian invented worlds, sword-and-sorcery adventure

leaves.label: Mythic Fiction
leaves.defn: A series that retells myth, legend or epic, or brings old gods into the modern world (Hercules: The Legendary Journeys, Merlin, Alif Laila, American Gods).
leaves.see: B9-14 High Fantasy; B9-16 Fairy Tale & Portal Fantasy
leaves.axis: by the mythology drawn on: Greco-Roman, Arthurian and European, Arabian and Asian epics, gods in the modern world

leaves.label: Fairy Tale & Portal Fantasy
leaves.defn: A series that retells fairy tales or sends its characters through a door into a magical land (Once Upon a Time, The 10th Kingdom, His Dark Materials, A Series of Unfortunate Events).
leaves.see: B10 Children's Series; B9-14 High Fantasy
leaves.axis: by the frame: fairy-tale retelling, portal or parallel world, children's literary fantasy

leaves.label: Historical Fantasy
leaves.defn: A period series in which magic or the uncanny is woven into recognisable history (Jonathan Strange & Mr Norrell, The Nevers, Carnival Row).
leaves.see: A8 Historical & Period Film; B9-18 Urban Fantasy
leaves.axis: by setting and mode: steampunk and gaslamp fantasy first, other historical fantasy after

leaves.label: Urban Fantasy
leaves.defn: A series in which witches, shapeshifters, fae, angels or demons live hidden in the present-day world (Charmed, Lost Girl, The Magicians, Preacher). Teen-centred versions go to B9-21; investigators of the uncanny to B9-22.
leaves.see: B9-21 Supernatural Teen Drama; B9-22 Occult Detective Fiction
leaves.axis: by the hidden beings: witches, shapeshifters and fae, hidden magical worlds, angels, demons and immortals

leaves.label: Magic Realism
leaves.defn: A realist drama with one impossible premise taken matter-of-factly — a body swap, a second life, a grim reaper at work (Reborn Rich, Dead Like Me, Mystic Pop-up Bar, Wonderfalls). Fully supernatural worlds go to B9-18.
leaves.see: B9-20 Paranormal Romance; B2 Korean Drama
leaves.axis: by the impossible premise: body swap, rebirth and second life, afterlife and fate, other magic-realist dramas

leaves.label: Paranormal Romance
leaves.defn: A romance whose lover is supernatural — a gumiho, ghost, angel or beast (Tale of the Nine-Tailed, Bring It On, Ghost, A Discovery of Witches). Vampire romance goes to B9-23.
leaves.axis: by tradition: Korean fantasy romance, Chinese and Japanese supernatural romance, Western paranormal romance

leaves.label: Supernatural Teen Drama
leaves.defn: A teen drama in which adolescents fight, love or become monsters (Buffy the Vampire Slayer, The Vampire Diaries, Teen Wolf, Stranger Things).
leaves.see: B9-18 Urban Fantasy; B9-23 Vampire Fiction
leaves.axis: by the teens' role: slayers, witches, vampire and werewolf romances, teen horror mysteries

leaves.label: Occult Detective Fiction
leaves.defn: A series of cases solved by investigators of the paranormal — agents, psychics, hunters (The X-Files, Supernatural, Medium, Grimm). A serial enigma with no case-of-the-week goes to B9-4.
leaves.see: B9-4 Mystery Box; B7 Crime & Thriller Series
leaves.axis: by the investigator: paranormal agents, psychics and mediums, monster hunters and exorcists, supernatural cops and consultants

leaves.label: Vampire Fiction
leaves.defn: A series centred on vampires (Dracula, True Blood, The Strain, Angel). Teen vampire romance goes to B9-21.
leaves.see: B9-21 Supernatural Teen Drama; B9-20 Paranormal Romance
leaves.axis: by the vampire's role: Gothic monster, plague, lover and society, detective or hero

leaves.label: Ghost Story
leaves.defn: A horror series driven by the dead returning to haunt a place, a family or an object (The Haunting of Hill House, Ju-On: Origins, Rose Red, Archive 81).
leaves.see: B9-25 Supernatural Horror; B9-19 Magic Realism
leaves.axis: by what is haunted: houses and Gothic settings, Asian ghost horror, cursed media

leaves.label: Supernatural Horror
leaves.defn: A horror series whose threat is demonic, occult or cosmic (The Exorcist, Midnight Mass, Lovecraft Country, Penny Dreadful). Ghosts go to B9-24; vampires to B9-23.
leaves.aliases: folk horror; religious horror; cosmic horror
leaves.see: B9-24 Ghost Story; B9-26 Horror Anthology
leaves.axis: by the evil's source: demons and religion, cults and folk ritual, the cosmic, Gothic literature

leaves.label: Horror Anthology
leaves.defn: A horror series with new stories by episode or by season (Tales from the Crypt, American Horror Story, Masters of Horror).
leaves.axis: by format: hosted classic anthologies, season-long anthologies, episodic modern anthologies

leaves.label: Slasher
leaves.defn: A horror series in which a killer stalks and picks off a group one by one (Scream: The TV Series, Harper's Island, Chucky).
leaves.see: B9-30 Psychological Horror; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Zombie Apocalypse
leaves.defn: A series about survival among the risen or infected dead (The Walking Dead, All of Us Are Dead, The Last of Us). Non-zombie collapse goes to B9-9.
leaves.axis: by franchise and tradition: The Walking Dead franchise, other zombie survival, East Asian zombie series

leaves.label: Creature Feature
leaves.defn: A series whose threat or wonder is a monster or prehistoric beast (Primeval, Tremors, Sweet Home, Parasyte: The Grey).
leaves.axis: by the creature: dinosaurs and lost worlds, giant monsters and sea creatures, monster-siege survival, body horror and parasites

leaves.label: Psychological Horror
leaves.defn: A horror series whose terror is in minds and violence rather than the supernatural (Hannibal, Servant, Yellowjackets).
leaves.see: B9-27 Slasher; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Comedy Horror
leaves.defn: A horror series played for laughs (Ash vs Evil Dead, The Baby, Post Mortem: No One Dies in Skarnes).
leaves.see: B8 Comedy Series; B9-11 Comic Science Fiction & Comic Fantasy

subs.label: Children's Series
subs.axis: Axis: by age and mode: preschool first, then educational, sketch, sitcom and drama for older children, realistic and fantastic adventure; the seasonal Christmas calendar last

leaves.label: Preschool Television
leaves.defn: A live-action or puppet series made for children under about six, teaching through song, repetition and play (Sesame Street, Mister Rogers' Neighborhood, Teletubbies, Blue's Clues). Animated preschool series go to C13.
leaves.see: B10-2 Educational Children's Series; C13 Animated Series

leaves.label: Educational Children's Series
leaves.defn: A school-age children's series whose purpose is teaching reading, science or history, often with a presenter (The Electric Company, Reading Rainbow, Bill Nye the Science Guy, Blue Peter).
leaves.see: B10-1 Preschool Television; B10-3 Children's Sketch & Puppet Comedy

leaves.label: Children's Sketch & Puppet Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy series for children made of sketches, puppet routines or variety segments rather than a single story (You Can't Do That on Television, All That, Pee-wee's Playhouse, 31 Minutes).
leaves.see: B8-13 Sketch Comedy; B10-1 Preschool Television

leaves.label: Teen Sitcom
leaves.defn: A sitcom made for children's networks about tweens and teens at school, at home or in showbusiness (Saved by the Bell, Lizzie McGuire, Hannah Montana, iCarly). A teen comedy for adults goes to B8-7.
leaves.aliases: tween sitcom; kidcom; Disney Channel / Nickelodeon sitcom
leaves.see: B8-7 Teen Comedy; B1-7 Teen Drama
leaves.axis: by the premise: school and everyday life first, then family and siblings, showbusiness and double lives, magic and superpowers; hotels and camps last

leaves.label: Children's Adventure Series
leaves.defn: A live-action children's series of realistic adventure: animal companions, literary classics and kid-gang mysteries (Lassie, Pippi Longstocking, Emil of Lönneberga, De Zevensprong). Magic and science fiction go to B10-7.
leaves.see: B10-7 Children's Fantasy Series; A17 Children's & Family Film
leaves.axis: by the source of adventure: an animal companion first, then a literary classic; kid-gang and detective adventures last

leaves.label: Children's Fantasy Series
leaves.defn: A live-action children's series built on magic, the supernatural, science fiction or horror (Arabela, Round the Twist, The Worst Witch, Goosebumps).
leaves.see: B10-6 Children's Adventure Series; B9 Speculative Series
leaves.axis: by the impossible element: fairy-tale magic in everyday life first, then magic schools and supernatural teens, science fiction and superheroes; horror anthologies last

leaves.label: Christmas Calendar
leaves.defn: A Nordic television serial of 24 episodes broadcast daily from 1 to 24 December (Jul i Skomakergata, Nissebanden, Sunes jul); adult parodies of the form (The Julekalender) stay here.

subs.label: Documentary Series
subs.axis: Axis: by subject: the natural world and science first, then history and war, lives, music, sport and the arts, travel and food, investigation; true crime and the paranormal last

leaves.label: Nature Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series about animals, plants and ecosystems, including reconstructions of prehistoric life (Life on Earth, Planet Earth, Blue Planet II, Walking with Dinosaurs).
leaves.axis: by approach: the landmark global series first, then the Attenborough "Life" surveys, regional portraits, presenter-led wildlife; prehistoric reconstructions last

leaves.label: Science Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series explaining science, space, the body or how things work (Cosmos: A Personal Voyage, NOVA, How the Universe Works, Explained).
leaves.see: B11-1 Nature Documentary Series; B10-2 Educational Children's Series
leaves.axis: by subject: the cosmos first, then general science strands; explainer and pop-science formats last

leaves.label: History Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series narrating past events, eras or peoples (other than war), from archive narration to docudrama (American Experience, Prohibition, The Century of the Self, Mayday). War history goes to B11-4.
leaves.see: B11-4 War Documentary Series; A8 Historical & Period Film
leaves.axis: by method: narrative national history first, then social and cultural history, docudrama hybrids, essay and polemic; disaster and event retrospectives last

leaves.label: War Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series about a war or the military history of an era (The World at War, The Civil War, The Vietnam War, Apocalypse: The Second World War).
leaves.see: B11-3 History Documentary Series; A9 War Film

leaves.label: Biographical Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series portraying the life of a person (other than athletes and musicians) through archive and interview (Biography, The Roosevelts, Arnold, Harry & Meghan). Athletes go to B11-7; musicians to B11-6.
leaves.see: B11-6 Music Documentary Series; B11-7 Sports Documentary Series; A11 Biographical Film
leaves.axis: by subject: entertainers first, then politicians, royals and business figures; artists and writers last

leaves.label: Music Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series about musicians, genres or music scenes (The Beatles Anthology, Jazz, Hip Hop Evolution, The Beatles: Get Back).
leaves.see: B11-5 Biographical Documentary Series; A14 Musical & Dance Film

leaves.label: Sports Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series about athletes, teams or sporting events (30 for 30, The Last Dance, Formula 1: Drive to Survive, Last Chance U). Live sport goes to B16.
leaves.see: B16 Live Event & Sports Television; B11-5 Biographical Documentary Series
leaves.axis: by time: all-access season followed as it happens first; retrospectives and athlete portraits last

leaves.label: Arts & Pop-Culture Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series about art, design, film, television, toys or pop culture, including making-of series (Civilisation, The Story of Film: An Odyssey, The Toys That Made Us, LIGHT & MAGIC).
leaves.see: B11-5 Biographical Documentary Series; B11-6 Music Documentary Series

leaves.label: Travel & Food Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A non-competitive documentary series following a presenter through places or cuisines (Michael Palin: Around the World in 80 Days, An Idiot Abroad, Chef's Table, Street Food: Asia). Cooking competitions go to B13.
leaves.see: B13 Competition Formats; B14 Factual Entertainment Formats
leaves.axis: by approach: classic travelogues first, then comic and celebrity travelogues; food and culinary documentary last

leaves.label: Investigative & Observational Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A documentary series exposing wrongdoing or observing an institution or community from inside, and the anthology strands that carry such films (Dirty Money, Rotten, Hopkins, POV). Criminal cases go to B11-11.
leaves.aliases: exposé series; fly-on-the-wall documentary; documentary strand
leaves.see: B11-11 True Crime Docuseries; B14 Factual Entertainment Formats
leaves.axis: by method: investigative exposé first, then observational access; anthology strands last

leaves.label: True Crime Docuseries
leaves.defn: A documentary series reconstructing a real crime, investigation or trial (Making a Murderer, The Jinx, Tiger King, Forensic Files). A dramatized true-crime series goes to B7.
leaves.see: B11-10 Investigative & Observational Documentary Series; B7 Crime & Thriller Series
leaves.axis: by the crime: the single murder case first, then serial killers, wrongful conviction and trials, cults and abuse, fraud and cons, organised crime and terror; case-of-the-week strands last

leaves.label: Paranormal & Pseudo-Documentary Series
leaves.defn: A series in documentary form about hauntings, aliens or lost civilisations, presenting fringe claims as investigation (Ancient Aliens, Paranormal Witness, Ancient Apocalypse).
leaves.see: B11-3 History Documentary Series; B14 Factual Entertainment Formats

subs.label: Serial Drama Traditions
subs.axis: Axis: by the named national or regional long-form serial tradition, Latin American telenovela first, then the Anglo-European soap opera, the Turkish dizi, South Asian serials, the Arabic musalsal, the Philippine teleserye last.

leaves.label: Telenovela
leaves.defn: A closed-ended Latin American (or Latin-modelled) melodrama serial of one central love story told over months of daily episodes (Los ricos también lloran, María la del Barrio, Yo soy Betty, la fea, Rebelde). Brazilian novelas go to B12-2; narco serials go to B12-3.
leaves.see: B12-2 Brazilian Telenovela; B12-3 Narconovela; B12-12 Teleserye
leaves.axis: by production tradition, the Mexican Televisa melodrama first, then South American, Colombian and US Hispanic schools, the youth telenovela, telenovelas made outside Latin America last

leaves.label: Brazilian Telenovela
leaves.defn: A Brazilian novela, typically a Globo prime-time serial with large ensembles and social themes alongside the central romance (Roque Santeiro, Vale Tudo, The Clone). Spanish-language telenovelas go to B12-1.

leaves.label: Narconovela
leaves.defn: A telenovela-format serial built around drug traffickers, cartels and the women around them (The Cartel, Pablo Escobar: The Drug Lord, La Reina del Sur). A narco crime series made in a non-telenovela format goes to B7.
leaves.see: B12-1 Telenovela; B7 Crime & Thriller Series

leaves.label: Soap Opera
leaves.defn: An open-ended continuing drama broadcast daily or several times a week, with interwoven storylines in a fixed community that can run for decades (Coronation Street, Days of Our Lives, Neighbours, Gute Zeiten, schlechte Zeiten). A weekly prime-time serial of glamour and wealth goes to B12-5.
leaves.aliases: continuing drama; daytime soap; daily soap
leaves.see: B12-5 Prime-Time Soap Opera; B12-7 Indian Television Soap Opera
leaves.axis: by broadcasting tradition: American daytime soaps first, British and Irish continuing drama, Australian and New Zealand soaps, European daily soaps last

leaves.label: Prime-Time Soap Opera
leaves.defn: A weekly evening serial of wealth, glamour, family feuds and revenge, with cliffhangers in place of closure (Dallas, Dynasty, Melrose Place, Desperate Housewives). A daily continuing soap goes to B12-4.
leaves.see: B12-4 Soap Opera; B1-3 Family Drama

leaves.label: Dizi
leaves.defn: A Turkish television serial, typically of long weekly episodes, from the romance melodrama to Ottoman epics (What is Fatmagul's Fault?, Ezel, Erkenci Kuş, The Magnificent Century). A Turkish streaming miniseries outside the broadcast form goes to its genre leaf in B1.
leaves.axis: by dizi genre: the melodrama first, the romantic-comedy dizi, crime, revenge and action dizi, family dizi, teen dizi, the Ottoman historical dizi last

leaves.label: Indian Television Soap Opera
leaves.defn: A Hindi (or other Indian-language) daily serial of joint-family conflict, marriage and the saas-bahu (mother-in-law and daughter-in-law) axis (Kyunki Saas Bhi Kabhi Bahu Thi, Yeh Rishta Kya Kehlata Hai, Anupamaa). Mythological serials go to B12-8.
leaves.see: B12-8 Mythological Serial; B12-9 Pakistani Drama

leaves.label: Mythological Serial
leaves.defn: An Indian television serial retelling Hindu epics and Puranic stories of gods and heroes (Ramayan, Mahabharat, Devon Ke Dev...Mahadev). Biblical and Islamic epics go to B1-19.
leaves.see: B12-7 Indian Television Soap Opera; B1-19 Historical Drama

leaves.label: Pakistani Drama
leaves.defn: A Pakistani Urdu drama serial, typically a closed 20–30 episode story of love, marriage and family duty (Humsafar, Zindagi Gulzar Hai, Meray Paas Tum Ho). Indian daily soaps go to B12-7.

leaves.label: Sri Lankan Teledrama
leaves.defn: A Sinhala-language teledrama, the daily or weekly serial of Sri Lankan television (Deweni Inima, Koombiyo). Kept small as the attested national tradition.

leaves.label: Musalsal
leaves.defn: An Arabic television serial, classically a 30-episode drama made for the Ramadan season (Bab Al-Hara, Omar, Al Hayba, Raafat Al Haggan). Turkish serials go to B12-6.
leaves.axis: by musalsal genre: the historical and religious epic first, the social and family serial, crime, spy and thriller serials last

leaves.label: Teleserye
leaves.defn: A Philippine prime-time television serial in the telenovela mould, from romance to fantasy (Marimar, The Promise (Pangako Sa 'Yo), On the Wings of Love). Latin American telenovelas go to B12-1.

leaves.label: Sinetron
leaves.defn: The Indonesian television serial (sinema elektronik): long-running daily or weekly family, romance, religious and comedy serials of the private networks RCTI, SCTV and Indosiar (Si Doel Anak Sekolahan, Para Pencari Tuhan, Ikatan Cinta).

subs.label: Competition Formats
subs.axis: Axis: by what contestants are judged on — performance first (talent, singing, idol debut), then survival in a social game, then a craft, then knowledge, luck or play.

leaves.label: Talent Show
leaves.defn: A competition in which acts perform before judges or the public (Got Talent, Strictly Come Dancing, RuPaul's Drag Race). Singing-only contests go to B13-2.
leaves.axis: by the act: open variety talent, dance, celebrity performance, comedy, magic and novelty

leaves.label: Singing Competition
leaves.defn: A competition among singers decided by judges or votes (The Voice, Pop Idol, The X Factor, Star Academy). Idol-group debut shows go to B13-3.

leaves.label: Idol Survival Show
leaves.defn: A competition in which trainees vie for places in a debuting pop group, or groups battle for rank (Produce 101, Girls Planet 999, Queendom, I-LAND).
leaves.see: B13-2 Singing Competition; B15-2 Real Variety

leaves.label: Reality Competition
leaves.defn: An unscripted contest in which players live, travel or endure under rules and are eliminated until one wins (Survivor, Big Brother, The Amazing Race, Physical: 100).
leaves.see: B14-1 Dating Show; B13-6 Game Show
leaves.axis: by the contest's engine: live-in social elimination, races, physical challenges, strategy games, skill and business contests, comedy endurance

leaves.label: Cooking Competition
leaves.defn: A contest among cooks or bakers (MasterChef, The Great British Bake Off, Iron Chef, Culinary Class Wars). How-to cookery goes to B14-8.

leaves.label: Game Show
leaves.defn: A studio programme in which contestants play a game for prizes (Who Wants to Be a Millionaire?, The Price Is Right, Family Feud, Taskmaster). Comedy panel shows go to B15-4.
leaves.see: B15-4 Panel Show; B13-4 Reality Competition
leaves.axis: by the game played: quiz, words and puzzles, panel and guessing, chance and pricing, physical, music, comedy

subs.label: Factual Entertainment Formats
subs.axis: Axis: by the real situation the camera arranges — courtship, everyday lives, an experiment, a transformation, a trick, a ghost hunt, a journey, a lesson, a ruling.

leaves.label: Dating Show
leaves.defn: A programme that sets up real people to date, pair or marry (The Bachelor, Love Is Blind, Single's Inferno, Taken Out).
leaves.see: B13-4 Reality Competition; B5 Boys' Love & Girls' Love Drama
leaves.axis: by format: studio dating games, dating reality, same-sex dating reality

leaves.label: Docusoap
leaves.defn: An observational series following real people's lives as ongoing serial drama (The Osbournes, Jersey Shore, Terrace House, Cops).
leaves.see: B11 Documentary Series; B14-3 Social Experiment
leaves.axis: by whose lives are followed: celebrities and families, ensembles in structured reality, people at work

leaves.label: Social Experiment
leaves.defn: A factual format that places people in a contrived situation to see how they cope (Wife Swap, Undercover Boss, 60 Days In, The Rehearsal).

leaves.label: Makeover Show
leaves.defn: A format that transforms a person, home or business before the camera (Queer Eye, Extreme Makeover: Home Edition, Supernanny, Ramsay's Kitchen Nightmares).
leaves.axis: by what is made over: the person, the property, the troubled life or business

leaves.label: Hidden Camera
leaves.defn: A programme that films unwitting people reacting to staged pranks, or stunts staged for the camera (Candid Camera, Punk'd, Impractical Jokers, Jackass).
leaves.see: B14-3 Social Experiment; B15-1 Variety Show

leaves.label: Paranormal Television
leaves.defn: A factual series investigating hauntings and the unexplained (Ghost Hunters, Paranormal State). Scripted ghost hunters go to B9-22.
leaves.axis: premise

leaves.label: Travel Documentary
leaves.defn: A presenter-led entertainment series built on a journey or road trip (Top Gear, The Grand Tour, Running Wild with Bear Grylls, Conan O'Brien Must Go).
leaves.see: B11 Documentary Series; B15-2 Real Variety
leaves.axis: premise

leaves.label: Instructional Television
leaves.defn: A how-to or explainer programme that teaches a skill or tests ideas (The Joy of Painting, Good Eats, MythBusters, Antiques Roadshow).
leaves.see: B13-5 Cooking Competition; B10 Children's Series
leaves.axis: subject taught

leaves.label: Court Show
leaves.defn: A programme in which a television judge arbitrates real small-claims disputes (Judge Judy, Judy Justice).

leaves.label: Business Reality Television
leaves.defn: Factual entertainment built around running or financing a business: entrepreneurs pitching to investors, experts rescuing failing restaurants, bars and hotels, bosses going undercover, and dealers trading, pawning and buying at auction (Dragons' Den, Kitchen Nightmares, Bar Rescue, Undercover Boss, Pawn Stars).
leaves.axis: premise

leaves.label: Property & Home Improvement Television
leaves.defn: Lifestyle television about buying, selling, building and renovating homes: house-hunting and relocation shows, renovation and flipping shows, self-build and design series, and luxury real-estate docusoaps (Location, Location, Location, House Hunters, Grand Designs, Fixer Upper, Selling Sunset). One-off makeovers of a home as a gift stay in B14-4 Makeover Show.
leaves.aliases: property television; home improvement television; HGTV-style renovation shows
leaves.axis: premise

leaves.label: Crime & Law-Enforcement Reality
leaves.defn: Reality television that follows police, border, custody and prison officers, bounty hunters and investigators at work, filmed on ride-alongs, in custody suites and in stings (Cops, Live PD, Border Security, 24 Hours in Police Custody, Dog the Bounty Hunter). Documentary investigations of past cases go to B11-11 True Crime Docuseries.
leaves.aliases: crime reality TV; police reality; first-responder reality
src: Wikipedia (Reality television: Professional activities / first responder reality)
leaves.axis: setting

subs.label: Variety & Talk Formats
subs.axis: Axis: by what the host-led show presents — a revue of acts, cast members at play, conversation, comedy panels, clips, a single performance broadcast.

leaves.label: Variety Show
leaves.defn: A hosted revue of comedy, music and novelty acts (The Ed Sullivan Show, The Red Skelton Show, The Flip Wilson Show, Wetten, dass..?). Korean cast-based variety goes to B15-2.
leaves.axis: era

leaves.label: Real Variety
leaves.defn: A Korean-style variety programme in which a fixed celebrity cast plays missions, travels, runs a business or is observed living (Running Man, New Journey to the West, I Live Alone, Run BTS!).
leaves.see: B15-1 Variety Show; B13-3 Idol Survival Show
leaves.axis: by what the cast does: missions and games, being observed, travel and hospitality, idol-group content

leaves.label: Talk Show
leaves.defn: A host-led programme of conversation with guests or audience (The Tonight Show Starring Johnny Carson, The Daily Show, The Ellen DeGeneres Show, The Graham Norton Show).
leaves.axis: by slot and voice: late-night, satirical news, daytime and tabloid, celebrity chat

leaves.label: Panel Show
leaves.defn: A comedy programme in which a panel of comedians plays a loose quiz or improvisation game (Have I Got News for You, QI, Whose Line Is It Anyway?). Prize-driven games go to B13-6.
leaves.see: B13-6 Game Show; B15-3 Talk Show
leaves.axis: by the game: topical news quiz, comedy panel game, improvisation

leaves.label: Clip Show
leaves.defn: A hosted programme built from home videos or viral clips (America's Funniest Home Videos, Ridiculousness, Tosh.0).

subs.label: Live Event & Sports Television
subs.axis: Axis: by the kind of live event the broadcast carries: sporting competition (by sport, then multi-sport and anthology), professional wrestling, then ceremonies, contests and pageants, civic and state occasions, fund-raising broadcasts, and stage performances (concert, theatre, circus, stand-up)

leaves.label: Association Football Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive association football played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (FIFA World Cup, UEFA Champions League, Match of the Day, Sportschau). A multi-sport Saturday programme that merely carries football goes to B16-17.
leaves.aliases: soccer on television; Fußball im Fernsehen
leaves.see: B16-17 Sports Anthology & Magazine Shows; B16-16 Multi-Sport Event Coverage
leaves.axis: by competition level, highlights apart: international tournaments, continental club competitions, domestic league and cup coverage; highlights and magazine programmes last

leaves.label: American Football Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive American (gridiron) or Canadian football played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Super Bowl, Monday Night Football, The NFL Today, Grey Cup). The Super Bowl halftime show as a concert goes to B16-25.
leaves.aliases: gridiron football on television; NFL on television

leaves.label: Basketball Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive basketball played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (NBA Finals, Inside the NBA, NCAA March Madness).
leaves.see: B16-2 American Football Broadcasts; B16-4 Baseball Broadcasts

leaves.label: Baseball Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive baseball played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (World Series, Sunday Night Baseball, Japan Series, Little League World Series).

leaves.label: Ice Hockey Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive ice hockey played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Hockey Night in Canada, Stanley Cup Final, Summit Series). Olympic hockey games famous in their own right stay here with see_also B16-16.

leaves.label: Cricket Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive cricket played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Cricket World Cup, The Ashes, Indian Premier League, World Series Cricket).

leaves.label: Rugby Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive rugby union or rugby league played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Rugby World Cup, Six Nations Championship, State of Origin series, Rugby Special).
leaves.see: B16-6 Cricket Broadcasts; B16-1 Association Football Broadcasts

leaves.label: Tennis Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive tennis played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Wimbledon, Breakfast at Wimbledon, Battle of the Sexes).

leaves.label: Golf Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive golf played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Masters Tournament, The Open Championship, Ryder Cup, Shell's Wonderful World of Golf).

leaves.label: Motorsport Broadcasts
