leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive motor racing on cars or motorcycles played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Formula One World Championship, Indianapolis 500, Daytona 500, 24 Hours of Le Mans). A motoring magazine such as Top Gear is factual entertainment (B14).
leaves.see: B14 Factual Entertainment Formats; B16-11 Cycling Broadcasts

leaves.label: Cycling Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive road or track cycling played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Tour de France, Giro d'Italia, Paris–Roubaix).
leaves.see: B16-10 Motorsport Broadcasts; B16-12 Athletics Broadcasts

leaves.label: Athletics Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive track-and-field athletics or road running played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (World Athletics Championships, London Marathon, Diamond League). Athletics inside the Olympics goes to B16-16.
leaves.aliases: track and field on television; marathon coverage

leaves.label: Snooker & Darts Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive snooker, pool or darts played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport, the indoor sports that became mass television in Britain (Pot Black, World Snooker Championship, PDC World Darts Championship). A darts game show such as Bullseye is a competition format (B13).

leaves.label: Combat Sports Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive boxing, mixed martial arts, kickboxing or sumo played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport, including named landmark bouts sold as pay-per-view events (Rumble in the Jungle, HBO World Championship Boxing, UFC 1, NHK Ōzumō). Professional wrestling, whose outcomes are scripted, goes to B16-18.

leaves.label: Horse Racing Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of competitive horse racing played as it happens (or as its recording), together with the named broadcast strands, studio and highlights programmes built around that sport (Kentucky Derby, Grand National, Melbourne Cup, Channel 4 Racing).
leaves.see: B16-12 Athletics Broadcasts; B16-23 State & Royal Occasions

leaves.label: Multi-Sport Event Coverage
leaves.defn: The broadcast of a multi-sport games as one event, including its opening and closing ceremonies as landmark broadcasts (Olympic Games, 2012 Summer Olympics opening ceremony, Commonwealth Games, X Games). A single-sport championship goes to its sport leaf.
leaves.see: to B16-15 single-sport leaves; B16-23 State & Royal Occasions

leaves.label: Sports Anthology & Magazine Shows
leaves.defn: A recurring studio-based programme that covers many sports, by live inserts, highlights, results, features or debate, rather than one sport (ABC's Wide World of Sports, Grandstand, SportsCenter, Das aktuelle Sportstudio). A highlights show for one sport goes to that sport's leaf; a sports quiz is a competition format (B13).
leaves.aliases: sports anthology series; sports magazine programme; sports talk show
leaves.see: B16-1 Association Football Broadcasts; B13 Competition Formats; B11 Documentary Series

leaves.label: Professional Wrestling Television
leaves.defn: A programme or event of professional wrestling: athletic performance with scripted outcomes and serial storylines, broadcast as live or live-to-tape matches (WWE Raw, WCW Monday Nitro, WrestleMania, Wrestle Kingdom). Unscripted combat sports go to B16-14.
leaves.see: B16-14 Combat Sports Broadcasts; B15 Variety & Talk Formats
leaves.axis: by broadcast form, foreign traditions apart: weekly episodic shows, pay-per-view and premium live events; puroresu and lucha libre programmes last

leaves.label: Award Ceremonies
leaves.defn: The televised ceremony at which an academy, industry body or publication presents its annual awards, hosted and staged as a show (Academy Awards, Primetime Emmy Awards, Grammy Awards, Tony Awards). A song contest whose prize is decided on the night goes to B16-20.
leaves.see: B16-20 Song Contests & Music Festival Broadcasts
leaves.axis: by the field honoured: film, television, music; theatre, sports and multi-field awards last

leaves.label: Song Contests & Music Festival Broadcasts
leaves.defn: The broadcast of a song contest, in which new songs or national entries compete live for a prize, or of a named music festival as a televised event (Eurovision Song Contest, NHK Kōhaku Uta Gassen, Sanremo Music Festival, Melodifestivalen). A talent-search series with weekly eliminations (The X Factor) is a competition format (B13).
leaves.aliases: song festival; national selection; kayō festival
leaves.see: B13 Competition Formats; B16-19 Award Ceremonies; B16-25 Concert Broadcasts & Specials

leaves.label: Beauty Pageants
leaves.defn: The televised final of a beauty pageant, in which contestants are judged on stage for a title (Miss Universe, Miss World, Miss America). A reality series about pageant children (Toddlers & Tiaras) is factual entertainment (B14).

leaves.label: Parades & New Year's Eve Broadcasts
leaves.defn: Annual live coverage of a civic parade, carnival or calendar festivity, above all New Year's Eve countdown shows (Macy's Thanksgiving Day Parade, Dick Clark's New Year's Rockin' Eve, CCTV New Year's Gala, Jools' Annual Hootenanny). Military and state parades go to B16-23.
leaves.aliases: holiday specials; New Year's Eve special; Chunwan
leaves.see: B16-23 State & Royal Occasions; B15 Variety & Talk Formats

leaves.label: State & Royal Occasions
leaves.defn: Live coverage of a ceremony of state: coronations, royal weddings, state funerals, inaugurations, national-day and military parades (Coronation of Elizabeth II, Wedding of Prince Charles and Lady Diana Spencer, Trooping the Colour). Political news coverage is out of scope.
leaves.aliases: royal broadcast; national ceremony; outside broadcast
leaves.see: B16-22 Parades & New Year's Eve Broadcasts; B16-16 Multi-Sport Event Coverage

leaves.label: Telethons & Benefit Concerts
leaves.defn: A broadcast staged to raise money for a cause, either a long-form appeal telethon or a benefit concert broadcast live (Live Aid, Jerry Lewis MDA Labor Day Telethon, Comic Relief, 24-Hour Television). A concert without a fund-raising purpose goes to B16-25.

leaves.label: Concert Broadcasts & Specials
leaves.defn: A musical performance before an audience broadcast as a programme, as a one-off concert special or a recurring concert strand (Elvis: Aloha from Hawaii, Vienna New Year's Concert, MTV Unplugged, Austin City Limits). Studio chart and music-variety shows go to B15; benefit concerts to B16-24; opera and ballet to B16-26.
leaves.aliases: concert special; television special; music special
leaves.see: B15 Variety & Talk Formats; B16-24 Telethons & Benefit Concerts; B16-26 Theatre; Opera & Ballet Broadcasts

leaves.label: Theatre, Opera & Ballet Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A staged theatrical work (play, musical, opera, ballet) broadcast live or relayed from the stage, including the live television musical (Great Performances, Live from Lincoln Center, The Metropolitan Opera: Live in HD, The Sound of Music Live!). A drama written for television (anthology drama) goes to B1.
leaves.aliases: live theatre broadcast; event cinema; live television musical
leaves.see: B1 Drama Series; B16-25 Concert Broadcasts & Specials

leaves.label: Circus & Spectacle Broadcasts
leaves.defn: A broadcast of a circus show or of a live stunt or feat staged as a television event outside organized sport (Circus of the Stars, International Circus Festival of Monte-Carlo, Evel Knievel's Snake River Canyon jump, Skywire).
leaves.see: B16-26 Theatre; Opera & Ballet Broadcasts; B14 Factual Entertainment Formats

leaves.label: Stand-Up Comedy Specials
leaves.defn: A recorded stand-up (or live improvised) comedy performance before an audience broadcast or streamed as a special, or a showcase series of such sets (Eddie Murphy: Delirious, Chris Rock: Bring the Pain, Nanette, Live at the Apollo). A theatrically released concert film goes to A12; sketch shows go to B8 or B15.
leaves.see: A12 Comedy; B8 Comedy Series; B15 Variety & Talk Formats
leaves.axis: by outlet and form: premium-cable and broadcast specials, streaming-era specials, showcase series; musical and improvised comedy specials last

fams.label: Animation
fams.test: animation in any format and from anywhere: anime, Japanese animation in any format (C1–C11, by genre; TV, film, OVA and ONA are a filter), and non-Japanese animated features (C12), series (C13) and shorts (C14).
key: C1 Action & Battle Anime — by the fighting engine and its tradition: shōnen power battles first, then contest, school and urban-fantasy forms, adult and martial traditions, heroes, street and gun action, military last

C2 Mecha & Science Fiction Anime — by the science-fiction premise: giant robots first, then tokusatsu, space, war and tech-noir premises, then future societies, time and alien premises, anthologies last
C3 Fantasy & Isekai Anime — by where the fantastic lies relative to our world: other worlds entered from ours, invented secondary worlds, myth, then the supernatural inside the modern world
C4 Magical Girl Anime — by what the heroine's magic is for: everyday wishes, battle, and the deconstruction of both
C5 Romance Anime — by the romantic engine: the girl's love story, comedy and harem forms, drama, then supernatural, fantasy and same-sex romance traditions
C6 Slice of Life & Iyashikei Anime — by what the everyday life is organised around: a healing mood, a cute ensemble, a club, a stage, food, a job or a household.
C7 Sports & Game Anime — by the sport or game that is played.
C8 Drama, Mystery & Psychological Anime — by the dramatic engine: a puzzle to solve, a mind under pressure, a deadly game, crime, history and war, or an emotional arc.
C9 Horror Anime — by the source of the dread: ghosts and curses, the village, the vampire, the dead, the body, or dread played for laughs.
C10 Comedy Anime — by the comic engine: absurd gag, parody, spin-off, school life, otaku life, a fantasy or science-fiction premise, action, harem and fanservice.
C11 Children's & Family Anime — by the kind of children's property: everyday family anime, monster-partner franchise, toy tie-in, literary classic, or pre-war film.

C12 Animated Feature — by the studio canon, production mode or tradition the feature belongs to (studio canons first, then franchise modes, national traditions, technique and auteur/adult cinema last)
C13 Animated Series — by format and audience (prime-time and adult first, then network-canon children's comedy, action genres, national traditions and preschool last)
C14 Animated Short — by production context (theatrical studio cartoons, studio shorts, art shorts, technique, television specials)

subs.label: Action & Battle Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the fighting engine and its tradition: shōnen power battles first, then contest, school and urban-fantasy forms, adult and martial traditions, heroes, street and gun action, military last

leaves.label: Battle Shōnen
leaves.defn: A long-running shōnen serial whose engine is an escalating ladder of fights inside a power system, with a hero who grows through rivals, training arcs and tournaments (One Piece, Hunter x Hunter, Fairy Tail, Fullmetal Alchemist). If the powers are ki-based martial arts it goes to C1-9; if the foes are demons, yōkai or curses, to C1-2.
leaves.see: C1-2 Supernatural Battle Shōnen; C1-9 Martial Arts Anime; C3 Fantasy & Isekai Anime
leaves.axis: by the world the fights happen in: sea and quest worlds first, then fantasy kingdoms, then modern cities, contest formats last

leaves.label: Supernatural Battle Shōnen
leaves.defn: A battle shōnen whose fighters hunt or channel the supernatural, shinigami, yōkai, demons, curses, as an organised calling (Bleach, Kimetsu no Yaiba, Jujutsu Kaisen, InuYasha). Vampire hunting goes to C1-7; adult splatter to C1-8.
leaves.see: C1-1 Battle Shōnen; C1-7 Vampire Anime; C9 Horror Anime
leaves.axis: by the kind of spirit fought: the afterlife first, then yōkai and demons, then curses and exorcism

leaves.label: Superpower Anime (chōnōryoku)
leaves.defn: Action whose combatants are espers or ability users with one personal power each, and whose drama is the rules of those powers (JoJo no Kimyou na Bouken, Toaru Kagaku no Railgun, Bungou Stray Dogs, Darker than Black). Costumed hero work goes to C1-13.
leaves.see: C1-13 Superhero Anime; C1-1 Battle Shōnen
leaves.axis: by how the powers are organised: one-to-one ability duels, then esper cities, then agencies and syndicates, then hunted test subjects

leaves.label: Battle Royale & Death Game Anime
leaves.defn: Action built on an enclosed, rule-bound contest in which participants must kill or be eliminated until one survives (Fate/Zero, Gantz, Darwin's Game, Juuni Taisen). An open tournament without killing goes to C1-9.
leaves.aliases: death game (desu gēmu), Holy Grail War
leaves.see: C8 Drama; Mystery & Psychological Anime; C1-3 Superpower Anime
leaves.axis: by the contest: the Holy Grail War franchise first, then other kill-or-die games

leaves.label: Battle School Anime
leaves.defn: A school or academy series, usually from a light novel, in which students rank, duel and graduate by combat magic or weapons (Mahouka Koukou no Rettousei, Rakudai Kishi no Cavalry, Gakusen Toshi Asterisk, Kill la Kill). A school setting in a Jump battle serial stays in C1-1.
leaves.aliases: gakuen battle, battle academy, magic high school
leaves.see: C1-6 Urban Fantasy Action; C5 Romance Anime
leaves.axis: by what the hierarchy rests on: magic-school rankings first, then duel-harem and uniform-weapon academies

leaves.label: Urban Fantasy Action
leaves.defn: Action in which a hidden magical or otherworldly order breaks into the contemporary city and ordinary teens fight it, chiefly from light novels and games (Shakugan no Shana, Persona 4 the Animation, Ore dake Level Up na Ken, X). Shōnen-magazine demon hunting goes to C1-2.
leaves.see: C1-2 Supernatural Battle Shōnen; C3 Fantasy & Isekai Anime
leaves.axis: by what breaks in: hidden magic among us, then dungeon gates and hunters, then demon and otherworld incursions

leaves.label: Vampire Anime
leaves.defn: Action whose fighters are vampires or vampire hunters and whose conflict is the war between the undead and the living (Hellsing Ultimate, Strike the Blood, Owari no Seraph, Blade).
leaves.see: C1-2 Supernatural Battle Shōnen; C9 Horror Anime

leaves.label: Seinen Action Anime
leaves.defn: Adult-demographic action whose fights are graphic, its heroes monstrous or compromised, and its tone nihilist (Tokyo Ghoul, Ajin, Terra Formars, Akame ga Kill!). Horror without a fighting engine goes to C9.
leaves.see: C9 Horror Anime; C1-2 Supernatural Battle Shōnen
leaves.axis: era

leaves.label: Martial Arts Anime
leaves.defn: Anime whose fights are bodily martial technique, ki, styles and lineages, contested in duels and tournaments (Dragon Ball Z, Grappler Baki, Hokuto no Ken, Saint Seiya). Weapon-based Japanese swordsmanship goes to C1-11; Chinese martial worlds to C1-12.
leaves.see: C1-1 Battle Shōnen; C1-12 Wuxia & Xianxia Animation; A7 Action & Martial Arts
leaves.axis: by the fighting tradition: ki power-escalation first, then armoured warriors, tournaments, game adaptations, school brawlers and the post-apocalyptic fist

leaves.label: Ninja Anime
leaves.defn: Anime whose fighters are shinobi using ninjutsu or ninpō, historical or modern (Naruto, Basilisk: Kouga Ninpou Chou, Juubee Ninpuuchou, Nabari no Ou).
leaves.see: C1-11 Samurai & Chanbara Anime; C1-1 Battle Shōnen
leaves.axis: by setting: the Naruto franchise first, then historical ninpō duels, then modern ninja

leaves.label: Samurai & Chanbara Anime
leaves.defn: A jidaigeki in animation: swordsmen of feudal or Bakumatsu Japan whose engine is the blade duel (Rurouni Kenshin, Samurai Champloo, Shigurui, Hakuouki). Ninja go to C1-10.
leaves.see: C1-10 Ninja Anime; A8 Historical & Period Film
leaves.axis: by era and engine: wandering swordsmen first, then Bakumatsu and Shinsengumi, Sengoku warlords, supernatural jidaigeki, battle-shōnen jidaigeki

leaves.label: Wuxia & Xianxia Animation
leaves.defn: Chinese animation (donghua) of the martial world (wuxia) or of Daoist cultivation toward immortality (xianxia), including modern-city cultivation (Mo Dao Zu Shi, Doupo Cangqiong, Scissor Seven, Yi Ren Zhi Xia).
leaves.see: C1-9 Martial Arts Anime; C3 Fantasy & Isekai Anime
leaves.axis: by the martial world: jianghu wuxia first, then xianxia cultivation epics, then modern-city cultivation

leaves.label: Superhero Anime
leaves.defn: Anime about costumed or transforming heroes who protect the public, including hero societies, henshin teams, deconstructions and American comics made in Japan (Boku no Hero Academia, One Punch Man, Tiger & Bunny, Kagaku Ninja-tai Gatchaman). Tokusatsu-derived giant heroes go to C2-5.
leaves.see: C1-3 Superpower Anime; C2-5 Tokusatsu & Kaiju Anime
leaves.axis: by the hero tradition: hero society first, then henshin and cyborg teams, parody and deconstruction, American comics

leaves.label: Delinquent Anime (yankī)
leaves.defn: Anime about high-school delinquents and bōsōzoku gangs whose engine is the street brawl and gang loyalty (Tokyo Revengers, Wind Breaker, Beelzebub).
leaves.see: C1-9 Martial Arts Anime; C10 Comedy Anime

leaves.label: Gun Action Anime
leaves.defn: Action whose engine is gunplay by hitmen, sweepers, mercenaries or armed heroines (Black Lagoon, City Hunter, Noir, Lycoris Recoil). Military units go to C1-17; cyborg police to C2-8.
leaves.aliases: girls with guns, gun fu, hitman anime
leaves.see: A2 Crime; C1-17 Military Action Anime; C2-8 Cyberpunk Anime
leaves.axis: by who holds the gun: hitmen and sweepers, then girls with guns, then mercenaries and mafia

leaves.label: Spy Anime
leaves.defn: Action whose heroes are secret agents running covert missions (Princess Principal, Spy Kyoushitsu, R.O.D: Read or Die, Yozakura-san Chi no Daisakusen).

leaves.label: Military Action Anime
leaves.defn: Action about soldiers, pilots and units in present-day or alternate-history warfare, without mecha or space settings (Area 88, Pumpkin Scissors, Kouya no Kotobuki Hikoutai). Future warfare goes to C2-7.
leaves.see: C2-7 Military Science Fiction Anime; A9 War Film

subs.label: Mecha & Science Fiction Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the science-fiction premise: giant robots first, then tokusatsu, space, war and tech-noir premises, then future societies, time and alien premises, anthologies last

leaves.label: Super Robot
leaves.defn: Mecha anime in which a unique, near-mythic giant robot piloted by a hot-blooded hero fights monsters or invaders, with named attacks and combinations (Mazinger Z, Tengen Toppa Gurren Lagann, Shinseiki Evangelion, Yuusha-Ou GaoGaiGar). Mass-produced machines in a realistic war go to C2-2.
leaves.see: C2-2 Real Robot; C2-5 Tokusatsu & Kaiju Anime
leaves.axis: by the robot's mode: 1970s classics first, then hot-blooded revivals, deconstructions, occult giants, surreal and parody robots

leaves.label: Real Robot
leaves.defn: Mecha anime in which robots are mass-produced weapons or tools in a plausible war or society, with logistics, politics and attrition (Soukou Kihei Votoms, Macross, Code Geass, Kidou Keisatsu Patlabor). The Gundam franchise is C2-3.
leaves.see: C2-3 Gundam; C2-1 Super Robot; C2-7 Military Science Fiction Anime
leaves.axis: by the battlefield: military mecha wars first, then rebellion and politics, transforming fighters, alien wars, police mecha, fantasy-world mecha, teen and comedy mecha

leaves.label: Gundam
leaves.defn: Any entry of Sunrise's Gundam franchise, the founding real-robot saga (Kidou Senshi Gundam, Kidou Senshi Zeta Gundam, Gundam Wing, Kidou Senshi Gundam: Suisei no Majo).
leaves.axis: by continuity: the Universal Century first, then alternate universes, then Gunpla battle spin-offs

leaves.label: Mecha Musume
leaves.defn: Anime whose fighters are girls fused with machine parts, warships or aircraft, or girl-shaped machines (Strike Witches, Kantai Collection: KanColle, Aoki Hagane no Arpeggio, Frame Arms Girl).
leaves.see: C2-7 Military Science Fiction Anime; C6 Slice of Life & Iyashikei Anime

leaves.label: Tokusatsu & Kaiju Anime
leaves.defn: Animation of the tokusatsu tradition, giant monsters (kaiju), Ultra-type giant heroes and Kamen Rider-type henshin armour (SSSS.Gridman, Ultraman, Godzilla: Kaijuu Wakusei, Kaijuu 8-gou).
leaves.see: C1-13 Superhero Anime; C2-1 Super Robot

leaves.label: Space Opera Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction set among starships and planets, whose scale is interstellar war, piracy or roaming adventure (Ginga Eiyuu Densetsu, Uchuu Senkan Yamato, Cowboy Bebop, Uchuu Kaizoku Captain Herlock). Space mecha go to C2-1/C2-2. Grounded spaceflight drama (Planetes, Ouritsu Uchuugun: Honneamise no Tsubasa) sits in the last section.
leaves.see: C2-2 Real Robot; C2-7 Military Science Fiction Anime
leaves.axis: by the voyage: galactic war epics first, then space pirates and wanderers, space westerns and bounty hunters, adventure, survival and grounded spaceflight last

leaves.label: Military Science Fiction Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction about future or alternate-world soldiers, fleets and wars, without giant robots as the core (Last Exile, Blue Gender, Gyakusatsu Kikan, All You Need Is Kill).
leaves.see: C2-2 Real Robot; C1-17 Military Action Anime

leaves.label: Cyberpunk Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction of high tech and low life: cyborgs, networks and megacities policed by corporations and states (Akira, Koukaku Kidoutai, Psycho-Pass, Cyberpunk: Edgerunners).
leaves.see: C2-9 Virtual Reality Anime; C2-11 Dystopian Anime
leaves.axis: by the cyberpunk strand: Ghost in the Shell first, then cyber-police and hardsuits, cyborg and android noir, megacity dystopias

leaves.label: Virtual Reality Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction whose stakes play out inside virtual worlds, games or augmented reality (Accel World, Summer Wars, Dennou Coil, Sword Art Online Alternative: Gun Gale Online). Trapped-in-another-world fantasy goes to C3.
leaves.see: C3 Fantasy & Isekai Anime; C2-8 Cyberpunk Anime

leaves.label: Android & Artificial Intelligence Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction whose subject is robots, androids and AIs as persons (Tetsuwan Atom, Pluto, Eve no Jikan, Vivy: Fluorite Eye's Song). Giant piloted robots go to C2-1/C2-2.
leaves.see: C2-8 Cyberpunk Anime; C2-1 Super Robot

leaves.label: Dystopian Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction of a controlled, unjust future society that its heroes expose or resist (Shinsekai yori, No.6, Harmony, Guilty Crown). Tech-noir megacities go to C2-8.
leaves.see: C2-8 Cyberpunk Anime; C2-12 Post-Apocalyptic Anime

leaves.label: Post-Apocalyptic Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction set after the collapse of civilisation, about surviving, wandering or rebuilding (Kaze no Tani no Nausicaä, Dr. Stone, Shoujo Shuumatsu Ryokou, Casshern Sins). Hokuto no Ken stays in C1-9.
leaves.see: C2-11 Dystopian Anime; C1-9 Martial Arts Anime
leaves.axis: by what follows the fall: rebuilding first, then wasteland action, eco-apocalypse, quiet end-of-world journeys

leaves.label: Time Travel Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction whose plot engine is time travel, time loops or crossing between parallel worlds (Steins;Gate, Toki wo Kakeru Shoujo, Noein, Gnosia).

leaves.label: Alien Invasion & First Contact Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction about aliens arriving on Earth, invading, infiltrating, or simply moving in (Kiseijuu: Sei no Kakuritsu, Seikaisuru Kado, Dead Dead Demons Dededede Destruction, Ansatsu Kyoushitsu).
leaves.see: C2-6 Space Opera Anime; C10 Comedy Anime

leaves.label: Steampunk Anime
leaves.defn: Science fiction of an alternate steam-age technology, airships and clockwork (Steamboy, Fushigi no Umi no Nadia, Sakura Taisen, Clockwork Planet).
leaves.see: C2-2 Real Robot; C1-16 Spy Anime

leaves.label: Science Fiction Anthology Film
leaves.defn: An omnibus of short SF films by several directors under one title (Memories, Robot Carnival, Manie-Manie: Meikyuu Monogatari, Genius Party).
leaves.see: C14 Animated Short; C2-8 Cyberpunk Anime

subs.label: Fantasy & Isekai Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by where the fantastic lies relative to our world: other worlds entered from ours, invented secondary worlds, myth, then the supernatural inside the modern world

leaves.label: Isekai (Transported to Another World)
leaves.defn: A series or film whose protagonist is physically carried, summoned or dropped from our world into another, and whose story turns on being an outsider there (Fushigi Yuugi, Re:Zero, Tate no Yuusha no Nariagari, Gate). Rebirth into the other world goes to C3-2; being trapped inside a game goes to C3-4.
leaves.aliases: isekai, isekai tenni, portal fantasy, reverse isekai
leaves.see: C3-2 Isekai Tensei; C3-4 Game-World Isekai; C3-3 Otome Isekai
leaves.axis: by how the hero crosses and what he does there: classic portal journeys, summoned heroes, free adventurers, modern know-how, parody; reverse isekai last

leaves.label: Isekai Tensei (Reincarnation)
leaves.defn: A story whose protagonist dies in our world and is reborn, with memories intact, into a fantasy world, as a person or as something else (Mushoku Tensei, Tensei shitara Slime Datta Ken, Kumo desu ga, Nani ka?, Isekai Nonbiri Nouka). Reborn into an otome game goes to C3-3.
leaves.aliases: tensei, isekai tensei, reincarnation isekai, slow life
leaves.axis: by what the hero is reborn as and the pace of the second life: new human life, non-human body, slow life

leaves.label: Otome Isekai (Villainess)
leaves.defn: A story whose heroine (rarely a hero) is reborn or transported into the world of an otome game or romance novel, typically as its doomed villainess, and must rewrite the plot (Otome Game no Hametsu Flag shika Nai Akuyaku Reijou ni Tensei shiteshimatta, Akuyaku Reijou Level 99, Seijo no Maryoku wa Bannou desu). A villainess romance with no crossing goes to C5-9.
leaves.aliases: akuyaku reijō, villainess isekai, otome-game isekai
leaves.see: C3-2 Isekai Tensei; C5-9 Romantic Fantasy; C5-3 Reverse Harem

leaves.label: Game-World Isekai (VRMMO & LitRPG)
leaves.defn: A story set inside an online or video game, or a world run on its rules, where the hero is a player, trapped player or transported avatar (Sword Art Online, .hack//Sign, Log Horizon, Overlord, Shangri-La Frontier). A fantasy world with mere status screens stays in C3-1.
leaves.aliases: VRMMO, LitRPG, trapped in a game
leaves.see: C3-1 Isekai; C7 Sports & Game Anime
leaves.axis: by whether the players can log out: trapped in the game, transported into a game world, voluntary VR play

leaves.label: High Fantasy
leaves.defn: A story set wholly in an invented secondary world with its own history, kingdoms and magic, built around wars, courts, journeys or the craft of magic rather than a questing party (Arslan Senki, Kemono no Souja Erin, Kino no Tabi, Little Witch Academia). Party adventure goes to C3-6; grim violence to C3-8.
leaves.see: C3-6 Sword and Sorcery; C3-8 Dark Fantasy; C5-9 Romantic Fantasy
leaves.axis: by what the world-building serves: war, court, journey, magic craft, fable

leaves.label: Sword and Sorcery
leaves.defn: A fantasy-world adventure whose engine is a hero or party of swordsmen, mages and thieves questing, fighting monsters and delving dungeons (Lodoss-tou Senki, Sousou no Frieren, Dungeon ni Deai wo Motomeru no wa Machigatteiru Darou ka, Tales of Zestiria the X). Comic sword and sorcery goes to C3-7; grimdark to C3-8.
leaves.aliases: adventure fantasy, adventurer guild, tsuihō (party exile)
leaves.see: C3-5 High Fantasy; C3-7 Comic Fantasy; C1 Action & Battle Anime
leaves.axis: by the adventuring frame: questing parties, dungeons and guilds, party-exile stories, video-game franchises last

leaves.label: Comic Fantasy
leaves.defn: A secondary-world fantasy whose primary engine is comedy and genre parody (Slayers, Dragon Half, Mairimashita! Iruma-kun). Isekai parody goes to C3-1 section 5.
leaves.see: C3-6 Sword and Sorcery; C10 Comedy Anime

leaves.label: Dark Fantasy
leaves.defn: A fantasy whose world is defined by horror, cruelty and despair, with demons, monsters and graphic violence (Berserk, Claymore, Shingeki no Kyojin, Devilman: Crybaby, Made in Abyss). Pure horror without a fantasy world goes to C9.
leaves.see: C3-6 Sword and Sorcery; C9 Horror Anime
leaves.axis: by the source of the darkness: grimdark warriors, demonic transformation, siege by monsters, gothic and fairy-tale darkness

leaves.label: Science Fantasy
leaves.defn: A fantasy whose world mixes magic with lost technology, steampunk machines or a post-apocalyptic future (Tenkuu no Shiro Laputa, Final Fantasy VII: Advent Children, Utawarerumono, Houseki no Kuni). Hard science fiction goes to C2.
leaves.see: C2 Mecha & Science Fiction Anime; C3-5 High Fantasy

leaves.label: Mythic Fiction
leaves.defn: A story built from myth and religion: gods, kami, demons and the afterlife acting in a world or limbo of their own (Mononoke Hime, Haibane Renmei, Angel Beats!, Campione!). Chinese gods-and-demons stories go to C3-11; yōkai to C3-13.
leaves.axis: by the mythology: Japanese gods and kami, gods and demons of world myth, afterlife and limbo

leaves.label: Shenmo & Xianxia
leaves.defn: A Chinese-tradition fantasy of gods, demons, immortals and spirit beasts, from the shenmo classics to cultivation (xianxia) and fox-spirit tales (Hakujaden, Nezha Zhi Mo Tong Jiang Shi, Huyao Xiao Hongniang, Fanren Xiu Xian Zhuan). Martial-arts combat-first wuxia goes to C1.
leaves.aliases: shenmo xiaoshuo, gods and demons fiction, xianxia, cultivation
leaves.see: C3-10 Mythic Fiction; C1 Action & Battle Anime

leaves.label: Urban Fantasy
leaves.defn: A story set in the contemporary everyday world where magic, monsters or a hidden supernatural society exist alongside ordinary life (Durarara!!, Kara no Kyoukai, Kyoukai no Kanata, Bakemonogatari). Japanese folklore spirits go to C3-13; ghost hunters to C3-14; vampires to C3-15.
leaves.aliases: contemporary fantasy, low fantasy, modern fantasy
leaves.see: C3-13 Yōkai; C3-14 Occult Detective Fiction; C3-15 Vampire Fiction; C1 Action & Battle Anime
leaves.axis: by how the supernatural is organised: hidden mage societies, beings in the city, everyday magic and contemporary fantasy films, the Monogatari oddity cycle

leaves.label: Yōkai Fiction
leaves.defn: A story whose supernatural beings are the yōkai, kami and spirits of Japanese folklore, met by seers, children or guardians (Natsume Yuujinchou, Mushishi, Gegege no Kitarou, Sen to Chihiro no Kamikakushi). Yōkai romances go to C5-8.
leaves.see: C3-10 Mythic Fiction; C3-12 Urban Fantasy; C5-8 Paranormal Romance
leaves.axis: by the encounter: seer and spirit tales, yōkai comedy and everyday life, battles with and for yōkai, the spirit world as a place

leaves.label: Occult Detective Fiction
leaves.defn: A story whose protagonists investigate and exorcise ghosts, curses and demons as a profession or calling (Tokyo Babylon, Ga-Rei: Zero, Koukyuu no Karasu, Muhyo to Rouji). Battle-first exorcist shōnen goes to C1.
leaves.see: C3-12 Urban Fantasy; C9 Horror Anime

leaves.label: Vampire Fiction
leaves.defn: A story whose central figures are vampires, as hunters, monsters or anti-heroes (Vampire Hunter D, Trinity Blood, Vanitas no Karte, Kizumonogatari). A vampire love story goes to C5-8.
leaves.see: C5-8 Paranormal Romance; C9 Horror Anime

subs.label: Magical Girl Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by what the heroine's magic is for: everyday wishes, battle, and the deconstruction of both

leaves.label: Majokko (Classic Magical Girl)
leaves.defn: A magical-girl series whose heroine uses magic, often with a transforming item and mascot, in everyday life rather than in battle (Mahoutsukai Sally, Mahou no Tenshi Creamy Mami, Cardcaptor Sakura, Ojamajo Doremi). Teams fighting monsters go to C4-2.
leaves.see: C4-2 Magical Girl Warrior; C11 Children's & Family Anime

leaves.label: Magical Girl Warrior
leaves.defn: A magical-girl series whose transformed heroines, usually a team, fight monsters or villains (Bishoujo Senshi Sailor Moon, Futari wa Precure, Mahou Shoujo Lyrical Nanoha, Senki Zesshou Symphogear). Grim deconstructions go to C4-3.
leaves.aliases: sentai magical girl, battle magical girl, magical boy
leaves.see: C4-1 Majokko; C4-3 Dark Magical Girl; C1 Action & Battle Anime
leaves.axis: by audience and gender play: shōjo warrior teams, otaku-oriented battle magical girls, magical boys and parodies last

leaves.label: Dark Magical Girl
leaves.defn: A magical-girl series that deconstructs the form, making the contract, battles and transformation sources of trauma, death or despair (Mahou Shoujo Madoka Magica, Yuuki Yuuna wa Yuusha de Aru, Mahou Shoujo Ikusei Keikaku, Mahou Shoujo Site).
leaves.see: C4-2 Magical Girl Warrior; C8 Drama; Mystery & Psychological Anime

subs.label: Romance Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the romantic engine: the girl's love story, comedy and harem forms, drama, then supernatural, fantasy and same-sex romance traditions

leaves.label: Shōjo Romance
leaves.defn: A love story told from a girl's point of view in the shōjo-manga tradition, about first love, confession and the couple's bond (Kimi ni Todoke, Ao Haru Ride, Marmalade Boy, Fruits Basket). Comedy-first school romance goes to C5-4; one heroine wooed by many to C5-3.
leaves.see: C5-2 Josei Romance; C5-3 Reverse Harem; C5-4 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by setting: school first love, comic and boy's-eye shōjo romance, period and adult shōjo romance

leaves.label: Josei Romance
leaves.defn: A love story about adult women's work, friendship and relationships, from the josei-manga tradition (Nana, Hachimitsu to Clover, Paradise Kiss, Wotaku ni Koi wa Muzukashii).
leaves.see: C5-1 Shōjo Romance; C5-6 Romantic Drama
leaves.axis: by tone: adult romantic drama, workplace comedy

leaves.label: Reverse Harem
leaves.defn: A romance in which one heroine is surrounded and courted by several young men (Ouran Koukou Host Club, Hana yori Dango, Uta no Prince-sama-type otome adaptations such as Kiniro no Corda, Diabolik Lovers).
leaves.see: C5-1 Shōjo Romance; C5-5 Harem; C3-3 Otome Isekai
leaves.axis: by source: shōjo-manga reverse harem, otome-game adaptations

leaves.label: Romantic Comedy
leaves.defn: A romance whose engine is comic: misunderstandings, pride, teasing and slow-burning confessions between one central couple (Toradora!, Kaguya-sama wa Kokurasetai, Karakai Jouzu no Takagi-san, Tonikaku Kawaii). A boy courted by many girls goes to C5-5; a girl's first-love story to C5-1.
leaves.see: C5-5 Harem; C5-1 Shōjo Romance; C10 Comedy Anime
leaves.axis: by the comic engine: school love comedy, teasing, otaku and gamer romance, marriage and cohabitation, workplace

leaves.label: Harem
leaves.defn: A romance in which one ordinary male lead is surrounded by several girls who desire him (Love Hina, Tenchi Muyou!, Nisekoi, 5-toubun no Hanayome). One girl courted by many men goes to C5-3.
leaves.see: C5-3 Reverse Harem; C5-4 Romantic Comedy
leaves.axis: by what assembles the harem: domestic and school setting, dating-sim adaptation, sci-fi and fantasy arrivals

leaves.label: Romantic Drama
leaves.defn: A love story whose engine is longing, loss, illness, love triangles or separation rather than comedy (Clannad, White Album 2, Byousoku 5 Centimeter, Koi wa Ameagari no You ni).
leaves.see: C5-4 Romantic Comedy; C5-7 Sekai-kei; C8 Drama; Mystery & Psychological Anime
leaves.axis: by source and age: visual-novel drama, school-age drama, adult drama, feature films

leaves.label: Sekai-kei
leaves.defn: A love story in which a teenage couple's relationship is tied directly to the fate of the world, with society in between left out (Saishuu Heiki Kanojo, Kimi no Na wa., Tenki no Ko, Seishun Buta Yarou).
leaves.see: C5-6 Romantic Drama; C2 Mecha & Science Fiction Anime

leaves.label: Paranormal Romance
leaves.defn: A love story between a human and a supernatural or artificial being: goddess, android, alien, yōkai, vampire or ghost (Aa! Megami-sama!, Chobits, Kamisama Hajimemashita, Vampire Knight). Supernatural stories without a romance engine go to C3.
leaves.see: C5-5 Harem; C3-13 Yōkai Fiction; C3-15 Vampire Fiction
leaves.axis: by the beloved's nature: goddess, android and alien; yōkai and monster; vampire; ghost

leaves.label: Romantic Fantasy
leaves.defn: A love story set in a fantasy or fairy-tale kingdom whose engine is the courtship (Akagami no Shirayuki-hime, Akatsuki no Yona, Unnamed Memory, Loop 7-kaime no Akuyaku Reijou). Rebirth into an otome game goes to C3-3.
leaves.aliases: fantasy romance, villainess romance, konyaku haki
leaves.see: C3-3 Otome Isekai; C3-5 High Fantasy
leaves.axis: by the romance plot: fairy-tale and court romance, villainess and broken-engagement romance

leaves.label: Boys' Love
leaves.defn: A romance between male characters in the boys' love (yaoi) tradition (Junjou Romantica, Given, Sasaki to Miyano, Loveless).
leaves.see: C5-11 Yuri; B5 Boys' Love & Girls' Love Drama
leaves.axis: by setting and mode: school and youth BL, adult and workplace BL, fantasy and OVA BL

leaves.label: Yuri
leaves.defn: A romance or intense bond between female characters in the yuri tradition (Maria-sama ga Miteru, Yagate Kimi ni Naru, Adachi to Shimamura, Citrus).
leaves.see: C5-10 Boys' Love; B5 Boys' Love & Girls' Love Drama
leaves.axis: by mode: everyday and school yuri, fantasy and comic yuri

subs.label: Slice of Life & Iyashikei Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by what the everyday life is organised around: a healing mood, a cute ensemble, a club, a stage, food, a job or a household.

leaves.label: Iyashikei
leaves.defn: A series or film whose purpose is to soothe: unhurried days, gentle landscapes and an absence of real conflict carry it (Aria the Animation, Non Non Biyori, Yokohama Kaidashi Kikou, Yuru Camp). If the healing comes mainly from a cast of cute girls bantering, it goes to C6-2; if from food, C6-7.
leaves.see: C6-2 Cute Girls Doing Cute Things; C6-7 Cooking & Gourmet Anime
leaves.axis: by what does the soothing: countryside and sea, a fantastical or after-the-end world, a pet, the road or the campsite

leaves.label: Cute Girls Doing Cute Things
leaves.defn: An ensemble of (usually) teenage girls whose small daily pleasures and banter are the whole story, usually adapted from a four-panel manga (Azumanga Daiou, K-On!, Kiniro Mosaic, Gochuumon wa Usagi desu ka?). A healing landscape series goes to C6-1; a band or idol arc that drives the plot goes to C6-4 or C6-5.
leaves.aliases: CGDCT; moe slice of life; kirara-kei
leaves.see: C6-1 Iyashikei; C10-4 School Comedy Anime
leaves.axis: by what the girls gather around: the classroom, a hobby or club, a café or job, a supernatural roommate, moe militaria, cat-girls and fanservice

leaves.label: Club Activity Anime (Bukatsu)
leaves.defn: A series built around an after-school or university club (bukatsu) whose activity is a hobby rather than a sport or a band: otaku circles, film-making, diving, odd societies (Genshiken, Eizouken ni wa Te wo Dasu na!, Grand Blue). A sports club goes to C7; a girls' hobby ensemble with no arc goes to C6-2.
leaves.see: C6-2 Cute Girls Doing Cute Things; C10-4 School Comedy Anime

leaves.label: Idol Anime
leaves.defn: A series whose protagonists train, debut and perform as Japanese-style pop idols (Love Live!, The iDOLM@STER, Uta no Prince-sama, Zombieland Saga). A rock band goes to C6-5; a thriller set in the idol industry goes to C8-2.
leaves.see: C6-5 Music Anime; C6-6 Performing Arts Anime
leaves.axis: by who the idols are: girl units, boy units, and genre hybrids that put idols in a horror, comedy or fantasy frame

leaves.label: Music Anime
leaves.defn: A series or film about making music as players, where rehearsal and performance are the dramatic spine (Beck, Hibike! Euphonium, Shigatsu wa Kimi no Uso, Bocchi the Rock!). Idol units go to C6-4; staged theatre and rakugo go to C6-6; a cute-girls band ensemble without a performance arc (K-On!) stays in C6-2.
leaves.see: C6-4 Idol Anime; C6-6 Performing Arts Anime
leaves.axis: by the ensemble and repertoire: rock and pop bands, concert bands and orchestras, classical soloists, and other scenes (jazz, rap battle, traditional instruments)

leaves.label: Performing Arts Anime
leaves.defn: A series about stage performers outside pop music: actors, revue and theatre troupes, rakugo storytellers, voice actors and dancers (Shouwa Genroku Rakugo Shinjuu, Kageki Shoujo!!, Glass no Kamen, Shoujo Kageki Revue Starlight). Idols go to C6-4; competitive ballroom goes to C7-11.
leaves.see: C6-4 Idol Anime; C6-5 Music Anime

leaves.label: Cooking & Gourmet Anime
leaves.defn: A series in which preparing, serving or eating food is the engine of each episode: cooking battles, home cooking, gourmet drinking and fantasy restaurants (Shokugeki no Souma, Amaama to Inazuma, Isekai Shokudou, Wakako-zake). A café used only as a backdrop for cute girls goes to C6-2.
leaves.aliases: Gurume anime; food anime; cooking manga adaptations

leaves.label: Workplace Anime (Oshigoto)
leaves.defn: A series about doing a job, in which the profession's routines, deadlines and colleagues drive the story (Shirobako, Working!!, Aggressive Retsuko, Bakuman.). A café that only frames a cute-girls ensemble goes to C6-2; a restaurant whose dishes drive it goes to C6-7.
leaves.aliases: Oshigoto anime; occupational anime; work comedy
leaves.see: C6-2 Cute Girls Doing Cute Things; C6-7 Cooking & Gourmet Anime
leaves.axis: by the trade: creative industries (anime, manga, games, voice acting), service and retail, office and salaryman life, other professions and trades

leaves.label: Family Slice of Life (Home Drama)
leaves.defn: An episodic series about a household — a single parent, a found family, siblings or a new marriage — whose daily care and quarrels are the story (Usagi Drop, Kakushigoto, Gakuen Babysitters, Ani ni Tsukeru Kusuri wa Nai!). Arc-driven family films go to C8-7; family comedy for small children goes to C11-1.
leaves.aliases: Hōmu dorama; parenting anime; ikuji anime
leaves.see: C8-7 Coming-of-Age Drama Anime; C11-1 Kodomo Anime
leaves.axis: by the household: parents and found families, siblings and household comedies, supernatural and fantasy households

leaves.label: Monster Girl Anime
leaves.defn: A slice-of-life or comedy series in which a dragon, demi-human, mermaid, vampire or other non-human girl lives in the human everyday (Kobayashi-san Chi no Maid Dragon, Demi-chan wa Kataritai, Shinryaku! Ika Musume). A fanservice harem of monster girls goes to C10-9; a demon lord working a day job goes to C10-6.
leaves.see: C10-6 Fantasy Comedy Anime; Harem Anime

subs.label: Sports & Game Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the sport or game that is played.

leaves.label: Baseball Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series or film whose contests are baseball games, typically high-school Koushien drives (Major, Touch, Diamond no Ace, Ookiku Furikabutte). A baseball con-game thriller such as One Outs stays here with see-also C8-3.

leaves.label: Football Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series whose contests are association football or another football code — rugby, American football — or a kindred contact team game (Captain Tsubasa, Inazuma Eleven, Blue Lock, Eyeshield 21).
leaves.see: C7-1 Baseball Anime; C7-3 Basketball Anime
leaves.axis: by code: association football first, then rugby, gridiron and other contact team games

leaves.label: Basketball Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series or film whose contests are basketball games (Slam Dunk, Kuroko no Basket, Ahiru no Sora). Franchise omake and NG reels stay with their series.

leaves.label: Volleyball Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series whose contests are volleyball, indoor or beach (Haikyuu!!, Attack No.1, Harukana Receive). The Attack No.1 shoujo spokon is the canonical ancestor; franchise specials stay with their series.

leaves.label: Racket Sports Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series whose contests are played with a racket or paddle: tennis, badminton, table tennis (Tennis no Oujisama, Baby Steps, Ping Pong the Animation, Hanebado!). Gag shorts such as Teekyuu go to C10-1.

leaves.label: Combat Sports Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series about a ring or mat contest — boxing, pro wrestling, judo, sumo, kendo (Ashita no Joe, Hajime no Ippo, Megalo Box, Yawara!). Fantasy fighting tournaments go to C1.

leaves.label: Racing Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series or film whose contests are races on wheels — street and touge racing, circuit and formula racing, road cycling (Initial D, Mach GoGoGo, Redline, Yowamushi Pedal).
leaves.axis: by vehicle and venue: street and touge racing, circuit and formula racing, road cycling

leaves.label: Swimming & Water Sports Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series about swimming, diving, surfing or racing on water (Free!, Dive!!, Wave!! Surfing Yappe!!). A fanservice swim-club series goes to C10-10; a diving-club comedy to C6-3.

leaves.label: Winter & Ice Sports Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series about figure skating, ice hockey or other sports on ice (Yuri!!! on Ice, Medalist, Skate-Leading Stars). Idol series that only use skating go to C6-4.

leaves.label: Horse Racing Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series about thoroughbred racing, literal or through horse-girls (Uma Musume: Pretty Derby, Gunjou no Fanfare). Small, but a recognised franchise canon.

leaves.label: Individual Sports Anime
leaves.defn: A sports series about a sport scored person by person rather than by a ball team: track and running, gymnastics and cheer, archery and golf, climbing and skating, shooting and airsoft (Kaze ga Tsuyoku Fuiteiru, Tsurune, Birdie Wing, SK8 the Infinity). Ball team sports go to C7-1 to C7-4.
leaves.see: C7-5 Racket Sports Anime; C7-6 Combat Sports Anime
leaves.axis: by discipline: track and running, gymnastics cheer and dance sport, archery golf and precision sports, climbing skating and extreme sports, shooting airsoft and tankery

leaves.label: Board Game & Mind Sport Anime
leaves.defn: A series about competitive play at a traditional table game — go, shogi, karuta, mahjong — or a quiz (Hikaru no Go, Chihayafuru, Saki, 3-gatsu no Lion). Gambling for ruinous stakes goes to C8-3.
leaves.see: C7-13 Card Game Anime; C8-3 Death Game Anime
leaves.axis: by the game: go and shogi, karuta, mahjong, other tabletop and quiz games

leaves.label: Card Game Anime
leaves.defn: A series whose battles are trading-card-game duels, usually a tie-in to the card game itself (Yu-Gi-Oh!, Cardfight!! Vanguard, Selector Infected WIXOSS). Spinning-top and figure battles go to C11-3.

leaves.label: Esports & Video Game Anime
leaves.defn: A series about competitive video-gaming or puzzle contests played as a sport (Quanzhi Gaoshou, Bokura no Ame-iro Protocol, Phi Brain). Isekai trapped in a game world go to C3.

leaves.label: Spokon (Sports-Guts Anime)
leaves.defn: The Shōwa-era supōtsu konjō ('sports guts') cycle launched by Ikki Kajiwara's Kyojin no Hoshi: a sports series of brutal training, self-sacrifice and fighting spirit, chiefly 1968–1980s (Kyojin no Hoshi, Attack No.1, Ashita no Joe, Ace wo Nerae!, Tiger Mask). Later sports anime go to their sport (C7).

subs.label: Drama, Mystery & Psychological Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the dramatic engine: a puzzle to solve, a mind under pressure, a deadly game, crime, history and war, or an emotional arc.

leaves.label: Detective & Mystery Anime
leaves.defn: A series or film built on cases to solve: a detective, sleuthing student or investigator reasons from clues to a solution (Meitantei Conan, Hyouka, Kusuriya no Hitorigoto, Gosick). A thriller where the mind duel matters more than the solution goes to C8-2.
leaves.see: C8-2 Psychological Thriller Anime; C8-4 Crime & Gangster Anime
leaves.axis: by who solves and what kind of puzzle: the boy-detective franchise, teen and school sleuths, everyday mysteries, occult and supernatural detectives, period mysteries, procedural and sci-fi investigators

leaves.label: Psychological Thriller Anime
leaves.defn: A series or film whose suspense comes from minds under pressure — duels of wits, unstable identity, manipulation and paranoia (Death Note, Perfect Blue, Monster, Zankyou no Terror). A deadly game with rules goes to C8-3; supernatural dread goes to C9.
leaves.see: C8-3 Death Game Anime; C9 Horror Anime
leaves.axis: by the source of the pressure: duels of wits and manipulation, fractured identity and perception, conspiracy and science-fiction paranoia, dark adolescence

leaves.label: Death Game Anime
leaves.defn: A series in which characters are forced into a game whose losers die, are ruined or enslaved — battle royales, survival games and high-stakes gambling (Kaiji, Mirai Nikki, Danganronpa, Kakegurui). An open-ended mind duel without a game goes to C8-2.
leaves.aliases: Death game; desu gēmu; battle royale anime; gambling anime
leaves.see: C8-2 Psychological Thriller Anime; C7-12 Board Game & Mind Sport Anime
leaves.axis: by the stakes: gambling and mind-game contests first, then death games and battle royales

leaves.label: Crime & Gangster Anime
leaves.defn: A series or film whose protagonists are criminals, thieves, gangsters or the cops who chase them (Lupin III, 91 Days, Baccano!, Banana Fish). A case-solving detective goes to C8-1.
leaves.axis: by who is at the centre: gentleman thieves and con artists, mafia and gangsters, cops and period lawmen

leaves.label: War Anime
leaves.defn: A series or film about a real or alternate-history war, its soldiers or its civilians (Hotaru no Haka, Hadashi no Gen, Kono Sekai no Katasumi ni, Kingdom). Space and mecha wars go to C2.
leaves.see: C8-6 Historical Drama Anime; C2 Mecha & Science Fiction Anime
leaves.axis: by front: home front and civilian experience, battlefield and campaign epics, espionage and alternate-history war

leaves.label: Historical Drama Anime
leaves.defn: A series or film set in a recreated historical period, whose drama comes from that period's people and politics (Vinland Saga, Versailles no Bara, Heike Monogatari, Golden Kamuy). A war-centred story goes to C8-5.
leaves.axis: by setting: Japanese period drama (jidaigeki), Chinese historical drama, European and other historical drama

leaves.label: Coming-of-Age Drama Anime
leaves.defn: A drama, series or film whose subject is growing up — first loss, friendship, vocation, identity — resolved through an emotional arc (Ano Hi Mita Hana no Namae, Koe no Katachi, Sora yori mo Tooi Basho, Blue Period). Episodic daily life goes to C6; a romance-led story goes to C5.
leaves.see: C6 Slice of Life & Iyashikei Anime; C5 Romance Anime
leaves.axis: by the arc: school-youth drama, grief and healing, vocation and adult lives, family and growing-up films, disaster and survival

leaves.label: Melodrama Anime
leaves.defn: A drama built to make the audience cry — terminal illness, lost memory, doomed love, shoujo hardship — often from nakige visual novels (Violet Evergarden, Little Busters!, Candy Candy, Kokoro Connect). A quieter coming-of-age arc goes to C8-7.

leaves.label: Medical Drama Anime
leaves.defn: A series about doctors, rescuers or the body as a hospital whose cases drive each episode (Black Jack, Young Black Jack, Megumi no Daigo).

leaves.label: Art Anime
leaves.defn: An auteur or independent work valued for form over story — wordless, painterly or allegorical (Tenshi no Tamago, Kanashimi no Belladonna, Tsumiki no Ie, Mind Game).
leaves.see: A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde; C14 Animated Short
leaves.axis: school & era

subs.label: Horror Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the source of the dread: ghosts and curses, the village, the vampire, the dead, the body, or dread played for laughs.

leaves.label: Ghost Story Anime (Kaidan)
leaves.defn: A horror series or film whose terror is a ghost, curse or urban legend in the tradition of the Japanese kaidan (Yami Shibai, Jigoku Shoujo, Another, Gakkou no Kaidan). A village cult or rural curse goes to C9-2.
leaves.aliases: Kaidan; J-horror anime; urban legend horror
leaves.see: C9-2 Folk Horror Anime; C9-6 Comedy Horror Anime
leaves.axis: by form of haunting: anthologies and urban-legend shorts, haunted schools, curses and vengeance, occult investigators and exorcists

leaves.label: Folk Horror Anime
leaves.defn: A horror series set in an isolated village or community whose customs, gods or rites are the danger (Higurashi no Naku Koro ni, Hikaru ga Shinda Natsu, Ookamikakushi).

leaves.label: Zombie Anime
leaves.defn: A horror series or film about the walking dead and the outbreak they cause (Highschool of the Dead, Biohazard: Degeneration, Gakkougurashi!).

leaves.label: Body Horror & Cosmic Horror Anime
leaves.defn: A horror series or film whose dread is the mutated body, the grotesque (ero guro) or an incomprehensible cosmic order (Uzumaki, Itou Junji: Collection, Elfen Lied, Pupa).

leaves.label: Comedy Horror Anime
leaves.defn: A series whose ghosts, curses or zombies are played for laughs as much as frights (Mieruko-chan, Zom 100, Jigoku Sensei Nube). Pure gag series with a monster mascot go to C10.

subs.label: Comedy Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the comic engine: absurd gag, parody, spin-off, school life, otaku life, a fantasy or science-fiction premise, action, harem and fanservice.

leaves.label: Gag Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy whose engine is the gag itself — non sequitur, slapstick, manzai timing, satire — with little or no plot (Nichijou, Poputepipikku, Bobobo-bo Bo-bobo, Sayonara Zetsubou Sensei). Parody of a named work goes to C10-2; a spin-off of a non-comedy series goes to C10-3.
leaves.see: C10-2 Parody Anime; C10-4 School Comedy Anime
leaves.axis: by how the gag works: surreal and absurdist, slapstick and manzai, satirical, short-form and flash

leaves.label: Parody Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy whose jokes depend on the audience knowing the genre, franchise or history it mocks (Gintama, Hayate no Gotoku!, Haiyore! Nyaruko-san, Hetalia). A chibi spin-off of one specific series goes to C10-3.
leaves.see: C10-3 Chibi Spin-off Anime; A12 Comedy
leaves.axis: by the target: jidaigeki and shounen (Gintama), genre and media parody, magical-girl and tokusatsu parody, national and historical parody

leaves.label: Chibi Spin-off Anime
leaves.defn: A short comedy spin-off of a (usually non-comedy) series, often drawn super-deformed: theatre shorts, crossovers of several franchises, omake and picture dramas (Isekai Quartet, Carnival Phantasm, Sword Art Offline, Shingeki! Kyojin Chuugakkou). An original parody goes to C10-2.
leaves.axis: by form: chibi theatres and four-panel shorts, multi-franchise crossovers, omake specials and picture dramas

leaves.label: School Comedy Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy whose jokes come from school life — classmates, the student council, a club, a teacher — rather than from a romance (Baka to Test to Shoukanjuu, Seitokai Yakuindomo, Tonari no Seki-kun, Saiki Kusuo no Psi-nan). A school romcom goes to C5; a cute-girls ensemble goes to C6-2.
leaves.see: C5 Romance Anime; C6-2 Cute Girls Doing Cute Things
leaves.axis: by the school setting: student council and club comedies, classroom and deskmate comedies, delinquents and teachers, superpowered students, elementary-school comedies

leaves.label: Otaku Comedy Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy about otaku life — fandom, games, doujinshi, cosplay, shut-ins and their embarrassments (Himouto! Umaru-chan, Watashi ga Motenai no wa Dou Kangaetemo Omaera ga Warui!, Otaku no Video). An otaku club arc goes to C6-3.
leaves.see: C6-3 Club Activity Anime; C10-2 Parody Anime

leaves.label: Fantasy Comedy Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy whose premise is a fantasy being or world — demons, gods, vampires, youkai, isekai heroes — dropped into absurd situations (Hataraku Maou-sama!, Hoozuki no Reitetsu, Saint Oniisan, Kono Healer, Mendokusai). A monster girl's quiet daily life goes to C6-10.
leaves.see: C6-10 Monster Girl Anime; C3 Fantasy & Isekai Anime
leaves.axis: by premise: demons and gods next door, vampires youkai and spirits, isekai and RPG-world comedy, witches and magic

leaves.label: Science Fiction Comedy Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy whose premise is science fiction — aliens, robots, time travel, space crews (Urusei Yatsura, Keroro Gunsou, Space Dandy, Hinamatsuri).
leaves.axis: by the science-fiction premise: alien visitors and invaders, robots androids and the body, space crews and space opera, time travel and other premises

leaves.label: Action Comedy Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy built on fights, missions or chases — martial artists, spies, ninja, cops, delinquents (Ranma 1/2, Spy x Family, Kyou kara Ore wa!!, Taiho Shichau zo).
leaves.axis: by who fights: martial artists, spies assassins and ninja, delinquents and yakuza, cops and prison comedies

leaves.label: Harem Comedy
leaves.defn: A comedy in which one protagonist is surrounded by several romantic candidates, usually with fanservice (To LOVE-Ru, High School DxD, Rosario to Vampire, Sekirei). Without the harem structure, fanservice comedy goes to C10-10; a romance-led story goes to C5.
leaves.see: C10-10 Ecchi Anime; C5 Romance Anime
leaves.axis: by premise: supernatural and demon harems, alien and science-fiction harems, fantasy-world and battle harems, domestic and school harems

leaves.label: Ecchi Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy or action series whose main appeal is sexual fanservice short of explicit sex (Prison School, Queen's Blade, Getsuyoubi no Tawawa, Keijo!!!!!!!!). With a harem structure it goes to C10-9; explicit erotica is out of scope.
leaves.axis: by vehicle of the fanservice: fanservice battle series, ecchi comedies, fetish and pin-up shorts, sports fanservice, mature and taboo ecchi

leaves.label: Gender-Bender Anime
leaves.defn: A comedy or romance whose engine is a character's change or concealment of sex: magical sex change and body transformation, or crossdressing (josō) passing (Ranma ½, Stop!! Hibari-kun!, Kämpfer, Princess Princess, Oniichan wa Oshimai!). Serious drama of gender identity goes to C8-7; body-swap romance to C5.
leaves.axis: device

subs.label: Children's & Family Anime
subs.axis: Axis: by the kind of children's property: everyday family anime, monster-partner franchise, toy tie-in, literary classic, or pre-war film.

leaves.label: Kodomo Anime
leaves.defn: Anime made for young children and the family audience: household comedies, animal tales and gentle fantasy (Doraemon, Crayon Shin-chan, Sazae-san, Gamba no Bouken). Monster-collecting franchises go to C11-2.
leaves.see: C11-2 Monster-Collecting Anime; C6-9 Family Slice of Life
leaves.axis: by mode: everyday family comedy, animal tales and fables, fantasy and adventure for children

leaves.label: Monster-Collecting Anime
leaves.defn: A children's franchise in which kids befriend, collect and battle with monster partners, tied to games (Pokemon, Digimon Adventure, Youkai Watch).
leaves.axis: by franchise: Pokemon, Digimon, other monster-partner franchises

leaves.label: Toy & Game Tie-in Anime
leaves.defn: A children's series made to sell a toy line or video game, whose battles are fought with the product (Bakuten Shoot Beyblade, Bakugan Battle Brawlers, Medarot, Rockman.EXE). Trading-card duels go to C7-13.

leaves.label: World Masterpiece Theater
leaves.defn: Nippon Animation's Sekai Meisaku Gekijou adaptations of Western children's classics and the kindred literary adaptations of the period (Akage no Anne, Flanders no Inu, Haha wo Tazunete Sanzenri, Muumin).

leaves.label: Early Japanese Animation
leaves.defn: Japanese animation from the silent era to the early 1960s, before television anime: folk-tale shorts, wartime propaganda, post-war shorts (Namakura Gatana, Momotarou: Umi no Shinpei, Kobutori).
leaves.axis: era

subs.label: Animated Feature
subs.axis: Axis: by the studio canon, production mode or tradition the feature belongs to (studio canons first, then franchise modes, national traditions, technique and auteur/adult cinema last)

leaves.label: Disney Animated Canon
leaves.defn: A theatrical feature produced by Walt Disney Animation Studios and counted in its official canon, hand-drawn or computer-animated (Snow White and the Seven Dwarfs, The Lion King, Frozen). Disney direct-to-video sequels go to C12-10; Pixar to C12-3.
leaves.aliases: Walt Disney Animation Studios features; Disney classics
leaves.see: C12-3 Pixar Films; C12-10 Direct-to-Video Animated Feature
leaves.axis: by era of the canon, in order

leaves.label: Traditional Animated Feature
leaves.defn: A hand-drawn (cel) theatrical feature from an English-language studio other than Disney (The Secret of NIMH, Watership Down, The Iron Giant). European and other auteur hand-drawn features go to C12-18.
leaves.aliases: hand-drawn animation; cel animation; classical animation
leaves.see: C12-1 Disney Animated Canon; C12-18 Arthouse Animation
secs: Studio Rivals of the Disney Renaissance and After
leaves.axis: by producing tradition

leaves.label: Pixar Films
leaves.defn: A feature produced by Pixar Animation Studios (Toy Story, WALL·E, Inside Out, Coco). Pixar short films go to C14-2.
leaves.see: C12-1 Disney Animated Canon; C14-2 Pixar Short Films

leaves.label: DreamWorks Animation
leaves.defn: A feature produced by DreamWorks Animation, from its hand-drawn epics to its computer-animated franchises (The Prince of Egypt, Shrek, Kung Fu Panda, How to Train Your Dragon). DreamWorks shorts and specials go to C14.
leaves.axis: by the film's engine or franchise

leaves.label: Computer-Animated Family Film
leaves.defn: A computer-animated family feature from a Hollywood or American studio other than Disney, Pixar and DreamWorks (Despicable Me, Ice Age, Cloudy with a Chance of Meatballs, The Lego Movie). European, Latin American and Asian mainstream features go to C12-7; motion-capture films to C12-6.
leaves.aliases: CGI family film; CG animated comedy
leaves.see: C12-4 DreamWorks Animation; C12-6 Performance-Capture Animation; C12-7 International Family Animated Feature
secs: Warner Bros. CG Features & Lego Films
leaves.axis: by producing studio

leaves.label: Performance-Capture Animation
leaves.defn: A feature animated from motion- or performance-captured actors rather than keyframed (The Polar Express, Beowulf, The Adventures of Tintin). Rotoscoped films go to C12-17.
leaves.see: C12-17 Rotoscoped Feature; C12-5 Computer-Animated Family Film

leaves.label: International Family Animated Feature
leaves.defn: A mainstream family feature (mostly computer-animated) from a European, Latin American, African or Asian studio outside the auteur circuit (Arthur and the Invisibles, Planet 51, Mavka: The Forest Song, BoBoiBoy: The Movie). Festival auteur features go to C12-18; Chinese features to C12-14.
leaves.see: C12-18 Arthouse Animation; C12-14 Chinese Animation
leaves.axis: by region of production

leaves.label: Live-Action/Animated Film
leaves.defn: A feature combining live-action footage with animated characters, including photoreal 'live-action' remakes made wholly in CG (Who Framed Roger Rabbit, Space Jam, Cool World, The Lion King (2019)).
leaves.see: C12-5 Computer-Animated Family Film; C12-1 Disney Animated Canon

leaves.label: Television Spin-off Feature
leaves.defn: A feature (theatrical, streaming or TV movie) continuing the cast and world of a specific animated series (The Simpsons Movie, The SpongeBob SquarePants Movie, South Park: Bigger, Longer & Uncut, Futurama: Bender's Big Score). Scooby-Doo films go to C12-10; DC and Marvel films to C12-12.
leaves.see: C12-10 Direct-to-Video Animated Feature; C13-7 Nicktoons
leaves.axis: by the series' network or audience

leaves.label: Direct-to-Video Animated Feature
leaves.defn: A feature made for home video (later streaming) as a sequel to a theatrical film or as an entry of a long-running franchise (The Return of Jafar, Tinker Bell, Scooby-Doo on Zombie Island, The Land Before Time II).
leaves.see: C12-1 Disney Animated Canon; C12-9 Television Spin-off Feature
leaves.axis: by franchise

leaves.label: Toy-Based Film
leaves.defn: A feature produced to extend a toy or doll line (Barbie in the Nutcracker, Monster High: Ghouls Rule!, Bionicle: Mask of Light, My Little Pony: Equestria Girls). Theatrical Lego films go to C12-5.
leaves.see: C12-10 Direct-to-Video Animated Feature; C13-12 Toy-Based Animated Series
leaves.axis: by toy line

leaves.label: Superhero Animated Feature
leaves.defn: An animated feature whose protagonists are comic-book superheroes, chiefly DC and Marvel (Batman: Mask of the Phantasm, Batman: Under the Red Hood, Justice League: The Flashpoint Paradox, Spider-Man: Into the Spider-Verse). Superhero comedies of a studio canon (The Incredibles) stay with C12-3.
leaves.aliases: DC Universe Animated Original Movies; DCAU films
secs: Superman, Wonder Woman & Green Lantern Films
leaves.axis: by franchise

leaves.label: Franco-Belgian Comics Adaptation
leaves.defn: An animated feature adapting a bande dessinée or Spanish historieta series (Asterix the Gaul, The Twelve Tasks of Asterix, Seven Crystal Balls and the Prisoners of the Sun). Sony's Smurfs films stay in C12-5.
leaves.see: C12-18 Arthouse Animation; C12-7 International Family Animated Feature

leaves.label: Chinese Animation
leaves.defn: A feature from the Chinese animation tradition (donghua), from the Shanghai Animation Film Studio classics to the 2010s revival (Havoc in Heaven, Big Fish & Begonia, Ne Zha).
leaves.axis: era

leaves.label: Faith-Based Animated Film
leaves.defn: An animated feature made to retell scripture or religious narrative for devotional audiences (The Star, The King of Kings, Mahavatar Narsimha). DreamWorks' The Prince of Egypt stays in C12-4.
leaves.aliases: Christian animation; Bible animation; devotional film

leaves.label: Stop-Motion Feature
leaves.defn: A feature animated frame by frame with puppets, clay, cut-outs or objects (The Nightmare Before Christmas, Chicken Run, Coraline, My Life as a Zucchini).
leaves.see: C14-6 Stop-Motion & Puppet Short; C12-18 Arthouse Animation
leaves.axis: by studio tradition

leaves.label: Rotoscoped Feature
leaves.defn: A feature animated by tracing or painting over live-action footage (Waking Life, A Scanner Darkly, Loving Vincent, Bakshi's The Lord of the Rings).
leaves.see: C12-6 Performance-Capture Animation; C12-19 Adult Animation

leaves.label: Arthouse Animation
leaves.defn: An auteur-driven animated feature made for the festival and art-cinema circuit, usually outside the US studio system (The Triplets of Belleville, The Secret of Kells, Persepolis, Flow). Stop-motion auteur features go to C12-16; mainstream European family films to C12-7.
leaves.aliases: auteur animation; independent animation; European animation
leaves.see: C12-16 Stop-Motion Feature; C12-7 International Family Animated Feature
secs: North American, Israeli & South Asian Independent
leaves.axis: by national tradition

leaves.label: Adult Animation
leaves.defn: An animated feature made for adults through explicit sex, violence or transgressive comedy (Fritz the Cat, Heavy Metal, Sausage Party, The Witcher: Nightmare of the Wolf). Adult auteur features go to C12-18; adult series features to C12-9.
leaves.see: C12-18 Arthouse Animation; C12-17 Rotoscoped Feature
leaves.axis: by the adult engine

leaves.label: Animated Documentary
leaves.defn: A non-fiction film told wholly or chiefly through animation: reconstructed memory, testimony or reportage drawn, painted or modelled instead of filmed (Waltz with Bashir, Flee, Ryan, The Sinking of the Lusitania). Live-action documentaries with animated inserts stay in A19.

subs.label: Animated Series
subs.axis: Axis: by format and audience (prime-time and adult first, then network-canon children's comedy, action genres, national traditions and preschool last)

leaves.label: Animated Sitcom
leaves.defn: A situation comedy in animated form built on a fixed household, workplace or ensemble (The Simpsons, King of the Hill, Futurama, Daria). Adult Swim-style absurdist or shock comedy goes to C13-2; network-canon children's comedies to C13-7–C13-9.
leaves.see: C13-2 Adult Animated Comedy; B8 Comedy Series
leaves.axis: by setting and comic engine

leaves.label: Adult Animated Comedy
leaves.defn: An animated comedy series for adults whose engine is parody, absurdism or shock rather than the sitcom household (Aqua Teen Hunger Force, Robot Chicken, South Park, Archer).
leaves.see: C13-1 Animated Sitcom; C13-3 Adult Animated Action & Drama
leaves.axis: by comic engine

leaves.label: Adult Animated Action & Drama
leaves.defn: A non-comic animated series for adults: violent action, horror, epic or psychological drama (Æon Flux, Castlevania, Arcane, Invincible).
leaves.see: C13-2 Adult Animated Comedy; C13-11 Superhero Animated Series
leaves.axis: by source and mode

leaves.label: Saturday-Morning Cartoon
leaves.defn: A comedy cartoon series made for US network or syndicated children's slots from the 1960s to the 1990s, including television packages and revivals of theatrical cartoon stars (The Bugs Bunny Show, The Yogi Bear Show, Scooby-Doo, Where Are You!, Animaniacs). Action cartoons of the same slots go to C13-11–C13-13.
leaves.see: C13-6 The Disney Afternoon; C14-1 Theatrical Cartoon
leaves.axis: by origin of the characters

leaves.label: The Disney Afternoon
leaves.defn: A series of the Disney Afternoon syndicated block and its revivals (DuckTales, Chip 'n' Dale Rescue Rangers, Darkwing Duck, Gargoyles).
leaves.see: C13-9 Disney Television Animation; C13-10 Film Spin-off Series

leaves.label: Nicktoons
leaves.defn: An original animated series of Nickelodeon's Nicktoons brand (Rugrats, The Ren & Stimpy Show, SpongeBob SquarePants, The Loud House). Nickelodeon's action series (Avatar) go to C13-13.
leaves.see: C13-8 Cartoon Cartoons; C13-9 Disney Television Animation

leaves.label: Cartoon Cartoons
leaves.defn: An original series of Cartoon Network Studios, from the Cartoon Cartoons brand to its later creator-driven shows (Dexter's Laboratory, The Powerpuff Girls, Adventure Time, Steven Universe). Samurai Jack and DC series go to C13-13 and C13-11.
leaves.see: C13-7 Nicktoons; C13-9 Disney Television Animation
leaves.axis: by period of the brand

leaves.label: Disney Television Animation
leaves.defn: An original series of Disney Television Animation for Disney Channel, Disney XD or ABC, not based on a feature film (Recess, Phineas and Ferb, Gravity Falls, The Owl House). Feature spin-offs go to C13-10; Disney Junior series to C13-15.
leaves.see: C13-6 The Disney Afternoon; C13-10 Film Spin-off Series

leaves.label: Film Spin-off Series
leaves.defn: A series continuing the characters of a specific feature film (Lilo & Stitch: The Series, The Penguins of Madagascar, The Real Ghostbusters, Dug Days). Star Wars and superhero series go to their genre leaves.
leaves.see: C13-6 The Disney Afternoon; C12-9 Television Spin-off Feature
leaves.axis: by source studio

leaves.label: Superhero Animated Series
leaves.defn: A series whose protagonists are costumed superheroes (Batman: The Animated Series, X-Men, Teen Titans, The Spectacular Spider-Man). Adult superhero series go to C13-3.
leaves.see: C13-3 Adult Animated Action & Drama; C12-12 Superhero Animated Feature
leaves.axis: by franchise

leaves.label: Toy-Based Animated Series
leaves.defn: A series created with or to sell a toy line, the 'program-length commercial' of 1980s syndication and its reboots (He-Man and the Masters of the Universe, The Transformers, G.I. Joe, My Little Pony: Friendship Is Magic).
leaves.see: C13-13 Action-Adventure Animated Series; C12-11 Toy-Based Film
leaves.axis: by period and toy type

leaves.label: Action-Adventure Animated Series
leaves.defn: A children's or family series built on adventure, quests and combat rather than gags (Jonny Quest, Star Wars: The Clone Wars, Avatar: The Last Airbender, Code Lyoko). Superhero and toy-line series go to C13-11 and C13-12.
leaves.see: C13-11 Superhero Animated Series; C13-12 Toy-Based Animated Series
leaves.axis: by premise

leaves.label: European Children's Animated Series
leaves.defn: A children's series from a European tradition, from Soyuzmultfilm and the Czech, Polish and Hungarian studios to British and French television (Well, Just You Wait!, The Adventures of the Mole, Bolek and Lolek, Oggy and the Cockroaches). European preschool series go to C13-15.
leaves.axis: by national tradition

leaves.label: Preschool Animated Series
leaves.defn: A series made for children under six, built on gentle storytelling, curriculum or play (Little Bear, Dora the Explorer, Thomas & Friends, Bluey).
leaves.aliases: preschool television; Disney Junior; Nick Jr.
leaves.axis: by format

leaves.label: Educational Animated Series
leaves.defn: A series whose stated purpose is teaching a subject, from history to science and literacy (Schoolhouse Rock!, Once Upon a Time… Man, The Magic School Bus).

subs.label: Animated Short
subs.axis: Axis: by production context (theatrical studio cartoons, studio shorts, art shorts, technique, television specials)

leaves.label: Theatrical Cartoon
leaves.defn: A short made for cinema programmes by a studio or pioneer from the silent era to the end of the studio system (Gertie the Dinosaur, Steamboat Willie, Duck Amuck, What's Opera, Doc?).
leaves.aliases: Golden Age cartoon; Looney Tunes; Silly Symphonies
leaves.axis: studio of the Golden Age of American animation

leaves.label: Pixar Short Films
leaves.defn: A short produced by Pixar or its Lucasfilm Graphics Group precursor (Luxo Jr., Geri's Game, Bao, Jack-Jack Attack).
leaves.see: C12-3 Pixar Films; C14-3 Studio Short Film
leaves.axis: by period and release

leaves.label: Studio Short Film
leaves.defn: A post-studio-era short from a major animation studio or franchise, released theatrically, on home video or streaming (Paperman, Feast, Far Far Away Idol, The Longest Daycare).
leaves.see: C14-2 Pixar Short Films; C14-7 Animated Television Special
secs: Franchise Shorts from Television & Other Studios
leaves.axis: by studio

leaves.label: Abstract Animation
leaves.defn: A short of non-figurative form, colour and rhythm, often drawn on film or set to music (Begone Dull Care, Motion Painting No. 1, Free Radicals). Figurative auteur shorts go to C14-5.
leaves.aliases: visual music; direct animation; absolute film
leaves.see: C14-5 Auteur Animated Short; A20 Experimental & Avant-Garde
leaves.axis: by era of release, earliest first

leaves.label: Auteur Animated Short
leaves.defn: An independent or state-studio art short driven by its maker's vision, the festival short of the European and world schools (Piccolo, Hedgehog in the Fog, The Street, Father and Daughter, The Windshield Wiper). American independents go to American Independent Animation; the National Film Board of Canada to its own leaf; stop-motion art shorts to C14-6.
leaves.aliases: art short; festival short; NFB; Zagreb School
leaves.see: C14-4 Abstract Animation; C14-6 Stop-Motion & Puppet Short
secs: Italian, Iberian, German, Dutch & Nordic Shorts
leaves.axis: by national school: the Zagreb School first, then the Polish School, the Czech-Hungarian-Bulgarian studios, the Soviet and post-Soviet schools, British, French-Belgian-Swiss and other Western European shorts, and the rest of the world last

leaves.label: American Independent Animation
leaves.breadth: US auteur shorts outside the studio system, from the underground to the festival circuit
leaves.defn: An auteur animated short made in the United States outside the studio system — the underground collage and experimental film, the independent studio short of the Hubleys and their circle, the art-school short, the web-era indie and the studio artist's personal festival short (Number 11: Mirror Animations, The Hole, Asparagus, Rejected, World of Tomorrow, Hair Love). Test: American production, an individual maker's vision; non-figurative work goes to C14-4, studio shorts to C14-3.
leaves.axis: by circle and era: underground and collage animation first, then the Hubleys and the independent studio short, the art-school and underground cartoon, Hertzfeldt and the web-era indies, and studio artists' personal festival shorts last

leaves.label: National Film Board of Canada Animation
leaves.breadth: auteur shorts of the NFB animation studios and the Canadian state-broadcaster tradition beside them
leaves.defn: An auteur animated short from the National Film Board of Canada's English and French animation studios, or from the Canadian public-broadcaster tradition around it (Neighbours, The Street, The Sweater, The Big Snit, The Man Who Planted Trees, When the Day Breaks). Test: a Canadian state-studio production; independents elsewhere stay in C14-5.

leaves.label: Stop-Motion & Puppet Short
leaves.defn: A short animated with puppets, clay or objects (The Cameraman's Revenge, Dimensions of Dialogue, The Wrong Trousers, Harvie Krumpet).
leaves.see: C12-16 Stop-Motion Feature; C14-5 Auteur Animated Short
leaves.axis: by tradition

leaves.label: Animated Television Special
leaves.defn: A one-off animated programme made for television, typically a holiday special (A Charlie Brown Christmas, How the Grinch Stole Christmas!, Rudolph the Red-Nosed Reindeer, The Gruffalo).
leaves.see: C14-3 Studio Short Film; C12-10 Direct-to-Video Animated Feature
leaves.axis: by period and source

leaves.label: Soviet Animation
leaves.defn: The state-studio animation of the USSR, above all Soyuzmultfilm (Moscow) with Kievnauchfilm, Uzbekfilm and Ekran: fairy-tale features and shorts, satirical and modernist art shorts and the children's classics of its 'Golden Collection' (The Snow Queen, Film, Film, Film, Winnie-the-Pooh, Hedgehog in the Fog, Three from Prostokvashino). Soviet TV serials go to C13-14; Estonian and post-Soviet auteur shorts to C14-5.
leaves.axis: era

familyKey: 1. Is it animated, in any format? → C Animation: Japanese animation (anime) by genre in C1–C11; other animation as C12 feature, C13 series or C14 short.

2. Is it internet-native — a web series, an online video channel or show, an app micro-drama? → not classified here: it belongs to the future Interactive Entertainment Taxonomy (the finder keeps a row). A series made for subscription streaming (Netflix, Prime, iQIYI, Tencent, Indian streaming 'web series') is television.
3. Is it a single film? → A Film: 40 minutes or less → A21 Short Film; otherwise by movement and genre (A1–A20).

4. Otherwise it is television → B: a live event or sports broadcast → B16; an unscripted format → B13–B15; a long-running serial in a named serial tradition (telenovela, soap opera, dizi, Indian daily soap, musalsal, teleserye) → B12; a series in a named East or Southeast Asian drama tradition → B2–B6; any other scripted series or documentary series → its genre sub-family (B1, B7–B11).
precedence: A film with a home in a named genre cycle (chanbara, kaidan, J-horror, yakuza, film noir, pink film, Roman Porno, pinky violence, kaiju, tokusatsu, Taiyōzoku) goes to that cycle, even when a movement's reference sources list it as a member. A movement leaf keeps the attested members with no cycle home; every attested member carries the movement as a tag (D1).
A named cycle with its own canon (J-horror, kaiju eiga, yakuza eiga, pink film) beats the general genre leaf (supernatural horror, monster film, gangster film, sexploitation).
